passages.passage_text:
If someone asked you where the skyscraper was born, what would you answer? Most people would probably say New York City, but they would be wrong. Chicago was the birthplace of the skyscraper.

Dictionaries define a skyscraper as "a building of great height which is constructed on a steel skeleton." The first building to fit that description was the Home Insurance Company Building. It was built in Chicago in 1884. It was 10 storeys, i.e. floors, high - a great height for that time. It had a strong framework (structure) of iron and steel instead of walls of stone to support it.

The Home Insurance Company Building does not exist any more, they pulled it down in 1931, but visitors to the city can still see other early Chicago skyscrapers. One of them is the 16-storey Reliance Building, which was completed in 1894. The Reliance Building had windows that, for the first time, covered almost the entire surface.

For many years, Chicago was behind New York in the construction of skyscrapers. It got back into the competition with buildings like the John Hancock Center, built in 1968. There are luxury flats on forty-nine of the Center's 100 floors. Sometimes people who live on a high floor look out on a sunny sky while those on the downstairs floors can watch the rain from their windows.

Architects and engineers have the technology to build even taller structures, but to do this, they must find the money for them and these new skyscrapers should not harm the environment.

Back in 1956, the famous architect Frank Lloyd Wright dreamed of a skyscraper of 528 floors. He planned to build it near the shore of Lake Michigan in Chicago. Wright's dream never became a reality, but who knows? Someday somebody may build his tower in the city where the skyscraper was born.

passages.title: Skyscrapers
passages.tts_script:
Skyscrapers.

If someone asked you where the skyscraper was born, what would you answer? Most people would probably say New York City, but they would be wrong. Chicago was the birthplace of the skyscraper.

Dictionaries define a skyscraper as "a building of great height which is constructed on a steel skeleton." The first building to fit that description was the Home Insurance Company Building. It was built in Chicago in 1884. It was 10 storeys, that is, floors, high, a great height for that time. It had a strong framework, or structure, of iron and steel instead of walls of stone to support it.

The Home Insurance Company Building does not exist any more, they pulled it down in 1931, but visitors to the city can still see other early Chicago skyscrapers. One of them is the 16-storey Reliance Building, which was completed in 1894. The Reliance Building had windows that, for the first time, covered almost the entire surface.

For many years, Chicago was behind New York in the construction of skyscrapers. It got back into the competition with buildings like the John Hancock Center, built in 1968. There are luxury flats on forty-nine of the Center's 100 floors. Sometimes people who live on a high floor look out on a sunny sky while those on the downstairs floors can watch the rain from their windows.

Architects and engineers have the technology to build even taller structures, but to do this, they must find the money for them and these new skyscrapers should not harm the environment.

Back in 1956, the famous architect Frank Lloyd Wright dreamed of a skyscraper of 528 floors. He planned to build it near the shore of Lake Michigan in Chicago. Wright's dream never became a reality, but who knows? Someday somebody may build his tower in the city where the skyscraper was born.

passages.passage_text:
There are many different types of climate in the world. This article discusses the various types of temperate climates, that is, the climates that are free from very high and very low temperatures.

The world's temperate regions are divided into warm and cool zones. In the warm temperate zones, the average temperature does not drop below 6°C in the coldest month of the year. This is the lowest possible temperature necessary for growing plants all year round. There are two different kinds of warm temperate regions. One is the western or Mediterranean type (dry, hot summers and mild, wet winters) found on the western coasts and across southern Europe. The other kind is called the eastern or China type. This kind of climate is influenced by winds and is wetter, with mild winters and hot, humid summers.

The cool temperate zones, on the other hand, have a cold season. There are as many as five months a year when the average temperature goes below 6°C. There are two different kinds of cool temperate zones. One type is called a maritime zone, with frequent changes in weather conditions. The other is called a continental region, with warmer summers and cold winters.

passages.passage_text:
Man has never been satisfied with simply talking. For some reason he has always considered his ideas to be so important that he has always tried to find ways to record them on paper. Man has developed many systems of writing; he also developed various tools with which to write.

One of the first instruments developed by man for writing was the stylus. It was a sharp instrument made of bone or metal, and with it the writer could make marks on stone or wood. It was used for thousands of years and was very practical.

The idea of using pen and ink was developed by the Egyptians. Their version of the pen was made from bamboo. They sharpened one end of the stem (or the body) to make a nib, that is, the point which you write with. Then they filled the empty part of the stem with ink and forced the ink onto the nib. It was a good idea, but when paper was later introduced, a much finer instrument was needed.

The problem was solved with the introduction of the quill pen. The quill is a large feather from the wing or tail of a bird. The quill also gave us the word 'pen' - feather in Latin is penna. Because this pen was a feather, however, it had to be sharpened quite often. A special instrument was made for this purpose, the penknife.

The quill was used from the 6th through the 18th century, but in the 19th century a machine was invented which successfully made a nib out of metal and which, thus, solved the problem of sharpening. The nib could be fitted into a holder and dipped into a bottle of ink. Finally, in 1884, a young American, Lewis Waterman, found a way of putting the ink into the holder, and the fountain pen as we know it was complete.

Although the fountain pen was very popular, a more popular kind of pen was introduced in 1943. This was the ball-point pen, invented by Laszlo Biro, an Argentinian.

For example, students who take handwritten notes often understand complex lessons more deeply because they must summarize key ideas in their own words. Second, a pen requires no battery, internet connection, or electricity, making it reliable in almost any situation—from filling out official forms to jotting down quick reminders. Finally, handwritten letters and cards carry a personal touch that digital messages cannot easily replace. Of course, computers and smartphones are much faster for editing long documents and sharing work across distances. Nevertheless, teaching and practicing handwriting alongside digital skills ensures that people stay creative, focused, and independent of technology when necessary.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Kalem.

İnsanoğlu hiçbir zaman yalnızca konuşmakla yetinmemiştir. Nedense fikirlerini her zaman o kadar önemli görmüştür ki onları kâğıda kaydetmenin yollarını bulmaya çalışmıştır. İnsan birçok yazı sistemi geliştirmiş; aynı zamanda yazı yazmak için çeşitli araçlar da geliştirmiştir.

İnsanoğlunun yazı yazmak için geliştirdiği ilk araçlardan biri stilus (yazı çubuğu) idi. Kemikten veya metalden yapılmış sivri bir aletti ve yazar bununla taş veya ahşap üzerine işaretler yapabiliyordu. Binlerce yıl boyunca kullanıldı ve çok pratikti.

Kalem ve mürekkep kullanma fikri Mısırlılar tarafından geliştirildi. Onların kalem versiyonu bambudan yapılmıştı. Gövdenin bir ucunu sivriltip yazı yazılan uç olan kalem ucunu oluşturdular. Ardından gövdenin boş kısmını mürekkeple doldurup mürekkebi uca doğru ittiler. Bu iyi bir fikirdi; ancak daha sonra kâğıt ortaya çıktığında çok daha ince bir araca ihtiyaç duyuldu.

Sorun, tüy kalemin ortaya çıkmasıyla çözüldü. Tüy kalem, bir kuşun kanadından veya kuyruğundan alınan büyük bir tüydür. Latincede tüy anlamına gelen "penna" kelimesinden dolayı İngilizcedeki "pen" (kalem) sözcüğü de buradan gelmektedir. Ancak bu kalem bir tüy olduğu için oldukça sık yontulması gerekiyordu. Bu amaçla özel bir alet yapıldı: çakı (penknife).

Tüy kalem 6. yüzyıldan 18. yüzyıla kadar kullanıldı; ancak 19. yüzyılda metalden başarıyla kalem ucu üreten ve böylece yontma sorununu çözen bir makine icat edildi. Uç bir sapın içine yerleştirilebiliyor ve mürekkep şişesine batırılabiliyordu. Nihayet 1884'te Lewis Waterman adlı genç bir Amerikalı mürekkebi sapın içine koymanın bir yolunu buldu ve bugün bildiğimiz dolma kalem tamamlanmış oldu.

Dolma kalem çok popüler olmasına rağmen, 1943'te daha da popüler bir kalem türü piyasaya sürüldü. Bu, Arjantinli Laszlo Biro tarafından icat edilen tükenmez kalemdi.

passages.passage_text:
Students of English as a foreign language often ask teachers which newspaper to read. They naturally suppose that reading an English newspaper will be a good way of improving their knowledge of the language. But they are frequently disappointed because they cannot understand popular newspapers and think the 'quality' newspapers will be even more difficult.

In fact, the opposite is usually the case. Popular newspapers are written for people who haven't got much time for reading and who, perhaps, do not read as fast or enjoy reading as much as people who buy 'quality' newspapers. So, the editors try to attract the readers' attention with sensational headlines in big black type. The headlines do not explain the content of the news item underneath. On the contrary, they are often designed to puzzle the reader so that he will be persuaded to read the item to find out the meaning of the headline! Apart from that, they use double meanings, so a foreign reader is usually confused by them. Editors are also afraid that the readers will not be patient enough to read a long paragraph. Therefore, almost every sentence becomes a paragraph in itself, which is also a disadvantage for the student of English as a foreign language.

passages.title: Popular vs. Quality Newspapers
passages.tts_script:
Popular versus Quality Newspapers.

Students of English as a foreign language often ask teachers which newspaper to read. They naturally suppose that reading an English newspaper will be a good way of improving their knowledge of the language. But they are frequently disappointed because they cannot understand popular newspapers and think the quality newspapers will be even more difficult.

In fact, the opposite is usually the case. Popular newspapers are written for people who haven't got much time for reading and who, perhaps, do not read as fast or enjoy reading as much as people who buy quality newspapers. So, the editors try to attract the readers' attention with sensational headlines in big black type. The headlines do not explain the content of the news item underneath. On the contrary, they are often designed to puzzle the reader so that he will be persuaded to read the item to find out the meaning of the headline! Apart from that, they use double meanings, so a foreign reader is usually confused by them. Editors are also afraid that the readers will not be patient enough to read a long paragraph. Therefore, almost every sentence becomes a paragraph in itself, which is also a disadvantage for the student of English as a foreign language.

Neden-sonuç bağlaçlarını (because, therefore, so that) doğru ve akıcı kullandım.
Kelime sayısını ve İngilizce dil bilgisi doğruluğunu kontrol ettim.

task1.model_answer: Many English learners assume that quality newspapers are harder to read than popular ones, yet the reverse is usually true. Popular newspapers target busy readers who may dislike long reading sessions. Consequently, editors rely on eye-catching headlines that hide the story's meaning, use wordplay with double meanings, and turn single sentences into separate paragraphs. While these techniques attract casual readers, they often confuse language learners and make popular newspapers surprisingly difficult to follow.
task1.prompt: Summarize why popular newspapers can be more difficult for English learners than quality newspapers.
task1.title: Summarizing Challenges of Popular Newspapers

task2.model_answer: Reading news in English is a great habit for language learners, and choosing the right kind of source makes a big difference. Based on the passage, quality newspapers are generally more useful than popular newspapers for improving English. First, quality newspapers usually write clear headlines that summarize the article, helping learners predict the main topic before reading. By contrast, puzzling headlines and double meanings in popular papers waste time and create frustration. Second, full paragraphs in quality newspapers show how ideas connect naturally through linking words, which teaches students both reading comprehension and good writing structure. However, learners should still choose topics they genuinely enjoy, such as technology, sports, or culture, and start with short articles rather than trying to read an entire newspaper at once. Using an online dictionary sparingly for key unknown words will also keep reading enjoyable. Overall, clear and well-structured news articles provide the best support for language growth.

Bunun dışında çift anlamlı ifadeler kullanırlar, bu yüzden yabancı bir okuyucunun bunlardan dolayı kafası genellikle karışır. Editörler ayrıca okuyucuların uzun bir paragrafı okuyacak kadar sabırlı olmayacağından da korkarlar. Bu nedenle neredeyse her cümle tek başına bir paragraf hâline gelir ki bu da İngilizceyi yabancı dil olarak öğrenen öğrenci için bir başka dezavantajdır.

Acid rain is caused by burning coal or oil. When either fuel is burned, it releases poisonous gases which are carried up into the atmosphere and sometimes transported long distances.

Over 3,000 research projects have been carried out to look into acid rain, and a decision to tackle the problem has been taken in most of the Western European countries. Measures have been taken in Scandinavia and in Central Europe to stop the pollution before it is dumped on the environment, and a diplomatic campaign has been launched to convince the other countries that the problem has to be considered as a major ecological threat.

"Five years ago this issue was not being treated seriously," says one leading environmental group, "but now that damage has been reported in large areas of forest and lakeland, our politicians are being forced to take action. This problem must be solved quickly: if governments do nothing, they will be faced in two or three years' time with the accusation that they have allowed our forests to die." passages.passage_text:
According to some scientists, one of the most serious problems for the environment is acid rain. Acid rain is caused mainly by power plants that burn coal to produce electricity. The smoke from these power plants contains acidic substances which later fall back to earth in rain or snow. As a result, the amount of acid in lakes and rivers increases, causing the fish to die. passages.passage_text:
In the middle of the Pacific Ocean, thousands of miles from the nearest mainland, lie the islands of Polynesia. On some of the islands, there are ancient roads and buildings. These show that there have been ancient civilizations on the islands. The most mysterious of the Polynesian Islands is Easter Island, where there are giant heads made of stone. Some of them are as tall as a four-storey building. These are very old. Obviously men have been living on these islands for a long, long time. But how did the islanders first get to the islands so long ago, and how did they do it when there weren't any big ships? These are some of the questions which are difficult to answer.

Thor Heyerdahl, a Norwegian explorer, thought he had the answer to the mystery. He believed the people from Ancient Peru sailed more than 6,000 kilometres across the Pacific Ocean on their small rafts to start a new life on the islands of Polynesia.

Nobody believed Heyerdahl because they knew that the people of ancient Peru only had wooden rafts to sail on. How did the people sail from Peru to the islands? Heyerdahl wanted to show everybody that his theory was right. Together with four friends, he started to build a raft like those of the ancient Peruvians. When it was finished they called it Kon-Tiki, the name of an ancient god. They spent a long time planning their journey and deciding what to take with them.

The natural movement of the water (a current called the Peru Current) carried them west. Although they had lots of problems during their journey with the weather and sharks, the boat was fine—it didn't sink. After 102 hard days at sea, the explorers arrived on one of the Polynesian Islands. Heyerdahl proved it was possible.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Kon-Tiki Yolculuğu, 1947.

Pasifik Okyanusu'nun ortasında, en yakın anakaradan binlerce mil uzakta Polinezya adaları yer alır. Adaların bazılarında antik yollar ve binalar vardır. Bunlar, adalarda eski uygarlıkların var olduğunu gösterir. Polinezya Adaları'nın en gizemlisi, taştan yapılmış dev başların bulunduğu Paskalya Adası'dır. Bunların bazıları dört katlı bir bina kadar uzundur. Bunlar çok eskidir. Belli ki insanlar bu adalarda çok ama çok uzun zamandır yaşamaktadır. Peki ada sakinleri bu kadar uzun zaman önce adalara ilk olarak nasıl ulaştılar ve büyük gemilerin olmadığı bir dönemde bunu nasıl başardılar? Bunlar yanıtlanması zor sorulardan bazılarıdır.

Norveçli bir kâşif olan Thor Heyerdahl, bu gizemin cevabını bildiğini düşünüyordu. Antik Peru'daki insanların, Polinezya adalarında yeni bir hayata başlamak için küçük sallarıyla Pasifik Okyanusu boyunca 6.000 kilometreden fazla yol katettiğine inanıyordu.

Kimse Heyerdahl'a inanmadı çünkü antik Peru halkının denize açılmak için yalnızca ahşap sallara sahip olduğunu biliyorlardı. İnsanlar Peru'dan adalara nasıl yelken açmıştı? Heyerdahl, teorisinin doğru olduğunu herkese göstermek istedi. Dört arkadaşıyla birlikte antik Perulularınkine benzer bir sal inşa etmeye başladı. Tamamlandığında ona eski bir tanrının adı olan Kon-Tiki adını verdiler. Yolculuklarını planlamak ve yanlarına ne alacaklarına karar vermek için uzun zaman harcadılar.

Peru Akıntısı adı verilen doğal su hareketi onları batıya doğru taşıdı. Yolculukları boyunca hava koşulları ve köpekbalıklarıyla ilgili birçok sorun yaşamalarına rağmen tekne sağlam kaldı ve batmadı. Denizde geçen 102 zorlu günün ardından kâşifler Polinezya Adaları'ndan birine ulaştı. Heyerdahl bunun mümkün olduğunu kanıtlamıştı.

passages.passage_text:
The problems of the American cities - pollution, crime, a lack of planning, accidents - are bad, but they were worse in the so-called 'good old days'. Pollution from cars is one example. It is bad now but there was a lot of pollution from horses and other animals in American cities in the 19th century.

Most cities had their own slaughterhouses. Butchers were careless about the cows and pigs which they killed and they left the remains of the animals here and there. And the sewer system for waste water from the kitchens and bathrooms did almost not exist.

Pollution was a very important problem for city governments in the last century, especially the problem of water supplies. They knew that they polluted water, but they didn't know how it was polluted. Trying to get pure water was a big problem.

People like to talk about the good old days but, actually, the cities of the 19th century were dirtier than today. Because of the dirt, communicable diseases were a great problem. When one of these diseases was seen, the situation was dangerous for all of the people in that area. Examples of such diseases were smallpox, yellow fever, malaria, cholera and typhoid. The number of children who died was high.

Some of the problems that disturbed people who lived in the cities during that period are still with us - poor planning, crime and accidents. The planning of cities and their neighbourhoods was controlled by real estate developers who were only interested in earning more money. Actually, their real job was to build well-planned cities and provide the population with both durable housing and a good-looking neighbourhood.

Crime was a great concern then, too. The police had to work hard to stop it. Pickpockets, who were very skilled, were able to quickly steal the purses and wallets of the people and run away with them.

It is true that people were not being killed by cars. However, they were killed or seriously injured (hurt) by runaway horses, which were running around out of control. It was quite a common scene.

The situations and problems of American cities have not changed so much. We must look back at the past and try to learn from it so that developments can be made.

passages.title: U.S. Cities: Past and Present
passages.tts_script:
U.S. Cities: Past and Present.

The problems of the American cities, pollution, crime, a lack of planning, and accidents, are bad, but they were worse in the so-called good old days. Pollution from cars is one example. It is bad now, but there was a lot of pollution from horses and other animals in American cities in the 19th century.

Most cities had their own slaughterhouses. Butchers were careless about the cows and pigs which they killed, and they left the remains of the animals here and there. And the sewer system for waste water from the kitchens and bathrooms did almost not exist.

Pollution was a very important problem for city governments in the last century, especially the problem of water supplies. They knew that they polluted water, but they didn't know how it was polluted. Trying to get pure water was a big problem.

People like to talk about the good old days, but actually, the cities of the 19th century were dirtier than today. Because of the dirt, communicable diseases were a great problem. When one of these diseases was seen, the situation was dangerous for all of the people in that area. Examples of such diseases were smallpox, yellow fever, malaria, cholera, and typhoid. The number of children who died was high.

Some of the problems that disturbed people who lived in the cities during that period are still with us: poor planning, crime, and accidents. The planning of cities and their neighbourhoods was controlled by real estate developers who were only interested in earning more money. Actually, their real job was to build well-planned cities and provide the population with both durable housing and a good-looking neighbourhood.

Crime was a great concern then, too. The police had to work hard to stop it. Pickpockets, who were very skilled, were able to quickly steal the purses and wallets of the people and run away with them.

It is true that people were not being killed by cars. However, they were killed or seriously injured by runaway horses, which were running around out of control. It was quite a common scene.

The situations and problems of American cities have not changed so much. We must look back at the past and try to learn from it so that developments can be made.

ABD Şehirleri: Geçmiş ve Günümüz.

Amerikan şehirlerinin kirlilik, suç, plansızlık ve kazalar gibi sorunları kötüdür, ancak sözde o "eski güzel günlerde" durum daha da kötüydü. Arabalardan kaynaklanan kirlilik bunun bir örneğidir. Şu anda kötüdür, ancak 19. yüzyılda Amerikan şehirlerinde atlardan ve diğer hayvanlardan kaynaklanan çok fazla kirlilik vardı.

Çoğu şehrin kendi mezbahaları vardı. Kasaplar kestikleri inek ve domuzlar konusunda dikkatsizdi ve hayvan kalıntılarını oraya buraya bırakırlardı. Mutfaklardan ve banyolardan gelen atık sular için kanalizasyon sistemi ise neredeyse hiç yoktu.

Kirlilik, geçen yüzyılda şehir yönetimleri için çok önemli bir sorundu; özellikle de su kaynakları sorunu. Suyu kirlettiklerini biliyorlardı ama nasıl kirlendiğini bilmiyorlardı. Temiz su bulmaya çalışmak büyük bir sorundu.

İnsanlar eski güzel günlerden bahsetmeyi severler, ama aslında 19. yüzyıl şehirleri bugünkünden daha pisti. Pislik yüzünden bulaşıcı hastalıklar büyük bir sorundu. Bu hastalıklardan biri görüldüğünde, durum o bölgedeki herkes için tehlikeli hâle gelirdi. Bu tür hastalıklara örnek olarak çiçek hastalığı, sarıhumma, sıtma, kolera ve tifo sayılabilir. Ölen çocukların sayısı yüksekti.

O dönemde şehirlerde yaşayan insanları rahatsız eden sorunlardan bazıları hâlâ bizimle: kötü planlama, suç ve kazalar. Şehirlerin ve mahallelerin planlaması, yalnızca daha fazla para kazanmakla ilgilenen emlak geliştiricileri tarafından kontrol ediliyordu. Aslında onların gerçek işi, iyi planlanmış şehirler kurmak ve halka hem dayanıklı konutlar hem de göze hoş görünen bir mahalle sunmaktı.

Suç da o zamanlar büyük bir endişe kaynağıydı. Polis bunu durdurmak için çok çalışmak zorundaydı. Çok usta olan yankesiciler, insanların el çantalarını ve cüzdanlarını hızla çalıp kaçabiliyorlardı.

İnsanların arabalar tarafından öldürülmediği doğrudur. Ancak, kontrolden çıkmış bir şekilde etrafta koşturan başıboş atlar tarafından öldürülüyor veya ağır yaralanıyorlardı. Bu oldukça yaygın bir manzaraydı.

Amerikan şehirlerinin koşulları ve sorunları pek fazla değişmedi. İlerleme kaydedebilmek için geçmişe dönüp bakmalı ve ondan ders çıkarmaya çalışmalıyız.

passages.passage_text:
Water is the oldest treatment in medical history. It has been used for its healing properties since the earliest days by men and women to soothe and heal the injured and hurting parts of their bodies. Thus, their ill bodies feel better and also more relaxed.

Today, spas, which use water and mud to heal people, are very famous in Europe. Millions of visitors each year go to their favourite spa resort to drink and bathe in mineral springs so that their backs, arms and legs will stop aching or their rough skin will feel smooth again. Some of the most famous resorts are Baden Bein Wein in Austria, Vichy in France, Marienbad in Czechoslovakia, Baden Baden in Germany, where guests put hot mud on their bodies, and Abano Terme in Italy, a resort which offers health-giving radioactive mud to its guests.

Some treatments provide bizarre and strange experiences. The spa of Badgastein in Austria, for instance, has an old miner's tunnel, now a 'health tunnel'. You drive into the mountain in a truck and wear a helmet to protect your head. When you reach the depths of the tunnel, you take off your clothes and lie down naked while rich vapours surround you. Because of the heat, a person sweats and can lose hundreds of calories in an hour and thus decrease in weight. Visitors who have had this experience are very pleased and say that spa treatments are very relaxing.

But are spa resorts really beneficial? That is, do people really get something good and useful for their money?

Many governments think they do. German, French and Austrian visitors' spa expenses are paid by the national health system. Obviously, these governments believe in the healing factor of spas or they wouldn't let the health services pay so much money.

Not all experts, however, think spas are helpful. One doctor, for instance, recently reported, "It is silly to think that you can become a healthy person in a week or two at a spa when you have an unhealthy lifestyle."

Some other sources also tell us that we should be careful about spas. Not long ago, a British banker told members of his staff not to go to spas. He said, "There is usually a casino nearby where you can lose a lot of money in card games and the like."

passages.tts_script_tr:
Kaplıcalar: İyi mi Kötü mü?

Su, tıp tarihindeki en eski tedavi yöntemidir. En eski zamanlardan beri kadınlar ve erkekler tarafından vücutlarının yaralı ve ağrıyan bölgelerini yatıştırmak ve iyileştirmek amacıyla şifalı özellikleri için kullanılmıştır. Böylece hasta bedenleri kendini daha iyi ve daha rahatlamış hisseder.

Bugün insanları iyileştirmek için su ve çamur kullanan kaplıcalar Avrupa'da çok ünlüdür. Her yıl milyonlarca ziyaretçi, sırtlarının, kollarının ve bacaklarının ağrısının dinmesi ya da pürüzlü ciltlerinin yeniden pürüzsüzleşmesi için maden suyu kaynaklarından içmek ve banyo yapmak amacıyla en sevdikleri kaplıca merkezine gider. En ünlü merkezlerden bazıları Avusturya'daki Baden Bein Wein, Fransa'daki Vichy, Çekoslovakya'daki Marienbad, konukların vücutlarına sıcak çamur sürdüğü Almanya'daki Baden Baden ve konuklarına şifa veren radyoaktif çamur sunan İtalya'daki Abano Terme'dir.

Bazı tedaviler tuhaf ve garip deneyimler sunar. Örneğin Avusturya'daki Badgastein kaplıcasında, artık bir sağlık tüneli olan eski bir maden tüneli vardır. Bir kamyonla dağın içine doğru sürersiniz ve başınızı korumak için kask takarsınız. Tünelin derinliklerine ulaştığınızda kıyafetlerinizi çıkarıp çıplak bir şekilde uzanırsınız ve etrafınızı yoğun buharlar sarar. Sıcaklık nedeniyle kişi terler ve bir saat içinde yüzlerce kalori yakarak kilo verebilir. Bu deneyimi yaşayan ziyaretçiler çok memnun kalır ve kaplıca tedavilerinin son derece rahatlatıcı olduğunu söyler.

passages.passage_text:
In October 1981, newspapers in the USA and the UK reported plans for a 169-storey building in Chicago. If this is built, it will be almost twice as tall as the 384-metre Empire State Building in New York.

Since the early days of civilised man, buildings have been getting higher all the time. Today, all large cities have tall buildings, either for use as offices or as flats. These are called high-rise buildings. The tallest of all, in fact, are not used for offices or for living, but are special structures for radio and television. For instance, Warsaw Radio Mast in Poland, which is 646 metres tall, is the tallest of such structures. The world's tallest office building is the Sears Tower in Chicago. This has 110 storeys, and reaches a height of 443 metres. 16,700 people work inside the building, and there are more than one hundred lifts for their use.

But why do we have high buildings? Is there any real advantage? The most common reason given is that in many cities there is a lack of space.

The island of Manhattan, New York City, is a good example of this. Here, office space is very expensive. There is no more land. Buildings have to go up. The same reason is given for high office buildings in Tokyo, London and other large cities of the world.

But what about people? Is it really necessary to build high buildings for people to live in?

Today, there are many who believe high buildings actually damage people's minds and feelings. These people believe high-rise buildings:
- have no advantages, except for their owners and for banks
- are not cheap to build
- do not help create open space
- destroy the landscape
- cause crime
- are not good for children
- are expensive to look after

High-rise buildings lower the quality of life. The following reports show this.

Report from England, 1967: The higher people live off the ground, the more likely they are to suffer from mental illnesses. Women, because they spend most time at home, suffer most.

Living in high-rise apartment buildings has both advantages and disadvantages, and its suitability depends largely on city conditions and residents' needs. On one hand, crowded cities often lack land for single-family houses. passages.passage_text:
Atoms are the smallest particles of matter that have the properties of the chemical elements - hydrogen, oxygen, iron, and so on. They are so small that it is impossible to see them even with a high-powered microscope. Everything on Earth is made up of atoms in different chemical combinations. Water, for instance, is a compound of two elements, two atoms of hydrogen and one atom of oxygen. However, some elements, such as gold and diamonds exist uncombined.

Ninety-two elements occur naturally. They range from the lightest, hydrogen, to the heaviest, uranium. Each of the elements has been assigned a number - 1 for hydrogen, 8 for oxygen, 29 for copper, 92 for uranium. They are usually arranged on a chart called the periodic table, which puts elements with the same chemical properties in the same column. Thus, all inert gases, such as helium, appear in one column in the periodic table.

The formulation of the atomic theory is one of the great achievements of science. It has enabled us to understand the properties of the elements, the basic building blocks of all matter, so that we know which elements can combine with each other. The science of chemistry is based on our understanding of atoms and their behaviour in interacting with each other.

Another science called nuclear physics came into being to study the structure of the atom itself. As scientists investigated the atom, it became apparent that the atom was not a solid piece of matter, but was made up of even smaller particles. The first subatomic particle that scientists identified was the electron, a tiny piece of matter with a negative electric charge. The weight of an electron was very small indeed - approximately one eighteen-hundredth of the weight of a hydrogen atom, the lightest of all the elements. Scientists came to believe that the electrons orbited the nucleus of the atom, in which almost all of the weight of the atom was concentrated. It is now known that electrons revolve around the nucleus at incredibly fast rates of speed.

For many years scientists did many different kinds of experiments and all had the same idea about the structure of atoms. However, when they managed to obtain more evidence, they had to modify the atomic theory. There was not just one kind of particle in the nucleus of an atom; there were two. One of these has a positive electric charge and is called a proton. The other is neutral, that is, it has no electric charge. For this reason, it was called a neutron.

passages.title: Atoms (1)
passages.tts_script:
Atoms (1).

Atoms are the smallest particles of matter that have the properties of the chemical elements, such as hydrogen, oxygen, iron, and so on. They are so small that it is impossible to see them even with a high-powered microscope. Everything on Earth is made up of atoms in different chemical combinations. Water, for instance, is a compound of two elements, two atoms of hydrogen and one atom of oxygen. However, some elements, such as gold and diamonds, exist uncombined.

Ninety-two elements occur naturally. They range from the lightest, hydrogen, to the heaviest, uranium. Each of the elements has been assigned a number: 1 for hydrogen, 8 for oxygen, 29 for copper, and 92 for uranium. They are usually arranged on a chart called the periodic table, which puts elements with the same chemical properties in the same column. Thus, all inert gases, such as helium, appear in one column in the periodic table.

The formulation of the atomic theory is one of the great achievements of science. It has enabled us to understand the properties of the elements, the basic building blocks of all matter, so that we know which elements can combine with each other. The science of chemistry is based on our understanding of atoms and their behaviour in interacting with each other.

Another science called nuclear physics came into being to study the structure of the atom itself. As scientists investigated the atom, it became apparent that the atom was not a solid piece of matter, but was made up of even smaller particles. The first subatomic particle that scientists identified was the electron, a tiny piece of matter with a negative electric charge. The weight of an electron was very small indeed, approximately one eighteen-hundredth of the weight of a hydrogen atom, the lightest of all the elements. Scientists came to believe that the electrons orbited the nucleus of the atom, in which almost all of the weight of the atom was concentrated. It is now known that electrons revolve around the nucleus at incredibly fast rates of speed.

For many years scientists did many different kinds of experiments and all had the same idea about the structure of atoms. However, when they managed to obtain more evidence, they had to modify the atomic theory. There was not just one kind of particle in the nucleus of an atom; there were two. One of these has a positive electric charge and is called a proton. The other is neutral, that is, it has no electric charge. For this reason, it was called a neutron.

While chemistry examines how atoms combine and interact, nuclear physics investigates the atom's internal structure. Early research identified fast-moving, negatively charged electrons orbiting a dense nucleus. Later experiments revealed that the nucleus itself contains two distinct particles: positively charged protons and uncharged neutrons, prompting scientists to revise the atomic theory.

task2.model_answer:
Scientific theories should never be treated as final truths because our understanding of the natural world improves as technology and experimental methods advance. The history of atomic theory provides a clear example of this process. For many years, scientists shared a simpler view of the atom, believing its nucleus contained only one kind of particle. However, once researchers gathered stronger experimental evidence, they had to revise that model to include both protons and neutrons.

If scientists refused to question established ideas, major breakthroughs in physics, medicine, and chemistry would never occur. At the same time, revising a theory does not mean past work was useless; rather, each modification builds on earlier discoveries to create a more accurate picture of reality. For example, understanding subatomic particles later enabled advances ranging from medical imaging to modern electronics. Therefore, remaining open to new evidence is essential for scientific progress.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Atomlar (1).

Atomlar; hidrojen, oksijen, demir ve benzeri kimyasal elementlerin özelliklerini taşıyan en küçük madde parçacıklarıdır. O kadar küçüktürler ki yüksek güçlü bir mikroskopla bile onları görmek imkânsızdır. Dünya üzerindeki her şey, farklı kimyasal bileşimlerdeki atomlardan oluşur. Örneğin su, iki elementin — iki hidrojen atomu ile bir oksijen atomunun — birleşiminden oluşan bir bileşiktir. Ancak altın ve elmas gibi bazı elementler birleşmemiş hâlde bulunur.

Doğada doksan iki element kendiliğinden bulunur. Bunlar en hafif olan hidrojenden en ağır olan uranyuma kadar uzanır. Elementlerin her birine bir numara verilmiştir: hidrojen için 1, oksijen için 8, bakır için 29 ve uranyum için 92. Genellikle, aynı kimyasal özelliklere sahip elementleri aynı sütuna yerleştiren periyodik tablo adlı bir çizelgede düzenlenirler. Böylece helyum gibi tüm asal gazlar periyodik tabloda tek bir sütunda yer alır.

Atom teorisinin ortaya konması bilimin büyük başarılarından biridir. Bu teori, tüm maddenin temel yapı taşları olan elementlerin özelliklerini anlamamızı sağlamış, böylece hangi elementlerin birbirleriyle birleşebileceğini bilmemize imkân tanımıştır. Kimya bilimi, atomları ve birbirleriyle etkileşime girerken sergiledikleri davranışları anlamamıza dayanır.

Atomun kendi yapısını incelemek üzere nükleer fizik adı verilen başka bir bilim dalı ortaya çıkmıştır. Bilim insanları atomu araştırdıkça, atomun katı bir madde parçası olmadığı, aksine çok daha küçük parçacıklardan oluştuğu anlaşılmıştır. Bilim insanlarının tanımladığı ilk atom altı parçacık, negatif elektrik yüküne sahip küçücük bir madde parçacığı olan elektrondur. Bir elektronun ağırlığı gerçekten de çok küçüktü; tüm elementlerin en hafifi olan hidrojen atomunun ağırlığının yaklaşık bin sekiz yüzde biri kadardı. Bilim insanları, elektronların atomun neredeyse tüm ağırlığının yoğunlaştığı atom çekirdeğinin yörüngesinde döndüğüne inanmaya başladılar. Günümüzde elektronların çekirdeğin etrafında inanılmaz derecede yüksek hızlarla döndüğü bilinmektedir.

Bilim insanları uzun yıllar boyunca pek çok farklı deney yaptı ve hepsi atomların yapısı hakkında aynı görüşe sahipti. Ancak daha fazla kanıt elde etmeyi başardıklarında atom teorisini değiştirmek zorunda kaldılar. Bir atomun çekirdeğinde yalnızca tek bir tür parçacık değil, iki tür parçacık bulunuyordu. Bunlardan biri pozitif elektrik yüküne sahiptir ve proton olarak adlandırılır. Diğeri ise nötrdür, yani elektrik yükü yoktur. Bu nedenle nötron olarak adlandırılmıştır.

passages.passage_text:
Vibration is movement and sound that comes from objects which vibrate. For example, guitar strings, when touched, vibrate and make a sound; and drum skins, when hit, vibrate and make a sound.

Vibrations are described in terms of amplitude and frequency. In the case of a guitar, the amplitude, or loudness, is the distance the string moves; and in the case of a drum, the skin moves at a certain speed and vibrates a certain number of times each second. If the skin, or the string, vibrates 440 times per second, then we say it has a frequency of 440 Hertz (or 440 Hz for short). If it moves faster or slower, then it has a higher or lower frequency.

The human ear cannot detect all sounds. Sounds must have a certain amplitude, and a frequency between 40 Hz and 16,000 Hz. Vibrations above or below these will not be detected by the human ear even if they are extremely loud. Many animals have better hearing than us. Dogs, for example, can hear higher frequencies; and bats can hear sounds with incredibly high frequencies - up to 48,000 Hz.

The vibrating object first causes the molecules in the air around it to vibrate at the same frequency and amplitude. These molecules then cause other molecules to vibrate and so it continues until molecules of air inside our ears vibrate. Finally, our eardrums vibrate and cause minute, i.e. very small, electrical signals to be sent to the brain.

All sounds come from vibrations. But not all sounds are the same. Some are pleasant to hear, such as music. Others are unpleasant and these we call noise. What's the difference between the two? This is a difficult question to answer. But the sounds of musical instruments, which are usually good to hear, do have a special characteristic: musical instruments, such as the guitar and the drum, vibrate at more than one frequency. Thus, when a guitar string produces the note of A, the vibration of greatest amplitude has a frequency of 440 Hz. But there are vibrations of other frequencies present, too. They have less amplitude, and so we do not consciously hear them. But they add to the sound and form a pattern of frequencies which is pleasant to hear. This is called harmonics. It is harmonics which help us to identify the musical instrument we hear.

Of course, there are other characteristics of music, too. One of these is rhythm, the sequence of sounds. Rhythm is not exclusive to musical sound; but it is one of the factors which help make music pleasant to hear.

task1.model_answer: All sounds originate from vibrations, which are measured by amplitude (loudness) and frequency (vibrations per second, measured in Hertz). When an object vibrates, surrounding air molecules carry the motion to our eardrums, generating tiny electrical signals for the brain. However, human hearing is limited to frequencies between 40 Hz and 16,000 Hz, whereas animals like dogs and bats can detect much higher frequencies. What distinguishes pleasant music from noise is largely harmonics and rhythm. Musical instruments vibrate at several frequencies simultaneously: alongside the loudest main frequency, quieter secondary frequencies create a pleasing pattern called harmonics that also helps us recognize each instrument.

task2.model_answer:
While both music and noise come from physical vibrations, the difference between them depends on acoustic structure as well as human perception. As the passage explains, musical instruments generate harmonics—ordered patterns of multiple frequencies—alongside rhythm, which generally makes their sound enjoyable. Noise, by contrast, lacks such harmonious patterns and often feels jarring.

However, whether a sound is considered music or noise can also be subjective and cultural. For example, a person who enjoys heavy percussion or experimental electronic tracks may find rhythmic industrial beats exciting, whereas another listener might perceive the exact same sounds as unpleasant noise. Similarly, even classical music becomes an unwelcome disturbance when played too loudly late at night while someone is trying to sleep.

In short, physics explains why certain combinations of frequencies naturally appeal to the human ear, yet context, volume, and personal taste ultimately determine how we experience sound. Understanding both the science and the psychology of sound helps us appreciate music while protecting our ears from harmful noise.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Müzik mi, Gürültü mü?

Titreşim, titreşen nesnelerden gelen hareket ve sestir. Örneğin gitar telleri, dokunulduğunda titreşir ve ses çıkarır; davul derileri de vurulduğunda titreşir ve ses çıkarır.

Titreşimler genlik ve frekans açısından tanımlanır. Gitar örneğinde genlik, yani ses yüksekliği, telin hareket ettiği mesafedir; davul örneğinde ise deri belirli bir hızda hareket eder ve saniyede belirli sayıda titreşir. Eğer deri ya da tel saniyede 440 kez titreşirse, bunun 440 Hertz ya da kısaca 440 Hz frekansa sahip olduğunu söyleriz. Daha hızlı veya daha yavaş hareket ederse, frekansı daha yüksek veya daha düşük olur.

İnsan kulağı tüm sesleri algılayamaz. Seslerin belirli bir genliğe ve 40 Hertz ile 16.000 Hertz arasında bir frekansa sahip olması gerekir. Bunların üzerindeki veya altındaki titreşimler, son derece gürültülü olsalar bile insan kulağı tarafından algılanmaz. Birçok hayvan bizden daha iyi işitir. Örneğin köpekler daha yüksek frekansları duyabilir; yarasalar ise 48.000 Hertz'e kadar çıkan inanılmaz derecede yüksek frekanslı sesleri duyabilir.

Titreşen nesne, ilk olarak etrafındaki havada bulunan moleküllerin aynı frekans ve genlikte titreşmesine neden olur. Bu moleküller daha sonra diğer moleküllerin titreşmesine yol açar ve bu durum kulaklarımızın içindeki hava molekülleri titreşene kadar böyle devam eder. Son olarak kulak zarlarımız titreşir ve beyne çok küçük, yani minicik elektrik sinyallerinin gönderilmesine neden olur.

Tüm sesler titreşimlerden gelir. Ancak tüm sesler aynı değildir. Müzik gibi bazılarının duyulması hoştur. Diğerleri ise hoş değildir ve bunlara gürültü deriz. Bu ikisi arasındaki fark nedir? Bu yanıtlanması zor bir sorudur. Fakat genellikle kulağa hoş gelen müzik aletlerinin seslerinin özel bir niteliği vardır: gitar ve davul gibi müzik aletleri birden fazla frekansta titreşir. Böylece bir gitar teli La notasını çıkardığında, en büyük genliğe sahip titreşimin frekansı 440 Hertz olur. Ancak başka frekanslardaki titreşimler de mevcuttur. Bunların genliği daha düşüktür ve bu yüzden onları bilinçli olarak duymayız. Fakat sese eklenirler ve kulağa hoş gelen bir frekans örüntüsü oluştururlar. Buna armonikler denir. Duyduğumuz müzik aletini tanımamıza yardımcı olan şey de armoniklerdir.

Elbette müziğin başka özellikleri de vardır. Bunlardan biri, seslerin dizilişi olan ritimdir. Ritim yalnızca müzik sesine özgü değildir; ancak müziğin kulağa hoş gelmesine yardımcı olan etkenlerden biridir.

passages.passage_text:
'Aborigines' are the first or original inhabitants of a country. The Australian Aborigines have lived in Australia for over 40,000 years. At one stage in their history, there were possibly over a million Aborigines. However, when the first white settlers arrived in the 18th century and stole their land, many Aborigines died fighting to protect it. Today, only about 100,000 survive. passages.passage_text:
The water on the earth is recycled constantly in a process known as the hydrologic cycle. First, the water in the oceans evaporates. It changes into vapour and forms clouds in the sky. Water accumulates in clouds and returns to the surface of the earth in some form of precipitation, which can be either rain, snow, or ice. When the water reaches the earth's surface, it runs off into streams, rivers, lakes, and at last, into the oceans, where the cycle begins again. The water on the surface of the earth and in the atmosphere is known as the hydrosphere. Not all precipitation goes into rivers. Some of it seeps into the ground by a process called infiltration. This water collects under the earth's surface and is groundwater.

Groundwater is important for two reasons. First, 95 per cent of the earth's water is in the oceans. It is salty and useless for plants, animals, or humans. Fresh water, which people can use for drinking or for agriculture, is either on the earth's surface in lakes and rivers or underground. Surface water is 0.05 per cent of the earth's water while underground water is 4 per cent of the earth's water. Consequently, groundwater provides 95 per cent of the available fresh water on the earth. Second, groundwater is important not only because of the size of the supply, but also because of its dependability. It is always available since it does not depend on seasonal precipitation.

Today, there seems to be a problem with groundwater. Until recently, groundwater was clean. It was not necessary to purify it before people drank it. However, for many years, people have been burying garbage and poisonous wastes underground. These poisons have polluted the groundwater in many places. Therefore, it is unsafe for human use unless the dirty and harmful substances are removed first.

Aquifers are geologic formations that allow groundwater to accumulate and move through them. Although they are often called underground rivers, these formations are not like surface rivers. The water accumulates in one area underground. The amount of water an aquifer contains is enough to be easily pumped out for use.

People have been using groundwater for many years. With an increasing population, the need for water has also increased. Some cities depend only on groundwater for their water supply. They are using underground water very quickly. In some places the water supply may soon be used up, and there will be no water for a large population. One example of this is Tucson, Arizona, which is located in the Sonora desert in southwestern United States. It is on a very large aquifer which supplies water for the area at the present. The aquifer provides water for an increasing population in the city and for agriculture throughout southern Arizona. At the present time, the city is using 225,000 acre feet of water per year, 75,000 acre feet are being returned to the aquifer through the natural processes of the hydrologic cycle. Therefore, people are using about three times more water than nature is supplying. The water table, which is the level of the water in the aquifer, is dropping lower every year. Some wells have already gone dry and have either been closed or drilled deeper. Scientists predict that the supply of water in the aquifer will run out in twenty to eighty years.

Aquifers contain a generous supply of water. They are large, easily available, and mostly clean. Still, people who depend only on aquifers for their water supply must use their water carefully. Their lives and their children's lives depend on conserving the water they have.

task1.model_answer: Earth's water continuously circulates through the hydrologic cycle, where ocean water evaporates, falls as precipitation, and either flows into surface waterways or seeps underground as groundwater. Providing 95 percent of available fresh water and remaining independent of seasonal rainfall, groundwater—stored in underground rock formations called aquifers—is vital for drinking and agriculture. However, two major threats endanger this resource. First, buried garbage and toxic wastes have polluted groundwater in many regions, requiring purification before use. Second, rapid population growth has led to overconsumption. In Tucson, Arizona, residents use three times more water than nature replenishes, causing the water table to fall and threatening depletion within decades unless people conserve water carefully.

task2.model_answer:
Fresh groundwater is one of the most valuable yet overlooked natural resources on Earth. As cities expand and climates become less predictable, over-pumping and underground pollution seriously threaten aquifers that millions of people rely on daily. Governments and citizens must therefore take urgent, practical steps to protect these supplies.

First, strict regulations are needed to stop groundwater contamination. Authorities should ban burying hazardous industrial waste and poorly sealed garbage near aquifer recharge zones, while heavily fining companies that pollute soil and water. Second, cities must reduce excessive extraction. In dry regions like Tucson, using three times as much water as nature replaces is unsustainable. Municipal programs can encourage water-saving appliances, fix leaking pipes, and promote drought-resistant landscaping instead of water-heavy lawns.

Finally, farmers and citizens alike need education on conservation. Modern drip irrigation can cut agricultural waste dramatically, and everyday habits such as shorter showers or reusing greywater make a real difference when adopted widely. Protecting aquifers today is essential to guarantee safe drinking water for future generations.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Akiferler.

Dünya üzerindeki su, hidrolojik döngü olarak bilinen bir süreçle sürekli olarak geri dönüştürülür. İlk olarak okyanuslardaki su buharlaşır. Buhara dönüşür ve gökyüzünde bulutları oluşturur. Su bulutlarda birikir ve yağmur, kar ya da buz biçiminde bir yağış olarak yeryüzüne geri döner. Su yeryüzüne ulaştığında derelere, nehirlere, göllere ve en sonunda döngünün yeniden başladığı okyanuslara akar. Yeryüzündeki ve atmosferdeki su, hidrosfer olarak bilinir. Yağışın tamamı nehirlere gitmez. Bir kısmı sızma adı verilen bir süreçle toprağın içine işler. Bu su yer kabuğunun altında toplanır ve yer altı suyunu oluşturur.

Yer altı suyu iki nedenden ötürü önemlidir. Birincisi, dünyadaki suyun yüzde 95'i okyanuslardadır. Bu su tuzludur ve bitkiler, hayvanlar ya da insanlar için kullanılamaz. İnsanların içmek veya tarım için kullanabileceği tatlı su, ya yeryüzündeki göllerde ve nehirlerde ya da yer altındadır. Yüzey suyu dünyadaki suyun yüzde 0,05'ini oluştururken, yer altı suyu dünyadaki suyun yüzde 4'ünü oluşturur. Sonuç olarak, yer altı suyu dünyadaki kullanılabilir tatlı suyun yüzde 95'ini sağlar. İkincisi, yer altı suyu yalnızca kaynağın büyüklüğü nedeniyle değil, aynı zamanda güvenilirliği nedeniyle de önemlidir. Mevsimsel yağışlara bağlı olmadığı için her zaman mevcuttur.

Günümüzde yer altı suyuyla ilgili bir sorun var gibi görünmektedir. Yakın zamana kadar yer altı suyu temizdi. İnsanların içmeden önce onu arıtması gerekmiyordu. Ancak yıllardır insanlar yer altına çöp ve zehirli atıklar gömmektedir. Bu zehirler birçok yerde yer altı suyunu kirletmiştir. Bu nedenle, kirli ve zararlı maddeler önceden uzaklaştırılmadıkça insan kullanımı için güvenli değildir.

Akiferler, yer altı suyunun içlerinde birikmesine ve hareket etmesine olanak tanıyan jeolojik oluşumlardır. Sıklıkla yer altı nehirleri olarak adlandırılsalar da bu oluşumlar yüzey nehirleri gibi değildir. Su, yer altında tek bir bölgede birikir. Bir akiferin içerdiği su miktarı, kullanılmak üzere kolayca pompalanıp çıkarılabilecek kadar fazladır.

İnsanlar uzun yıllardır yer altı suyunu kullanmaktadır. Artan nüfusla birlikte suya olan ihtiyaç da artmıştır. Bazı şehirler su temini için yalnızca yer altı suyuna bağımlıdır. Yer altı suyunu çok hızlı tüketmektedirler. Bazı yerlerde su kaynağı yakında tükenebilir ve büyük bir nüfus için hiç su kalmayabilir. Bunun bir örneği, Amerika Birleşik Devletleri'nin güneybatısındaki Sonora Çölü'nde bulunan Arizona eyaletindeki Tucson şehridir. Şehir, günümüzde bölgeye su sağlayan çok büyük bir akiferin üzerinde yer almaktadır. Bu akifer, şehirdeki artan nüfusa ve güney Arizona genelindeki tarıma su sağlamaktadır. Şu anda şehir yılda 225.000 akre-fit su kullanırken, hidrolojik döngünün doğal süreçleriyle akifere yılda 75.000 akre-fit su geri dönmektedir. Dolayısıyla insanlar, doğanın sağladığından yaklaşık üç kat daha fazla su tüketmektedir. Akiferdeki suyun seviyesi olan su tablası her yıl daha da düşmektedir. passages.passage_text:
After rising steadily for almost a century, standards of education in the public schools of Europe and North America have come to a standstill. In fact, in the opinion of many parents and employers, they are actually falling. More and more children are leaving school at an early age. Naturally, they have very little knowledge of reading and writing. Thus, the number of illiterate people is increasing, bringing about a social problem once again. With dropout rates of twenty-seven per cent in high schools and fifty per cent in colleges, the American education system is clearly in trouble. In Europe, the number of children who leave school is going up too, though lower than that in the United States.

There are various factors that cause the decrease in educational standards. Some people say that overcrowding and lack of discipline are major factors. Others say that much importance has been given to subjects like art and drama. However, more practical subjects have been neglected. For many teachers, on the other hand, the problem is not of falling standards but of rising expectations of parents and employers. According to these teachers, the demands of parents and employers are getting higher and this is causing the problem.

Whether or not standards in public schools are actually falling, many parents feel that the only way to secure a good education for their children is to send them to private schools, which generally have smaller classes and stricter discipline. The popularity of such schools is growing steadily, despite the high tuition. In the United States, for example, eleven per cent of all school children attend private schools; in Europe, over sixteen per cent do so.

task2.model_answer:
Many people believe that sending children to private schools is the best way to ensure a quality education, mainly because these institutions often provide smaller class sizes and stricter discipline. However, relying heavily on private education can widen the gap between wealthy and lower-income families. When more resources and motivated students move to private schools, public schools may face even greater challenges.

A healthier long-term solution is to improve public education for everyone. Governments should invest in reducing classroom overcrowding, supporting teachers, and balancing practical skills with creative subjects like art and drama. If public schools receive proper funding and clear academic standards, every child can gain strong reading, writing, and critical-thinking skills regardless of family income. Ultimately, strengthening public schools benefits society as a whole far more than expanding private alternatives.

Eğitim Standartları.

Neredeyse bir yüzyıl boyunca istikrarlı bir şekilde yükseldikten sonra, Avrupa ve Kuzey Amerika'daki devlet okullarında eğitim standartları durma noktasına gelmiştir. Hatta birçok ebeveyn ve işverenin görüşüne göre aslında düşmektedir. Giderek daha fazla çocuk erken yaşta okulu bırakmaktadır. Doğal olarak, okuma ve yazma konusunda çok az bilgiye sahip olmaktadırlar. Böylece okuryazar olmayan kişilerin sayısı artmakta ve bu durum yeniden bir toplumsal soruna yol açmaktadır. Liselerde yüzde yirmi yedi ve üniversitelerde yüzde elli olan okulu bırakma oranlarıyla Amerikan eğitim sistemi açıkça sıkıntı içindedir. Avrupa'da da okulu bırakan çocukların sayısı Amerika Birleşik Devletleri'ndekinden daha düşük olmakla birlikte artmaktadır.

Eğitim standartlarındaki düşüşe neden olan çeşitli etkenler vardır. Bazıları aşırı kalabalık sınıfların ve disiplin eksikliğinin başlıca etkenler olduğunu söylemektedir. Bazıları ise resim ve tiyatro gibi derslere fazla önem verildiğini belirtmektedir. Buna karşın daha uygulamalı dersler ihmal edilmiştir. Öte yandan birçok öğretmene göre sorun düşen standartlar değil, ebeveynlerin ve işverenlerin artan beklentileridir. Bu öğretmenlere göre ebeveynlerin ve işverenlerin talepleri giderek yükselmekte ve soruna bu durum yol açmaktadır.

Devlet okullarındaki standartlar gerçekten düşüyor olsun ya da olmasın, pek çok ebeveyn çocuklarına iyi bir eğitim sağlamanın tek yolunun onları genellikle daha küçük sınıflara ve daha sıkı disipline sahip özel okullara göndermek olduğunu düşünmektedir. Yüksek öğrenim ücretlerine rağmen bu tür okulların popülerliği istikrarlı bir şekilde artmaktadır. Örneğin Amerika Birleşik Devletleri'nde tüm okul çağındaki çocukların yüzde on biri özel okullara devam etmektedir; Avrupa'da ise bu oran yüzde on altının üzerindedir.

passages.passage_text:
"It demands your total concentration, energy and capabilities. In return it gives you the best friends you could ever wish for. More important than this, you get the opportunity to discover yourself." According to Heidi Meyer, a former student of Atlantic College, that makes the college such a good place for education.

Atlantic College is the world's first residential sixth form college and this week it is 25 years old. The college was founded at St. Donats Castle, in South Wales, by Kurt Hahn to promote peace and international understanding through education.

Atlantic College students are from 70 countries. They study for the International Baccalaureate diploma. This course was pioneered at the college during the early 1970's and now, it is offered at more than 350 colleges across the world. Six subjects are studied and some British experts are considering it as a replacement for A-levels.

"It is rather like the proposed national curriculum," said Jeff Neuss, the college's head of chemistry. "Everyone has to study his or her native language, a modern foreign language, a humanities subject, a science and maths. As a result of this broad curriculum, all our students become intellectual adults while studying their own subjects. Thus, we have scientists who can write essays, and art specialists who are numerate and competent in science."

Academic work is only one part of the college. It also wants to be part of the community. Therefore, it expects students to undertake community services that include sea rescue and running its 50-acre farm. "We were the first co-ordinated beach and inshore rescue service in Britain and we developed the Atlantic Class of inshore lifeboats now used as standard by the RNLI," said Neuss. "We are officially responsible for safety along a 15-mile stretch of coastline. Our lifeboats have saved 150 lives."

Every summer, the students run courses for physically and mentally handicapped young people. They visit London to teach English to Bangladeshi youngsters and run a Youth Training Scheme course for local teenagers. And the students maintain their own college buildings and classrooms.

Atlantic College offers an unusually diverse educational experience, but how are students selected? "Academic ability and school recommendation are of course taken into consideration as in all colleges. However, applicants without the personal qualities of tolerance and a willingness to mix with others can't possibly get into our college," said Neuss.

The fees are £6,400 a year, but scholarships ensure there is no discrimination on financial grounds. Some countries, such as Norway, allocate funds to allow Ethiopian refugees to attend.

The college gives its students a wide perspective on world affairs, said Monica Moreno, a Brazilian: "Immediately after you arrive, a learning process starts which makes you realise your own roots and carries an irresistible force for change and understanding of others."

task1.model_answer: Founded in South Wales by Kurt Hahn to foster peace, Atlantic College brings together students from 70 countries to study the broad International Baccalaureate curriculum. task2.model_answer:
Education is often viewed primarily as a pathway to exams and careers, yet schools like Atlantic College demonstrate that community service and cultural diversity are equally transformative. When students participate in real-world service—such as sea rescue, farming, or teaching underserved communities—they develop practical responsibility and empathy that textbooks alone cannot teach.

Similarly, studying alongside peers from diverse backgrounds challenges stereotypes and builds genuine tolerance. In an increasingly interconnected world, technical knowledge without cross-cultural understanding is incomplete. By combining rigorous study across both arts and sciences with meaningful social engagement, schools prepare young people not only to succeed professionally, but also to contribute thoughtfully to a peaceful, cooperative society.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Değişim Okulu.

"Tüm odaklanmanızı, enerjinizi ve yeteneklerinizi ister. Karşılığında ise isteyebileceğiniz en iyi arkadaşları size verir. Bundan daha da önemlisi, kendinizi keşfetme fırsatı elde edersiniz." Atlantic College'ın eski öğrencilerinden Heidi Meyer'e göre, koleji eğitim açısından böylesine iyi bir yer yapan şey budur.

Atlantic College, dünyanın ilk yatılı lise son kademe kolejidir ve bu hafta 25. yılını dolduruyor. Kolej, eğitim yoluyla barışı ve uluslararası anlayışı teşvik etmek amacıyla Kurt Hahn tarafından Güney Galler'deki St. Donats Kalesi'nde kurulmuştur.

Atlantic College öğrencileri 70 ülkeden gelmektedir. Uluslararası Bakalorya diploması için eğitim görürler. Bu program 1970'lerin başında bu kolejde öncü olarak başlatılmıştır ve şimdi dünya genelinde 350'den fazla kolejde sunulmaktadır. Altı ders okutulur ve bazı İngiliz uzmanlar bunu A-level sınavlarının yerine geçecek bir seçenek olarak değerlendirmektedir.

Kolejin kimya bölüm başkanı Jeff Neuss, "Önerilen ulusal müfredata oldukça benziyor," dedi. "Herkes kendi ana dilini, modern bir yabancı dili, bir beşerî bilimler dersini, bir fen dersini ve matematiği okumak zorunda. Bu kapsamlı müfredatın sonucunda, tüm öğrencilerimiz kendi alanlarında eğitim görürken entelektüel bireyler olarak yetişiyor. Böylece deneme yazabilen bilim insanlarımız ve sayısal becerilere sahip, fen bilimlerinde yetkin sanat uzmanlarımız oluyor."

Akademik çalışma kolejin yalnızca bir parçasıdır. Kolej aynı zamanda toplumun da bir parçası olmak istemektedir. Bu nedenle öğrencilerden deniz kurtarma ve koleje ait 50 akrelik çiftliği işletme gibi toplum hizmetlerini üstlenmeleri beklenir. Neuss, "Britanya'daki ilk eşgüdümlü plaj ve kıyı kurtarma hizmeti bizdik ve şu anda RNLI tarafından standart olarak kullanılan Atlantic Sınıfı kıyı cankurtaran botlarını biz geliştirdik," dedi. "15 millik bir kıyı şeridi boyunca güvenlikten resmen sorumluyuz. Cankurtaran botlarımız 150 hayat kurtardı."

Öğrenciler her yaz fiziksel ve zihinsel engelli gençler için kurslar düzenlerler. Bangladeşli gençlere İngilizce öğretmek için Londra'ya giderler ve yerel gençler için bir Gençlik Eğitim Programı kursu yürütürler. Ayrıca öğrenciler kolejin kendi binalarının ve sınıflarının bakımını da yaparlar.

When the next Olympic Games begin, satellites will carry TV pictures of the opening ceremony to millions of people thousands of miles away. From their armchairs these people will be able to see their country's athletes competing in events and maybe winning a bronze, silver or even gold medal.

When we consider the size, the spectacle and the commercialism of the modern Olympic Games, it is difficult to remember that they started in Olympia in Greece in 776 BC with only one race, a sprint, for which the prize for the winner was an olive wreath.

The idea of an international Olympic Games was conceived by a Frenchman, Baron Pierre de Coubertin, and, appropriately, the first modern Olympic Games opened in Athens in 1896. Nowadays, major cities compete to host the Olympic Games, not just for the honour the Games bring, but for the vast amount of profit a host country can make.

In circumstances like these, the Olympic ideal and spirit comes into question. And for athletes, there is less value in winning a gold medal if the best of the world's athletes are not competing. passages.passage_text:
A report recently prepared for a large international travel service and banking company found out that travel and tourism accounted for almost $2 trillion of the sales in 1987, making it the largest source of employment in the world. Personal travel constituted about two thirds of this, leaving the rest for business and government travel. The biggest spenders on personal travel were the US, Japan, Germany, Britain and France; and in most of these developed countries it was the third largest item of household spending after housing and food.

Tour operators say the industry is experiencing "a second revolution". In the first, Europe revolutionised travel with the cheap package holiday within the continent, which transformed many Mediterranean economies. More recently, tourists have begun to travel further away. Until the mid-1980's, the market was limited to the rich on the one hand and the backpackers on the other.

Rising incomes and expectations have changed all that. Travellers who are tired of the Mediterranean or those who can afford second holidays in the winter expect the package holiday concept to be extended to intercontinental destinations. By chartering 500-seat jumbo jets and booking hotels and apartments in Florida and the Caribbean, tour operators have made formerly luxury tourist spots available to a lower-income market.

Although this poses risks which developing countries have not faced before, the benefits are more immediately apparent. The Caribbean Tourist Association estimates that the industry now provides jobs directly or indirectly for 330,000 people in the region. Others put the figure higher. Some estimates put Third World employment in travel and tourism at more than 50 million.

After Europe's first travel revolution of affordable continental package holidays transformed Mediterranean economies, the industry entered a second phase. task2.model_answer:
Mass tourism brings substantial economic opportunities to developing countries, yet it also creates environmental and social pressures that must be managed carefully. On the positive side, international visitors generate vital foreign income and create millions of direct and indirect jobs in hotels, transport, and local services. For regions with limited industrial sectors, tourism can rapidly reduce unemployment and fund infrastructure improvements such as airports and roads.

However, rapid expansion carries clear risks. Heavy reliance on foreign tour operators may mean that much of the profit leaves the local economy, while seasonal demand can result in unstable employment. Furthermore, building large resorts for mass tourism often strains water supplies, damages coastal ecosystems, and drives up housing costs for local residents.

Overall, the benefits of mass tourism outweigh its drawbacks only when governments enforce sustainable planning. By protecting natural habitats and supporting locally owned businesses, developing nations can secure long-term prosperity from global travel.

Seyahat ve Turizm.

Büyük bir uluslararası seyahat hizmeti ve bankacılık şirketi için yakın zamanda hazırlanan bir rapor, seyahat ve turizmin 1987 yılında neredeyse 2 trilyon dolarlık satış hacmine ulaştığını ve bu sayede dünyadaki en büyük istihdam kaynağı olduğunu ortaya koydu. Kişisel seyahatler bunun yaklaşık üçte ikisini oluştururken, geri kalanı iş ve devlet seyahatlerinden oluşuyordu. Kişisel seyahate en çok harcama yapan ülkeler ABD, Japonya, Almanya, Britanya ve Fransa oldu; bu gelişmiş ülkelerin çoğunda seyahat, konut ve gıdadan sonra hane halkı harcamalarının üçüncü en büyük kalemiydi.

Tur operatörleri, sektörün "ikinci bir devrim" yaşadığını söylüyor. İlk devrimde Avrupa, kıta içindeki ucuz paket turlarla seyahat anlayışını kökten değiştirmiş ve bu durum birçok Akdeniz ekonomisini dönüştürmüştü. Daha yakın dönemde ise turistler daha uzak yerlere seyahat etmeye başladı. 1980'lerin ortalarına kadar pazar, bir yanda zenginler diğer yanda sırt çantalı gezginlerle sınırlıydı.

Welcome to Harrods - a different world for a million reasons. Harrods is the largest store in Europe with goods displayed in 60 windows and 5.5 hectares of selling space. In one year over 14 million purchases are made in the 214 departments where you can buy anything from a pin to an elephant - if you can convince the manager of the Pet Department that you are a suitable elephant owner, that is!

Harrods stocks a wide and exciting range of merchandise in every department. It is because of this policy that Harrods can give the customer a choice of goods which is unique in its variety and which no other store can match: Harrods stocks 100 different whiskies, including 57 single malts, 450 different cheeses, 8,000 dresses, 500 types of shirts and 9,000 ties to go with them. Moreover, it has a staff of 4,000, rising to 6,000 at Christmas time.

Harrods has a world-wide reputation due to several reasons in addition to those mentioned above. It offers a number of special services to its customers. These include a bank, an insurance department, a travel agency and a theatre ticket agency. Another reason is the range of exported goods. £40 million worth of goods are exported annually from Harrods and the Export Department can deal with any customer purchase or order and will pack and send goods to any address in the world. Recently, for example, six bread rolls were sent to New York, a handkerchief to Los Angeles, and a £5,000 chess set to Australia. It is this first-class service that has made Harrods so famous.

Harrods sells 5 million different products, not all of which are actually kept in stock in the store itself. To handle this enormous range, a new computerised warehouse is being built. It will be the largest warehouse in Britain and the second largest in Europe and will deal with a wider range of goods than any other distribution centre in the world. Thanks to its modern technology, a customer will be able to order any product (for example, a dining table or a dishwasher) from any assistant in the store. The assistant will be able to check its availability immediately on a computer screen, decide with the customer on a suitable delivery date and time and then pass the order directly to the warehouse through the computer. The time of delivery will be guaranteed to within one hour.

task2.model_answer:
Although online shopping has grown rapidly for its convenience and low prices, large luxury department stores like Harrods still offer an experience that websites cannot fully replace. Shopping online is undeniably practical for everyday goods, as customers can compare prices and place orders within minutes from home.

However, traditional flagship stores provide sensory and social benefits that attract shoppers from around the world. Seeing window displays, examining fabric quality in person, and receiving attentive help from knowledgeable staff turn shopping into a memorable leisure activity rather than a simple transaction. Furthermore, as Harrods demonstrates with its computerised warehouse and guaranteed delivery times, physical stores can combine modern technology with personal service.

In conclusion, while e-commerce dominates routine purchasing, iconic department stores will continue to thrive by offering exceptional service, curated variety, and a unique atmosphere.

Milyonlarca nedenden ötürü farklı bir dünya olan Harrods'a hoş geldiniz. Harrods, 60 vitrinde sergilenen ürünleri ve 5,5 hektarlık satış alanıyla Avrupa'nın en büyük mağazasıdır. Harrods'ı bu kadar ünlü yapan işte bu birinci sınıf hizmetidir.

Harrods, 5 milyon farklı ürün satmaktadır ve bunların tamamı aslında mağazanın kendi içinde stokta tutulmamaktadır. Bu devasa ürün yelpazesini yönetebilmek için bilgisayarlı yeni bir depo inşa edilmektedir. Modern teknolojisi sayesinde bir müşteri, mağazadaki herhangi bir satış danışmanından örneğin bir yemek masası ya da bulaşık makinesi gibi dilediği herhangi bir ürünü sipariş edebilecektir. Satış danışmanı ürünün stok durumunu hemen bilgisayar ekranından kontrol edebilecek, müşteriyle birlikte uygun bir teslimat tarihi ve saati belirleyebilecek ve ardından siparişi bilgisayar üzerinden doğrudan depoya iletebilecektir. Teslimat saati bir saatlik zaman aralığı içinde garanti edilecektir.
