passages.passage_text:
The Reader's Guide to Periodical Literature is a subject and author list of many (but not all) magazine articles published in the U.S. This list, called an index, is sent to U.S. libraries every two weeks so that interested people can find out quickly what current information is available. For university or college students who must frequently do research, this list of subjects written about in magazines of general interest can be valuable. Learning to use The Reader's Guide is, therefore, important to all university students in the U.S.

The content of The Reader's Guide consists of subject and author entries to periodicals; that is, magazines published regularly. This information is listed alphabetically. After the subject or author's name, information is given which tells the student where to find the magazine article. For example, if you want to look up the subject 'Education', you should look up the letter 'E' and then find the word 'Education'. If you want to look up an author whose last name is 'Rodriquez', you should look up the letter 'R' and then find the word 'Rodriquez'. Under the subject or the author listing, you will find articles listed, in alphabetical order, about that subject or by that author. Each article is listed by the first word in the title of the article except for the words 'a', 'an', and 'the'; these initial words are not considered in the alphabetizing of articles.

The Reader's Guide also has two kinds of cross-references; that is, information about other places to look in The Reader's Guide for more articles about a subject. After a heading, you might find the word 'see' which is followed by other subject headings also found in the index. For example, 'Higher Education' isn't a subject heading in The Reader's Guide; if you look up 'Higher Education' you will find: "see Universities and Colleges". Then you will look under 'U' for universities. The other kind of cross-reference is 'see also'. For instance, if you look for 'Education', The Reader's Guide will list articles about education, but it also says: "see also: Adult Education, Elementary Education, Special Education". If you are interested in any of those headings, you can look them up in The Reader's Guide.

Entries are arranged alphabetically by subject and by the author's last name, followed by details showing where to find each article. task2.model_answer:
Although modern digital databases have largely replaced printed guides like The Reader's Guide to Periodical Literature, learning how indexes work remains useful for students.

On the one hand, online search engines are much faster and more convenient. Students can type a few keywords into a database and instantly read full articles from home, without visiting a library or checking alphabetical volumes every two weeks.

On the other hand, printed indexes taught researchers valuable skills that are still important today. Understanding subject headings and cross-references helps students think systematically about how topics are connected. Even in digital libraries, knowing how to broaden a search with related terms—similar to a "see also" reference—leads to stronger and more complete research results.

In conclusion, while digital tools are clearly superior in speed and access, the basic organization principles behind traditional library indexes continue to support effective academic research.

Reader's Guide Nasıl Kullanılır.

Süreli Yayınlar Okuyucu Rehberi (The Reader's Guide to Periodical Literature), ABD'de yayımlanan pek çok dergi makalesinin (hepsinin olmasa da) konu ve yazar listesidir. Dizin adı verilen bu liste, ilgili kişilerin hangi güncel bilgilerin mevcut olduğunu hızlıca öğrenebilmesi için her iki haftada bir ABD'deki kütüphanelere gönderilir. passages.passage_text:
To answer questions about the ancient geography of the earth in order to make comparisons with the present day geography, it is necessary to make maps of the lands and seas that existed during past ages. This process of reconstructing ancient geography is called paleogeography (from the Greek word palaious, meaning ancient).

Like a modern day detective, the geologist must search for clues about the nature of the ancient geography among the rocks. The clues are of two main kinds: the types of fossils preserved in rocks and the properties of the rocks themselves. By studying these clues, the geologist gains direct knowledge about the distribution of the lands and seas and also the natural environment of the area, such as climate, the temperature and salinity, i.e. the salt content, of the water, and the downhill direction of slopes on the earth's surface. The last item is very important in helping the geologist to guess where the mountains and basins were located in the geologic past.

The distribution of fossils (skeletons, shells, leaf impressions, footprints, and dinosaur eggs) in rocks can provide information about the ancient distribution of lands and seas. For example, the remains of corals and clamshells (sea animals) in very old limestone deposits indicate that the area was once part of a shallow sea. Similarly, when the remains of ancient animals, such as horses and camels, are found, it can be assumed that the area was dry land or that land was nearby. Fossils can also show the depth and temperature of ancient waters. For example, certain kinds of shelled sea animals live in shallow water, others in deep water. Certain kinds of present day coral need warm and shallow tropical salt waters to be able to live. When similar types of coral are found in ancient limestone, it can be surmised that the area at one time had a warm, tropical climate.

The properties of rocks are also important clues about the ancient past and are used as guides to reconstruct paleogeography. In 1863, the famous naturalist, Louis Agassiz, helped to solve a mystery about the origin of certain kinds of rocks, containing a mixture of sand, silt and clay. Some experts thought the rocks originated during the Biblical flood, but others suggested that they were caused by sediment, i.e., anything left behind from melting icebergs.

After a summer in the Swiss Alps studying glaciers and glacial deposits, Agassiz discovered that the rocks found, for example, in much of Europe had been spread by large continental glaciers. Much of what Agassiz saw could be explained only by glacial action. Because a glacier is a solid mass of ice, it moves slowly, and as it moves, it picks up all sizes of debris: in other words, the scattered remains of broken particles, ranging from huge rocks to silt and clay. As the ice melts, all the debris is left behind in the form of a layer of material of many kinds.

Using these two important clues - fossils and rocks - plus other information, geologists are able to reconstruct ancient geography to make comparisons with the earth's present geography. By comparing these, geologists know that the appearance of the earth's continents has been constantly changing over the centuries. And this changing of the earth's surface is still going on today, but it is so gradual that people are aware of the change only occasionally. Earthquakes and the formation of new volcanoes are two spectacular actions used by nature to change the face of continents.

Truly, we live in a changing world.

task1.model_answer: Paleogeography is the scientific reconstruction of the Earth's ancient landscapes and seas, allowing geologists to compare past geography with the present. To achieve this, scientists rely primarily on two types of geological evidence: fossils and rock properties. Fossils reveal whether an area was once ocean or dry land, as well as the depth, salinity, and temperature of ancient waters. For instance, tropical coral fossils in limestone point to warm, shallow seas, while horse or camel remains suggest nearby land. Rock properties offer additional insights, as shown by Louis Agassiz, who proved that widespread mixtures of sand, silt, and clay were deposited by moving continental glaciers rather than floods. Together, these clues confirm that continents continuously and gradually evolve.
task1.prompt: Summarize how geologists reconstruct ancient geography and what their findings reveal about the Earth's continents. Use your own words as much as possible.
task1.title: Summary: Reconstructing Earth's Ancient Geography

task2.model_answer:
Understanding the Earth's geological past is far more than an academic curiosity; it is essential for navigating both present environmental challenges and future planetary changes. By reconstructing ancient climates and coastlines through fossils and rock deposits, geologists can identify long-term natural patterns that short-term human records cannot capture.

First, paleogeography provides vital context for modern climate science. Discovering tropical coral in regions that are now temperate or arid demonstrates how dramatically sea levels and temperatures can shift over geological time. Studying these natural transitions helps scientists distinguish between gradual planetary cycles and rapid human-driven climate change. Second, understanding how continental plates, mountain ranges, and basins formed allows researchers to better assess natural hazards such as earthquakes and volcanic activity. Although continental change usually occurs imperceptibly, sudden geological events continue to reshape populated regions.

In conclusion, investigating the distant past equips humanity with perspective and practical knowledge. By learning how our changing world behaved millions of years ago, societies can make wiser decisions about resource management, urban planning, and disaster preparedness today.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Paleocoğrafya.

Günümüz coğrafyasıyla karşılaştırmalar yapabilmek amacıyla dünyanın eski coğrafyasına dair soruları yanıtlamak için, geçmiş çağlarda var olmuş kara ve denizlerin haritalarını çıkarmak gerekir. Eski coğrafyayı yeniden oluşturma sürecine, Yunanca "eski" anlamına gelen palaious sözcüğünden türetilmiş paleocoğrafya adı verilir.

Modern bir dedektif gibi jeolog da eski coğrafyanın doğasına dair ipuçlarını kayaların arasında aramalıdır. Bu ipuçları iki ana türdedir: kayalarda korunmuş fosil türleri ve kayaların kendi özellikleri. Jeolog, bu ipuçlarını inceleyerek kara ve denizlerin dağılımı hakkında ve ayrıca iklim, suyun sıcaklığı ve tuzluluğu (yani suyun tuz oranı) ile yeryüzündeki yamaçların eğim yönü gibi bölgenin doğal çevresi hakkında doğrudan bilgi edinir. Sonuncusu, jeoloğun jeolojik geçmişte dağların ve havzaların nerede bulunduğunu tahmin etmesine yardımcı olmada çok önemlidir.

İskeletler, deniz kabukları, yaprak izleri, ayak izleri ve dinozor yumurtaları gibi fosillerin kayalardaki dağılımı, kara ve denizlerin eski dağılımı hakkında bilgi sağlayabilir. Örneğin, çok eski kireçtaşı tortularında deniz hayvanları olan mercan ve istiridye kabuğu kalıntılarının bulunması, bölgenin bir zamanlar sığ bir denizin parçası olduğunu gösterir. Benzer şekilde, at ve deve gibi eski hayvanların kalıntıları bulunduğunda, bölgenin kuru kara olduğu veya yakınlarda kara bulunduğu varsayılabilir. Fosiller ayrıca eski suların derinliğini ve sıcaklığını da gösterebilir. Örneğin, belirli türdeki kabuklu deniz hayvanları sığ sularda, diğerleri ise derin sularda yaşar. Günümüzdeki bazı mercan türleri yaşayabilmek için ılık ve sığ tropikal tuzlu sulara ihtiyaç duyar. Eski kireçtaşlarında benzer mercan türleri bulunduğunda, bölgenin bir zamanlar ılık, tropikal bir iklime sahip olduğu tahmin edilebilir.

Kayaların özellikleri de eski geçmişe dair önemli ipuçlarıdır ve paleocoğrafyayı yeniden oluşturmada rehber olarak kullanılır. 1863 yılında ünlü doğa bilimci Louis Agassiz; kum, mil ve kil karışımı içeren belirli kaya türlerinin kökenine dair bir gizemi çözmeye yardımcı oldu. Bazı uzmanlar bu kayaların Kutsal Kitap'taki tufan sırasında oluştuğunu düşünüyordu, ancak diğerleri bunların tortudan, yani eriyen buzdağlarından geriye kalan her türlü maddeden kaynaklandığını öne sürdü.

İsviçre Alplerinde buzulları ve buzul tortularını inceleyerek geçirdiği bir yazın ardından Agassiz, örneğin Avrupa'nın büyük bir bölümünde bulunan kayaların büyük kıtasal buzullar tarafından yayıldığını keşfetti. Agassiz'in gördüklerinin çoğu yalnızca buzul hareketiyle açıklanabilirdi. Bir buzul katı bir buz kütlesi olduğu için yavaş hareket eder ve hareket ettikçe dev kayalardan mil ve kile kadar her boyuttaki döküntüyü, yani kırılmış parçacıkların dağınık kalıntılarını toplar. Buz eridikçe, tüm bu döküntüler pek çok farklı türden maddeden oluşan bir tabaka halinde geride bırakılır.

Jeologlar, bu iki önemli ipucunu, yani fosilleri ve kayaları, ayrıca diğer bilgileri kullanarak dünyanın bugünkü coğrafyasıyla karşılaştırmalar yapmak üzere eski coğrafyayı yeniden oluşturabilirler. Bunları karşılaştırarak jeologlar, dünyanın kıtalarının görünümünün yüzyıllar boyunca sürekli değiştiğini bilirler. Yeryüzünün bu değişimi günümüzde de devam etmektedir, ancak o kadar yavaştır ki insanlar bu değişimi yalnızca ara sıra fark ederler. Depremler ve yeni yanardağların oluşumu, doğanın kıtaların yüzünü değiştirmek için kullandığı iki görkemli olaydır.

Gerçekten de değişen bir dünyada yaşıyoruz.

passages.passage_text:
During the late 1970's about 1,500 pedestrians, most of whom were teenagers, were killed or badly injured on the roads in Britain. By the 1980's, the figure had doubled.

There was a debate about the relentless rise in these figures at the European Road Safety Year Conference in London, where various people expressed their opinions on the topic:

Frank West, Chairman of the Pedestrians' Association:
This killing of pedestrians, especially children, is a national disaster but it is obscured by the decline in road casualties as a whole. Among reasons for that general decline are stronger cars, the wearing of seat belts and less walking. The result is that people think the roads are safer, although for pedestrians they are becoming more and more dangerous. We know from the work of Professor Ian Howarth at the University of Nottingham that most casualties occur in residential areas hardly because children ignore drivers, but it is just the other way round. We need to narrow the roads and use policemen to slow down cars. We also want to see better policing and improved driver training as well. In Norway, you get a driving licence only after passing two tests. You receive a temporary licence after the first but it is made permanent only after passing another test, a year later. Something similar should be introduced for new drivers in Britain.

Reducing casualties among the ten-fourteen-year-olds presents special difficulties. Such children are beginning to explore on their own and tend to give up the basic rules for crossing roads taught at school. They begin to cross the roads by copying adults, learning the dangerous and difficult trick of choosing a gap in the traffic, and marching right into the road. Whatever the case is, children can be excused but not adults. We do not want to see another 3,000 pedestrians, especially young boys and girls, killed or hurt in the 1990's.

David Smith, The Department of Transport, Head of Road Safety:
We are aware that the decline in casualties among motorists seems likely to leave pedestrians the largest single road-user casualty group in the 1990's. Therefore, any required action for reducing casualties to the minimum will be taken.

Peter Bottomley, Minister for Roads:
We advise town planners and road safety engineers to switch their attention from vehicles to people. A third of all journeys are made entirely on foot. Most other journeys involve walking to some degree. That must make pedestrians the most important class of road users. Too often planners and road safety engineers seem to forget that.

passages.title: A Case for Safety
passages.tts_script:
A Case for Safety.

During the late 1970's, about 1,500 pedestrians, most of whom were teenagers, were killed or badly injured on the roads in Britain. By the 1980's, the figure had doubled.

There was a debate about the relentless rise in these figures at the European Road Safety Year Conference in London, where various people expressed their opinions on the topic.

Frank West, Chairman of the Pedestrians' Association, said: This killing of pedestrians, especially children, is a national disaster, but it is obscured by the decline in road casualties as a whole. Among reasons for that general decline are stronger cars, the wearing of seat belts, and less walking. The result is that people think the roads are safer, although for pedestrians they are becoming more and more dangerous. We know from the work of Professor Ian Howarth at the University of Nottingham that most casualties occur in residential areas, hardly because children ignore drivers, but it is just the other way round. We need to narrow the roads and use policemen to slow down cars. We also want to see better policing and improved driver training as well. In Norway, you get a driving licence only after passing two tests. You receive a temporary licence after the first, but it is made permanent only after passing another test, a year later. Something similar should be introduced for new drivers in Britain.

Reducing casualties among the ten- to fourteen-year-olds presents special difficulties. Such children are beginning to explore on their own and tend to give up the basic rules for crossing roads taught at school. They begin to cross the roads by copying adults, learning the dangerous and difficult trick of choosing a gap in the traffic, and marching right into the road. Whatever the case is, children can be excused, but not adults. We do not want to see another 3,000 pedestrians, especially young boys and girls, killed or hurt in the 1990's.

David Smith, Head of Road Safety at the Department of Transport, stated: We are aware that the decline in casualties among motorists seems likely to leave pedestrians the largest single road-user casualty group in the 1990's. Therefore, any required action for reducing casualties to the minimum will be taken.

Peter Bottomley, Minister for Roads, added: We advise town planners and road safety engineers to switch their attention from vehicles to people. A third of all journeys are made entirely on foot. Most other journeys involve walking to some degree. That must make pedestrians the most important class of road users. Too often planners and road safety engineers seem to forget that.

task1.model_answer: At the European Road Safety Year Conference in London, three officials addressed the doubling of pedestrian deaths and serious injuries in Britain. Frank West, Chairman of the Pedestrians' Association, warned that falling motorist casualties hide the growing danger to pedestrians, especially children aged ten to fourteen who imitate careless adult crossing habits. Because drivers often ignore children in residential areas, he called for narrower roads, stronger policing, and a two-stage driving test like Norway's. David Smith from the Department of Transport acknowledged that pedestrians could soon become the largest road-user casualty group and pledged action to minimize losses. Finally, Minister for Roads Peter Bottomley urged planners and engineers to prioritize pedestrians over vehicles, since most journeys involve walking.

task2.model_answer:
Although traffic education in schools teaches children how to cross streets safely, lasting reductions in pedestrian casualties depend far more on improving driver behavior and redesigning urban streets.

First, relying primarily on children to protect themselves places an unfair burden on young road users. As Frank West points out, older children naturally begin exploring independently and often copy adults who dart between moving vehicles. Even well-trained children can misjudge vehicle speed or distance, whereas adult drivers control heavy machines and bear the primary legal and moral responsibility for vigilance in residential neighborhoods.

Second, physical road design and stricter licensing standards address the root causes of accidents continuously. Narrowing residential streets, enforcing speed limits, and requiring new drivers to pass a second test after a probationary year—as practiced in Norway—force motorists to slow down and pay attention. When town planners prioritize people over traffic flow, every journey becomes safer regardless of a pedestrian's age or experience.

In conclusion, while school safety lessons remain useful, meaningful protection for pedestrians requires stricter driver accountability and people-centered street design.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Güvenlik İçin Bir Sav.

1970'lerin sonlarında, çoğu gençlerden oluşan yaklaşık 1.500 yaya Britanya yollarında hayatını kaybetti veya ağır yaralandı. 1980'lere gelindiğinde bu sayı iki katına çıkmıştı.

Londra'daki Avrupa Yol Güvenliği Yılı Konferansı'nda bu rakamlardaki amansız artış hakkında bir tartışma yapıldı ve çeşitli kişiler konuyla ilgili görüşlerini dile getirdi.

Yayalar Derneği Başkanı Frank West şöyle dedi: Başta çocuklar olmak üzere yayaların bu şekilde ölmesi ulusal bir felakettir, ancak toplam trafik kazası kayıplarındaki düşüş nedeniyle gözden kaçmaktadır. Bu genel düşüşün nedenleri arasında daha sağlam arabalar, emniyet kemeri kullanımı ve daha az yürümek yer almaktadır. Bunun sonucunda insanlar yolların daha güvenli olduğunu düşünmektedir, oysa yayalar için yollar giderek daha tehlikeli hale gelmektedir. Nottingham Üniversitesi'nden Profesör Ian Howarth'ın çalışmalarından biliyoruz ki, kazaların çoğu yerleşim alanlarında meydana gelmektedir; bunun nedeni çocukların sürücüleri görmezden gelmesi değil, tam tersidir. Yolları daraltmamız ve arabaları yavaşlatmak için polis görevlendirmemiz gerekiyor. Ayrıca daha iyi bir polis denetimi ve geliştirilmiş sürücü eğitimi de görmek istiyoruz. Norveç'te ehliyeti yalnızca iki sınavı geçtikten sonra alırsınız. İlkinden sonra geçici bir ehliyet alırsınız, ancak ehliyet ancak bir yıl sonra başka bir sınavı geçtiğinizde kalıcı hale gelir. Britanya'daki yeni sürücüler için de benzer bir uygulama getirilmelidir.

On ila on dört yaş arasındakilerdeki can kayıplarını ve yaralanmaları azaltmak özel zorluklar doğurmaktadır. Bu yaştaki çocuklar kendi başlarına keşfe çıkmaya başlar ve okulda öğretilen temel karşıdan karşıya geçme kurallarını bırakma eğilimindedir. Yetişkinleri taklit ederek karşıdan karşıya geçmeye başlar, trafikte bir boşluk seçip doğrudan yola atılma gibi tehlikeli ve zor bir yöntemi öğrenirler. Durum ne olursa olsun, çocuklar mazur görülebilir ama yetişkinler görülemez. 1990'larda başta genç erkek ve kız çocukları olmak üzere 3.000 yayanın daha öldüğünü veya yaralandığını görmek istemiyoruz.

Ulaştırma Bakanlığı Yol Güvenliği Dairesi Başkanı David Smith şunları söyledi: Sürücüler arasındaki kayıpların azalmasının, 1990'larda yayaları en büyük tekil yol kullanıcısı kayıp grubu haline getireceğinin farkındayız. Bu nedenle, kayıpları en aza indirmek için gereken her türlü önlem alınacaktır.

Yollardan Sorumlu Bakan Peter Bottomley ise şunları ekledi: Şehir plancılarına ve yol güvenliği mühendislerine dikkatlerini araçlardan insanlara çevirmelerini tavsiye ediyoruz. Tüm yolculukların üçte biri tamamen yürüyerek yapılmaktadır. Diğer yolculukların çoğu da bir ölçüde yürümeyi içermektedir. Bu da yayaları en önemli yol kullanıcısı sınıfı yapmalıdır. Plancılar ve yol güvenliği mühendisleri bunu çoğu zaman unutuyor gibi görünüyor.

passages.passage_text:
Although the weathermen's forecasts for a month ahead are only a little better than guesswork, they are now making long-term forecasts into the next century with growing confidence. For the dominant trend in the world's climate in the coming decades will, scientists say, be a predictable result of man's activities.

At the start of the industrial revolution nearly two centuries ago, man innocently set off a gigantic experiment in planetary engineering. Unaware of what he was doing, he spared no thought for the consequences. Today, the possible outcome is alarmingly clear, but the experiment is unstoppable. Within the lifetimes of many of us, the earth may become warmer than it has been for a thousand years. By the middle of the next century, it may be warmer than it has been since before the last Ice Age. And the century after that may be hotter than any in the past 70 million years.

Superficially, a warmer climate may seem welcome. But it could bring many hazards - disruption of crops in the world's main food-producing regions, famine, economic instability, civil unrest and even war.

In the much longer term, melting of the great ice-caps of Greenland and Antarctica could raise sea-levels throughout the world. The average sea-level has already risen a foot since the turn of the century, and if the ice-caps disappear entirely, it would rise by nearly 200 feet. Complete melting might take many centuries, but even a small increase in sea-level would threaten low-lying parts of the world such as the Netherlands.

The man-made agent of climatic change is the carbon dioxide that has been pouring out of the world's chimneys in ever-increasing quantities since the industrial revolution began. And in the past few years, scientists have begun to suspect that there is a second man-made source of carbon dioxide which may be as important as the burning of fossil fuels, namely the steady destruction of the world's great forests. Trees and other vegetation represent a huge stock of carbon removed from circulation like money in a bank. As the vast tropical forests are cut down, most of the carbon they contain finds its way back into the atmosphere as carbon dioxide.

The amount of CO2 (carbon dioxide) in the atmosphere is still tiny. But it has climatic effects out of all proportion to its concentration. It acts rather like the glass in a greenhouse, letting through short-wave radiation from the sun, but trapping the longer-wave radiation by which the earth loses heat to outer space.

Computer studies have suggested that if the concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere were to be twice that of today's, there would be a rise of between 2°C and 3°C in average temperature.

task1.model_answer: Global climate change is largely driven by human activities that began during the industrial revolution. Although rising temperatures might initially appear pleasant, they pose serious risks such as crop failure, famine, economic instability, and conflict, while melting polar ice-caps could dramatically raise sea-levels and threaten low-lying nations. The primary cause is increasing carbon dioxide emissions from burning fossil fuels and destroying major tropical forests, which normally store carbon. task2.model_answer:
Addressing climate change requires coordinated action from both governments and individual citizens, as neither group can solve a global problem alone. Without strong government policies, industrial emissions and large-scale deforestation cannot be curtailed effectively. Governments have the authority to regulate fossil fuel consumption, invest in renewable energy, and enforce laws that protect tropical forests. Because these structural changes directly shape how energy is produced and consumed, national and international leadership is indispensable.

However, individual choices also play an important role in accelerating systemic change. When citizens reduce their energy consumption, use public transportation, and support environmentally responsible companies, they create market demand for sustainable alternatives. Moreover, public awareness encourages voters to hold leaders accountable for long-term environmental commitments. In conclusion, while governments hold the primary power to transform energy and land-use systems, lasting progress depends on active participation from individuals as well.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Dünya İklimindeki Değişimler.

Meteorologların bir ay sonrası için yaptıkları tahminler tahminden pek de öteye gidemese de, artık gelecek yüzyıla yönelik uzun vadeli tahminleri artan bir güvenle yapıyorlar. Çünkü bilim insanları, önümüzdeki on yıllarda dünya iklimindeki baskın eğilimin insan faaliyetlerinin öngörülebilir bir sonucu olacağını söylüyor.

Yaklaşık iki yüzyıl önce Sanayi Devrimi'nin başlangıcında insanoğlu, masumane bir şekilde gezegen mühendisliği alanında devasa bir deney başlattı. Ne yaptığının farkında olmadan, sonuçlarını hiç düşünmedi. Bugün, olası sonuç endişe verici derecede net, ancak deney durdurulamaz durumda. Birçoğumuzun ömrü içinde Dünya, son bin yıldır olduğundan daha sıcak hale gelebilir. Gelecek yüzyılın ortalarına doğru, son Buzul Çağı öncesinden bu yana olduğundan daha sıcak olabilir. Ondan sonraki yüzyıl ise son 70 milyon yılın herhangi bir döneminden daha sıcak olabilir.

Yüzeysel olarak bakıldığında, daha sıcak bir iklim hoş görünebilir. Ancak beraberinde pek çok tehlike getirebilir: dünyanın başlıca gıda üreten bölgelerinde mahsullerin zarar görmesi, kıtlık, ekonomik istikrarsızlık, toplumsal huzursuzluk ve hatta savaş.

Çok daha uzun vadede, Grönland ve Antarktika'daki büyük buz örtülerinin erimesi dünya genelinde deniz seviyelerini yükseltebilir. Ortalama deniz seviyesi yüzyılın başından bu yana şimdiden bir fit (yaklaşık 30 cm) yükseldi ve buz örtüleri tamamen yok olursa neredeyse 200 fit (yaklaşık 60 metre) yükselecektir. Tamamen erime yüzyıllar sürebilir, ancak deniz seviyesindeki küçük bir artış bile Hollanda gibi dünyanın alçak kesimlerini tehdit edecektir.

İklim değişikliğinin insan yapımı etkeni, Sanayi Devrimi başladığından beri dünyanın bacalarından giderek artan miktarlarda çıkan karbondioksittir. Ve son birkaç yılda bilim insanları, fosil yakıtların yakılması kadar önemli olabilecek ikinci bir insan yapımı karbondioksit kaynağı daha olduğundan şüphelenmeye başladılar: dünyanın büyük ormanlarının sürekli yok edilmesi. Ağaçlar ve diğer bitki örtüsü, tıpkı bir bankadaki para gibi dolaşımdan çekilmiş devasa bir karbon stoğunu temsil eder. Geniş tropikal ormanlar kesildikçe, içerdikleri karbonun çoğu karbondioksit olarak atmosfere geri döner.

Atmosferdeki karbondioksit miktarı hala çok küçüktür. Ancak yoğunluğuyla orantısız derecede büyük iklimsel etkilere sahiptir. Tıpkı bir seradaki cam gibi davranarak güneşten gelen kısa dalga ışınlarının geçmesine izin verir, ancak dünyanın uzaya ısı kaybetmesini sağlayan daha uzun dalga ışınlarını hapseder.

Bilgisayar çalışmaları, atmosferdeki karbondioksit yoğunluğunun bugünkünün iki katına çıkması halinde, ortalama sıcaklıkta 2 santigrat derece ile 3 santigrat derece arasında bir artış olacağını ortaya koymuştur.

passages.passage_text:
An antiseptic is a substance which destroys bacteria or keeps them from increasing. Today, many types of antiseptics such as alcohol, iodine, iodoform and formalin are manufactured and used quite commonly. In addition to these manufactured antiseptics, the body itself has certain ways in which it defends itself against bacteria or germs. Tears, sweat, saliva (the fluid in the mouth) and blood contain substances which resist common infections. The greatest of nature's antiseptics are the white corpuscles in the blood, which are called phagocytes. These have the important quality of being able to consume harmful bacteria that enter the blood stream or infect a part of the body. When such bacteria are present in the body, the phagocytes rush to the infected spot and devour the invaders. The phagocytes are usually strong enough to destroy the bacteria unless the latter increases in number too quickly.

In the same way that bacteria attack human beings and cause infections, so they attack meat and vegetables and other food, making them go bad. Bacteria need favourable conditions to grow. These include moisture, and a fairly warm atmosphere. Thus, meat which has to be kept for a long time is frozen, and this makes it too cold for bacteria to grow until it is thawed out again.

task2.model_answer:
Understanding how bacteria grow is essential for protecting everyday health in both personal hygiene and food preparation. In daily life, minor cuts and scrapes can easily become infected if harmful germs enter the body. While our immune system relies on natural defenses such as white blood cells to fight invaders, simple hygiene habits—like washing hands and applying manufactured antiseptics to wounds—prevent bacteria from multiplying faster than the body can destroy them.

The same scientific knowledge helps families keep food safe and reduce waste. Because bacteria thrive in warm, moist environments, leaving meat or vegetables at room temperature allows them to spoil quickly. By refrigerating or freezing perishable items, people create conditions that are too cold for bacteria to grow. Furthermore, thawing frozen food safely in a refrigerator rather than on a warm counter minimizes risk. Overall, basic biological awareness turns simple habits into powerful protection against illness.

Antiseptikler.

Antiseptik, bakterileri yok eden veya çoğalmalarını önleyen bir maddedir. Günümüzde alkol, iyot, iyodoform ve formalin gibi birçok antiseptik türü üretilmekte ve oldukça yaygın olarak kullanılmaktadır. Üretilen bu antiseptiklere ek olarak, vücudun kendisi de bakteri veya mikroplara karşı kendini savunduğu belirli yollara sahiptir. Gözyaşı, ter, tükürük, yani ağızdaki sıvı ve kan, yaygın enfeksiyonlara direnç gösteren maddeler içerir. Doğanın en büyük antiseptikleri, kanda bulunan ve fagosit adı verilen akyuvarlardır. Bunlar, kan dolaşımına giren veya vücudun bir bölümünü enfekte eden zararlı bakterileri tüketebilme gibi önemli bir özelliğe sahiptir. Vücutta bu tür bakteriler bulunduğunda, fagositler hızla enfekte olan bölgeye akın eder ve istilacıları yutar. Bakterilerin sayısı çok hızlı artmadığı sürece, fagositler genellikle bakterileri yok edecek kadar güçlüdür.

Bakterilerin insanlara saldırıp enfeksiyonlara yol açtığı gibi, ete, sebzelere ve diğer yiyeceklere de saldırarak onların bozulmasına neden olurlar. Bakterilerin çoğalabilmesi için elverişli koşullara ihtiyacı vardır. Bunlar arasında nem ve oldukça ılık bir ortam yer alır. Bu nedenle, uzun süre saklanması gereken et dondurulur ve bu durum, yeniden çözülene kadar bakterilerin çoğalması için ortamı fazlasıyla soğuk hale getirir.

passages.passage_text:
All research agrees on loving care as an essential ingredient in healthy child development. But there is increasing doubt that the 24-hour-a-day, seven-day-a-week mother is the best way to provide it. Two recent studies have come up with the same result: 40 per cent of the mothers who stay at home with children under five are depressed. Doctor Michael Rutter and Doctor Steward Prince, among others, have shown that depressed mothers produce depressed, neurotic and backward children. There are many other mothers who, without being depressed, are exhausted and, therefore, oppressed by the unending repetitive task of caring for a baby, or by the constant demands of a young child, and so get less pleasure from their children than they might. A full-time mother at home is very likely to feel imprisoned and depressed. A depressed mother can be psychologically very damaging to her child because she will certainly not be able to give proper attention to it. There is good evidence that withdrawal of attention is more harmful to children than physical absence.

Therefore, a husband with common sense will certainly agree to make arrangements so that the mother can take some time off to pursue her own interests. He may choose to stay at home and take over the responsibility or a baby sitter may be employed. Any arrangement will do the mother good as long as it is regular and doesn't involve renegotiation every time. For instance, once a week, a completely free day and evening during which the mother is relieved of all responsibility is optimal. She can visit friends, go to a museum, or spend all morning buying a pair of shoes and she needn't come back until she feels like it. The only rule is that she must go out, not stay at home doing housework. It is actually best of all if arrangements are made so that parents can regularly spend a night out together.

passages.title: How to Be a Happier Mother
passages.tts_script:
How to Be a Happier Mother.

All research agrees on loving care as an essential ingredient in healthy child development. But there is increasing doubt that the 24-hour-a-day, seven-day-a-week mother is the best way to provide it. Two recent studies have come up with the same result: 40 percent of the mothers who stay at home with children under five are depressed. Doctor Michael Rutter and Doctor Steward Prince, among others, have shown that depressed mothers produce depressed, neurotic, and backward children. There are many other mothers who, without being depressed, are exhausted and, therefore, oppressed by the unending repetitive task of caring for a baby, or by the constant demands of a young child, and so get less pleasure from their children than they might. A full-time mother at home is very likely to feel imprisoned and depressed. A depressed mother can be psychologically very damaging to her child because she will certainly not be able to give proper attention to it. There is good evidence that withdrawal of attention is more harmful to children than physical absence.

Therefore, a husband with common sense will certainly agree to make arrangements so that the mother can take some time off to pursue her own interests. He may choose to stay at home and take over the responsibility, or a babysitter may be employed. Any arrangement will do the mother good as long as it is regular and doesn't involve renegotiation every time. For instance, once a week, a completely free day and evening during which the mother is relieved of all responsibility is optimal. She can visit friends, go to a museum, or spend all morning buying a pair of shoes, and she needn't come back until she feels like it. The only rule is that she must go out, not stay at home doing housework. It is actually best of all if arrangements are made so that parents can regularly spend a night out together.

Light pollution is a growing problem in modern cities, and it affects far more than just professional astronomers. passages.passage_text:
The number of people who die as a result of starvation is increasing every day. People don't always die just because they don't eat; they die because they are so weakened from lack of food that they get ill very easily. Very few people die of measles in Great Britain. Measles is just a childhood disease that most of us experience and shake off in a week or two. For those whose bodies are weakened by starvation, however, measles is a killer. And so are hundreds of other diseases. Last year about 30,000,000 people died of such minor diseases. That's the equivalent of the majority of the population of Great Britain. There can be no doubt that if those people had gotten proper food, many of them would still be alive today.

Firms in this country are currently spending millions of pounds manufacturing meat. Not meat from cows but completely synthetic, artificial meat. They are making it out of a certain kind of fungus and from other vegetable matter. By adding flavour and other constituents, this 'meat' is said to be indistinguishable from the meat taken from animals. It has the same protein and other beneficial elements that a pound of steak or chicken contains and we are assured that within a few years we will be eating it as readily as we now eat lamb or beef.

A large number of us will be extremely hesitant about this synthetic foodstuff and therefore, the firms involved will have to spend many more millions on persuading us, through advertising, that we really need the new food. So, by the time the first vegetable sausage sizzles in our frying pans, millions of pounds will have been spent on the research, manufacture and selling of the new product.

If it is true that such meat can be produced, if it is true that it really is as good as the real thing, and if it is going to be cheap, these products should not be directed at those who already have enough food but at those who have none. Let the major firms forget about spending millions trying to persuade us to eat it and use their marvellous new invention to feed the vast mass of the world's population who have never even seen meat. Half a loaf of bread is better than none: synthetic meat is better than an occasional handful of rice.

Every year the major agricultural countries of the world produce too much of certain products - the quantity is beyond what is needed or consumed. Milk, vegetables and the like go off quickly as they cannot be efficiently stored. Modern food technology has presented us with the ability to freeze and to dehydrate (or freeze-dry) food. Could we not be sensible and make use of this surplus of products by processing them to give them longer life and flying them out to where they are needed?

Those countries which sometimes have too much should make their surplus available in some form to those which have too little. Don't tell me that it would cost too much money. If a tenth of what is spent on advertising, packaging, and distributing food is creamed off and spent on processing it for the starving, we would save a great many lives.

task2.model_answer:
Reducing global hunger requires practical cooperation rather than simply increasing food production. As the passage suggests, a huge amount of food produced in developed countries goes to waste because surpluses are not preserved or distributed where they are needed most. By investing a small fraction of food marketing budgets into dehydration, freezing, and international transport, governments and charities could deliver nutritious supplies to famine-stricken regions before they spoil.

In addition, new food technologies such as plant-based or synthetic proteins can play a valuable role if they are affordable and aimed at populations facing severe protein shortages. However, emergency food aid alone is not enough for the long term. Wealthier nations should also share agricultural training, irrigation tools, and storage infrastructure so developing regions can build resilient local food systems. Combining immediate surplus redistribution with sustainable local farming offers the most effective path toward ending preventable starvation.

passages.passage_text:
At a dinner party two men were discussing The Right Stuff, a book about the Mercury space programme. While Ted went on and on about the technical details he had picked up from the book, Dan offered only a few comments. "Ted got so much more out of the reading than I did." Dan later said, "Is he more intelligent than I am?"

The two men had similar educational backgrounds and intelligence levels. It was later discovered that Ted just knew how to learn better than Dan did. Ted had made his brain more absorbent by using a few simple skills.

For years, experts had believed that an individual's ability to learn was a fixed capacity. During the last two decades, however, leading psychologists and educators have come to think otherwise. "We have increasing proof that human intelligence is expandable," says Jack Lochhead, director of the Cognitive Development Project at the University of Massachusetts in Amherst. "We know that with proper skills people can actually improve their learning ability."

Moreover, these skills are basic enough so that almost anyone can master them with practice. Here, gathered from the ideas of experts across the country, are several proven ways to boost your learning ability.

1. Look at the big picture first. When reading new, unfamiliar material, scan it first. Skim subheads, photo captions and any available summaries. This previewing will help anchor in your mind what you then read.

2. Practise memory-enhancing techniques. These techniques, also called mnemonics, transform new information into more easily remembered formulations. For instance, to a student who cannot spell the word arithmetic, a teacher can teach a sentence that remains locked in mind for years: "A rat in Tom's house may eat Tom's ice cream." The first letters of each word spell arithmetic. Although mnemonics were once dismissed by researchers, they are now considered an effective means of boosting memory - doubling or even tripling the amount of new material that test subjects can retain.

3. Organise facts into categories. In studies at Stanford University, students were asked to memorize 112 words. These included names of animals, items of clothing, types of transportation, and occupations. For one group, the words were divided into these four categories. For a second group, the words were listed at random. Those who studied the material in organised categories consistently outperformed the others, recalling two to three times more words. For example, to remember the names of all former U.S. presidents in proper order, cluster the leaders into groups - those before the War of 1812, those from 1812 until the Civil War, those from the Civil War to World War I, and those after World War I. By thus organising complex material into logical categories, you create a permanent storage technique.

4. Discover your own learning style. What's your style? Try some self-analysis. What, for example, is your approach to putting together an unassembled item? Do you concentrate better in the morning or in the evening? In a noisy environment or a quiet one? In a library or in your own room? Make a list of all the pluses and minuses you can identify. Then use this list to create the learning environment best for you. Whichever style works for you, the good news is that you can expand your learning capacity. And this can make your life fuller and more productive.

task2.model_answer:
In today's fast-paced academic and professional world, knowing how to learn efficiently is just as important as what we learn. Among the strategies mentioned in the passage, organizing facts into categories seems to be the most effective for long-term success.

When students try to memorize isolated details, their brains quickly become overloaded and forget key information. By contrast, grouping related ideas into clear categories gives the mind a logical structure to follow. For instance, when preparing for a history or biology exam, dividing events into eras or classifying organisms by shared traits makes complex material much easier to understand and recall under pressure. The Stanford University study clearly supports this approach, showing that categorized lists double or even triple recall.

While previewing, mnemonics, and personalizing one's study environment are all valuable habits, categorization directly strengthens how knowledge is connected and stored. Ultimately, combining a well-organized study method with self-awareness allows learners to unlock their full potential and achieve better results with less stress.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Daha Hızlı Öğrenmenin Anahtarları.

Bir akşam yemeği davetinde iki adam, Mercury uzay programını konu alan The Right Stuff adlı kitap hakkında sohbet ediyordu. Ted kitaptan edindiği teknik ayrıntıları durmadan anlatırken, Dan yalnızca birkaç yorum yapabildi. Dan daha sonra, "Ted okuduklarından benden çok daha fazla şey çıkardı," dedi. "Acaba benden daha mı zeki?"

İki adamın da eğitim geçmişleri ve zekâ düzeyleri benzerdi. Daha sonra, Ted'in sadece Dan'den daha iyi öğrenmeyi bildiği ortaya çıktı. Ted, birkaç basit beceri kullanarak beynini bilgiyi daha kolay özümseyen bir hâle getirmişti.

Yıllar boyunca uzmanlar, bir bireyin öğrenme yeteneğinin sabit bir kapasite olduğuna inanmıştı. Ancak son yirmi yılda önde gelen psikologlar ve eğitimciler farklı düşünmeye başladı. Amherst'teki Massachusetts Üniversitesi Bilişsel Gelişim Projesi direktörü Jack Lochhead, "İnsan zekâsının geliştirilebilir olduğuna dair giderek artan kanıtlarımız var," diyor. "Doğru becerilerle insanların öğrenme yeteneklerini gerçekten geliştirebileceğini biliyoruz."

Üstelik bu beceriler, neredeyse herkesin pratik yaparak ustalaşabileceği kadar temeldir. İşte ülke çapındaki uzmanların fikirlerinden derlenen, öğrenme yeteneğinizi artırmanın kanıtlanmış birkaç yolu.

1 Numara: Önce büyük resme bakın. Yeni ve aşina olmadığınız bir materyali okurken önce göz gezdirin. Alt başlıkları, fotoğraf altı yazılarını ve mevcut özetleri hızlıca tarayın. Bu ön inceleme, ardından okuyacağınız şeylerin zihninizde yer etmesine yardımcı olacaktır.

2 Numara: Hafızayı güçlendiren teknikleri uygulayın. Bellek destekleyici teknikler (mnemonikler) olarak da adlandırılan bu yöntemler, yeni bilgileri daha kolay hatırlanan kalıplara dönüştürür. Örneğin, İngilizcede "arithmetic" kelimesini yazamayan bir öğrenciye, bir öğretmen yıllarca akılda kalacak bir cümle öğretebilir: "A rat in Tom's house may eat Tom's ice cream." ("Tom'un evindeki bir sıçan Tom'un dondurmasını yiyebilir.") Her kelimenin ilk harfi "arithmetic" kelimesini oluşturur. Mnemonikler bir zamanlar araştırmacılar tarafından önemsenmese de artık hafızayı güçlendirmenin, deneklerin aklında tutabildiği yeni materyal miktarını iki hatta üç katına çıkarmanın etkili bir yolu olarak kabul edilmektedir.

3 Numara: Bilgileri kategoriler hâlinde düzenleyin. Stanford Üniversitesi'nde yapılan çalışmalarda öğrencilerden 112 kelimeyi ezberlemeleri istendi. Bunlar hayvan adları, giyim eşyaları, ulaşım türleri ve meslekleri içeriyordu. Bir grup için kelimeler bu dört kategoriye ayrıldı. İkinci bir grup içinse kelimeler rastgele sıralandı. Materyali düzenli kategoriler hâlinde çalışanlar sürekli olarak diğerlerinden daha iyi performans gösterdi ve iki ila üç kat daha fazla kelime hatırladı. Örneğin, tüm eski ABD başkanlarının isimlerini doğru sırayla hatırlamak için liderleri gruplara ayırın: 1812 Savaşı'ndan öncekiler, 1812'den İç Savaş'a kadar olanlar, İç Savaş'tan Birinci Dünya Savaşı'na kadar olanlar ve Birinci Dünya Savaşı'ndan sonrakiler. Böylece karmaşık materyali mantıklı kategorilere ayırarak kalıcı bir depolama tekniği oluşturmuş olursunuz.

4 Numara: Kendi öğrenme tarzınızı keşfedin. Sizin tarzınız ne? Biraz öz analiz yapmayı deneyin. Örneğin, demonte bir eşyayı birleştirirken nasıl bir yaklaşım izlersiniz? Sabahları mı yoksa akşamları mı daha iyi odaklanırsınız? Gürültülü bir ortamda mı yoksa sessiz bir ortamda mı? Kütüphanede mi yoksa kendi odanızda mı? Tespit edebileceğiniz tüm artıların ve eksilerin bir listesini yapın. Ardından bu listeyi sizin için en uygun öğrenme ortamını oluşturmak için kullanın. Sizin için hangi tarz işe yararsa yarasın, iyi haber şu ki öğrenme kapasitenizi artırabilirsiniz. Ve bu da hayatınızı daha dolu ve daha verimli hâle getirebilir.

passages.passage_text:
In the mid-1800's scientists wanted to know whether the atom was really indivisible. They also wanted to know why atoms of different elements had different properties.

A major breakthrough came with the invention of the Crookes' tube, or cathode-ray tube. What is a cathode-ray tube and how does it work? Everybody knows that some substances conduct electric current; that is, they are conductors, while other substances do not. But with enough electrical power, a current can be driven through any substance - solid, liquid, or gas. In the cathode-ray tube, a high voltage electric current is driven through a vacuum. The tube contains two pieces of metal, called electrodes. Each electrode is attached by a wire to the source of an electric current. The source has two terminals, positive and negative. The electrode attached to the positive electric terminal is called the anode; the electrode attached to the negative terminal is called the cathode. Crookes showed that when the current was turned on, a beam moved from the cathode to the anode; in other words, the beam moved from the negative to the positive terminal. Therefore, the beam had to be negative in nature.

The German physicists in Crookes's time favoured the wave theory of cathode rays because the beam travelled in straight lines, like water waves. But the English physicists favoured the particle theory. They said that the beam was composed of tiny particles which moved very quickly - so quickly that they were hardly influenced by gravity. That was why the particles moved in a straight path. Notice how an experimental observation led to two different theories.

Crookes proposed a method to solve the dilemma. If the beam was composed of negative particles, a magnet would deflect them. But if the beam was a wave, a magnet would cause almost no change in direction. Particles would also be more easily deflected by an electric field. In 1897, the English physicist J.J. Thomson used both these techniques - magnetic and electric - to show that the rays were composed of particles. Today we call these particles electrons. (The term electron was suggested by the Irish physicist George Stoney, in 1891, to represent the fundamental unit of electricity.) In 1911, a young American physicist named Robert Millikan determined the mass of the electron: 9.11 x 10^-28 grams. (To get an idea of how small this is, notice that minus sign up there in the exponent, and think of all the zeros we would have to put before the 9 if we wrote the entire number as a decimal.)

Next, someone had to prove that the electrons weren't coming from the electricity, but were being given off by the metal electrodes. Proof that metals do give off electrons came from the laboratories of Philipp Lenard, a German physicist. In 1902, he showed that ultraviolet light directed onto a metal makes it send out, or emit, electrons. This effect, known as the photoelectric effect, indicated that atoms contain electrons.

extra_questions.explanation: English physicists argued that the beam consisted of tiny particles moving so rapidly that gravity barely affected them, causing them to travel in a straight path.
options: Because the vacuum inside the tube eliminated all gravity
Because the positive anode pulled the beam upward with great force

passages.title: The Discovery of the Electron
passages.tts_script:
The Discovery of the Electron.

In the mid-1800s scientists wanted to know whether the atom was really indivisible. They also wanted to know why atoms of different elements had different properties.

A major breakthrough came with the invention of the Crookes' tube, or cathode-ray tube. What is a cathode-ray tube and how does it work? Everybody knows that some substances conduct electric current; that is, they are conductors, while other substances do not. But with enough electrical power, a current can be driven through any substance, whether solid, liquid, or gas. In the cathode-ray tube, a high-voltage electric current is driven through a vacuum. The tube contains two pieces of metal, called electrodes. Each electrode is attached by a wire to the source of an electric current. The source has two terminals, positive and negative. The electrode attached to the positive electric terminal is called the anode; the electrode attached to the negative terminal is called the cathode. Crookes showed that when the current was turned on, a beam moved from the cathode to the anode; in other words, the beam moved from the negative to the positive terminal. Therefore, the beam had to be negative in nature.

The German physicists in Crookes's time favoured the wave theory of cathode rays because the beam travelled in straight lines, like water waves. But the English physicists favoured the particle theory. They said that the beam was composed of tiny particles which moved very quickly, so quickly that they were hardly influenced by gravity. That was why the particles moved in a straight path. Notice how an experimental observation led to two different theories.

Crookes proposed a method to solve the dilemma. If the beam was composed of negative particles, a magnet would deflect them. But if the beam was a wave, a magnet would cause almost no change in direction. Particles would also be more easily deflected by an electric field. In 1897, the English physicist J.J. Thomson used both these techniques, magnetic and electric, to show that the rays were composed of particles. Today we call these particles electrons. The term electron was suggested by the Irish physicist George Stoney, in 1891, to represent the fundamental unit of electricity. In 1911, a young American physicist named Robert Millikan determined the mass of the electron: 9.11 times 10 to the minus 28 grams. To get an idea of how small this is, notice that minus sign up there in the exponent, and think of all the zeros we would have to put before the 9 if we wrote the entire number as a decimal.

Next, someone had to prove that the electrons weren't coming from the electricity, but were being given off by the metal electrodes. Proof that metals do give off electrons came from the laboratories of Philipp Lenard, a German physicist. In 1902, he showed that ultraviolet light directed onto a metal makes it send out, or emit, electrons. This effect, known as the photoelectric effect, indicated that atoms contain electrons.

Using a vacuum tube with two metal electrodes, William Crookes showed that a beam travelled from the negative cathode to the positive anode, proving its negative charge. Although German physicists argued the beam was a wave and English physicists believed it consisted of fast-moving particles, J.J. Thomson settled the debate in 1897 by deflecting the rays with magnetic and electric fields. Later, in 1911, Robert Millikan measured the electron's tiny mass. task2.model_answer:
Major scientific breakthroughs rarely happen in isolation; instead, they grow out of international debate and collaboration. The discovery of the electron clearly illustrates how disagreement and shared inquiry among scientists from different countries accelerate progress.

When William Crookes introduced the cathode-ray tube, his observations sparked an active debate between German physicists, who favoured the wave theory, and English physicists, who supported the particle theory. Rather than slowing science down, this disagreement pushed researchers to design better experiments. By testing Crookes's proposed method, J.J. Thomson ultimately proved the particle theory correct and confirmed the existence of the electron, a name suggested earlier by an Irish physicist. Subsequent contributions from the German physicist Philipp Lenard and the American physicist Robert Millikan revealed where electrons come from and how much they weigh.

Because each researcher built upon—or challenged—another's findings, humanity gained a complete picture of atomic structure far faster than any single scientist could have achieved alone. Open debate and global cooperation remain essential to modern scientific discovery.

Elektronun Keşfi.

1800'lerin ortalarında bilim insanları atomun gerçekten bölünemez olup olmadığını bilmek istiyorlardı. Ayrıca farklı elementlerin atomlarının neden farklı özelliklere sahip olduğunu da öğrenmek istiyorlardı.

Büyük bir atılım, Crookes tüpünün veya diğer adıyla katot ışını tüpünün icadıyla geldi. Katot ışını tüpü nedir ve nasıl çalışır? Herkes bazı maddelerin elektrik akımını ilettiğini, yani iletken olduğunu, diğer maddelerin ise iletmediğini bilir. Ancak yeterli elektrik gücüyle, ister katı, ister sıvı, ister gaz olsun herhangi bir maddenin içinden akım geçirilebilir. Katot ışını tüpünde, bir vakumun içinden yüksek voltajlı bir elektrik akımı geçirilir. Tüp, elektrot adı verilen iki metal parçası içerir. Her bir elektrot bir telle elektrik akımı kaynağına bağlıdır. Kaynağın pozitif ve negatif olmak üzere iki kutbu vardır. Pozitif elektrik kutbuna bağlı elektrota anot, negatif kutba bağlı elektrota ise katot denir. Crookes, akım açıldığında katottan anoda doğru bir ışının hareket ettiğini; başka bir deyişle ışının negatif kutuptan pozitif kutba doğru ilerlediğini gösterdi. Dolayısıyla, ışının doğası gereği negatif olması gerekiyordu.

Crookes'un dönemindeki Alman fizikçiler, ışın tıpkı su dalgaları gibi düz çizgiler hâlinde ilerlediği için katot ışınlarının dalga teorisini destekliyordu. Fakat İngiliz fizikçiler parçacık teorisini benimsedi. Işının çok hızlı hareket eden, o kadar hızlı ki yerçekiminden neredeyse hiç etkilenmeyen minik parçacıklardan oluştuğunu söylediler. Parçacıkların düz bir yolda ilerlemesinin nedeni buydu. Deneysel bir gözlemin nasıl iki farklı teoriye yol açtığına dikkat edin.

Crookes bu ikilemi çözmek için bir yöntem önerdi. Eğer ışın negatif parçacıklardan oluşuyorsa bir mıknatıs onları saptırırdı. Ancak ışın bir dalga olsaydı bir mıknatıs yönünde neredeyse hiç değişiklik yaratmazdı. Parçacıklar ayrıca bir elektrik alanı tarafından da daha kolay saptırılırdı. 1897'de İngiliz fizikçi J.J. Thomson, ışınların parçacıklardan oluştuğunu göstermek için hem manyetik hem de elektrik olmak üzere bu iki tekniği de kullandı. Bugün bu parçacıklara elektron diyoruz. Elektron terimi, elektriğin temel birimini temsil etmek üzere 1891 yılında İrlandalı fizikçi George Stoney tarafından önerilmişti. 1911'de Robert Millikan adlı genç bir Amerikalı fizikçi elektronun kütlesini belirledi: 9,11 çarpı 10 üzeri eksi 28 gram. Bunun ne kadar küçük olduğu hakkında bir fikir edinmek için üstteki o eksi işaretine dikkat edin ve sayının tamamını ondalık olarak yazsaydık 9'un önüne koymamız gerekecek tüm o sıfırları düşünün.

Ardından birinin, elektronların elektrikten gelmediğini, metal elektrotlar tarafından yayıldığını kanıtlaması gerekiyordu. Metallerin gerçekten elektron yaydığına dair kanıt, Alman fizikçi Philipp Lenard'ın laboratuvarlarından geldi. 1902'de, bir metalin üzerine yöneltilen morötesi ışığın, metalin elektron göndermesine veya yaymasına yol açtığını gösterdi. Fotoelektrik etki olarak bilinen bu olay, atomların elektron içerdiğini ortaya koydu.

passages.passage_text:
Inflation has attracted more public interest than any other aspect of economics, for the simple reason that everyone finds himself immediately affected by it. The common belief is that inflation is necessarily a negative occurrence but there are various reasons why this might not be the case. Let us consider some of the arguments.

Simply described, inflation is the situation where increased wage demands result in higher prices of consumer goods, which causes further increased wage demands. This is called an inflation spiral. The following example will make this point clear. The workers in the car industry demand and receive a wage increase. This causes producers to increase the market price of cars in order to make a profit. People see that they cannot so easily afford to buy cars and, as a result, they ask for higher wages in order to maintain the same standard of living as before. These new wage increases result in rising prices for goods and services in all sectors of the economy. Car industry workers now face higher prices so they demand higher wages. A side effect of this spiral is that workers in other industries may ask for similar increases before any price rises occur, simply because they feel that they, too, should have more money.

The general effects of inflation can be discussed according to whether they are largely positive or largely negative. The positive effects will be considered first and may be divided into two main groups: effects on prices and wages and effects on loans. The consumer discovers he has to pay more for goods and services although he can find himself better off than other groups of workers if his wages increase faster than theirs. In this way, income gaps between low-paid and high-paid workers can be narrowed by allowing low-paid workers to have a larger increase. Everybody gets a rise, but some receive more than others. Obviously, if all wages are increased by the same percentage as prices in general, no change in standard of living takes place.

The effect of inflation on loans is beneficial to the borrower. In other words, loans reduce in value so that a borrower only has to pay back the nominal value of the loan and not its true, or real, value. This benefits the borrower, as the following example shows. A student borrows £10,000 to study medicine and become a doctor. This is the amount that a qualified doctor earns in 1 1/2 years. When the student pays back the loan six years later, £10,000 is the equivalent of only nine months' salary. Even if normal interest rates are added to the loan, this will not significantly change the final result.

task1.model_answer: Inflation attracts widespread attention because it immediately affects everyone. Although it is commonly viewed negatively, the passage explains both how it develops and how it can produce positive effects. Inflation often begins as an inflation spiral: higher wage demands force producers to raise prices, prompting further wage demands across the economy. Nevertheless, inflation can benefit certain groups. If low-paid workers receive larger wage increases than high-paid workers, income gaps can narrow. Additionally, inflation helps borrowers because loans lose real value over time, allowing borrowers to repay only the original nominal sum rather than its true purchasing power.

task2.model_answer:
Although moderate inflation can occasionally benefit borrowers or adjust wage disparities, I believe that inflation is largely harmful to society as a whole. First, rapid price increases reduce the purchasing power of ordinary households. People on fixed incomes, such as retirees, suffer the most because their pensions rarely rise as fast as the cost of food, housing, and healthcare. Furthermore, as the passage illustrates, inflation can trigger a damaging spiral in which rising wages and rising prices continuously feed each other, creating economic instability.

On the other hand, as the text notes, borrowers may find it easier to repay fixed loans when money loses value over time. However, this benefit is uneven and often comes at the expense of savers and lenders, who see the real value of their money shrink. When uncertainty grows, businesses also hesitate to invest in long-term projects. Therefore, while limited inflation may bring minor advantages to some individuals, stable prices are far healthier for long-term economic well-being.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Enflasyon.

Enflasyon, ekonominin diğer tüm yönlerinden daha fazla kamuoyu ilgisi çekmiştir; bunun basit nedeni ise herkesin bundan doğrudan etkilendiğini görmesidir. Yaygın kanı enflasyonun mutlaka olumsuz bir durum olduğu yönündedir, ancak durumun böyle olmayabileceğine dair çeşitli nedenler vardır. Bu argümanlardan bazılarını ele alalım.

Basitçe ifade etmek gerekirse enflasyon, artan ücret taleplerinin tüketim mallarının fiyatlarının yükselmesine yol açtığı ve bunun da daha fazla ücret talebine neden olduğu durumdur. Buna enflasyon sarmalı denir. Aşağıdaki örnek bu noktayı netleştirecektir. Otomotiv sektöründeki işçiler ücret artışı talep eder ve alırlar. Bu durum, üreticilerin kâr elde edebilmek için otomobillerin piyasa fiyatını artırmasına neden olur. İnsanlar otomobilleri eskisi kadar kolay satın alamadıklarını görürler ve bunun sonucunda öncekiyle aynı yaşam standardını koruyabilmek için daha yüksek ücretler isterler. Bu yeni ücret artışları, ekonominin tüm sektörlerindeki mal ve hizmet fiyatlarının yükselmesine yol açar. Otomotiv sektörü işçileri artık daha yüksek fiyatlarla karşılaşır ve bu yüzden daha yüksek ücretler talep ederler. Bu sarmalın bir yan etkisi de diğer sektörlerdeki işçilerin, henüz herhangi bir fiyat artışı gerçekleşmeden önce, sırf kendilerinin de daha fazla paraya sahip olması gerektiğini düşündükleri için benzer artışlar isteyebilmesidir.

Enflasyonun genel etkileri, büyük ölçüde olumlu ya da büyük ölçüde olumsuz olmalarına göre ele alınabilir. İlk olarak olumlu etkiler incelenecektir ve bunlar iki ana gruba ayrılabilir: fiyatlar ve ücretler üzerindeki etkiler ile krediler üzerindeki etkiler. Tüketici, mal ve hizmetler için daha fazla ödeme yapması gerektiğini fark eder; ancak kendi ücretleri diğer işçi gruplarınınkinden daha hızlı artarsa kendini onlardan daha iyi durumda bulabilir. Bu şekilde, düşük ücretli işçilere daha büyük bir artış sağlanarak düşük ücretli ve yüksek ücretli işçiler arasındaki gelir farkları daraltılabilir. Herkes zam alır, ancak bazıları diğerlerinden daha fazla alır. Açıkçası, tüm ücretler genel olarak fiyatlarla aynı oranda artırılırsa yaşam standardında hiçbir değişiklik meydana gelmez.

Enflasyonun krediler üzerindeki etkisi borç alan kişi için avantajlıdır. Başka bir deyişle, kredilerin değeri düşer; böylece borç alan kişinin kredinin gerçek, yani reel değerini değil, yalnızca nominal değerini geri ödemesi gerekir. Aşağıdaki örneğin de gösterdiği gibi bu durum borç alan kişiye fayda sağlar. Bir öğrenci tıp okuyup doktor olmak için on bin sterlin borç alır. Bu, uzman bir doktorun bir buçuk yılda kazandığı miktardır. Öğrenci altı yıl sonra krediyi geri ödediğinde, on bin sterlin yalnızca dokuz aylık maaşa eşdeğerdir. Krediye normal faiz oranları eklense bile bu durum nihai sonucu önemli ölçüde değiştirmeyecektir.

passages.passage_text:
Today, finding a source of fresh water is becoming more and more difficult. Many of our streams, rivers and lakes have been contaminated with sewage, and many towns and cities obtain their drinking water from these same streams, rivers and lakes. To prevent this constant contamination, sewage treatment plants are being built in many places. These are capable of converting sewage into pure drinkable water.

Another way to solve the problem of fresh water is to make use of the most abundant source of water we have: the sea. If we could learn to get potable water from sea water easily and cheaply, we would solve the problem. Man cannot live on sea water directly because of the high proportion of minerals (mainly salt) in it. More than 2% of salt in a solution is dangerous for the human body. Sea water contains 3.5% of salt. Such a high quantity causes dehydration in human body; that is, the body loses the liquids necessary for life. Thus, it is necessary to reduce the percentage of salt in sea water to an acceptable level before using it. A number of methods can be used to do this. The most common method is distillation. Sea water is heated until the water evaporates and the salt is left behind. The steam then condenses into pure water. Another method is freezing. When this is done, the water freezes first, leaving the salt behind. The ice is then removed and pure water is obtained. A third method is called reverse osmosis. Pure water molecules are separated from the salt molecules under great pressure.

Recently scientists have been working on a completely new idea: the idea of obtaining fresh water from the air. Winds coming from the sea carry a lot of water vapour. This vapour condenses into water if it strikes something cold. If scientists can build a large condenser, then they can collect and store fresh water easily. Unfortunately, the main problem with all of the mentioned methods is their high cost. That's why scientists are looking for ways of reducing the cost.

task1.model_answer: Finding fresh water is increasingly difficult because many rivers and lakes are polluted by sewage. One solution is building sewage treatment plants to turn waste into drinkable water. Another approach is obtaining fresh water from the sea, which contains too much salt to drink safely. Scientists use three main desalination methods: distillation, which boils and condenses water; freezing, which separates salt from ice; and reverse osmosis, which filters water under high pressure. Researchers are also exploring ways to condense water vapour from sea winds. However, all these solutions remain very expensive, so reducing costs is now a major priority.

task2.model_answer:
Although technological innovations such as desalination and atmospheric condensers offer promising ways to produce fresh water, governments should not rely on them alone to solve water shortages. Instead, they must balance investment in new technologies with strict water conservation and pollution prevention.

On one hand, as the passage highlights, the sea is our most abundant water source. In dry coastal regions where rivers and lakes are scarce or contaminated, investing in cheaper desalination methods is essential for long-term survival. On the other hand, desalination and large-scale condensers require substantial energy and financial resources, making them unaffordable for many developing regions. Protecting existing freshwater sources from industrial and domestic sewage is often far more cost-effective.

In conclusion, technology can expand our water supply, but it cannot replace responsible management. Governments should prioritize reducing waste and preventing contamination while continuing research into affordable purification methods.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Tatlı Su.

Günümüzde tatlı su kaynağı bulmak giderek daha da zorlaşıyor. Derelerimizin, nehirlerimizin ve göllerimizin birçoğu kanalizasyon sularıyla kirlenmiş durumda ve pek çok kasaba ve şehir içme suyunu yine bu derelerden, nehirlerden ve göllerden elde ediyor. Bu sürekli kirlenmeyi önlemek için birçok yerde atık su arıtma tesisleri inşa ediliyor. Bu tesisler, kanalizasyon suyunu saf ve içilebilir suya dönüştürebiliyor.

Tatlı su sorununu çözmenin bir başka yolu da sahip olduğumuz en bol su kaynağından, yani denizden yararlanmaktır. Deniz suyundan kolay ve ucuz bir şekilde içilebilir su elde etmeyi öğrenebilsek, sorunu çözmüş olurduk. İnsan, içinde başta tuz olmak üzere yüksek oranda mineral bulunduğu için doğrudan deniz suyuyla yaşayamaz. Bir çözeltide yüzde 2'den fazla tuz bulunması insan vücudu için tehlikelidir. Deniz suyu yüzde 3,5 oranında tuz içerir. Bu kadar yüksek bir miktar insan vücudunda dehidrasyona, yani vücudun yaşam için gerekli sıvıları kaybetmesine neden olur. Bu nedenle, deniz suyunu kullanmadan önce içindeki tuz oranını kabul edilebilir bir düzeye düşürmek gerekir. Bunu yapmak için çeşitli yöntemler kullanılabilir. En yaygın yöntem damıtmadır. Deniz suyu, su buharlaşana ve tuz geride kalana kadar ısıtılır. Ardından buhar yoğunlaşarak saf suya dönüşür. Bir diğer yöntem dondurmadır. Bu işlem yapıldığında önce su donar ve tuzu geride bırakır. Daha sonra buz çıkarılır ve saf su elde edilir. Üçüncü bir yönteme ise ters ozmoz denir. Saf su molekülleri, yüksek basınç altında tuz moleküllerinden ayrılır.

Son zamanlarda bilim insanları tamamen yeni bir fikir üzerinde çalışıyor: havadan tatlı su elde etme fikri. Denizden esen rüzgârlar çok miktarda su buharı taşır. Bu buhar soğuk bir şeye çarptığında yoğunlaşarak suya dönüşür. Bilim insanları büyük bir yoğunlaştırıcı inşa edebilirlerse tatlı suyu kolayca toplayıp depolayabilirler. Ne yazık ki bahsedilen tüm yöntemlerin temel sorunu maliyetlerinin yüksek olmasıdır. Bu nedenle bilim insanları maliyeti düşürmenin yollarını aramaktadır.

passages.passage_text:
Minerals are substances which are crystalline solids and which occur naturally. There are more than twenty different minerals in the body. Three of the most important minerals are calcium, phosphorus, and iron. Calcium and phosphorus work together. The bony skeletons of vertebrate animals, including man, are composed of calcium phosphate. If people have enough calcium and phosphorus, their bones and teeth will be strong and hard. In addition, their muscles, nerves, and heart will work properly. Calcium makes up about 2% of the human body. About 99% of that amount is contained in the teeth and bones. Milk and hard cheeses are the best sources of calcium. After the age of 19, people need only 400 to 500 milligrams of calcium a day. Phosphorus, on the other hand, makes up 1.1% of the human body. A number of high-energy compounds found in our bodies, such as adenosine triphosphate (ATP), contain phosphorus. ATP is capable of transferring as well as storing energy in living cells and is responsible for energy necessary for physical activity.

Iron is a mineral which makes the blood look red and which carries oxygen for our normal physical activities. All lean meats - especially liver - whole grains, nuts, some vegetables, and dried fruits are good sources of this mineral. Iron deficiency results in a disease called anemia. Anemic people do not have enough iron in their blood, and this causes their hearts to beat faster so that their bodies can get more oxygen. Such people, therefore, get tired easily, and their skins sometimes look rather white.

In my opinion, people should try to get their essential minerals from natural foods rather than relying on pills and supplements. passages.tts_script_tr:
Mineraller.

Mineraller, kristal katı hâlde olan ve doğal olarak bulunan maddelerdir. Vücutta yirmiden fazla farklı mineral vardır. En önemli minerallerden üçü kalsiyum, fosfor ve demirdir. Kalsiyum ve fosfor birlikte çalışır. İnsan da dâhil olmak üzere omurgalı hayvanların kemikli iskeletleri kalsiyum fosfattan oluşur. İnsanlar yeterli kalsiyum ve fosfora sahip olursa kemikleri ve dişleri güçlü ve sert olur. Ayrıca kasları, sinirleri ve kalbi düzgün çalışır. Kalsiyum, insan vücudunun yaklaşık yüzde 2'sini oluşturur. Bu miktarın yaklaşık yüzde 99'u dişlerde ve kemiklerde bulunur. Süt ve sert peynirler en iyi kalsiyum kaynaklarıdır. 19 yaşından sonra insanların günde yalnızca 400 ila 500 miligram kalsiyuma ihtiyacı vardır. Fosfor ise insan vücudunun yüzde 1,1'ini oluşturur. Vücudumuzda bulunan adenozin trifosfat veya ATP gibi bir dizi yüksek enerjili bileşik fosfor içerir. ATP, canlı hücrelerde enerjiyi depolamanın yanı sıra aktarma yeteneğine de sahiptir ve fiziksel aktivite için gerekli enerjiden sorumludur.
