passages.passage_text:
One of those misunderstandings which sometimes occurs when the gasman comes to call has brought puzzlement and ultimate good fortune into the domestic lives of two Essex women. Mrs. May Bradbrook and Mrs. Brenda Kerr live in Alton Gardens, Westcliff-on-Sea. Mrs. Bradbrook's home is number 40 and the Kerr residence is number 14. The difficulties began when Mrs. Bradbrook decided that the time had come to purchase a new cooker. She placed her order with the North Thames Gas Board, but the official who took the details misheard her address.

Paperwork duly went through for the delivery and installation of a new gas cooker at number 14, Alton Gardens. When the gasmen arrived with it, there was nobody at home. They were relieved, however, to find a considerate note saying, "Key next door." Mrs. Kerr was expecting a visit from the Eastern Electricity Board that day and had made arrangements for a neighbour to let them in. When the gas board appeared instead, the neighbour assumed that she had misunderstood Mrs. Kerr and handed over the key. The new cooker was installed and Mrs. Kerr's old one taken away.

Shortly afterwards, an aggrieved Mrs. Bradbrook telephoned the gas board saying that she had waited in all day but the cooker had not come. Inquiries were started. Meanwhile, Mrs. Kerr got home to find the unexpected and gleaming appliance in her kitchen. Clearly, something was amiss but before Mrs. Kerr could get down to deciding how to sort it out, she had an urgent priority. She had to cook her husband's tea. There was no other appliance in the house, so she used the new cooker.

The board, having heard from Mrs. Bradbrook and contacted its gasmen, was swift to realise the error. It assured Mrs. Bradbrook that there would be no further delay in getting the cooker to her. After all, it had only to travel a short way up the road.

But - Mrs. Bradbrook pointed out - it was no longer the new cooker she had ordered, was it? It had been used. The gas board saw her point and found that it also had a problem at number 14. It had assured Mrs. Kerr that her old cooker would be returned pronto. But it turned out that the cooker had been broken up for scrap immediately after it was taken away.

Both women had clearly suffered 'some inconvenience,' as the board acknowledged. The upshot of the affair is that Mrs. Bradbrook now has the cooker originally intended for her, but at a 20 per cent discount of £30. Mrs. Kerr has been given a reconditioned "good as new" cooker worth an estimated £350 to replace her scrapped one. And the North Thames Gas Board is some £380 out of pocket.

task2.model_answer:
When a company makes an administrative mistake that disrupts customers' daily lives, it has both a moral and a practical responsibility to compensate them fairly. In the case of Mrs. Bradbrook and Mrs. Kerr, the gas board's error wasted one woman's entire day and left the other without her original appliance. Although the financial loss of £380 was inconvenient for the company, offering a discount and a replacement was the right decision.

Fair compensation is essential because it restores customer trust. People rarely judge a service solely on whether everything goes smoothly; rather, they remember how the organisation responds when something goes wrong. If the gas board had refused to acknowledge Mrs. Bradbrook's objection or failed to replace Mrs. Kerr's scrapped cooker, both women would have been left frustrated and unlikely to recommend the service.

Of course, companies must verify legitimate complaints to prevent abuse, yet clear mistakes deserve swift, generous solutions. Ultimately, taking responsibility protects a company's reputation far more effectively than trying to save a small sum of money.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Bir Yanlış Anlama.

Bazen gaz görevlisi eve geldiğinde yaşanan o yanlış anlamalardan biri, Essexli iki kadının ev hayatına önce şaşkınlık, ardından da büyük bir şans getirdi. Bayan May Bradbrook ve Bayan Brenda Kerr, Westcliff-on-Sea'deki Alton Gardens'ta yaşıyor. Bayan Bradbrook'un evi 40 numara, Kerr ailesinin evi ise 14 numara. Sorunlar, Bayan Bradbrook'un yeni bir ocak alma zamanının geldiğine karar vermesiyle başladı. Siparişini North Thames Gaz İdaresi'ne verdi ancak bilgileri alan görevli adresini yanlış duydu.

Alton Gardens 14 numaraya yeni bir gazlı ocağın teslimatı ve kurulumu için evrak işleri usulünce tamamlandı. Gaz görevlileri ocakla geldiklerinde evde kimse yoktu. Ancak, "Anahtar yan komşuda." yazan düşünceli bir not bulunca rahatladılar. Bayan Kerr o gün Eastern Elektrik İdaresi'nden bir ziyaret bekliyordu ve onları içeri alması için bir komşusuyla anlaşmıştı. Onların yerine gaz idaresi gelince komşu, Bayan Kerr'i yanlış anladığını varsayıp anahtarı teslim etti. Yeni ocak kuruldu ve Bayan Kerr'in eski ocağı götürüldü.

Kısa bir süre sonra mağdur durumdaki Bayan Bradbrook gaz idaresini arayarak bütün gün evde beklediğini ancak ocağın gelmediğini söyledi. Araştırma başlatıldı. Bu sırada Bayan Kerr eve döndüğünde mutfağında beklenmedik, pırıl pırıl parlayan cihazı buldu. Açıkça bir terslik vardı ama Bayan Kerr bunu nasıl çözeceğine karar vermeye koyulamadan önce acil bir önceliği vardı. Kocasının akşam yemeğini pişirmesi gerekiyordu. Evde başka hiçbir cihaz yoktu, bu yüzden yeni ocağı kullandı.

Bayan Bradbrook'tan durumu öğrenen ve görevlileriyle iletişime geçen idare, hatayı çabucak fark etti. Bayan Bradbrook'a, ocağın kendisine ulaştırılmasında daha fazla gecikme olmayacağına dair güvence verdi. Ne de olsa ocağın yolun yalnızca biraz ilerisine gitmesi gerekiyordu.

Ancak Bayan Bradbrook, bunun artık sipariş ettiği yeni ocak olmadığını vurguladı, öyle değil mi? Kullanılmıştı. Gaz idaresi ona hak verdi ve 14 numarada da bir sorun olduğunu fark etti. Bayan Kerr'e eski ocağının derhâl geri getirileceğine dair güvence vermişti. Fakat ocağın, götürülür götürülmez hurda olarak parçalandığı ortaya çıktı.

İdarenin de kabul ettiği gibi, her iki kadın da açıkça 'biraz zahmet' çekmişti. Meselenin sonucu şu ki, Bayan Bradbrook artık başlangıçta kendisi için ayrılan ocağa sahip, üstelik 30 sterlinlik yüzde 20 indirimle. Bayan Kerr'e ise hurdaya çıkarılan ocağının yerine tahmini değeri 350 sterlin olan, yenilenmiş, "yeni gibi" bir ocak verildi. Ve North Thames Gaz İdaresi yaklaşık 380 sterlin zarara uğramış oldu.

passages.passage_text:
22-year-old Angela Medeiros was one of the lucky ones. She survived the blazing inferno that ravaged the forty-storey Torres building in downtown Sao Paolo yesterday. At least thirty people are known to have lost their lives in the fire that raged for over twelve hours. The final count is expected to be far higher as desperate relatives try to locate missing members of their families.

Angela was indeed lucky to survive. She worked on the twentieth floor, just three floors above where the fire is believed to have started as a result of an electrical fault in an air-conditioner.

Her first impression that something was wrong was when she saw a column of thick black smoke rising past the window of her office. "There was no sound of an alarm or anything," she said. "Just the cries of people screaming and running all over the place. It was terrible. My first thought was to cover myself with water, and I rushed to the bathroom. It was a very strange reaction. When I came out there was no one in the office; I was the only one there."

What followed was a nightmare. She tried to get to the emergency staircase, but by this time the smoke was too thick and she knew that she could either stay where she was or make an attempt to reach the roof, twenty floors above, where there was a helicopter landing-pad. She decided to stay where she was and managed to open a window and struggle out onto a ledge. It was then that she realised that she was probably safe. The fire had passed through her floor and although flames were everywhere, she could at least breathe. Her instinct told her to stay where she was and wait for rescue. "Somewhere I had read that the new ladders on the fire engines could be extended to reach the twentieth floor," she explained. "I hoped it was true!"

What happened over the next seven hours defies description. She witnessed people desperately throwing themselves out of the windows of the floors above her. She admits that she was tempted to do the same. She was afraid that no one would see her and that she would not be able to hold on. "I just prayed, and thought of my mother and father and the family, and about the holiday we were going to have in two weeks' time."

She was rescued after someone in the crowd below alerted firemen to the small figure huddled against a ledge in a corner of the twentieth storey. "I saw the ladder moving up towards me," said Angela, "but I must have lost consciousness, because that's the last thing I remember. The next thing I recall was waking up in the ambulance."

task1.model_answer: Angela Medeiros, a 22-year-old office worker, narrowly survived a devastating fire in the forty-storey Torres building in Sao Paolo, which claimed at least thirty lives. Working on the twentieth floor—just three floors above the electrical fault that started the blaze—she first noticed thick smoke outside her window and panicked cries, with no alarm sounding. After wetting herself in the bathroom, she found her colleagues gone and the emergency stairs blocked by dense smoke. task2.model_answer:
Angela Medeiros's harrowing escape highlights how dangerous high-rise buildings can become when fire safety systems fail. Because no alarm sounded in the Torres building, employees lost precious minutes before noticing the smoke, and thick fumes quickly cut off the emergency staircase. To prevent similar tragedies, strict safety regulations in tall buildings are essential.

First, every floor of a high-rise must be equipped with reliable smoke detectors, automatic sprinklers, and loud alarms that activate immediately. Early warnings allow people to evacuate before stairwells become impassable. Second, buildings should have pressurised, smoke-free emergency staircases and clearly marked refuge areas so occupants are not forced onto dangerous ledges. Regular evacuation drills are equally vital, as panic often leads people to react unpredictably in a crisis.

While modern fire engines have impressive ladders, rescue services cannot reach every victim during a massive fire. Ultimately, rigorous building codes and routine maintenance save far more lives than last-minute rescues.

passages.passage_text:
Pirkko Mononen's father, aged 59, died of a heart attack. He was one of nine children from a farming family; seven of them died the same way. Pirkko's husband, Heikki, knows how she feels. His father and mother had heart trouble and for both of them the third attack was fatal.

Their case is not unusual for Pirkko and Heikki, aged 46 and 47. They live in Finland, where the death rate from heart disease used to be the highest in the world. Not any more, though, as Scotland and Northern Ireland have taken over the lead.

The Mononens took part in a novel experiment. Their blood cholesterol levels were measured. They and 29 other families in their village then swapped their diet for the fresh vegetables and low saturated fat intake of an Italian community in the south of Naples.

The experiment changed their eating habits. It was part of a long-term state programme backed by the World Health Organisation. In 1971, MPs presented a petition from local people begging the government to do something about the alarming number of middle-aged men dying prematurely from heart attacks. At the start of the project, there were about 250 fatal attacks in the area each year. Today, that number has been reduced by about 100. An initial survey had showed smoking and diet to be the key factors. Sour and salty flavours were popular, meals were large, and milk was drunk at the table instead of water, wine or beer.

The Finland-Italy experiment caught people's imagination. Pirkko laughs when she confesses they ate no spaghetti over the six-week trial. "I prepared all kinds of Finnish traditional dishes, but I used vegetable fat instead of lard." The couple won a free trip to Pollica, the village chosen for the other half of the experiment, and saw a big difference. "The Italians used the fat on meat to make soap instead of eating it as they do here," said Heikki. His cholesterol level almost halved during the trial. Now, they have switched to low-fat milk - in spite of keeping a herd of dairy cows - and grow their own vegetables.

In the last ten years, people have been cleverly persuaded not to eat high-fat food. Housewives were taught new methods of food preparation, and special 'Long Life Parties' were organised where families would eat together. Between 1969 and 1979, deaths among middle-aged men in the area fell by 27%.

task1.model_answer: Alarmed by high rates of fatal heart attacks in Finland, where families like Pirkko and Heikki Mononen's lost many relatives prematurely, residents petitioned the government in 1971 for action. Backed by the World Health Organisation, a long-term health programme launched a six-week experiment in which 30 village families adopted the low-saturated-fat, vegetable-rich diet of an Italian town. Instead of abandoning local meals, participants adapted traditional Finnish recipes by replacing lard with vegetable fat. The results were dramatic: Heikki's cholesterol nearly halved, and the couple permanently switched to low-fat milk and home-grown vegetables. Combined with cooking education and community events, the campaign helped cut fatal heart attacks among middle-aged men by 27 percent between 1969 and 1979.

task1.title: Summary: Finland's Heart-Healthy Diet Experiment

task2.model_answer:
Preventing diet-related illnesses requires cooperation between governments and individuals, as neither side can succeed alone. While personal choices ultimately determine what ends up on our plates, public health campaigns create the knowledge and social support needed to sustain healthier lifestyles.

In the Finnish case, citizens themselves requested help after watching loved ones die prematurely. Without government backing, reliable cholesterol testing, cooking classes, and community events like 'Long Life Parties' would have been far harder to organise. Public programmes can also encourage food producers to offer healthier alternatives, making good choices more accessible and affordable.

Nevertheless, official policies fail unless people actively adapt them to daily life. Pirkko Mononen demonstrated this by keeping her family's traditional Finnish recipes while simply replacing lard with vegetable fat. When healthy habits respect local culture rather than forcing completely unfamiliar diets, people are much more likely to stick with them.

In conclusion, governments should provide education, medical guidance, and supportive environments, while individuals must take responsibility for applying those lessons at home.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Yedikleri Bir Şey Yüzünden miydi?

Pirkko Mononen'in babası 59 yaşında kalp krizinden öldü. Çiftçi bir ailenin dokuz çocuğundan biriydi; yedisi aynı şekilde hayatını kaybetti. Pirkko'nun kocası Heikki onun nasıl hissettiğini biliyor. Onun anne ve babası da kalp rahatsızlığı yaşıyordu ve ikisi için de üçüncü kriz ölümcül oldu.

46 ve 47 yaşlarındaki Pirkko ve Heikki için bu durum sıra dışı değil. Kalp hastalığından kaynaklanan ölüm oranının bir zamanlar dünyada en yüksek olduğu Finlandiya'da yaşıyorlar. Ancak artık öyle değil, çünkü İskoçya ve Kuzey İrlanda liderliği devralmış durumda.

Mononen çifti yenilikçi bir deneye katıldı. Kan kolesterol seviyeleri ölçüldü. Ardından onlar ve köylerindeki diğer 29 aile, beslenme düzenlerini Napoli'nin güneyindeki bir İtalyan topluluğunun taze sebzelerden ve düşük doymuş yağ alımından oluşan beslenme düzeniyle değiştirdiler.

Deney onların yeme alışkanlıklarını değiştirdi. Bu, Dünya Sağlık Örgütü tarafından desteklenen uzun vadeli bir devlet programının parçasıydı. 1971 yılında milletvekilleri, kalp krizinden erken yaşta ölen orta yaşlı erkeklerin endişe verici sayısına karşı hükümetten bir şeyler yapmasını isteyen bölge halkının dilekçesini sundu. Projenin başlangıcında bölgede her yıl yaklaşık 250 ölümcül kriz yaşanıyordu. Bugün bu sayı yaklaşık 100 azaltılmış durumda. İlk yapılan bir anket, sigara ve beslenmenin temel etkenler olduğunu göstermişti. Ekşi ve tuzlu tatlar popülerdi, öğünler büyüktü ve sofrada su, şarap veya bira yerine süt içiliyordu.

Finlandiya-İtalya deneyi insanların hayal gücünü yakaladı. Pirkko, altı haftalık deneme boyunca hiç spagetti yemediklerini itiraf ederken gülüyor. "Her türlü geleneksel Fin yemeğini hazırladım ama domuz yağı yerine bitkisel yağ kullandım." Çift, deneyin diğer yarısı için seçilen Pollica köyüne ücretsiz bir gezi kazandı ve büyük bir fark gördü. "İtalyanlar etin üzerindeki yağı bizim buradaki gibi yemek yerine sabun yapmak için kullanıyordu," dedi Heikki. Deneme sırasında kolesterol seviyesi neredeyse yarıya düştü. Şimdi ise bir süt ineği sürüsü beslemelerine rağmen az yağlı süte geçtiler ve kendi sebzelerini yetiştiriyorlar.

Son on yılda insanlar yüksek yağlı yiyecekler yememeye ustaca ikna edildi. Ev hanımlarına yeni yemek hazırlama yöntemleri öğretildi ve ailelerin birlikte yemek yediği özel 'Uzun Ömür Partileri' düzenlendi. 1969 ile 1979 yılları arasında bölgedeki orta yaşlı erkekler arasındaki ölümler yüzde 27 oranında düştü.

passages.passage_text:
In historical times, many societies operated a two-tier (a tier is a level in a system or organisation) system made up of people who controlled and those who worked and were controlled. Work was not an activity to be enjoyed. However, another group of people emerged alongside this system. They were the merchants and artisans. Merchants worked for profit, and artisans (people skilled in arts and crafts) worked for wages. These were the people who first gave us the idea of work as paid employment.

Today, people need to work in the same way they need to eat and drink. This is what we call the 'work ethic'. (An ethic is an idea or moral belief that influences the behaviour, attitudes and philosophy of life of a group of people.) People work for the money they need in order to live well, but there is another reason beyond this basic motivation which makes people want to work. Work gives people a feeling of being useful.

In a pre-industrial society, the work ethic did not exist. Work and leisure went together and only part of Sunday was taken as time off. In this society, singing, talking, drinking and gossiping went together with work. With the emergence of the work ethic, leisure and holidays were separated from work, thus changing the former ordinary social system of interaction. During the Industrial Revolution, for most people, work was so unpleasant that leisure was considered as a kind of freedom. Yet, in spite of the fact that life was hard and work was tiring, people slowly changed from having to work to wanting to work. Today, the work ethic is so strong that people feel it is their right to work.

The questions we should perhaps be asking ourselves are, firstly, whether we really like our jobs and secondly, even if we like them, whether they are really necessary. Many kinds of work are disappearing as natural resources are used up and new technologies appear. For example, computers are already replacing people in order to do boring, repetitive jobs and to improve efficiency. To a large extent, the price of labour, as compared with the cost of the new equipment, determines which jobs will be replaced. However, the new technologies will create new jobs both in the computer field and in the leisure industry.

It has been predicted that new technology could result in a period of growth and prosperity. This, however, does not mean that the ever-growing number of unemployed people will drop. What it means is that finance and resources will become available to improve social services, education and the health service. The quality of life can be improved with better facilities and a significant increase in the workforce behind the services.

It has taken more than a hundred years to reduce the working week from 60 to 55 hours, then 48, 44 and now 40. The next step will be a reduction to 35 and then, perhaps, to 32 hours. The current five-day working week will become a four-day or even a three-day event. In order to achieve this shortened working span, paid holidays will probably be increased and the age of retirement will be lowered. However, attitudes to work must change as well. Community life ought to become more important and the leisure industry needs to be expanded to cater for the needs of both young and old people, all of whom will have more spare time. In Europe, only France has taken this problem seriously enough to appoint a government official responsible for 'free-time'.

Making changes in the education system could solve a lot of problems. In fact, creativity and sensibility could start a totally new period, perhaps a new 'Working Renaissance'.

task1.model_answer: The idea of work has changed significantly over time. Originally, merchants and artisans introduced paid employment, while in pre-industrial societies work and social leisure were closely combined. During the Industrial Revolution, work became harsh and separate from free time, yet a strong work ethic eventually developed, leading modern people to view work as both a necessity and a right. Today, new technologies are replacing repetitive jobs, which may increase prosperity and fund better public services without necessarily reducing unemployment. As working hours continue to shrink and retirement ages drop, societies must expand leisure industries, strengthen community life, and reform education to create a healthier balance between work and free time.

task2.model_answer:
Reducing the standard working week to four days or fewer could bring substantial benefits to both workers and society, provided that economic and social systems adapt alongside it. First, shorter working hours give employees more time for rest, family, and community engagement, which can lower stress and improve overall mental health. When workers feel less exhausted, they are often more focused and productive during the hours they spend on the job.

However, a shorter working week also presents challenges. If wages are cut in proportion to hours, many families could struggle financially. Similarly, as the passage notes, people derive a sense of usefulness from their jobs, so having too much unstructured free time without strong community or educational programmes could lead to boredom or isolation.

In conclusion, shrinking the working week is a positive step forward if governments and employers maintain fair pay and invest in leisure, lifelong learning, and community services so everyone can use their extra time meaningfully.

Çalışma Rönesansına Doğru.

Tarihsel dönemlerde pek çok toplum, kontrol edenler ile çalışıp kontrol edilenlerden oluşan iki kademeli (kademe, bir sistem veya organizasyondaki bir düzeydir) bir sistem uyguluyordu. Çalışmak keyif alınacak bir etkinlik değildi. Ancak bu sistemin yanında başka bir insan grubu ortaya çıktı. Bunlar tüccarlar ve zanaatkârlardı. Tüccarlar kâr için, zanaatkârlar (sanat ve el sanatlarında usta kişiler) ise ücret karşılığında çalışıyordu. Ücretli istihdam olarak çalışma fikrini bize ilk kazandıranlar bu insanlardı.

Günümüzde insanların tıpkı yemek yemeye ve su içmeye ihtiyaç duydukları gibi çalışmaya da ihtiyaçları vardır. İşte buna 'iş etiği' diyoruz. (Etik, bir grup insanın davranışlarını, tutumlarını ve yaşam felsefesini etkileyen bir fikir veya ahlaki inançtır.) İnsanlar iyi yaşamak için ihtiyaç duydukları para için çalışırlar; ancak bu temel motivasyonun ötesinde insanların çalışmak istemesini sağlayan başka bir neden daha vardır. Çalışmak insanlara işe yarama duygusu verir.

Sanayi öncesi bir toplumda iş etiği yoktu. Çalışma ve boş zaman iç içeydi ve yalnızca pazar gününün bir bölümü izin olarak kullanılırdı. Bu toplumda şarkı söylemek, sohbet etmek, içki içmek ve dedikodu yapmak işle birlikte yürürdü. İş etiğinin ortaya çıkmasıyla boş zaman ve tatiller işten ayrıldı; böylece önceki olağan toplumsal etkileşim düzeni değişti. Sanayi Devrimi sırasında çoğu insan için çalışmak o kadar tatsızdı ki boş zaman bir tür özgürlük olarak görülüyordu. Yine de hayatın zor ve işin yorucu olmasına rağmen insanlar yavaş yavaş çalışmak zorunda olmaktan çalışmak istemeye doğru değişti. Günümüzde iş etiği o kadar güçlüdür ki insanlar çalışmanın kendi hakları olduğunu hissederler.

Belki de kendimize sormamız gereken sorular şunlardır: İlk olarak, işimizi gerçekten sevip sevmediğimiz; ikinci olarak da, sevsek bile bu işlerin gerçekten gerekli olup olmadığı. Doğal kaynaklar tükendikçe ve yeni teknolojiler ortaya çıktıkça pek çok iş türü ortadan kalkıyor. Örneğin, sıkıcı ve tekrarlayıcı işleri yapmak ve verimliliği artırmak için bilgisayarlar şimdiden insanların yerini alıyor. Yeni ekipmanın maliyetine kıyasla iş gücünün bedeli, hangi işlerin yerinin doldurulacağını büyük ölçüde belirlemektedir. Bununla birlikte yeni teknolojiler hem bilgisayar alanında hem de eğlence ve dinlence sektöründe yeni işler yaratacaktır.

Yeni teknolojinin bir büyüme ve refah dönemiyle sonuçlanabileceği öngörülmektedir. Ancak bu, giderek artan işsiz sayısının düşeceği anlamına gelmez. Bunun anlamı, sosyal hizmetleri, eğitimi ve sağlık hizmetlerini iyileştirmek için finansman ve kaynakların erişilebilir hale geleceğidir. Daha iyi imkânlar ve bu hizmetlerin arkasındaki iş gücünde önemli bir artışla yaşam kalitesi yükseltilebilir.

Haftalık çalışma süresini 60 saatten 55'e, ardından 48'e, 44'e ve şimdi 40 saate indirmek yüz yıldan fazla sürmüştür. Bir sonraki adım 35 saate ve ardından belki de 32 saate düşürmek olacaktır. Mevcut beş günlük çalışma haftası dört günlük, hatta üç günlük bir düzene dönüşecektir. Bu kısalmış çalışma süresine ulaşmak için muhtemelen ücretli tatiller artırılacak ve emeklilik yaşı düşürülecektir. Ancak çalışmaya yönelik tutumların da değişmesi gerekir. Topluluk yaşamı daha önemli hale gelmeli ve boş zaman sektörü, hepsi daha fazla serbest zamana sahip olacak hem gençlerin hem de yaşlıların ihtiyaçlarını karşılayacak şekilde genişletilmelidir. Avrupa'da yalnızca Fransa bu sorunu 'boş zamandan' sorumlu bir hükümet yetkilisi atayacak kadar ciddiye almıştır.

Eğitim sisteminde değişiklikler yapmak pek çok sorunu çözebilir. Hatta yaratıcılık ve duyarlılık tamamen yeni bir dönem, belki de yeni bir 'Çalışma Rönesansı' başlatabilir.

passages.passage_text:
Every community in the world recognises certain activities as crimes. Because of this, each has developed its own way of dealing with crimes and has chosen a number of different punishments to match them. So, society identifies crimes, administers justice, and then imposes suitable punishments.

It is surprising, however, how much the various societies of the world differ in the areas of crime, justice and punishment. What may be a crime in one country is often perfectly acceptable in another. For example, as you may know, jaywalking, that is, not crossing the road at the proper crossing place, is illegal in areas of the world such as North America, but in other areas, quite legal. As well as deciding what is legal and what is illegal, societies must also decide whether a crime is petty or serious. For example, carrying a gun is a very serious offence in some countries, but a very petty one in others.

Similarly, the ways of administering justice differ from country to country. In some countries a person is considered innocent until he is proved guilty, but in others the opposite is true. In other words, in the former it is the job of the authorities to prove that the person has committed a crime whereas in the latter it is the individual's task to prove his innocence.

Crimes vary, systems of justice vary, but the greatest variation between countries is in the methods of punishment that they use. For example, a person convicted of theft in some parts of the Middle East might face a severe penalty, whereas the same crime would receive a relatively lenient punishment in some Scandinavian countries. Denmark provides a good example of the more lenient approach to crime and punishment. About half the people sent to prison there go to what is called an 'open prison'. In these prisons, the inmates are allowed to wear their own clothes, provide their own food, bring in their own furniture and have their own radios or television in the cell.

They are not locked in their cells at night, although each prisoner is given a key to his own cell and can lock the door at night if he wishes. Most open prisons in Denmark also have special rooms where prisoners can entertain friends, husbands or wives unsupervised, in privacy and comfort, for at least an hour a week.

After four weeks in a Danish open prison, a prisoner is normally entitled to a 'holiday' outside the prison. Usually he is allowed out of prison for one weekend every three weeks. Of course, prisoners do not have to leave the prison every three weeks - they can save up their weekends away and take a break of up to eight days if they prefer.

Prisoners in open prisons in Denmark are also allowed out for a whole range of activities such as buying clothes, visiting the doctor or simply going for a walk with their visitors. If a prisoner needs to leave the prison for educational purposes - attending a course or receiving technical training - then, in certain circumstances, he may be allowed to spend the night outside the prison.

task1.model_answer: Societies around the world vary greatly in how they define crimes, run their justice systems, and punish offenders. An action that is illegal in one country, such as jaywalking or carrying a gun, may be minor or legal elsewhere. Countries also differ on whether the authorities must prove guilt or the accused must prove innocence. The sharpest contrast, however, lies in punishment. While theft can carry severe penalties in some regions, Denmark adopts a much more lenient model. task2.model_answer:
Lenient prison systems, such as Denmark's open prisons, can be highly effective at rehabilitating offenders, though they may not suit every type of criminal. When inmates are allowed to wear regular clothes, maintain family relationships, and attend educational courses, they retain a sense of dignity and normal social habits. As a result, they are far better prepared to re-enter society and find honest employment after their release, which reduces the likelihood of reoffending.

On the other hand, lenient approaches require careful screening. Violent or repeat offenders who pose an immediate danger to the public still need strict supervision in secure facilities to protect citizens and maintain trust in the justice system.

Overall, while serious violent crimes demand firmer restrictions, open and rehabilitative prisons offer a smarter, more humane solution for non-violent offenders, turning punishment into an opportunity for genuine reform.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Suçlar.

Dünyadaki her topluluk belirli eylemleri suç olarak kabul eder. Bu nedenle her biri suçlarla başa çıkmak için kendi yöntemini geliştirmiş ve bunlara karşılık gelecek çeşitli cezalar belirlemiştir. Yani toplum suçları tanımlar, adaleti uygular ve ardından uygun cezalar verir.

Ancak dünyadaki farklı toplumların suç, adalet ve ceza alanlarında ne kadar farklılaştığı şaşırtıcıdır. Bir ülkede suç olabilen bir şey başka bir ülkede çoğu zaman tamamen kabul edilebilir olabilmektedir. Örneğin bildiğiniz gibi, kurallara aykırı şekilde karşıdan karşıya geçmek, yani yolu uygun yaya geçidinden geçmemek Kuzey Amerika gibi dünyanın bazı bölgelerinde yasa dışıdır, ancak diğer bölgelerde tamamen yasaldır. Toplumlar neyin yasal neyin yasa dışı olduğuna karar vermenin yanı sıra bir suçun hafif mi yoksa ağır mı olduğuna da karar vermek zorundadır. Örneğin silah taşımak bazı ülkelerde çok ağır bir suçken bazılarında çok hafif bir suçtur.

Benzer şekilde adaleti uygulama yolları da ülkeden ülkeye değişir. Bazı ülkelerde bir kişi suçu kanıtlanana kadar masum kabul edilir, ancak diğerlerinde bunun tam tersi geçerlidir. Başka bir deyişle, ilkinde kişinin suç işlediğini kanıtlamak yetkililerin görevidir; oysa ikincisinde masumiyetini kanıtlamak bireyin kendi görevidir.

Suçlar çeşitlilik gösterir, adalet sistemleri çeşitlilik gösterir; ancak ülkeler arasındaki en büyük farklılık kullandıkları ceza yöntemlerindedir. Örneğin Orta Doğu'nun bazı bölgelerinde hırsızlıktan hüküm giyen bir kişi ağır bir cezayla karşılaşabilirken, aynı suç bazı İskandinav ülkelerinde nispeten hafif bir ceza alabilir. Danimarka, suç ve cezaya yönelik daha hoşgörülü yaklaşımın iyi bir örneğini sunar. Orada hapse gönderilen kişilerin yaklaşık yarısı 'açık cezaevi' olarak adlandırılan yerlere gider. Bu cezaevlerinde mahkûmların kendi kıyafetlerini giymelerine, kendi yiyeceklerini temin etmelerine, kendi mobilyalarını getirmelerine ve hücrelerinde kendi radyo veya televizyonlarını bulundurmalarına izin verilir.

Her mahkûma kendi hücresinin anahtarı verilse ve isterse gece kapıyı kilitleyebilse de, geceleri hücrelerine kilitlenmezler. Danimarka'daki açık cezaevlerinin çoğunda ayrıca mahkûmların haftada en az bir saat boyunca arkadaşlarını, kocalarını veya karılarını gözetimsiz, mahremiyet ve rahatlık içinde ağırlayabilecekleri özel odalar vardır.

Bir Danimarka açık cezaevinde dört hafta geçirdikten sonra bir mahkûm normalde cezaevi dışında bir 'tatil' hakkı kazanır. Genellikle üç haftada bir hafta sonu cezaevinden çıkmasına izin verilir. Elbette mahkûmlar her üç haftada bir cezaevinden çıkmak zorunda değildir; tercih ederlerse dışarıdaki hafta sonlarını biriktirip sekiz güne kadar izin kullanabilirler.

Danimarka'daki açık cezaevlerindeki mahkûmların kıyafet satın almak, doktora gitmek veya yalnızca ziyaretçileriyle yürüyüşe çıkmak gibi pek çok etkinlik için de dışarı çıkmalarına izin verilir. Bir mahkûmun eğitim amacıyla —bir kursa katılmak veya teknik eğitim almak için— cezaevinden ayrılması gerekirse, belirli koşullar altında geceyi cezaevi dışında geçirmesine izin verilebilir.

John Cheetham's magnificent obsession with reptiles began when he was a schoolboy in his hometown of Oldham, Lancashire.

A glimpse from the top of a bus of alligators basking in the sun at Manchester's famous Belle Vue Zoo set his imagination racing. He took every opportunity of visiting the zoo, and the more he saw of the creatures that seemed to have stepped out of the remote past, the more his fascination grew, until it embraced all reptiles. When he was 11, he bought a baby alligator from a local pet shop. It was the first step to becoming the only private collector of giant reptiles in Britain. It was also to lead to John's appearing with his own alligators and pythons in films and on television. And that same pet alligator is still with John, although he's grown a little during the 27 years they've been together. Big Boy, a magnificent specimen of Alligator mississippiensis, found in the southern states of North America, is now 10 ft. long and weighs 19 stone.

Big Boy and John have appeared with Roger Moore in Live and Let Die and Moonraker. Big Boy has also featured in Clash of the Titans and on TV advertisements. James Bond fans have seen quite a bit of John without realising it. It was his legs that did the spectacular dash to safety over the backs of alligators in Live and Let Die.

Among John's other pet reptiles to star in films are Aristotle, a 14-ft-long reticulated python aged six, and Pythagoras, a 14-ft Indian python who, at eighteen, is the grand old man among the snakes. Aristotle and Pythagoras both featured in the underwater wrestling scene in Moonraker with John in a friendly tussle, although the eventual result on film looks deadly serious.

John's collection also includes a giant tortoise, snapping turtles, the largest legless lizards or slowworms found in the world, and Nile crocodiles. Most of the giant reptiles in John's collection are housed at Beaver Water World, Tatsfield, which is owned by Jeff Wheeler, his friend and partner.

Collecting giant reptiles might seem a strange hobby for John, a teacher at Dorton House School for the Blind at Seal, near Sevenoaks. But John often introduces pupils to his pet snakes, letting them touch and hold them. John lets blind children and anyone else handle the pythons without any fear that they will attack. They are benign creatures. "All they want is a quiet life," he said.

task2.model_answer:
Keeping exotic animals such as giant reptiles as private pets or using them in entertainment is a controversial issue. While some collectors demonstrate genuine dedication and expertise, I believe strict regulations are necessary to protect both animal welfare and public safety.

On the one hand, experienced owners like John Cheetham show that exotic animals can receive proper care and even serve an educational purpose. When handled responsibly, reptiles can help people overcome common fears and learn more about wildlife conservation. In addition, filming with trained animals under safe conditions may seem harmless when the creatures are treated gently.

On the other hand, giant reptiles require specialized habitats, diets, and vast spaces that ordinary households cannot provide. When inexperienced owners buy exotic pets, the animals often suffer from neglect or are abandoned once they grow too large. Furthermore, film sets can expose wild creatures to bright lights, noise, and unnecessary stress.

In conclusion, private ownership and commercial use of exotic reptiles should only be permitted under strict licensing and regular inspections, ensuring that the animals' natural needs always come first.

passages.passage_text:
Below is the true story of Sue Usiskin, who suffers from epilepsy, a brain condition which causes a person suddenly to lose consciousness and sometimes to have violent fits.

Sue Usiskin was in a crowded Chinese restaurant with her family when she had an epileptic fit. Her husband Andrew helped her into a safe and comfortable position on the floor, held her hand while the fit lasted and, while she lay there recovering, he and the children started their meal. Then they settled her in a chair and carried on eating. "At first, everyone in the restaurant was absolutely horrified," laughs Sue. "Then, as we were leaving, a woman rushed over to congratulate Andrew on how naturally he had handled it all. She had realised that it must happen a lot."

Unfortunately for Sue, it does happen a lot. She is one of the 20% of sufferers from epilepsy whose fits cannot be completely controlled by drugs. She suffers at least three a month.

She is an inspiring example of someone who has not let epilepsy control her life. She has shared that inspiration in a new book, Living With Epilepsy, co-written with Dr. David Chadwick, consultant neurologist at Walton Hospital, Liverpool.

The indignity of, as she puts it, "collapsing on the ground in a noisy jerking heap" has long since ceased to worry her, although naturally it is never pleasant, but she has vivid memories of how, as a teenager, friends ran screaming from her when she had a fit in the playground at school. That she didn't lose all her self-confidence at that time is all due, she believes, to her parents. "They never tried to limit my activities because of what people might think if I had a fit and how it might affect me. On the contrary, I was encouraged to make an extra effort to overcome my difficulties and not allow them to become an excuse for doing less," she says.

"I tell people I am likely to see regularly that I suffer from epilepsy, and explain what they should do if I have a fit. I say, if I suddenly get up and lie on the ground, make sure I am away from anything I could hurt myself against, then stay with me and hold my hand. That makes them much more confident and comfortable."

She is adamant that children should be helped to understand what is going on and how to help right from the time they can crawl. "From a very early age, mine were used to seeing Andrew kneeling down with me, showing concern and protection. He always included them - he would encourage them to stroke my face. They soon knew what to do and they could do it right, if tearfully."

Her son, Oliver, is now 15 and Anna 12. "They are at the self-conscious stage and my fits must be an embarrassment to them. They have both gone through phases of being tense and anxious. But we have supported their feelings, whatever they are, and the fact that they are not frightened to voice them must be good."

She has always been very practical in her approach to coping. When the children were babies, she would never change them on the bed from where they might fall if she had a fit, or bath them if she were alone in the house with them. She uses casserole-style saucepans rather than long-handled ones which are easier to knock over. She chooses not to swim or ride or take escalators because she personally isn't comfortable about the risks. But she has never avoided going out for fear of what might happen.

Her own and her children's courage in that respect have been enormous. Once, when Oliver was two, she was dragged out of a taxi by the driver, who thought she was drunk, and was left to have a fit in the street in the pouring rain. On another occasion, she crumpled to the floor just inside a building society and the staff refused to come out and help because they thought she was a 'front' for a hold-up.

The children, when young, often had to try to dissuade onlookers in the street or shops from calling an ambulance, and Sue herself has often had to suffer having spoons thrust between her teeth to stop her biting her tongue (incorrect: only something soft, like the bunched edge of a towel, is suitable).

She is not bitter about such experiences, except where her children suffered, and looks back on many with humour. "This is my life and I've known no other for so long. I just get on and live it." But she is very keen to combat all the ignorance and prejudice. Once someone said to her that she must be very grateful to Andrew for marrying her and that shocked her. Conversely, she feels that doctors often over-estimate the quality of life that someone in her position can achieve. She regularly gives talks to medical students and GP trainees to give them a truer picture of epilepsy.

"I'm still terrified every time I have a fit," she says. "It is quite something to lose all control for three or four minutes. Believe me, it is a long time and I sometimes go unconscious after. It doesn't get easier. After a fit, it's like having a really heavy hang-over for the next two or three days. But there are positives, too. When you know what the rougher side of life can deal you, trivial things don't worry you at all. I never get upset if the washing machine breaks down."

task1.model_answer: Sue Usiskin lives with severe epilepsy that medication cannot fully control, causing at least three fits each month. Rather than letting the condition isolate her, she handles it openly with the support of her parents, her husband, and her children. She takes sensible precautions at home, such as using casserole-style saucepans and avoiding risky activities like swimming, while still going out regularly. Although she and her family have faced ignorance and mistaken first aid—from being mistaken for drunk or part of a robbery to having spoons forced into her mouth—Sue stays positive. task2.model_answer:
Chronic conditions such as epilepsy are often misunderstood by the general public, which can lead to unnecessary fear, embarrassment, and even dangerous first-aid mistakes. Educating society about these conditions is therefore essential for both safety and inclusion.

When people lack basic medical knowledge, they frequently misinterpret symptoms. As seen in Sue Usiskin's experience, onlookers may mistake a seizure for drunkenness or criminal behavior, leaving a vulnerable person without help. Even well-meaning bystanders can cause harm if they follow outdated myths, such as forcing hard objects between someone's teeth. Practical public awareness campaigns in schools, workplaces, and driving courses could replace panic with calm, effective assistance.

Equally important is reducing social stigma. When people understand what a condition involves, individuals living with chronic illnesses do not have to hide or feel ashamed in public spaces. Moreover, open communication from an early age helps children and families feel supported rather than isolated.

In conclusion, greater public education about invisible or misunderstood medical conditions protects people from physical harm and fosters a much more compassionate, supportive community.

"Sonra tam çıkarken bir kadın koşarak gelip Andrew'u her şeyi ne kadar doğal bir şekilde idare ettiği için tebrik etti. Bunun sık sık yaşanıyor olması gerektiğini anlamıştı."

Ne yazık ki Sue için bu gerçekten sık sık yaşanıyor. Nöbetleri ilaçlarla tamamen kontrol altına alınamayan yüzde 20'lik epilepsi hastası kesimin içinde yer alıyor. Ayda en az üç nöbet geçiriyor.

Epilepsinin hayatını kontrol etmesine izin vermeyen ilham verici bir örnek. Bu ilhamı, Liverpool'daki Walton Hastanesi'nde uzman nörolog olan Doktor David Chadwick ile birlikte kaleme aldığı yeni kitabı Living With Epilepsy'de (Epilepsiyle Yaşamak) paylaştı.

Kendi deyimiyle "gürültülü, sarsılan bir yığın hâlinde yere yığılmanın" verdiği o küçük düşürücü his onu uzun zamandır endişelendirmiyor; elbette hiçbir zaman hoş bir şey değil, ancak ergenlik çağındayken okul bahçesinde nöbet geçirdiğinde arkadaşlarının çığlık atarak ondan nasıl kaçtığına dair canlı anıları var. O dönemde özgüvenini tamamen kaybetmemesinin ise tamamen anne ve babası sayesinde olduğuna inanıyor. "Bir nöbet geçirirsem insanların ne düşüneceği ve bunun beni nasıl etkileyebileceği yüzünden aktivitelerimi kısıtlamaya hiç çalışmadılar. Aksine, zorluklarımın üstesinden gelmek için fazladan çaba göstermeye ve bunların daha az şey yapmam için bir bahane olmasına izin vermemeye teşvik edildim," diyor.

"Düzenli olarak görüşme ihtimalim olan kişilere epilepsi hastası olduğumu söylüyorum ve nöbet geçirirsem ne yapmaları gerektiğini açıklıyorum. Eğer aniden kalkıp yere uzanırsam, kendime zarar verebileceğim herhangi bir şeyden uzak olduğumdan emin olun, sonra yanımda kalın ve elimi tutun, diyorum. Bu, onların kendilerini çok daha güvende ve rahat hissetmelerini sağlıyor."

Çocukların daha emeklemeye başladıkları andan itibaren neler olup bittiğini ve nasıl yardım edeceklerini anlamalarına yardımcı olunması konusunda çok kararlı. "Benimkiler çok küçük yaşlardan itibaren Andrew'un yanıma diz çöküp ilgi ve koruma göstermesini görmeye alışıktı. Onları her zaman dâhil ederdi; yüzümü okşamaları için onları teşvik ederdi. Kısa sürede ne yapacaklarını öğrendiler ve gözleri yaşlı da olsa bunu doğru bir şekilde yapabiliyorlardı."

Oğlu Oliver şimdi 15, kızı Anna ise 12 yaşında. "Başkalarının bakışlarından çekindikleri bir dönemdeler ve nöbetlerim onlar için utanç verici olmalı. İkisi de gergin ve kaygılı oldukları dönemlerden geçti. Ama biz duyguları her ne olursa olsun onları destekledik ve duygularını dile getirmekten korkmamaları iyi bir şey olmalı."

Baş etme yaklaşımı her zaman çok pratik olmuştur. Çocuklar bebekken, nöbet geçirirse düşebilecekleri için altlarını asla yatak üzerinde değiştirmez, evde onlarla yalnızken de onları banyo yaptırmazdı. Devrilmesi daha kolay olan uzun saplı tencereler yerine iki kulplu güveç tipi tencereler kullanıyor. Riskler konusunda kişisel olarak rahat hissetmediği için yüzmemeyi, bisiklete ya da ata binmemeyi ve yürüyen merdiven kullanmamayı tercih ediyor. Ama başına gelebileceklerden korktuğu için dışarı çıkmaktan asla kaçınmadı.

Bu açıdan kendisinin ve çocuklarının gösterdiği cesaret muazzam. Bir keresinde, Oliver iki yaşındayken, sarhoş olduğunu düşünen bir şoför tarafından taksiden sürüklenerek çıkarılmış ve sağanak yağmur altında sokakta nöbet geçirmeye terk edilmişti. Başka bir seferinde, bir yapı tasarruf sandığının hemen içinde yere yığılmıştı ve personel, bir soygun için 'paravan' olduğunu düşündüğü için dışarı çıkıp yardım etmeyi reddetmişti.

Çocuklar küçükken sık sık sokaktaki ya da dükkânlardaki seyircileri ambulans çağırmaktan vazgeçirmeye çalışmak zorunda kalırlardı ve Sue da dilini ısırmasını önlemek için dişlerinin arasına kaşık sokulmasına sık sık katlanmak zorunda kalmıştı (yanlış bir uygulama: yalnızca katlanmış bir havlunun kenarı gibi yumuşak bir şey uygundur).

Çocuklarının acı çektiği durumlar dışında bu tür deneyimlere karşı içinde bir kırgınlık yok ve birçoğuna mizahla dönüp bakıyor. "Bu benim hayatım ve o kadar uzun zamandır başka bir hayat bilmedim ki. Sadece devam edip hayatımı yaşıyorum." Ancak tüm bu cehalet ve önyargıyla mücadele etmeye çok hevesli. Bir keresinde biri ona kendisiyle evlendiği için Andrew'a çok minnettar olması gerektiğini söylemişti ve bu onu şoke etmişti. Öte yandan, doktorların kendi durumundaki birinin ulaşabileceği yaşam kalitesini sık sık olduğundan yüksek tahmin ettiğini düşünüyor. Onlara epilepsi hakkında daha gerçekçi bir tablo sunmak için tıp öğrencilerine ve pratisyen hekim adaylarına düzenli olarak konuşmalar yapıyor.

"Her nöbet geçirdiğimde hâlâ dehşete kapılıyorum," diyor. "Üç dört dakika boyunca tüm kontrolü kaybetmek az buz bir şey değil. İnanın bana, bu uzun bir süre ve sonrasında bazen bilincimi kaybediyorum. Zamanla kolaylaşmıyor. Bir nöbetten sonra sonraki iki üç gün boyunca gerçekten çok ağır bir akşamdan kalmalık yaşıyormuşsunuz gibi oluyor. Ama olumlu yanları da var. Hayatın sert yüzünün size neler yaşatabileceğini bildiğinizde, önemsiz şeyler sizi hiç endişelendirmiyor. Çamaşır makinesi bozulduğunda asla üzülmem."

passages.passage_text:
From The Observer.

If you are considering double glazing, you must already have insulated your roof and walls. In an 'ordinary' home you lose 25 per cent of heat through the roof and 35 per cent through the walls, so they must be your priorities, unless your house is made of windows.

New buildings now have to meet new standards of insulation and are often fitted with double glazing when built. Usually this factory-made double glazing does not just add to the comfort, but is very well designed and actually looks quite good.

Still, it's a difficult decision to double glaze an existing home, since you're going to have to spend a lot of money on what will save you about 10 per cent of the heating bill in an ordinary small house.

Of course, there are other benefits besides the financial one. The room will be much more comfortable. You won't get a chilly feeling when sitting near the window and draughts will be fewer. So, on the whole, if you have money, double glazing is not a foolish investment, though even good double glazing won't be as effective as a brick wall!

Double glazing is not just 'Double Glazing'. There are several ways of achieving it. You can install 'replacement windows' with two sheets of single glass. Or you can have 'secondary windows', either fixed to the existing window or sealed to it. Secondary windows are cheaper, can often be installed by the owner, but are not likely to be so efficient as replacement windows.

If you want to do the job yourself, the simplest form of double glazing is the applied frame method, which means fixing a second pane of glass directly onto the original frame using beading or special frame sections. The most important thing is that any opening in the second leaf should be completely blocked with a long-lasting material. Points to check are: that condensation will not occur between the two panes; that you will be able to open 'openable' windows, (or that you're prepared to give up that luxury); that you will be able to clean the window and that you have some other way of letting fresh air in.

If you think that by double glazing you automatically insulate against sound too - think again. To have a noise insulating effect, the two leaves will need a gap of 110 mm or 200 mm; so double glazing with noise insulation needs to be specially made. It is more difficult to make it look nice and to fit it into the existing window openings. Moreover, with this gap it won't work as well for heat insulation. So, if you don't live directly under Concorde's flight path, it will hardly be worth insulating for sound.

task1.model_answer: The passage explains that homeowners should insulate their roofs and walls before installing double glazing, as 60 per cent of heat escapes through those areas. Although double glazing is expensive and cuts heating bills by only around 10 per cent in a small home, it significantly improves indoor comfort by reducing draughts and cold spots near windows. Homeowners can choose between more efficient replacement windows, cheaper secondary windows, or a DIY applied frame method, provided they prevent condensation and maintain ventilation and cleaning access. Finally, standard double glazing does not block noise effectively; soundproofing requires a much wider gap between panes, which reduces heat insulation and is rarely necessary unless noise is extreme.

task2.model_answer:
When renovating an older house, energy-saving improvements such as roof insulation and double glazing should take priority over purely decorative upgrades. While attractive interiors make a home pleasant to live in, poor insulation leads to constant heat loss, uncomfortable draughts, and unnecessarily high energy bills every winter. Investing in practical insulation first creates a warmer, healthier living environment and lowers long-term household expenses.

Moreover, modern energy-efficient upgrades no longer require sacrificing appearance. As the passage notes, contemporary factory-made windows are well designed and can blend smoothly with a building's style. Once a home is properly insulated and comfortable, owners can gradually focus on cosmetic improvements like paint or furniture without wasting money on escaping heat. Therefore, prioritizing energy efficiency is both financially wiser and more sustainable in the long run.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Çift Cam.

The Observer'dan.

Çift cam yaptırmayı düşünüyorsanız, çatınızın ve duvarlarınızın yalıtımını zaten yapmış olmalısınız. Sıradan bir evde ısının yüzde 25'ini çatıdan, yüzde 35'ini ise duvarlardan kaybedersiniz; dolayısıyla eviniz pencerelerden yapılmamışsa öncelikleriniz bunlar olmalıdır.

Yeni binalar artık yeni yalıtım standartlarını karşılamak zorunda ve genellikle inşa edilirken çift cam takılıyor. Çoğunlukla bu fabrika yapımı çift camlar sadece konforu artırmakla kalmıyor, aynı zamanda çok iyi tasarlanmış oluyor ve aslında oldukça şık görünüyor.

Yine de mevcut bir eve çift cam taktırmak zor bir karardır; çünkü sıradan küçük bir evde ısınma faturanızdan yaklaşık yüzde 10 tasarruf sağlayacak bir şey için çok fazla para harcamanız gerekecektir.

Elbette maddi yararın yanı sıra başka faydaları da vardır. Oda çok daha konforlu olacaktır. Pencere kenarında otururken üşüme hissi yaşamazsınız ve hava akımları da azalır. Dolayısıyla genel olarak, paranız varsa çift cam aptalca bir yatırım değildir; gerçi iyi bir çift cam bile bir tuğla duvar kadar etkili olmayacaktır!

Çift cam tek bir türden ibaret değildir. Bunu sağlamanın birkaç yolu vardır. İki adet tek cam tabakasından oluşan yeni pencereler taktırabilirsiniz. Ya da mevcut pencereye sabitlenen veya sızdırmaz şekilde yapıştırılan ikincil pencereler yaptırabilirsiniz. İkincil pencereler daha ucuzdur ve genellikle ev sahibi tarafından takılabilir, ancak yeni değiştirilen pencereler kadar verimli olmaları pek olası değildir.

İşi kendiniz yapmak istiyorsanız, çift camın en basit biçimi uygulamalı çerçeve yöntemidir; bu da çıta veya özel çerçeve profilleri kullanarak ikinci bir cam paneli doğrudan orijinal çerçevenin üzerine sabitlemek anlamına gelir. En önemli nokta, ikinci kanattaki herhangi bir açıklığın uzun ömürlü bir malzemeyle tamamen kapatılmasıdır. Kontrol edilmesi gereken noktalar şunlardır: iki cam arasında yoğuşma oluşmaması; açılabilir pencereleri açabilmeniz ya da bu lüksten vazgeçmeye hazır olmanız; pencereyi temizleyebilmeniz ve içeri temiz hava almanın başka bir yoluna sahip olmanız.

Çift cam yaptırarak otomatik olarak sese karşı da yalıtım sağladığınızı düşünüyorsanız, bir kez daha düşünün. Gürültü yalıtımı etkisi elde etmek için iki cam tabakası arasında 110 milimetre veya 200 milimetrelik bir boşluk gerekir; bu nedenle ses yalıtımlı çift camın özel olarak üretilmesi lazımdır. Bunun güzel görünmesini sağlamak ve mevcut pencere boşluklarına uydurmak daha zordur. Üstelik bu boşlukla ısı yalıtımı açısından da o kadar iyi çalışmaz. Dolayısıyla, doğrudan Concorde'un uçuş rotasının altında yaşamıyorsanız, ses yalıtımı yaptırmaya pek değmeyecektir.

passages.passage_text:
Over the past 25 years or so, there has been a sharp increase in the popularity of parachuting as a sport. Parachuting can be learnt at a parachute club. The training is extremely strict. The instructor makes sure that the beginner has learnt and understood everything before the first jump is made.

Like all parachutists, the beginner must wear two parachutes - a main one on the back and a slightly smaller reserve one on the front. Trainee parachutists do not open their parachutes themselves. By law, they have to make their first six descents using a parachute opened automatically by a 15-foot nylon static line fixed to the aeroplane. It takes about 2.7 seconds for the jumper's weight to pull on the line, and thus open the parachute.

Trainees are taught how to 'spreadeagle' - to lie stomach down and stretch their arms and legs out to slow down their fall. In this way, they descend at about 120 miles per hour before the parachute opens, whereas an experienced sky-diver, descending headfirst, can travel at over 200 mph. Novices jump from a height of about 2,500 feet, while experienced freefallers may jump from well over 7,000 feet, waiting until they are within 2,000 feet of the ground before pulling the ripcord to open their parachutes.

Automatically via a static line attached to the aeroplane
By pressing a button on the smaller reserve parachute
By an instructor who jumps right beside the trainee

passages.title: Parachuting
passages.tts_script:
Parachuting.

Over the past 25 years or so, there has been a sharp increase in the popularity of parachuting as a sport. Parachuting can be learnt at a parachute club. The training is extremely strict. The instructor makes sure that the beginner has learnt and understood everything before the first jump is made.

Like all parachutists, the beginner must wear two parachutes: a main one on the back and a slightly smaller reserve one on the front. Trainee parachutists do not open their parachutes themselves. By law, they have to make their first six descents using a parachute opened automatically by a 15-foot nylon static line fixed to the aeroplane. It takes about 2.7 seconds for the jumper's weight to pull on the line, and thus open the parachute.

Trainees are taught how to spreadeagle: to lie stomach down and stretch their arms and legs out to slow down their fall. In this way, they descend at about 120 miles per hour before the parachute opens, whereas an experienced sky-diver, descending headfirst, can travel at over 200 miles per hour. Novices jump from a height of about 2,500 feet, while experienced freefallers may jump from well over 7,000 feet, waiting until they are within 2,000 feet of the ground before pulling the ripcord to open their parachutes.

Unlike experienced sky-divers, trainees do not pull a ripcord during their first six jumps; instead, a static line attached to the plane opens their parachute automatically in under three seconds. Novices also jump from around 2,500 feet and use the spreadeagle position to slow their fall to about 120 miles per hour. By contrast, experienced freefallers may jump from over 7,000 feet, fall headfirst at over 200 miles per hour, and open their parachutes manually near 2,000 feet.

task2.model_answer:
Although parachuting is an extreme sport that carries real risks, I believe it can be safely encouraged as long as strict training and safety regulations are followed. As the passage shows, beginners are never sent into the air unprepared; instructors check their knowledge carefully, every jumper wears a reserve parachute, and static lines open the main chute automatically during early jumps.

For many people, extreme sports build confidence, discipline, and focus while offering an unforgettable sense of freedom. Rather than discouraging such activities out of fear, clubs and authorities should maintain high safety standards, regular equipment checks, and gradual progression from novice jumps to freefall. When proper precautions are respected, parachuting becomes a thrilling yet controlled adventure rather than reckless danger.

passages.passage_text:
The natural world is under violent assault from man. The seas and rivers are being poisoned by radioactive wastes, by chemical discharges and by the dumping of dangerous toxins and raw sewage. The air we breathe is polluted by smoke and fumes from factories and motor vehicles; even the rain is poisoned.

It's little wonder forests and lakes are being destroyed and everywhere wildlife is disappearing. Yet, the destruction continues. Governments and industries throughout the world are intensifying their efforts to extract the earth's mineral riches and to plunder its living resources.

The great rain-forests and the frozen continents are seriously threatened in the same way. Despite the warnings of the scientific community and the deep concern of millions of ordinary people, governments and industries don't even consider changing their policies.

The threat is there in spite of the fact that we can create environmentally-clean industries, harness the power of the sun, wind and waves for our energy needs and manage the finite resources of the earth in a way that will safeguard our future and protect all the rich variety of life-forms which share this planet with us.

But there is still hope. The forces of destruction are being challenged across the globe - and at the spearhead of this challenge is Greenpeace. Wherever the environment is in danger, Greenpeace has made a stand. Its scientific presentations and peaceful direct actions at sea and on land have shocked governments and industries into an awareness that Greenpeace will not allow the natural world to be destroyed. Those actions have also won the admiration and support of millions.

Now you can strengthen the thin green line; you can make your voice heard in defence of the living world by joining Greenpeace today.

Peaceful direct actions and public campaigns by environmental organizations such as Greenpeace play a crucial role in pushing governments and corporations toward change. When scientific reports alone fail to alter harmful policies, visible and non-violent protests capture media attention and force leaders to confront public concern. By exposing illegal dumping or destructive resource extraction, activists make it much harder for powerful industries to operate quietly without accountability.

At the same time, public campaigns alone cannot solve environmental crises unless they are backed by clear legislation and international cooperation. Protest movements raise awareness and build public pressure, which in turn encourages citizens to vote for greener policies and change their consumption habits. Therefore, while government regulation and clean technology are ultimately needed to transform industries, peaceful activism remains an essential catalyst for action.

passages.passage_text:
For centuries town and country have been regarded as being in opposition to each other. It has been suggested that the superficial differences between the two - wide open spaces contrasting with brick and concrete - are less important than the contrasting attitudes of town and country.

I am a city person who always says that, given the choice, I would prefer to live in the country away from the dirt and noise of a large city. I tell others that if it weren't for my job, I would immediately head out for the open spaces and go back to nature in a village buried in the country. But do I perceive the country as it really is?

Cities can be frightening places. The majority of the population live in massive tower blocks, noisy, squalid and impersonal. The sense of belonging to a community tends to disappear when you live fifteen floors up. All you can see from your window is the sky, or other blocks of flats. Children become aggressive and nervous - cooped up at home all day, with nowhere to play; their mothers feel isolated from the rest of the world. Strangely enough, whereas in the past the inhabitants of one street all knew each other, nowadays people on the same floor in tower blocks don't even say hello to each other.

Country life, on the other hand, differs from this kind of isolated existence in that a sense of community generally binds the inhabitants of small villages together. People have the advantage of knowing that there is always someone who will help them. But country life has disadvantages, too. While it is true that you may be among friends in a village, it is also true that you are cut off from the exciting and important events that take place in cities. There is little possibility of going to a new show or the latest movie. Shopping becomes a major problem, and for anything unusual you have to go to the nearest large town. The city-dweller who leaves for the country is often depressed by the stillness and quietness.

Which, then, is better to live in, the country or the city? The latter causes stress and a feeling of isolation - constant noise damages the senses. But one of its main advantages is that you are at the centre of things, and that life doesn't finish at half-past nine at night. The former has the advantage of peace and quiet, but suffers from the disadvantage of being cut off. Some people have found (or rather bought) a compromise between the two: they have moved to villages not too far from large urban centres. These people generally have nearly as much sensitivity as the plastic flowers they leave behind - they are polluted with strange ideas about change and improvement which they force on to the unwilling original inhabitants of the villages.

What, then, of my dreams of having a small cottage in the country? I'm keen on the idea, but you see there is my cat, Toby. I'm not at all sure that he would like all that fresh air and exercise in the long grass. No, he would rather have the electric imitation coal fire any day.

passages.title: Back to Nature
passages.tts_script:
Back to Nature.

For centuries town and country have been regarded as being in opposition to each other. It has been suggested that the superficial differences between the two, wide open spaces contrasting with brick and concrete, are less important than the contrasting attitudes of town and country.

I am a city person who always says that, given the choice, I would prefer to live in the country away from the dirt and noise of a large city. I tell others that if it weren't for my job, I would immediately head out for the open spaces and go back to nature in a village buried in the country. But do I perceive the country as it really is?

Cities can be frightening places. The majority of the population live in massive tower blocks, noisy, squalid and impersonal. The sense of belonging to a community tends to disappear when you live fifteen floors up. All you can see from your window is the sky, or other blocks of flats. Children become aggressive and nervous, cooped up at home all day, with nowhere to play; their mothers feel isolated from the rest of the world. Strangely enough, whereas in the past the inhabitants of one street all knew each other, nowadays people on the same floor in tower blocks don't even say hello to each other.

Country life, on the other hand, differs from this kind of isolated existence in that a sense of community generally binds the inhabitants of small villages together. People have the advantage of knowing that there is always someone who will help them. But country life has disadvantages, too. While it is true that you may be among friends in a village, it is also true that you are cut off from the exciting and important events that take place in cities. There is little possibility of going to a new show or the latest movie. Shopping becomes a major problem, and for anything unusual you have to go to the nearest large town. The city-dweller who leaves for the country is often depressed by the stillness and quietness.

Which, then, is better to live in, the country or the city? The latter causes stress and a feeling of isolation, as constant noise damages the senses. But one of its main advantages is that you are at the centre of things, and that life doesn't finish at half-past nine at night. The former has the advantage of peace and quiet, but suffers from the disadvantage of being cut off. Some people have found, or rather bought, a compromise between the two: they have moved to villages not too far from large urban centres. These people generally have nearly as much sensitivity as the plastic flowers they leave behind; they are polluted with strange ideas about change and improvement which they force on to the unwilling original inhabitants of the villages.

What, then, of my dreams of having a small cottage in the country? I'm keen on the idea, but you see there is my cat, Toby. I'm not at all sure that he would like all that fresh air and exercise in the long grass. No, he would rather have the electric imitation coal fire any day.

Deciding whether to raise a family in a big city or a small village involves weighing convenience against well-being. Doğaya Dönüş.

Yüzyıllardır kent ve kırsal birbirine zıt kavramlar olarak görülmüştür. İkisi arasındaki yüzeysel farklılıkların, yani tuğla ve betonla tezat oluşturan geniş açık alanların, kent ve kırsalın zıt yaklaşımlarından daha az önemli olduğu öne sürülmüştür.

Seçme şansım olsa büyük bir kentin kirinden ve gürültüsünden uzakta, kırsalda yaşamayı tercih edeceğimi her zaman söyleyen bir kent insanıyım. Başkalarına, işim olmasa hemen açık alanlara doğru yola çıkacağımı ve kırsalın derinliklerindeki bir köyde doğaya döneceğimi söylerim. Peki kırsalı gerçekten olduğu gibi mi algılıyorum?

Kentler korkutucu yerler olabilir. Nüfusun büyük çoğunluğu gürültülü, sefil ve soğuk dev yüksek apartmanlarda yaşamaktadır. On beş kat yukarıda yaşadığınızda bir topluluğa ait olma duygusu yok olma eğilimi gösterir. Pencerenizden görebileceğiniz tek şey gökyüzü ya da başka apartman bloklarıdır. Bütün gün evde kapalı kalan ve oynayacak hiçbir yeri olmayan çocuklar saldırgan ve gergin hale gelir; anneleri ise kendilerini dünyanın geri kalanından soyutlanmış hisseder. İşin garibi, geçmişte bir sokağın sakinlerinin tamamı birbirini tanırken günümüzde yüksek apartmanların aynı katında yaşayan insanlar birbirlerine merhaba bile dememektedir.

Öte yandan kırsal yaşam, bir topluluk duygusunun küçük köylerin sakinlerini genellikle birbirine bağlaması bakımından bu tür soyutlanmış bir varoluştan ayrılır. İnsanlar, kendilerine yardım edecek birinin her zaman bulunduğunu bilmenin avantajına sahiptir. Ancak kırsal yaşamın dezavantajları da vardır. Bir köyde dostlar arasında olabileceğiniz doğru olsa da, kentlerde gerçekleşen heyecan verici ve önemli olaylardan kopuk olduğunuz da bir gerçektir. Yeni bir gösteriye ya da en son çıkan bir filme gitme olanağı çok azdır. Alışveriş büyük bir soruna dönüşür ve olağandışı herhangi bir şey için en yakın büyük kasabaya gitmeniz gerekir. Kırsala giden bir kent sakini genellikle bu durgunluk ve sessizlik yüzünden bunalıma girer.

Öyleyse yaşamak için hangisi daha iyidir: kırsal mı yoksa kent mi? İkincisi, sürekli gürültü duyulara zarar verdiği için strese ve soyutlanma hissine yol açar. Ancak başlıca avantajlarından biri, olayların merkezinde olmanız ve yaşamın gece dokuz buçukta sona ermemesidir. İlki ise huzur ve sessizlik avantajına sahiptir, fakat kopuk olma dezavantajından muzdariptir. Bazı insanlar ikisi arasında bir orta yol bulmuş, daha doğrusu satın almıştır: büyük kent merkezlerinden çok da uzak olmayan köylere taşınmışlardır. Bu insanlar genellikle arkalarında bıraktıkları plastik çiçekler kadar duyarlılığa sahiptir; değişim ve iyileştirme hakkında tuhaf fikirlerle kirlenmişlerdir ve bunları köylerin isteksiz yerli sakinlerine zorla dayatırlar.

Peki ya kırsalda küçük bir kır evine sahip olma hayallerime ne demeli? Bu fikre çok hevesliyim ama görüyorsunuz ki kedim Toby var. Bunca temiz havayı ve uzun çimenlerde koşturmayı seveceğinden hiç emin değilim. Hayır, o elektrikli sahte kömür şöminesini her zaman tercih eder.

passages.passage_text:
Can earthquakes be predicted? Scientists are working on programs to predict where and when an earthquake will occur. They hope to develop an early warning system to save lives. Scientists who do this work are called seismologists.

Earthquakes are the most dangerous and deadly of all natural events. They occur in many parts of the world. Giant earthquakes have been recorded in Iran, China, Guatemala, Chile, India, and Alaska. Two of the biggest earthquakes that were ever recorded took place in China and Alaska. These earthquakes measured about 8.5 on the Richter Scale. The Richter Scale was devised by Charles Richter in 1935 and is used for comparing the energy level of earthquakes. An earthquake that measures 2 on the scale can be felt, but causes little damage. One that measures 4.5 on the scale can cause slight damage, and an earthquake that has a reading of over 7 can cause major damage.

How do earthquakes occur? Earthquakes are caused by the movement of rocks along cracks, or faults, in the earth's surface. The fault is produced when rocks near each other are pulled in different directions. The best-known fault in North America is the San Andreas fault in the State of California in the United States.

The nations that are actively involved in earthquake prediction programs include Japan, China, Russia, and the United States. These countries have set up stations in areas of their countries where earthquakes are known to occur. These stations are ready for warning signs that show the weakening of rock layers before an earthquake. Many kinds of seismic instruments are used by these places to watch the movements of the earth's surface. One of the instruments is a seismograph. It can follow vibrations in rock layers thousands of kilometers away. Tiltmeters are used to record surface movement along fault lines. Seismologists use gravimeters to measure and record changes in local gravity. The scientists also check water in deep wells. They watch for changes in the water level and temperature, which are signs of movement along faults.

Their energy level is measured on the Richter Scale, devised in 1935, where readings above 7 cause major damage and the largest recorded quakes reached about 8.5. To predict earthquakes and save lives, seismologists in countries like Japan, China, Russia, and the United States monitor earthquake-prone zones. task2.model_answer:
Although scientists cannot yet predict the exact time of every earthquake, investing heavily in prediction research and early warning systems is essential. Earthquakes remain one of the deadliest natural events, capable of destroying entire cities within seconds. Even a warning of a few seconds or minutes can allow trains to stop, factories to shut down dangerous machinery, and residents to move away from windows or collapsing structures.

Of course, earthquake-resistant buildings and strict construction standards are equally vital, because strong structures directly prevent loss of life during shaking. However, prediction programs and safe engineering are not mutually exclusive; rather, they work together. Monitoring fault lines, ground movements, and underground water changes also improves scientific knowledge about which regions face the greatest risk, helping governments decide where building codes must be reinforced first. Therefore, continued funding for seismic research is a wise and necessary investment in public safety.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Deprem Tahmini.

Depremler önceden tahmin edilebilir mi? Bilim insanları bir depremin nerede ve ne zaman meydana geleceğini tahmin etmeye yönelik programlar üzerinde çalışmaktadır. Hayat kurtarmak için bir erken uyarı sistemi geliştirmeyi umuyorlar. Bu işi yapan bilim insanlarına sismolog denir.

Depremler tüm doğa olaylarının en tehlikelisi ve en ölümcülüdür. Dünyanın birçok yerinde meydana gelirler. İran, Çin, Guatemala, Şili, Hindistan ve Alaska'da dev depremler kaydedilmiştir. Şimdiye kadar kaydedilen en büyük depremlerden ikisi Çin ve Alaska'da yaşanmıştır. Bu depremler Richter Ölçeği'ne göre yaklaşık 8,5 büyüklüğünde ölçülmüştür. Richter Ölçeği, 1935 yılında Charles Richter tarafından geliştirilmiştir ve depremlerin enerji düzeyini karşılaştırmak için kullanılır. Ölçekte 2 büyüklüğündeki bir deprem hissedilebilir ancak çok az hasara yol açar. Ölçekte 4,5 büyüklüğündeki bir deprem hafif hasara neden olabilir ve 7'nin üzerinde ölçülen bir deprem ise büyük hasara yol açabilir.

Depremler nasıl meydana gelir? Depremler, yerkabuğundaki çatlaklar ya da faylar boyunca kayaların hareket etmesinden kaynaklanır. Fay, birbirine yakın kayaların farklı yönlere çekilmesiyle oluşur. Kuzey Amerika'daki en iyi bilinen fay, Amerika Birleşik Devletleri'nin Kaliforniya eyaletindeki San Andreas fayıdır.

Deprem tahmini programlarında aktif olarak yer alan ülkeler arasında Japonya, Çin, Rusya ve Amerika Birleşik Devletleri bulunmaktadır. Bu ülkeler, kendi topraklarında depremlerin meydana geldiği bilinen bölgelere istasyonlar kurmuştur. Bu istasyonlar, bir depremden önce kaya katmanlarının zayıfladığını gösteren uyarı işaretlerini izlemeye hazırdır. Bu merkezlerde yeryüzünün hareketlerini gözlemlemek için pek çok sismik alet türü kullanılmaktadır. Bu aletlerden biri sismograftır. Binlerce kilometre uzaktaki kaya katmanlarındaki titreşimleri izleyebilir. Eğimölçerler, fay hatları boyunca yüzey hareketini kaydetmek için kullanılır. Sismologlar, yerel yer çekimindeki değişiklikleri ölçmek ve kaydetmek için gravimetreler kullanır. Bilim insanları ayrıca derin kuyulardaki suyu da kontrol eder. Faylar boyunca hareketin işaretleri olan su seviyesindeki ve sıcaklıktaki değişiklikleri takip ederler.
