passages.tts_script_tr:
Elektron Teorisi.

Bir zamanlar öğrencilere şöyle denirdi: "Elektriğin ne olduğunu bilmiyoruz, elektriğin katı bir telin içinden nasıl geçtiğini bilmiyoruz," ve benzeri şeyler. Elektron teorisi bu konuları açık ve basit bir şekilde açıklamaktadır. Buna ek olarak, voltajın, direncin ve benzeri kavramların gerçek anlamını da açıklar. Bu nedenle, elektron teorisini anlamak, elektrik ve elektronik teorisini anlamanın temelidir.

Bilim insanları artık evrenimizin temelde iki unsura bağlı olduğu konusunda hemfikirdir; bunlardan biri madde, diğeri ise enerjidir. Madde, uzayda yer kaplayan ve ağırlığı olan her şeydir. Üç halden herhangi birinde bulunabilir: katı, sıvı veya gaz.

Madde protonlardan, nötronlardan ve elektronlardan oluşur. Proton pozitif yüke sahiptir. Bu bileşenin ağırlığı çok azdır. Nötronun yükü yoktur ancak maddenin neredeyse tüm ağırlığını o sağlar. Elektron negatif yüke sahiptir. Onun da ağırlığı çok azdır. Bir bakır parçasının yapısına bakabilseydik, belirli bir şekilde düzenlenmiş belirli sayıda proton, nötron ve elektrondan oluştuğunu görürdük. Bir demir parçasında ise belirli sayıda proton, nötron ve elektron farklı bir şekilde düzenlenmiştir. Demirin protonu, bakırın ve diğer elementlerin protonuyla özdeştir. Hepsi aynı bileşenlerden oluşur. Onları farklı kılan, bu bileşenlerin dizilişidir.

Bir atomun elektronları çekirdeğin etrafında kabuklar halinde dizilmiştir. Son kabuktaki elektronlara değerlik elektronları denir ve bir malzemenin elektriksel özellikleri bu tür elektronların sayısına bağlıdır. Dörtten az değerlik elektronuna sahip atomlar bir veya daha fazla elektron verir ve değerlik elektronu sayısı ne kadar azsa bu durum o kadar kolaylaşır. Son kabuğunda dörtten fazla elektron bulunan atomlar bir veya daha fazla ek elektron alır. Elektriğin iletimi, dış kabuktaki serbest elektronlar sayesinde mümkün olur.

Metaller, dörtten az değerlik elektronuna sahip oldukları için iyi birer elektrik iletkenidir. Bu elektronlar çekirdeğe sıkıca bağlı değildir, ancak iç kabuktakiler sıkıca bağlıdır. Bu nedenle bir metalin içinde bir çekirdekten diğerine kolayca hareket edebilirler.

passages.passage_text:
Hydroponics is the technique of growing plants in water. It is generally thought that plants need soil for growing. In fact, what they need is the nutrients (vitamins and minerals) and moisture contained in the soil and these can be supplied through water, as well as through soil.

Hydroponics is not a new process. As long ago as the 1690's, an English physician tried growing plants in water in a laboratory experiment. However, it was not until the 1800's that German researchers used this method to develop many of the formulas for plant nutrient solutions still in use today.

About a generation ago, hydroponics moved out of the research laboratory into practical use. In the past 40 years, hydroponic farming has progressed in a number of areas, especially in those where water is in short supply and temperatures are too extreme for ordinary agriculture. This is because hydroponic farming is the only economical solution in such desert areas.

Each year, more than 2.7 million kilograms of vegetables and fruit are produced by hydroponic farming. These are mostly tomatoes but cucumbers, lettuce and melons are also grown. On hydroponic farms, each tomato plant produces an average of 6 kilograms of fruit twice a year - a total of 12 kilograms every year. An ordinary soil-grown plant, on the other hand, produces only a total of 9 kilograms per year.

In hydroponic farming, plants are grown in greenhouses. The greenhouses measure 8 by 39 metres and consist of steel frames covered with strong transparent plastic that is resistant to weather and lets in a maximum amount of light. The plants are fed by inorganic nutrients dissolved in water which is supplied by a plastic pipeline.

The feeding and watering system is automated. Electric sensing devices (sensors) determine when the plants are hungry or thirsty. The sensors send messages which automatically start the water and nutrient delivery system. When the sensors 'know' that the plants have had enough, the system turns off automatically.

Nothing is left to chance within the greenhouses. Temperature, humidity and air circulation are carefully controlled. Air conditioning and heating equipment keep the temperature at 29°C by day and 18°C by night.

In recent years, hydroponic farming has expanded to many parts of the world.

task1.model_answer: Hydroponics is a method of cultivating plants in nutrient-rich water instead of soil. Although its experimental roots date back to the late seventeenth and nineteenth centuries, it has become a practical agricultural solution over the past forty years, particularly in dry regions with extreme temperatures. Today, hydroponic farms produce over 2.7 million kilograms of crops annually, primarily tomatoes, which yield more fruit per plant than soil-grown varieties. task2.model_answer:
Hydroponic farming offers a promising way to address global food and water challenges, although it is unlikely to replace traditional agriculture completely. Because hydroponic systems deliver water and dissolved nutrients directly to plants in controlled greenhouses, they use resources far more efficiently than open-field farming. This makes hydroponics especially valuable in arid regions and urban areas where fertile soil and fresh water are scarce. Furthermore, precise control over temperature, humidity, and lighting enables higher yields throughout the year.

However, hydroponic installations require significant initial investment, reliable electricity, and specialized equipment such as sensors and climate-control systems. Staple crops like wheat, rice, and corn are still grown much more cheaply in open fields. Therefore, rather than replacing conventional farming, hydroponics will most likely serve as a vital complement to it, ensuring reliable vegetable and fruit production in regions facing harsh climates or rapid population growth.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Hidroponik.

Hidroponik, bitkileri suda yetiştirme tekniğidir. Genellikle bitkilerin büyümek için toprağa ihtiyaç duyduğu düşünülür. Aslında ihtiyaç duydukları şey toprakta bulunan besinler, vitaminler, mineraller ve nemdir; bunlar da toprak yoluyla olduğu kadar su yoluyla da sağlanabilir.

Hidroponik yeni bir yöntem değildir. 1690'lı yıllar kadar eski bir dönemde, bir İngiliz hekim laboratuvar deneyinde bitkileri suda yetiştirmeyi denemiştir. Ancak Alman araştırmacıların bugün hâlâ kullanılan bitki besin çözeltisi formüllerinin çoğunu geliştirmek için bu yöntemi kullanması 1800'leri bulmuştur.

Yaklaşık bir kuşak önce hidroponik, araştırma laboratuvarından çıkarak pratik kullanıma geçti. Son 40 yılda hidroponik tarım pek çok alanda, özellikle de su kaynaklarının kıt olduğu ve sıcaklıkların sıradan tarım için aşırı uçlarda seyrettiği bölgelerde ilerleme kaydetti. Bunun nedeni, bu tür çöl bölgelerinde tek ekonomik çözümün hidroponik tarım olmasıdır.

Her yıl hidroponik tarımla 2,7 milyon kilogramdan fazla sebze ve meyve üretilmektedir. Bunlar çoğunlukla domatestir ancak salatalık, marul ve kavun da yetiştirilmektedir. Hidroponik çiftliklerde her domates bitkisi yılda iki kez ortalama 6 kilogram, yani her yıl toplam 12 kilogram ürün verir. Buna karşılık, toprakta yetiştirilen sıradan bir bitki yılda toplam yalnızca 9 kilogram ürün verir.

Hidroponik tarımda bitkiler seralarda yetiştirilir. Seralar 8'e 39 metre ölçülerindedir ve hava koşullarına dayanıklı, içeriye maksimum miktarda ışık girmesini sağlayan güçlü şeffaf plastikle kaplı çelik iskeletlerden oluşur. Bitkiler, plastik bir boru hattıyla sağlanan su içinde çözünmüş inorganik besinlerle beslenir.

Besleme ve sulama sistemi otomatiktir. Sensör adı verilen elektrikli algılama cihazları, bitkilerin ne zaman aç veya susuz olduğunu belirler. Sensörler, su ve besin dağıtım sistemini otomatik olarak başlatan sinyaller gönderir. Sensörler bitkilerin yeterince aldığını anladığında sistem otomatik olarak kapanır.

Seraların içinde hiçbir şey şansa bırakılmaz. Sıcaklık, nem ve hava sirkülasyonu dikkatle kontrol edilir. İklimlendirme ve ısıtma ekipmanları sıcaklığı gündüz 29 santigrat derecede, gece ise 18 santigrat derecede tutar.

Son yıllarda hidroponik tarım dünyanın pek çok yerine yayılmıştır.

task2.model_answer:
Authorities responsible for public safety near nuclear facilities often face a difficult choice between transparent emergency preparation and avoiding public panic. In my view, informing residents and distributing protective measures such as anti-radiation tablets in advance is the right decision, provided it is accompanied by clear communication.

In an emergency involving a radiation leak, distributing medicine quickly can be chaotic and slow. Giving residents potassium iodate tablets beforehand ensures that families and workers can act immediately if an incident ever occurs. Although seeing emergency pills arrive may initially worry some people, secrecy or delayed preparation puts public health at far greater risk.

To reduce unnecessary alarm, local councils should organize clear public information campaigns explaining that the tablets are strictly a routine precaution rather than a sign of imminent danger. passages.passage_text:
Crocodiles are formidable enemies of man and most of the stories about them arise from tragic real experiences. At least 6 of the 23 species in the crocodile family will attack and eat human beings if they can, and many of the others are large enough to cause serious injury.

The well-known Nile crocodile, found from Egypt to the Cape of Good Hope, has a length of 5 metres. It is reported that crocodiles kill up to 1,000 people every year along the banks of the River Nile. Equally large and dangerous is the man-eating salt water crocodile, whose habitat ranges from India and China to northern Australia. The largest of all is the Madagascar crocodile, which may grow to 9 metres or longer, and the most dangerous is the Estuarine crocodile, which probably kills over 2,000 people each year.

Crocodiles have narrow, pointed snouts and rows of teeth in the lower jaw. The teeth can be seen even when the mouth is closed. The body is protected by thick leathery plates and the animal has webbed feet as well as a powerful, flattened tail. Baby crocodiles are greenish grey with black crossbands whereas most adults are olive coloured.

Sewage and garbage attract crocodiles by providing a rich diet which unfortunately inflames their aggression. That's probably why there are constant horror stories about the danger of crocodiles growing in sewage systems and waste dumps of big cities in Africa. However, this is certainly true for the City of Manzini in Swaziland, where the health officials captured man-eating crocodiles and put them to work in the City sewers and dumps to gobble up garbage. Now, the job is done cheaply and effectively!

Among the many legends about crocodiles, there are those of living to be a hundred years old. However, most crocodiles live for about fifty years. The oldest official age recorded is that of a crocodile which was born in Dresden Zoo in Germany in 1880 and which was recorded as being still alive in 1937. In fact, it might have lived on much longer if the zoo had not been completely destroyed in the Second World War.

Hatred has made the hunting of crocodiles so popular that the world population of them has been drastically reduced. Some 16 species are now almost extinct - among them the rare Cuban crocodile, which has been reduced to a mere 300 individuals living in a protected sanctuary in Cuba.

That's probably why there are constant horror stories about the danger of crocodiles growing in sewage systems and waste dumps of big cities in Africa. However, this is certainly true for the City of Manzini in Swaziland, where the health officials captured man-eating crocodiles and put them to work in the City sewers and dumps to gobble up garbage. Now, the job is done cheaply and effectively!

Among the many legends about crocodiles, there are those of living to be a hundred years old. However, most crocodiles live for about fifty years. The oldest official age recorded is that of a crocodile which was born in Dresden Zoo in Germany in 1880 and which was recorded as being still alive in 1937. In fact, it might have lived on much longer if the zoo had not been completely destroyed in the Second World War.

Hatred has made the hunting of crocodiles so popular that the world population of them has been drastically reduced. Some 16 species are now almost extinct, among them the rare Cuban crocodile, which has been reduced to a mere 300 individuals living in a protected sanctuary in Cuba.

task2.model_answer:
Even though dangerous predators such as crocodiles pose real risks to human life, protecting them from extinction remains essential. As the passage shows, human hatred and excessive hunting have already pushed 16 crocodile species to the brink of disappearance, which could severely disrupt natural ecosystems.

Every species plays a role in maintaining ecological balance. Predators help control populations of other animals and keep river and wetland environments healthy. Furthermore, the example of Manzini, where crocodiles were used to consume waste, demonstrates that these reptiles can even serve practical purposes when managed properly.

Instead of hunting dangerous animals to extinction, governments should focus on responsible wildlife management. Creating protected sanctuaries, such as the one for the rare Cuban crocodile, and educating local communities about safe boundaries can protect both people and endangered wildlife. Conservation and human safety do not have to be mutually exclusive.

passages.passage_text:
High on a hill in Mid-Wales near Machynlleth, a group of idealists have shown that man can harmlessly draw energy from nature.

In the past 13 years, this group, some 30 adults with their children, has demonstrated the success of harnessing the energy of the sun, the wind and the rain to generate sufficient power for their needs.

Although they were not taken seriously by locals as the 'hippies in the hills' when they first moved to the disused mining site a few miles from Machynlleth, their projects and enthusiasm have won them the support of the local people, big business, and international respect.

Opposed to the government's plans for both nuclear power and coal, the Centre for Alternative Technology is striving for a programme using renewable fuels which would protect the planet's future. "The way the world is going, we could actually run out of known forms of energy before we actually blow ourselves up," says Tim Kirby, an engineering graduate and CAT's technical officer.

The centre uses windmills, water turbines and solar panels to heat and effectively provide for all its facilities, and the group believes that there is no reason why such technology should not power the entire UK.

The CAT people live off the land, on organically-grown fruit and vegetables and naturally-bred animals. Some are vegetarian; all believe in a low meat diet. Most members of staff live on the site; others choose to emulate the lifestyle in the surrounding area.

While most of us were complaining about the lack of sunshine this summer, water pipes heated from solar panels at Machynlleth were red hot after just a couple of hours of autumnal sun. "Few people realise the power of the sun's rays," says Mr. Kirby. He claims that the owner of a house with a wall of solar panels now pays around £75 a year on fuel bills as opposed to £500 for the average house.

passages.passage_text:
To meet the demands of industry, technology, and other sciences, mathematicians have had to invent new branches of mathematics and expand the old ones. They have built a superstructure of new ideas that people who are trained in the classical branches of the subject would hardly recognise as mathematics at all.

Applied mathematicians have been dealing with the world's problems successfully, while pure mathematicians seem almost to have lost touch with the real world. To them, mathematics is an art and they don't care much whether it will ever have any practical use.

By applying the concepts of mathematics to worldly problems, the applied mathematician can often brush away the obscuring details and reveal simple patterns. Celestial mechanics, for example, enables astronomers to calculate the positions of the planets at any time in the past or future. Now, this ancient branch of mathematics has suddenly become very practical for calculating the orbits of Earth satellites.

Applied mathematicians, who are interested in worldly problems, have learned to solve many of them that were almost impossible to solve ten or twenty years ago. They have developed new statistical methods for controlling quality in high-speed industrial mass production. They have built the basis for Operations Research, which businessmen use to plan production and distribution. They have dealt with the complexities of human behaviour through 'game theory', which applies to military and business strategy. They have analysed the design of automatic controls for such complicated systems as factory production lines and supersonic aircraft. Now they are ready to tackle many problems of space travel.

Mathematicians have begun to turn their attention to the biological and social sciences as these sciences have started to use mathematics. The bond between mathematics and life sciences has been strengthened by a group of applied mathematics specialties, such as biometrics, psychometrics and econometrics.

Now that they have electronic computers, mathematicians are solving problems that they could never solve a few years ago. In a few minutes, they can get an answer that previously would have required months or even years of calculation. Furthermore, in designing computers and programming them to carry out instructions, mathematicians have had to develop new techniques. Computers have contributed very little to pure mathematical theory, but they have been used to test certain relationships among numbers.

task1.model_answer: Modern demands in science, technology, and industry have pushed mathematicians to develop entirely new mathematical fields. While pure mathematicians treat their subject as an art form disconnected from everyday utility, applied mathematicians focus on solving practical problems by uncovering simple patterns beneath complex details. Their methods now support satellite orbit calculations, industrial quality control, business planning through Operations Research, strategic analysis via game theory, and automated engineering systems. Mathematics has also expanded into the biological and social sciences through fields like biometrics and econometrics. Finally, electronic computers have drastically shortened calculation times from years to minutes, though their contribution to pure mathematical theory remains limited.

task2.model_answer: Although pure mathematics rarely offers immediate practical benefits, societies should continue to fund it alongside applied research. Critics often argue that public budgets should prioritize projects with clear economic returns, such as industrial engineering or medical statistics. However, history shows that abstract mathematical ideas frequently become indispensable decades or even centuries after they are discovered. As the passage notes, celestial mechanics was once studied mainly to track planets, yet it suddenly became essential for calculating the orbits of Earth satellites. Similarly, theoretical work on numbers and logic laid the groundwork for modern computing and encryption long before electronic computers existed. Treating mathematics solely as a tool for short-term problem solving risks cutting off the foundational discoveries that future applied scientists will depend on. Therefore, balanced funding that supports both curiosity-driven pure theory and practical applied research ensures both immediate progress and long-term innovation.

Endüstrinin, teknolojinin ve diğer bilim dallarının taleplerini karşılamak için matematikçiler matematiğin yeni dallarını icat etmek ve eskilerini genişletmek zorunda kalmışlardır. Konunun klasik dallarında eğitim almış kişilerin neredeyse hiç matematik olarak tanıyamayacağı yeni fikirlerden oluşan bir üstyapı inşa etmişlerdir.

Uygulamalı matematikçiler dünyanın sorunlarıyla başarıyla ilgilenirken, saf matematikçiler gerçek dünyayla bağlarını neredeyse koparmış gibi görünmektedir. Onlara göre matematik bir sanattır ve pratik bir faydasının olup olmayacağını pek umursamazlar.

Uygulamalı matematikçi, matematik kavramlarını dünyevi sorunlara uygulayarak genellikle kafa karıştırıcı ayrıntıları bir kenara atabilir ve basit örüntüleri ortaya çıkarabilir. Örneğin gök mekaniği, gökbilimcilerin geçmişte veya gelecekte herhangi bir zamandaki gezegen konumlarını hesaplamasına olanak tanır. Şimdi ise matematiğin bu kadim dalı, Dünya uydularının yörüngelerini hesaplamak için birdenbire çok pratik bir hale gelmiştir.

Dünyevi sorunlarla ilgilenen uygulamalı matematikçiler, on ya da yirmi yıl önce çözülmesi neredeyse imkansız olan bu sorunların birçoğunu çözmeyi öğrenmişlerdir. Yüksek hızlı endüstriyel seri üretimde kaliteyi kontrol etmek için yeni istatistiksel yöntemler geliştirmişlerdir. İş insanlarının üretim ve dağıtımı planlamak için kullandığı Yöneylem Araştırması'nın temelini oluşturmuşlardır. Askeri ve ticari stratejilere uygulanan "oyun teorisi" aracılığıyla insan davranışlarının karmaşıklıklarını ele almışlardır. Fabrika üretim hatları ve süpersonik uçaklar gibi karmaşık sistemler için otomatik kontrollerin tasarımını analiz etmişlerdir. Şimdi ise uzay yolculuğunun pek çok sorununu ele almaya hazırdırlar.

Biyoloji ve sosyal bilimler matematiği kullanmaya başladıkça, matematikçiler de dikkatlerini bu bilim dallarına çevirmeye başlamıştır. Matematik ile yaşam bilimleri arasındaki bağ; biyometri, psikometri ve ekonometri gibi bir dizi uygulamalı matematik uzmanlık alanı sayesinde güçlenmiştir.

Artık elektronik bilgisayarlara sahip oldukları için matematikçiler, birkaç yıl önce asla çözemeyecekleri problemleri çözmektedir. Önceden aylar hatta yıllar sürecek hesaplamalar gerektiren bir cevaba birkaç dakika içinde ulaşabilmektedirler. Dahası, bilgisayarları tasarlarken ve onları talimatları yerine getirecek şekilde programlarken matematikçiler yeni teknikler geliştirmek zorunda kalmıştır. Bilgisayarlar saf matematik teorisine çok az katkıda bulunmuştur, ancak sayılar arasındaki belirli ilişkileri test etmek için kullanılmışlardır.

passages.passage_text:
In 1805, the English chemist and physicist, John Dalton, stated that all matter consists of small particles which he called 'atoms'. Dalton's theory, which helped to explain many different observations that he and other scientists had made, has been supported and changed by scientists since his time, but it is basic to an understanding of chemistry and biology today.

The word 'atom' comes from a Greek word which means 'indivisible'. However, scientists in our century have found that atoms are not indivisible. All atoms are made up of different combinations of three smaller particles: electrons, neutrons and protons. Electrons are the main units of electricity and they carry a negative electrical charge (-). Protons carry a positive electrical charge (+). Neutrons, as their name suggests, are neutral. They carry no electrical charge.

How are these particles arranged inside the atom? The protons and neutrons together form the nucleus of the atom. The nucleus is in the centre and occupies a very small amount of the total space of the atom. All the rest of the empty space in the atom is used by the rapidly moving electrons. As a result of these rapid movements of electrons, an 'electron cloud' is formed around the nucleus. They seem to be everywhere at once. The number of electrons outside the nucleus equals the number of protons inside the nucleus. Thus, an atom is electrically balanced, or neutral. All chemical reactions involve only electrons, which travel around the nucleus in different orbits. These electrons can interact with the electrons of another atom to form compounds. The nucleus of an atom is not changed in a chemical reaction. It is changed only in nuclear reactions, which occur, for example, in radioactive minerals and in atomic reactors.

Atoms of different elements differ from one another in the number of protons, neutrons and electrons. On the other hand, atoms of the same element always have the same number of protons and electrons, although they may differ in the number of neutrons. These are called isotopes. For example, over 99% of all the oxygen atoms in nature are made up of 8 protons, 8 neutrons and 8 electrons. This is known as the Oxygen-16 isotope. 16 is the sum of the number of protons and neutrons. (The number of electrons is not included in this number because the number of electrons is the same as that of protons.) However, there is also a small amount of the Oxygen-18 isotope, whose atoms contain 8 protons and 10 neutrons.

Isotopes are important in biology because they can be used in following many processes in living cells. Radioactive isotopes are the most useful ones for this purpose. The nuclei of radioactive isotopes are not stable. They give off radiation and finally come apart. The radiation can be detected with a Geiger counter. For example, the radioactive isotope of carbon, Carbon-14, has helped biologists to follow the path of carbon in many complicated reactions inside living cells.

Many of the chemical elements which occur in nature are made up of mixtures of non-radioactive isotopes with stable nuclei. Others are composed of radioactive isotopes. In addition, radioactive isotopes of all the chemical elements can be produced artificially. These are called radioisotopes.

The most important source of radioisotopes is the atomic reactor, which yields large quantities of some isotopes from the fission of uranium. Other radioisotopes may be produced by the bombardment of suitable elements by neutrons in the reactor and some others by nuclear reactions.

task1.model_answer: Although the word 'atom' originally meant indivisible, modern science has shown that atoms consist of three subatomic particles: positively charged protons, neutral neutrons, and negatively charged electrons. Protons and neutrons form the central nucleus, while rapidly moving electrons create a surrounding cloud and balance the atom's charge. Chemical reactions involve only these electrons, whereas nuclear reactions alter the nucleus. Atoms of the same element always share the same proton and electron counts, yet they can have different numbers of neutrons, creating isotopes such as Oxygen-16 and Oxygen-18. Unstable radioactive isotopes emit detectable radiation and are widely used as tracers in biology, with atomic reactors serving as the primary source of artificially produced radioisotopes.
task1.prompt: In 100-120 words, summarize how an atom is structured and explain what distinguishes isotopes and radioisotopes according to the passage.
task1.title: Summarizing Atomic Structure and Isotopes

task2.model_answer:
Radioisotopes have become essential tools in modern science and medicine, even though working with radioactive materials requires strict safety measures. On the positive side, their ability to emit detectable radiation allows researchers to observe processes that would otherwise remain invisible. In biology, tracers such as Carbon-14 enable scientists to follow chemical pathways inside living cells. Similarly, medical specialists use controlled doses of radioisotopes to diagnose illnesses and treat certain diseases without invasive surgery.

However, the instability of radioactive nuclei also presents significant challenges. Because these isotopes give off radiation as they decay, careless handling or improper waste disposal can damage living tissue and contaminate the environment. Producing radioisotopes in atomic reactors also demands careful regulation to prevent accidents and protect workers.

Overall, while radiation carries real hazards, the scientific and medical benefits of radioisotopes outweigh the risks when strict safety protocols are followed. Continued advances in detection and containment will ensure they remain valuable for future research.
task2.prompt: Radioactive isotopes are useful tools in biological research, yet they also involve nuclear reactions and radiation. Write a short essay (150-200 words) discussing both the benefits and potential risks of using radioisotopes in science and medicine.
task2.title: The Role of Radioisotopes in Science and Medicine

passages.tts_script_tr:
Atomlar (2).

1805 yılında İngiliz kimyager ve fizikçi John Dalton, tüm maddelerin "atom" adını verdiği küçük parçacıklardan oluştuğunu belirtti. Kendisinin ve diğer bilim insanlarının yaptığı birçok farklı gözlemi açıklamaya yardımcı olan Dalton teorisi, o dönemden bu yana bilim insanları tarafından hem desteklenmiş hem de değiştirilmiştir; ancak günümüzde kimya ve biyolojiyi anlamanın temelini oluşturmaktadır.

"Atom" kelimesi, "bölünemez" anlamına gelen Yunanca bir kelimeden gelir. Ancak yüzyılımızdaki bilim insanları atomların bölünemez olmadığını keşfettiler. Tüm atomlar üç küçük parçacığın farklı birleşimlerinden oluşur: elektronlar, nötronlar ve protonlar. Elektronlar elektriğin temel birimleridir ve negatif elektrik yükü taşırlar. Protonlar pozitif elektrik yükü taşır. Nötronlar ise adından da anlaşılacağı gibi nötrdür. Hiçbir elektrik yükü taşımazlar.

Bu parçacıklar atomun içinde nasıl dizilmiştir? Protonlar ve nötronlar birlikte atomun çekirdeğini oluşturur. Çekirdek merkezde yer alır ve atomun toplam hacminin çok küçük bir kısmını kaplar. Atomdaki geri kalan tüm boş alan, hızla hareket eden elektronlar tarafından kullanılır. Elektronların bu hızlı hareketlerinin bir sonucu olarak, çekirdeğin etrafında bir "elektron bulutu" oluşur. Sanki aynı anda her yerdelermiş gibi görünürler. Çekirdeğin dışındaki elektronların sayısı, çekirdeğin içindeki protonların sayısına eşittir. Bu nedenle bir atom elektriksel olarak dengeli, yani nötrdür. Tüm kimyasal reaksiyonlar yalnızca çekirdeğin etrafında farklı yörüngelerde dolaşan elektronları içerir. Bu elektronlar bileşik oluşturmak için başka bir atomun elektronlarıyla etkileşime girebilir. Bir atomun çekirdeği kimyasal bir reaksiyonda değişmez. Çekirdek yalnızca, örneğin radyoaktif minerallerde ve atom reaktörlerinde meydana gelen nükleer reaksiyonlarda değişir.

Farklı elementlerin atomları proton, nötron ve elektron sayıları bakımından birbirinden farklıdır. Öte yandan, aynı elementin atomları nötron sayıları bakımından farklılık gösterebilse de her zaman aynı sayıda protona ve elektrona sahiptir. Bunlara izotop denir. Örneğin, doğadaki tüm oksijen atomlarının yüzde 99'undan fazlası 8 proton, 8 nötron ve 8 elektrondan oluşur. Bu, Oksijen-16 izotopu olarak bilinir. 16, proton ve nötron sayılarının toplamıdır. Elektronların sayısı protonlarınkiyle aynı olduğu için bu sayıya dahil edilmez. Ancak, atomları 8 proton ve 10 nötron içeren az miktarda Oksijen-18 izotopu da vardır.

İzotoplar biyolojide önemlidir çünkü canlı hücrelerdeki birçok süreci takip etmek için kullanılabilirler. Radyoaktif izotoplar bu amaç için en yararlı olanlardır. Radyoaktif izotopların çekirdekleri kararlı değildir. Radyasyon yayarlar ve sonunda parçalanırlar. Radyasyon, bir Geiger sayacı ile tespit edilebilir. Örneğin, karbonun radyoaktif izotopu olan Karbon-14, biyologların canlı hücrelerin içindeki birçok karmaşık reaksiyonda karbonun izlediği yolu takip etmelerine yardımcı olmuştur.

Doğada bulunan kimyasal elementlerin birçoğu, kararlı çekirdeklere sahip radyoaktif olmayan izotopların karışımlarından oluşur. Diğerleri ise radyoaktif izotoplardan oluşur. Ayrıca, tüm kimyasal elementlerin radyoaktif izotopları yapay olarak da üretilebilir. Bunlara radyoizotop denir.

Radyoizotopların en önemli kaynağı, uranyumun fisyonundan büyük miktarlarda bazı izotoplar üreten atom reaktörüdür. Diğer radyoizotoplar reaktörde uygun elementlerin nötronlarla bombardıman edilmesiyle, bazıları ise nükleer reaksiyonlarla üretilebilir.

passages.passage_text:
The word 'hypnosis' comes from the Greek word 'hypnos', which means 'sleep'. Although it is hard to define hypnosis, because it has many aspects and degrees, it might be said that hypnosis is a kind of trance (a sleeplike condition) in which the subject responds strongly to the suggestions of the hypnotist. It is difficult to know exactly what changes hypnotism produces in the functioning of the nervous system or the personality.

There are many theories on hypnosis, but no single theory is accepted as completely explaining all aspects of hypnosis. One of the oldest theories regards hypnosis to be a form of sleep. This concept originated in 1784, and was further developed by Ivan Pavlov. However, this theory is contradicted by evidence which indicates that the hypnotized person is not asleep: the knee reflex, which is absent in sleep, is present in the hypnotic state, and recordings of brain waves show the typical patterns of the state in which we are awake.

Methods of putting a subject into a trance have changed in recent years. Very few modern hypnotists use the old method of staring into the subject's eyes. Instead, they use methods which emphasize relaxing or even sleep. The subject sits in a comfortable chair while the hypnotist talks quietly, giving the subject directions and suggestions which lead him slowly into a trance. The hypnotist watches for signs for this state. For example, many subjects don't talk when they are in a trance. Instead of talking, they nod or shake their heads when they have to answer the questions the hypnotist asks them.

The hypnotic trance may be classified according to its degree, which depends partly on the hypnotist and partly on the subject. In a light trance, the eyes are closed, breathing becomes slower and the subject is able to carry out simple suggestions. The subject is usually unable to open his eyes or move his arms if the hypnotist tells him that he cannot.

In a medium-deep trance, the subject is able to experience feeling of movement even though he is not moving. After coming out of the trance, the subject may not remember what happened during the time he was in a trance.

In a deep trance, the hypnotist can produce very unusual effects. For example, he may tell the subject that, when he comes out of the trance, he will think that he sees a clock on the wall and that he will look at it and say it is midnight even though it's four o'clock in the afternoon. When he comes out of the trance, the subject will do what he is told to do, but he may not remember anything about what happened in the trance.

In contrast to many people who can be put into a deep trance quite easily, there are others who are not affected at all. The number of such people constitutes about 20% of the population, but this percentage may be higher among people who are 55 or older. Also, subjects who try too hard to fall into a trance may actually be difficult to hypnotize just like those who are afraid or suspicious of hypnosis or the hypnotist. People who resist the process can't be hypnotized either.

However, some experimenters have reported that it was easier to hypnotize people who did not know they were being hypnotized. These subjects were patients who needed treatment for various kinds of nervous conditions. They were simply told that the doctor would teach them how to relax.

Contrary to popular belief, there is no possibility of the subject not awakening as a result of an accident to the hypnotist. It is also not true that a hypnotized subject is completely under the will or power of the hypnotist.

passages.title: Trance
passages.tts_script:
Trance.

The word 'hypnosis' comes from the Greek word 'hypnos', which means 'sleep'. Although it is hard to define hypnosis, because it has many aspects and degrees, it might be said that hypnosis is a kind of trance, a sleeplike condition, in which the subject responds strongly to the suggestions of the hypnotist. It is difficult to know exactly what changes hypnotism produces in the functioning of the nervous system or the personality.

There are many theories on hypnosis, but no single theory is accepted as completely explaining all aspects of hypnosis. One of the oldest theories regards hypnosis to be a form of sleep. This concept originated in 1784, and was further developed by Ivan Pavlov. However, this theory is contradicted by evidence which indicates that the hypnotized person is not asleep: the knee reflex, which is absent in sleep, is present in the hypnotic state, and recordings of brain waves show the typical patterns of the state in which we are awake.

Methods of putting a subject into a trance have changed in recent years. Very few modern hypnotists use the old method of staring into the subject's eyes. Instead, they use methods which emphasize relaxing or even sleep. The subject sits in a comfortable chair while the hypnotist talks quietly, giving the subject directions and suggestions which lead him slowly into a trance. The hypnotist watches for signs for this state. For example, many subjects don't talk when they are in a trance. Instead of talking, they nod or shake their heads when they have to answer the questions the hypnotist asks them.

The hypnotic trance may be classified according to its degree, which depends partly on the hypnotist and partly on the subject. In a light trance, the eyes are closed, breathing becomes slower and the subject is able to carry out simple suggestions. The subject is usually unable to open his eyes or move his arms if the hypnotist tells him that he cannot.

In a medium-deep trance, the subject is able to experience feeling of movement even though he is not moving. After coming out of the trance, the subject may not remember what happened during the time he was in a trance.

In a deep trance, the hypnotist can produce very unusual effects. For example, he may tell the subject that, when he comes out of the trance, he will think that he sees a clock on the wall and that he will look at it and say it is midnight even though it's four o'clock in the afternoon. When he comes out of the trance, the subject will do what he is told to do, but he may not remember anything about what happened in the trance.

In contrast to many people who can be put into a deep trance quite easily, there are others who are not affected at all. The number of such people constitutes about 20 percent of the population, but this percentage may be higher among people who are 55 or older. Also, subjects who try too hard to fall into a trance may actually be difficult to hypnotize just like those who are afraid or suspicious of hypnosis or the hypnotist. People who resist the process can't be hypnotized either.

However, some experimenters have reported that it was easier to hypnotize people who did not know they were being hypnotized. These subjects were patients who needed treatment for various kinds of nervous conditions. They were simply told that the doctor would teach them how to relax.

Contrary to popular belief, there is no possibility of the subject not awakening as a result of an accident to the hypnotist. It is also not true that a hypnotized subject is completely under the will or power of the hypnotist.

task1.model_answer: Hypnosis is a sleeplike trance in which a person responds strongly to a hypnotist's suggestions, though its exact effects on the nervous system remain unclear. Although an early theory described it as a form of sleep, brain-wave patterns and the active knee reflex show that hypnotized people are actually awake. Modern hypnotists mainly use calm speech and relaxation rather than staring into the subject's eyes. Trances vary from light to deep: in deeper stages, subjects experience vivid illusions and may forget what happened. While about 20 percent of people cannot be hypnotized—especially those who resist, feel suspicious, or try too hard—patients unaware of the process often respond easily. task2.model_answer:
Medical hypnosis is increasingly discussed as a useful tool alongside conventional healthcare, particularly for managing anxiety, chronic pain, and stress-related conditions. Unlike stage performances, clinical hypnosis relies on relaxation and focused attention rather than dramatic control. As the passage explains, patients who simply learn to relax under a doctor's guidance often respond positively, and subjects remain safe and in control of their own will.

In my view, hypnosis can be a valuable complementary treatment when practiced by qualified medical or psychological professionals. Many people suffer from nervous conditions or phobias where medication alone may have side effects or limited success. Guided relaxation techniques can help these patients reduce fear and improve their daily well-being.

However, hypnosis should not replace evidence-based medical care for serious illnesses, nor does it work equally well for everyone. Roughly one-fifth of the population is unaffected, and skeptical individuals rarely respond. Therefore, hypnosis is best viewed as a helpful supportive therapy rather than a universal cure.

Trans.

'Hipnoz' kelimesi, 'uyku' anlamına gelen Yunanca 'hypnos' kelimesinden gelir. Pek çok yönü ve derecesi olduğu için hipnozu tanımlamak zor olsa da, hipnozun deneğin hipnozitörün telkinlerine güçlü bir şekilde yanıt verdiği, uykuya benzer bir tür trans durumu olduğu söylenebilir. Hipnotizmanın sinir sisteminin veya kişiliğin işleyişinde tam olarak ne gibi değişiklikler yarattığını bilmek zordur.

Hipnoz hakkında birçok teori vardır ancak tek bir teorinin hipnozun tüm yönlerini eksiksiz açıkladığı kabul edilmez. En eski teorilerden biri hipnozu bir uyku biçimi olarak görür. Bu kavram 1784 yılında ortaya çıkmış ve Ivan Pavlov tarafından daha da geliştirilmiştir. Ancak bu teori, hipnotize edilmiş kişinin uykuda olmadığını gösteren kanıtlarla çelişir: uykuda bulunmayan diz refleksi hipnotik durumda mevcuttur ve beyin dalgası kayıtları uyanık olduğumuz durumun tipik örüntülerini gösterir.

Bir deneği transa sokma yöntemleri son yıllarda değişmiştir. Günümüz hipnozitörlerinin çok azı deneğin gözlerinin içine dik dik bakma gibi eski yöntemi kullanır. Bunun yerine, rahatlamayı hatta uykuyu vurgulayan yöntemler kullanırlar. Denek rahat bir koltukta otururken hipnozitör alçak sesle konuşur, deneğe onu yavaşça transa götüren yönlendirmeler ve telkinler verir. Hipnozitör bu durumun belirtilerini gözlemler. Örneğin, birçok denek transteyken konuşmaz. Konuşmak yerine, hipnozitörün sorduğu soruları yanıtlamaları gerektiğinde başlarını aşağı yukarı sallar veya iki yana çevirirler.

Hipnotik trans, kısmen hipnozitöre ve kısmen de deneğe bağlı olarak derecesine göre sınıflandırılabilir. Hafif transta gözler kapalıdır, nefes alma yavaşlar ve denek basit telkinleri yerine getirebilir. Hipnozitör ona yapamayacağını söylerse, denek genellikle gözlerini açamaz veya kollarını hareket ettiremez.

Orta derinlikte bir transta denek, hareket etmemesine rağmen hareket hissi deneyimleyebilir. Transtan çıktıktan sonra denek, transteyken neler olduğunu hatırlamayabilir.

Derin bir transta hipnozitör çok sıra dışı etkiler yaratabilir. Örneğin deneğe, transtan çıktığında duvarda bir saat gördüğünü düşüneceğini, saate bakacağını ve öğleden sonra saat dört olmasına rağmen saatin gece yarısı olduğunu söyleyeceğini söyleyebilir. Denek transtan çıktığında kendisine söyleneni yapar ancak transteyken yaşananlara dair hiçbir şey hatırlamayabilir.

Oldukça kolay bir şekilde derin transa sokulabilen birçok insanın aksine, hiç etkilenmeyenler de vardır. Bu kişilerin sayısı nüfusun yaklaşık yüzde 20'sini oluşturur, ancak bu oran 55 yaş ve üzeri kişilerde daha yüksek olabilir. Ayrıca, transa girmek için aşırı çaba gösteren deneklerin hipnotize edilmesi, tıpkı hipnozdan veya hipnozitörden korkan ya da şüphe duyanlar gibi aslında zor olabilir. Sürece direnen kişiler de hipnotize edilemez.

Ancak bazı araştırmacılar, hipnotize edildiklerini bilmeyen kişileri hipnotize etmenin daha kolay olduğunu bildirmiştir. Bu denekler, çeşitli sinirsel rahatsızlıklar için tedaviye ihtiyaç duyan hastalardı. Kendilerine yalnızca doktorun onlara nasıl rahatlayacaklarını öğreteceği söylenmişti.

Yaygın inanışın aksine, hipnozitörün başına bir kaza gelmesi sonucu deneğin uyanmaması gibi bir ihtimal yoktur. Hipnotize edilmiş bir deneğin tamamen hipnozitörün iradesi veya gücü altında olduğu da doğru değildir.

passages.passage_text:
Until man invented ways of staying underwater for more than a few minutes, the wonders of the world below the sea were almost unknown. The main problem, of course, was air. How could air be supplied to swimmers below the surface of the sea? Pictures made about 2,900 years ago in Asia show men swimming under the surface with air bags tied to their bodies. A pipe from the bag carried air into the swimmer's mouth. Yet, little progress was made in the invention of diving devices until about 1490, when the famous Italian painter, Leonardo da Vinci, designed a complete diving suit.

In 1680, an Italian professor invented a large air bag with a glass window to be worn over the diver's head. To 'clean' the air, a breathing pipe went from the air bag, through another bag to remove moisture, and then again to the large air bag. The plan did not work, but it gave later inventors the idea of moving air around in diving devices.

In 1819, a German, Augustus Siebe, developed a way of forcing air into the head-covering by a machine operated above the water. Finally, in 1837 he invented the 'hard-hat suit', which was to be used for almost a century. It had a metal covering for the head and an air pipe attached to a machine above water. It also had small openings to remove unwanted air. But there were two dangers to the diver inside the hard-hat suit. One was a sudden rise to the surface, caused by too great a supply of air. The other was the crushing of the body, caused by a sudden dive into deep water. The sudden rise to the surface could kill the diver; a sudden dive could force his body up into the head covering, which could also result in death.

Gradually, the hard-hat suit was improved so that the diver could be given a constant supply of breathable air. The diver could then move around under the ocean without worrying about his air supply.

During the 1940's, diving underwater without a special suit became popular. Instead, divers used a breathing device and a face-mask, i.e., a small covering worn on the face made of rubber and glass. To increase the swimmers' speed another new invention was used: rubber shoes shaped like giant duck feet called flippers. The manufacture of snorkels, which are rubber breathing pipes, made it possible for the divers to float on the surface of the water, observing the marine life below them. A special rubber suit which prevented heat loss made diving comfortable enough to collect samples of plant and vegetable life even in icy waters.

The most important advance, however, was the invention of a self-contained underwater breathing apparatus, which is called a 'scuba'.

Invented by two Frenchmen, Jacques Yves Cousteau and Emile Gagnan, the scuba consists of a mouthpiece joined to one or two tanks of compressed air which are attached to the diver's back. The scuba makes it possible for a diver-scientist to work 200 feet underwater - or even deeper - for several hours. As a result, scientists can now move around freely at great depths, learning about the wonders of the sea.

task2.model_answer:
Technological advances in diving, particularly the invention of scuba gear, have transformed ocean exploration from a dangerous curiosity into a vital scientific field. As the passage notes, carrying compressed air allows researchers to work hundreds of feet underwater for hours, observing marine life and collecting samples in freezing waters.

I strongly believe that continuing to fund underwater exploration is worthwhile. The oceans cover most of our planet and play a central role in regulating the global climate, producing oxygen, and supporting biodiversity. Without direct observation and sampling at great depths, scientists would miss crucial data about changing ocean temperatures, coral ecosystems, and undiscovered species that could inspire future medicines.

Of course, deep-sea exploration carries serious physical risks and requires expensive safety equipment. passages.tts_script_tr:
Su Altında Kalmak.

İnsanoğlu su altında birkaç dakikadan fazla kalmanın yollarını icat edene kadar, denizlerin altındaki dünyanın harikaları neredeyse hiç bilinmiyordu. Elbette temel sorun havaydı. Deniz yüzeyinin altındaki yüzücülere nasıl hava sağlanabilirdi? Yaklaşık 2.900 yıl önce Asya'da yapılmış resimler, vücutlarına hava torbaları bağlayarak su yüzeyinin altında yüzen insanları göstermektedir. Torbadan çıkan bir boru yüzücünün ağzına hava taşıyordu. Yine de, ünlü İtalyan ressam Leonardo da Vinci'nin yaklaşık 1490 yılında eksiksiz bir dalış kıyafeti tasarlamasına kadar dalış cihazlarının icadında çok az ilerleme kaydedildi.

1680 yılında İtalyan bir profesör, dalgıcın başına geçirilen ve cam bir penceresi olan büyük bir hava torbası icat etti. Havayı 'temizlemek' için bir solunum borusu hava torbasından çıkıp nemi gidermek üzere başka bir torbadan geçiyor ve ardından tekrar büyük hava torbasına dönüyordu. Plan işe yaramadı, ancak daha sonraki mucitlere dalış cihazlarında havayı dolaştırma fikrini verdi.

1819'da Augustus Siebe adlı bir Alman, su üstünde çalıştırılan bir makine aracılığıyla başlığın içine hava basmanın bir yolunu geliştirdi. Nihayet 1837'de neredeyse bir yüzyıl boyunca kullanılacak olan 'sert başlıklı dalış kıyafetini' icat etti. Baş için metal bir kapağı ve su üstündeki bir makineye bağlı bir hava borusu vardı. Ayrıca istenmeyen havayı dışarı atmak için küçük açıklıklara da sahipti. Ancak sert başlıklı kıyafetin içindeki dalgıç için iki tehlike bulunuyordu. Biri, aşırı hava verilmesinden kaynaklanan yüzeye ani yükselişti. Diğeri ise derin suya ani dalışın yol açtığı vücut ezilmesiydi. Yüzeye ani yükseliş dalgıcı öldürebilirdi; ani bir dalış ise vücudunu yukarı doğru başlığın içine itebilirdi ki bu da ölümle sonuçlanabilirdi.

Zamanla sert başlıklı dalış kıyafeti, dalgıca sürekli solunabilir hava sağlanabilecek şekilde geliştirildi. Böylece dalgıç hava kaynağı konusunda endişelenmeden okyanus altında hareket edebiliyordu.

1940'larda özel bir kıyafet olmadan su altına dalmak popüler hale geldi. Bunun yerine dalgıçlar bir solunum cihazı ve yüz maskesi, yani kauçuk ve camdan yapılıp yüze takılan küçük bir koruyucu kullanıyordu. Yüzücülerin hızını artırmak için yeni bir icat daha kullanıldı: palet adı verilen, dev ördek ayakları şeklindeki kauçuk ayakkabılar. Kauçuk solunum boruları olan şnorkellerin üretimi, dalgıçların su yüzeyinde yüzerek altlarındaki deniz yaşamını gözlemlemelerini mümkün kıldı. Isı kaybını önleyen özel bir kauçuk kıyafet ise buzlu sularda bile bitkisel yaşam örnekleri toplamayı yeterince konforlu hale getirdi.

Ancak en önemli gelişme, 'scuba' adı verilen bağımsız bir su altı solunum cihazının icadı oldu.

İki Fransız, Jacques Yves Cousteau ve Emile Gagnan tarafından icat edilen scuba, dalgıcın sırtına bağlanan bir veya iki basınçlı hava tüpüne bağlı bir ağızlıktan oluşur. Scuba, bir bilim insanı-dalgıcın 200 fit su altında, hatta daha derinde birkaç saat boyunca çalışmasını mümkün kılar. Sonuç olarak, bilim insanları artık büyük derinliklerde serbestçe dolaşarak denizin harikaları hakkında bilgi edinebilmektedir.

passages.passage_text:
When plants and animals die, they normally decay, helped along by fungi and bacteria in the environment. Once decomposed, they provide nutrients for living organisms, and the respiration of fungi and bacteria causing decay releases carbon dioxide into the atmosphere.

Over a period of several hundred million years, however, comparatively small amounts of organic material have remained under layers of silt, soil or volcanic rock and, as there is no oxygen, have not fully decomposed. Instead, they have formed deposits of coal, natural gas and oil, often located far below the land surface or the sea-bed.

Oil is usually found in porous rock under a layer of hard rock which prevents it from escaping. It can, then, only be reached by drilling. The initial rush of oil out of a drill pipe is caused by the pressure of the gas compressed immediately above the oil deposits. In time, this pressure decreases and the oil has to be pumped to the surface.

Raising oil from below the sea-bed is an immensely difficult and dangerous operation. Although drilling engineers are exposed to high winds and heavy seas, they have to make test bores to see if it is worth exploring further. After they are satisfied that they have found an oilfield, they set up a platform. The quality of the oil which is piped up to the surface varies, but it all has to be brought ashore. This is done either by pumping it along pipelines or carrying it in tankers. In the North Sea, as they are constantly threatened by the weather, the big oil companies have, on the whole, preferred pipelines. In other locations, where they are favoured by better weather conditions, they often use tankers.

The crude oil raised directly from wells is not yet ready for use. It has to be refined. The first stage in this process is fractional distillation in a fractionating column. Those fractions, such as petrol and kerosene, which are lighter and more volatile, move towards the top of the column before condensing. The heavy residual fuel at the base of the column is extremely impure.

The fractional distillation of crude oil results in the production of several useful substances, all of them normally liquids except the gas from the top of the column and the solid residue at the base. Straight petrol, which vaporizes between 30° and 200° Centigrade, is used (when mixed with petrol produced from kerosene and heavy gas oil) as fuel for motor cars. The gas, which boils between 20° and 164°C, also has a use - many households rely on it for heating and cooking. Kerosene has, of course, become invaluable as the fuel consumed by jet planes. It boils between 200° and 300°C, whereas heavy gas oil and fuel oil vaporize within the range 300°C. The former is used to produce diesel fuel for lorries, buses and some cars, and the latter is redistilled to produce other fractions. The heavier fractions, such as petroleum jelly and paraffin, the former with a boiling point over 350°C and the latter with a melting point between 52° and 57°C, have a variety of uses. Petroleum jelly is a useful lubricant and is used on the skin, and paraffin is the main component of wax candles. The pitch and tar at the bottom of the column, which boil at over 430°C, are used to make asphalt. So, there is little wastage.

But distillation does not produce enough high grade petrol to meet today's high demand. The petrol offered for sale to motorists is a mixture of straight petrol and distilled petrol produced by chemical modification from certain other distillates.

task1.model_answer: Crude oil originates from ancient organic matter trapped without oxygen beneath layers of rock and silt for millions of years. Because it lies in porous rock beneath hard rock, engineers must drill to reach it, often working from offshore platforms in harsh marine environments. Once brought ashore by pipeline or tanker, the crude oil undergoes fractional distillation in a column. Lighter, more volatile fractions such as gas, petrol, and kerosene rise and condense near the top, whereas heavier substances like diesel oil, petroleum jelly, paraffin, and asphalt-forming pitch remain lower down. Finally, because distillation alone cannot satisfy modern demand for high-grade petrol, straight petrol is blended with chemically modified distillates for motorists.

task2.model_answer:
Crude oil has undeniably shaped the modern world, powering transportation, heating homes, and supplying raw materials for countless everyday products. However, societies today face a critical dilemma: while global economies remain deeply dependent on petroleum, extracting and burning fossil fuels carries severe environmental costs.

On the one hand, as the refining process illustrates, crude oil is remarkably versatile and efficient. Nearly every fraction has a practical application, from jet fuel and motor petrol to household gas, lubricants, and road asphalt, leaving very little industrial waste. Moreover, existing energy infrastructure is built around these fuels, making an immediate transition difficult.

On the other hand, offshore drilling poses serious safety and ecological risks, and the combustion of refined fuels releases vast amounts of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere, accelerating climate change. Therefore, while oil remains indispensable in the short term, governments and industries must invest steadily in renewable energy and cleaner technologies to reduce our long-term dependence on petroleum.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Petrolün Damıtılması.

Bitkiler ve hayvanlar öldüğünde, çevredeki mantarların ve bakterilerin yardımıyla normal olarak çürürler. Ayrıştıktan sonra canlı organizmalar için besin sağlarlar ve çürümeye neden olan mantarların ve bakterilerin solunumu atmosfere karbondioksit salar.

Ancak birkaç yüz milyon yıllık bir dönem boyunca, nispeten küçük miktarlarda organik madde mil, toprak veya volkanik kayaç katmanlarının altında kalmış ve oksijen olmadığı için tam olarak ayrışmamıştır. Bunun yerine, genellikle kara yüzeyinin veya deniz tabanının çok altında bulunan kömür, doğal gaz ve petrol yataklarını oluşturmuşlardır.

Petrol genellikle kaçmasını önleyen sert bir kayaç katmanının altındaki gözenekli kayaçta bulunur. Bu nedenle ona yalnızca sondajla ulaşılabilir. Sondaj borusundan ilk petrol fışkırması, petrol yataklarının hemen üzerinde sıkışmış olan gazın basıncından kaynaklanır. Zamanla bu basınç azalır ve petrolün yüzeye pompalanması gerekir.

Deniz tabanının altından petrol çıkarmak son derece zor ve tehlikeli bir işlemdir. Sondaj mühendisleri şiddetli rüzgarlara ve hırçın denizlere maruz kalsalar da, daha fazla araştırmaya değip değmeyeceğini görmek için deneme sondajları yapmak zorundadırlar. Bir petrol sahası bulduklarından emin olduktan sonra bir platform kurarlar. Borularla yüzeye çıkarılan petrolün kalitesi değişkenlik gösterir, ancak tamamının kıyıya ulaştırılması gerekir. Bu işlem ya boru hatlarıyla pompalanarak ya da tankerlerle taşınarak yapılır. Kuzey Denizi'nde hava koşulları tarafından sürekli tehdit edildikleri için büyük petrol şirketleri genel olarak boru hatlarını tercih etmiştir. Daha iyi hava koşullarının bulunduğu diğer yerlerde ise genellikle tankerleri kullanırlar.

Kuyulardan doğrudan çıkarılan ham petrol henüz kullanıma hazır değildir. Rafine edilmesi gerekir. Bu süreçteki ilk aşama, bir damıtma kolonunda yapılan ayrımsal damıtmadır. Benzin ve gazyağı gibi daha hafif ve daha uçucu olan fraksiyonlar, yoğunlaşmadan önce kolonun üst kısmına doğru hareket eder. Kolonun tabanındaki ağır kalıntı yakıt ise son derece safsızdır.

Ham petrolün ayrımsal damıtılması, kolonun üstünden çıkan gaz ve tabandaki katı kalıntı dışında normalde hepsi sıvı olan birkaç yararlı maddenin elde edilmesini sağlar. 30 ile 200 santigrat derece arasında buharlaşan ham benzin, gazyağı ve ağır gaz yağından üretilen benzinle karıştırıldığında motorlu taşıtlar için yakıt olarak kullanılır. 20 ile 164 santigrat derece arasında kaynayan gazın da bir kullanım alanı vardır; zira birçok hane ısınma ve yemek pişirme için buna güvenir. Gazyağı elbette jet uçaklarının tükettiği yakıt olarak vazgeçilmez hale gelmiştir. 200 ile 300 santigrat derece arasında kaynarken, ağır gaz yağı ve fuel oil 300 santigrat derece aralığında buharlaşır. İlki kamyonlar, otobüsler ve bazı otomobiller için dizel yakıt üretmek amacıyla kullanılır; ikincisi ise başka fraksiyonlar elde etmek için yeniden damıtılır. İlki 350 santigrat derecenin üzerinde kaynama noktasına, ikincisi ise 52 ile 57 santigrat derece arasında erime noktasına sahip olan vazelin ve parafin gibi daha ağır fraksiyonların çeşitli kullanım alanları vardır. Vazelin yararlı bir yağlayıcıdır ve cilt üzerinde kullanılır; parafin ise mumların ana bileşenidir. Kolonun dibinde bulunan ve 430 santigrat derecenin üzerinde kaynayan zift ve katran ise asfalt yapımında kullanılır. Dolayısıyla çok az atık oluşur.

Ancak damıtma, günümüzün yüksek talebini karşılayacak kadar yüksek kaliteli benzin üretmez. Sürücülere satışa sunulan benzin, ham benzin ile belirli diğer damıtık ürünlerden kimyasal modifikasyon yoluyla üretilen damıtılmış benzinin bir karışımıdır.

passages.passage_text:
A striking example of how man can drastically alter the interdependence patterns of ocean life has occurred off the coasts of southern California. In the nineteenth century, these waters had a large population of that busy little animal called the sea otter, which ate sea urchins, which, in turn, fed on large brown algae called kelp. Sea otters almost totally disappeared due to fur traders who encouraged hunters to kill off otters for their valuable furs. With the disappearance of the otter, sea urchins started to reproduce in vast numbers, leading to a great increase in their population. This caused sea urchins to almost entirely exhaust kelp beds. At this point, man had replaced the original balance of nature with a new pattern: The sea urchins, which previously had been the prey of the sea otter, had become the predator and the kelp had become the new prey. As the kelp began to disappear, sea urchins began to starve. With the reduction of the urchin population, the kelp managed to reproduce and increase their numbers. Yet, the sea urchins again increased and so on. A cycle taking from 10 to 12 years started to repeat itself.

A further step came when sewage pollution caused an additional destruction of kelp - not because sewage kills kelp but because sewage feeds sea urchins, which once again increased in numbers with this new source of food. If sea otters had been present in sufficient quantities, the kelp beds would still be abundant. In order to re-establish the proper balance in the ecosystem, marine biologists have put forward a number of solutions. In time and with the help of man, nature may regain its previous order.

passages.title: Patterns of Ocean Life
passages.tts_script:
Patterns of Ocean Life.

A striking example of how man can drastically alter the interdependence patterns of ocean life has occurred off the coasts of southern California. In the nineteenth century, these waters had a large population of that busy little animal called the sea otter, which ate sea urchins, which, in turn, fed on large brown algae called kelp. Sea otters almost totally disappeared due to fur traders who encouraged hunters to kill off otters for their valuable furs. With the disappearance of the otter, sea urchins started to reproduce in vast numbers, leading to a great increase in their population. This caused sea urchins to almost entirely exhaust kelp beds. At this point, man had replaced the original balance of nature with a new pattern: The sea urchins, which previously had been the prey of the sea otter, had become the predator and the kelp had become the new prey. As the kelp began to disappear, sea urchins began to starve. With the reduction of the urchin population, the kelp managed to reproduce and increase their numbers. Yet, the sea urchins again increased and so on. A cycle taking from 10 to 12 years started to repeat itself.

A further step came when sewage pollution caused an additional destruction of kelp, not because sewage kills kelp, but because sewage feeds sea urchins, which once again increased in numbers with this new source of food. If sea otters had been present in sufficient quantities, the kelp beds would still be abundant. In order to re-establish the proper balance in the ecosystem, marine biologists have put forward a number of solutions. In time and with the help of man, nature may regain its previous order.

task1.model_answer: Off the coast of southern California, human activity severely disrupted a natural marine food chain. Originally, sea otters controlled the population of sea urchins, which fed on giant brown algae known as kelp. When fur hunters nearly wiped out the sea otters in the nineteenth century, sea urchins multiplied rapidly and overgrazed the kelp beds. This triggered a repeating 10-to-12-year cycle of urchin starvation followed by kelp recovery and renewed urchin growth. Later, sewage pollution worsened the situation by providing sea urchins with an extra food source, further damaging kelp populations. Marine biologists are now proposing strategies to restore this damaged ecosystem.

task2.model_answer:
Ecosystems are intricate networks in which every species plays a vital role, and human interference often triggers unintended consequences. The case of southern California's kelp forests demonstrates how removing a single predator can destabilize an entire marine habitat. When sea otters were hunted for fur, the unchecked growth of sea urchins devastated kelp beds, and urban sewage later compounded the problem.

Nevertheless, human beings also possess the scientific knowledge required to repair ecological damage. Rather than passively observing environmental decline, society has a responsibility to intervene thoughtfully. Practical measures—such as protecting endangered keystone species, strictly regulating coastal waste and sewage discharge, and supporting marine restoration projects led by biologists—can help habitats recover.

Ultimately, protecting ocean ecosystems benefits humanity as well, since healthy marine environments sustain biodiversity, fisheries, and coastal stability. While nature has remarkable resilience, restoring balance often depends on responsible human stewardship and long-term environmental policies.

Okyanus Yaşamının Örüntüleri.

İnsanoğlunun okyanus yaşamındaki karşılıklı bağımlılık örüntülerini nasıl köklü bir şekilde değiştirebileceğinin çarpıcı bir örneği, güney Kaliforniya kıyılarında yaşanmıştır. On dokuzuncu yüzyılda bu sularda, denizkestanesi yiyen ve deniz su samuru adı verilen o hareketli küçük hayvandan büyük bir popülasyon bulunuyordu; denizkestaneleri de kelp adı verilen büyük kahverengi alglerle besleniyordu. Deniz su samurları, değerli kürkleri için avcıları su samurlarını öldürmeye teşvik eden kürk tüccarları yüzünden neredeyse tamamen yok oldu. Su samurlarının ortadan kaybolmasıyla birlikte denizkestaneleri çok büyük sayılarda üremeye başladı ve bu da popülasyonlarında büyük bir artışa yol açtı. Bu durum, denizkestanelerinin kelp yataklarını neredeyse tamamen tüketmesine neden oldu. Bu noktada insan, doğanın özgün dengesinin yerine yeni bir düzen getirmişti: Daha önce deniz su samurunun avı olan denizkestaneleri avcı konumuna geçmiş, kelp ise yeni av olmuştu. Kelp yok olmaya başladıkça denizkestaneleri aç kalmaya başladı. Denizkestanesi popülasyonunun azalmasıyla birlikte kelp yeniden üreyip sayıca artmayı başardı. Ancak denizkestaneleri tekrar çoğaldı ve bu böyle devam etti. 10 ila 12 yıl süren bir döngü kendini tekrar etmeye başladı.

Bir sonraki aşama ise kanalizasyon kirliliğinin kelpte ek bir tahribata yol açmasıyla geldi; bunun nedeni kanalizasyonun kelpi öldürmesi değil, denizkestanelerini beslemesiydi ve denizkestaneleri bu yeni besin kaynağıyla bir kez daha sayıca arttı. Eğer yeterli sayıda deniz su samuru mevcut olsaydı, kelp yatakları hâlâ bol miktarda olurdu. Ekosistemdeki doğru dengeyi yeniden kurmak amacıyla deniz biyologları bir dizi çözüm önerisi ortaya koymuştur. Zamanla ve insanın yardımıyla doğa eski düzenine yeniden kavuşabilir.

passages.passage_text:
When we are young, the house where we live is our whole world. Everything is provided for us - food and shelter, warmth and love. We obey our parents without question, because if mummy and daddy say it, it must be right. Every experience we have is classified as good or bad according to their reaction. We quickly learn to do those things which earn their praise, and to avoid doing those things which upset them and earn their disapproval.

As we grow older, we are more and more exposed to outside influences - school, friends and other adults. We soon start to realise that there are other values which are different from those our parents hold. For example, your parents have told you that some words, such as 'bloody', are swear words, and they have forbidden you to use them. However, in your friend's house, everyone - children and grown-ups - says things like 'Bloody hell!' when they are annoyed and no-one seems to think that there is anything wrong with it. You are confused; you wonder what the right thing to do is. You try to resolve the conflict of values between two groups of people - your parents on the one hand, and your friend's parents on the other - for whom you have equal respect. Eventually what happens is that we start to lead double lives; we reserve some forms of behaviour for the home, and others for the world outside the home.

The real conflict starts when we reach adolescence. We begin to question everything and everyone, including our parents and their values, because we want to establish our own independent values. Unfortunately, as long as we are living at home and are dependent on our parents, we cannot lead our own lives according to our own views of right and wrong. The trouble is that if our parents give us more freedom, we are bound to make mistakes, and they will wonder if they have given us too much freedom. On the other hand, if parents allow too little freedom, their teenage children are likely to become resentful and rebellious.

Somewhere between the two extremes, it ought to be possible to find a sort of 'democratic' alternative, which allows children the freedom to grow up and to make their own decisions, including mistakes, but which also offers them help and protection when they need it.

task1.model_answer: As children grow up, their understanding of right and wrong changes significantly. In early childhood, parents shape their entire world, and children obey without question to receive praise and avoid disapproval. Later, school and friends introduce new values that may clash with home rules, leading young people to behave differently inside and outside the house. During adolescence, teenagers begin questioning their parents' beliefs in order to build independence. Because they still rely on their families, too much freedom can lead to mistakes, while excessive control causes resentment. Therefore, the passage recommends a balanced, democratic approach that grants teenagers independence while continuing to offer guidance and protection.

task2.model_answer:
Raising teenagers requires a careful balance between granting independence and maintaining reasonable boundaries. While some parents believe strict rules protect adolescents from serious mistakes, excessive control often produces the opposite effect.

When teenagers are given no room to make personal choices, they may feel distrusted and become resentful or rebellious, hiding their actions rather than learning from them. On the other hand, complete freedom without supervision can leave young people overwhelmed when they face unfamiliar social pressures or difficult decisions.

A democratic approach works best because it respects adolescents' growing need for autonomy while keeping supportive guidance in place. By allowing teenagers to choose their friends, manage their study habits, and even experience minor failures, parents help them build responsibility and confidence. At the same time, open communication ensures that young people still know where to turn when they genuinely need help and protection.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Büyümek.

Küçükken yaşadığımız ev bizim tüm dünyamızdır. Bizim için her şey sağlanır: yiyecek ve barınak, sıcaklık ve sevgi. Anne ve babamıza sorgusuz sualsiz itaat ederiz çünkü anne ve baba bir şey söylüyorsa o mutlaka doğrudur. Yaşadığımız her deneyim, onların tepkisine göre iyi ya da kötü olarak sınıflandırılır. Onların övgüsünü kazandıran şeyleri yapmayı, onları üzen ve onaylamadıkları şeyleri yapmaktan ise kaçınmayı çabucak öğreniriz.

Büyüdükçe dış etkilere giderek daha fazla maruz kalırız: okul, arkadaşlar ve diğer yetişkinler. Çok geçmeden, anne ve babamızın benimsediği değerlerden farklı başka değerlerin de olduğunu fark etmeye başlarız. Örneğin anne ve babanız size 'bloody' gibi bazı kelimelerin küfür olduğunu söylemiş ve bunları kullanmanızı yasaklamıştır. Ancak arkadaşınızın evinde çocuklar ve yetişkinler dahil herkes sinirlendiğinde 'Bloody hell!' ('Lanet olsun!') gibi şeyler söyler ve kimse bunda yanlış bir şey olduğunu düşünmez. Kafanız karışır; yapılacak doğru şeyin ne olduğunu merak edersiniz. Bir yanda kendi anne ve babanız, diğer yanda arkadaşınızın anne ve babası olmak üzere eşit derecede saygı duyduğunuz iki grup insan arasındaki değer çatışmasını çözmeye çalışırsınız. Sonunda olan şey, ikili bir yaşam sürmeye başlamamızdır; bazı davranış biçimlerini ev için, diğerlerini ise ev dışındaki dünya için ayırırız.

Asıl çatışma ergenliğe ulaştığımızda başlar. Kendi bağımsız değerlerimizi oluşturmak istediğimiz için, anne ve babamız ve onların değerleri de dahil olmak üzere her şeyi ve herkesi sorgulamaya başlarız. Ne yazık ki evde yaşadığımız ve anne ve babamıza bağımlı olduğumuz sürece, kendi doğru ve yanlış anlayışımıza göre kendi hayatımızı yaşayamayız. Sorun şu ki, anne ve babamız bize daha fazla özgürlük verirse hata yapmamız kaçınılmaz olur ve onlar da bize fazla mı özgürlük verdiklerini sorgularlar. Öte yandan, ebeveynler çok az özgürlük tanırsa ergenlik çağındaki çocuklarının kırgın ve asi hale gelmesi muhtemeldir.

Bu iki uç arasında bir yerde, çocuklara büyümeleri ve hatalar da dahil olmak üzere kendi kararlarını vermeleri için özgürlük tanıyan, ama aynı zamanda ihtiyaç duyduklarında onlara yardım ve koruma sunan bir tür 'demokratik' alternatif bulmak mümkün olmalıdır.

passages.passage_text:
Loneliness is a curious thing. Most of us can remember feeling most lonely when we were not in fact lonely at all, but when we were surrounded by people. Everyone has experienced, at some time, that utter sense of isolation that comes over you when you are at a party. It suddenly seems to you as if everybody knows everybody; everybody, that is, except you.

This feeling of loneliness, which can overcome you when you are in a crowd, is very difficult to get rid of. People living alone are advised to tackle their loneliness by joining a club or a society, by going out and meeting people. Does this really help?

There are no easy solutions. Your first day at work or at a new school is a typical situation in which you are likely to feel lonely. You feel lonely because you feel left out of things. You feel that everybody else is full of confidence and knows what to do, but you are helpless. The fact of the matter is that, in order to survive, we all put on a show of self-confidence to hide our uncertainties and doubts. Therefore, it is wrong to assume that you are alone.

The trouble is that you may not be able to hide the fact that you are lonely, and the miserable look on your face might put people off. Thus, trying to look reasonably cheerful is a good starting point to combat loneliness.

The next thing to avoid is finding yourself in a group where you are a stranger; that is, you are in the sort of group where all the people already know each other. There is a natural tendency for people to stick together. You will do yourself no good by trying to establish yourself in a group which has so far managed to do very well without you. Groups generally resent intrusion, not because they dislike you personally, but because they have already had to work quite hard to turn the group into a functioning unit. To include you means having to go over a lot of ground again, so that you can learn their 'language' and get involved in their conversation at their level. In fact, the surest way of getting to know others is to have an interest in common with them. There is no guarantee that you will then like each other, but at least part of your life will be filled with sharing experiences with others. It is much better than feeling alone. If all this seems to be a rather pessimistic view of life, you have to accept the fact that we are all actually alone and that loneliness is sometimes unavoidable.

task2.model_answer:
Many people believe that simply joining a club or attending social events is enough to cure loneliness, yet this advice often overlooks the emotional complexity of building real connections. Being physically present in a crowd does not automatically create a sense of belonging.

On one hand, participating in structured activities can help when members share a genuine interest, such as a sport, book club, or volunteer project. Shared goals naturally spark conversation and reduce the awkwardness of meeting strangers. On the other hand, walking into a society where tight friendships already exist can leave newcomers feeling even more excluded if they expect instant acceptance.

In my view, joining a club is only a useful first step, not a guaranteed solution. Meaningful relationships require time, openness, and mutual effort. Approaching new environments with realistic expectations and a willingness to engage around common interests makes it far easier to turn casual encounters into genuine companionship.
