passages.tts_script_tr:
Yalnızlık.

Yalnızlık tuhaf bir şeydir. Çoğumuz, aslında hiç de yalnız olmadığımız, aksine insanlarla çevrili olduğumuz anlarda kendimizi en yalnız hissettiğimizi hatırlayabiliriz. Herkes bir zamanlar, bir partideyken insanın üzerine çöken o tam bir soyutlanmışlık duygusunu yaşamıştır. Birdenbire size herkes herkesi tanıyormuş gibi gelir; yani siz hariç herkesi.

Bir kalabalığın içindeyken sizi ele geçirebilen bu yalnızlık duygusundan kurtulmak çok zordur. Yalnız yaşayan insanlara, bir kulübe veya derneğe katılarak, dışarı çıkıp insanlarla tanışarak yalnızlıklarıyla başa çıkmaları tavsiye edilir. Bu gerçekten işe yarar mı?

Kolay çözümler yoktur. İşteki veya yeni bir okuldaki ilk gününüz, kendinizi yalnız hissetmenizin muhtemel olduğu tipik bir durumdur. Kendinizi yalnız hissedersiniz çünkü olayların dışında bırakılmış hissedersiniz. Diğer herkesin özgüvenle dolu olduğunu ve ne yapacağını bildiğini, kendinizin ise çaresiz olduğunu hissedersiniz. İşin aslı şu ki, ayakta kalabilmek için hepimiz belirsizliklerimizi ve şüphelerimizi gizlemek adına bir özgüven gösterisi sergileriz. Bu nedenle, yalnız olduğunuzu varsaymak yanlıştır.

Sorun şu ki, yalnız olduğunuz gerçeğini gizleyemeyebilirsiniz ve yüzünüzdeki mutsuz ifade insanları sizden uzaklaştırabilir. Dolayısıyla, makul ölçüde neşeli görünmeye çalışmak yalnızlıkla mücadele etmek için iyi bir başlangıç noktasıdır.

Kaçınmanız gereken bir sonraki şey, yabancı olduğunuz bir grubun içinde kalmaktır; yani herkesin birbirini zaten tanıdığı türden bir grupta bulunmaktır. İnsanların bir arada kalmaya yönelik doğal bir eğilimi vardır. Şimdiye kadar sizsiz de gayet iyi idare etmiş bir grupta kendinize yer edinmeye çalışarak kendinize hiçbir iyilik yapmış olmazsınız. Gruplar genellikle dışarıdan birinin dahil olmasından rahatsızlık duyar; bunun nedeni kişisel olarak sizden hoşlanmamaları değil, grubu işleyen bir bütün haline getirmek için zaten oldukça çok çaba harcamış olmalarıdır. Sizi gruba dahil etmek, onların 'dilini' öğrenmeniz ve sohbetlerine onların seviyesinde katılabilmeniz için pek çok konunun üzerinden tekrar geçmek zorunda kalmaları anlamına gelir. Aslında başkalarını tanımanın en garanti yolu, onlarla ortak bir ilgi alanına sahip olmaktır. O zaman birbirinizden hoşlanacağınızın garantisi yoktur, ancak en azından hayatınızın bir kısmı başkalarıyla deneyimler paylaşarak dolacaktır. Bu, kendini yalnız hissetmekten çok daha iyidir. Eğer bütün bunlar hayata oldukça karamsar bir bakış açısı gibi görünüyorsa, aslında hepimizin yalnız olduğu ve yalnızlığın bazen kaçınılmaz olduğu gerçeğini kabullenmeniz gerekir.

passages.passage_text:
One of the first things we try to find out about people is what their job is. It helps us to define their status. We can judge where they stand socially, and estimate how much they earn. However, it is more interesting to know how a man comes to choose his job than what he does.

The trouble is that we often choose a career for the wrong reasons. Take, for instance, those people who 'follow in father's footsteps', either entering the same trade or profession, or inheriting the family business. John decides to become a doctor because his father was a doctor. In fact, the word 'decides' is too strong; he probably never even thought about it. Funnily enough, some people make the opposite decision, namely that whatever else they might do, they will certainly not do what their father did. Our teachers are the first to persuade us to choose a specific career, probably because we are top students in that subject. We may also be persuaded by people whom we admire to select a career for which we are unsuited.

The attitude of our parents toward our choice of career is interesting. They are quite pleased when we announce our intention to study medicine, disappointed when we switch to languages and overjoyed when we finally start to study law. Clearly, they have a definite idea of the benefits different jobs will bring. Even though they appear to leave the choice entirely to their children, they know that their children will eventually respect their wishes.

Apart from these pressures from parents, teachers and other people, we may choose a career due to factors such as the attractiveness of the profession or the prospect of earning a lot of money in a short time. It ought to be easy to choose a career. We only have to do those things for which we have a natural talent. It is a pity, therefore, that we have to decide about our future at a stage in our lives when we can easily be influenced by factors which have little or nothing to do with the main issue.

Additionally, young people are frequently tempted by glamour or the promise of quick wealth. task2.model_answer:
Choosing a career is one of the most important decisions young people face, and following natural talent is far more reliable than chasing prestige or money. While high income and social status appear attractive at first, they rarely bring long-term satisfaction if a person dislikes the daily work.

For example, a student who has a natural gift for languages or design may feel pressured by parents to study law or medicine because those professions seem secure and respected. However, working for decades in an unsuitable field often leads to stress, burnout, and poor performance. By contrast, when individuals build careers around their genuine strengths, they learn faster, stay motivated, and are more likely to excel—which often brings financial stability over time as well.

Although practical factors like job security cannot be completely ignored, natural ability and personal interest should come first when choosing a future profession.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Kariyer Seçimi.

İnsanlar hakkında öğrenmeye çalıştığımız ilk şeylerden biri mesleklerinin ne olduğudur. Bu, onların statüsünü belirlememize yardımcı olur. Sosyal olarak nerede durduklarını değerlendirebilir ve ne kadar kazandıklarını tahmin edebiliriz. Ancak bir insanın ne iş yaptığından ziyade, işini nasıl seçtiğini bilmek daha ilginçtir.

Sorun şu ki, çoğu zaman yanlış nedenlerle kariyer seçimi yaparız. Örneğin, ya aynı zanaat veya mesleğe girerek ya da aile işini devralarak 'babasının izinden giden' insanları ele alalım. John, babası doktor olduğu için doktor olmaya karar verir. Aslında 'karar verir' kelimesi fazla iddialı kaçar; muhtemelen bunun üzerine hiç düşünmemiştir bile. Tuhaf bir şekilde, bazı insanlar bunun tam tersi bir karar alırlar; yani başka ne yaparlarsa yapsınlar, kesinlikle babalarının yaptığı işi yapmayacaklardır. Bizi belirli bir kariyeri seçmeye ikna eden ilk kişiler, muhtemelen o derste en başarılı öğrenciler olmamız nedeniyle öğretmenlerimizdir. Hayranlık duyduğumuz kişiler tarafından da bize uygun olmayan bir kariyeri seçmeye ikna edilebiliriz.

Anne ve babamızın kariyer seçimimize karşı tutumu ilginçtir. Tıp okuma niyetimizi açıkladığımızda oldukça memnun olurlar, dillere geçtiğimizde hayal kırıklığına uğrarlar ve sonunda hukuk okumaya başladığımızda sevinçten havalara uçarlar. Açıkçası, farklı mesleklerin getireceği faydalar konusunda kesin bir fikirleri vardır. Seçimi tamamen çocuklarına bırakıyor gibi görünseler de, çocuklarının sonunda kendi isteklerine saygı duyacağını bilirler.

Anne ve babadan, öğretmenlerden ve diğer insanlardan gelen bu baskıların yanı sıra, mesleğin cazibesi veya kısa sürede çok para kazanma ihtimali gibi etkenler nedeniyle de bir kariyer seçebiliriz. Kariyer seçmek kolay olmalıdır. Tek yapmamız gereken, doğal yeteneğimizin olduğu şeyleri yapmaktır. Bu nedenle, geleceğimiz hakkında hayatımızın, asıl meseleyle pek az ilgisi olan ya da hiç ilgisi olmayan etkenlerden kolayca etkilenebileceğimiz bir döneminde karar vermek zorunda olmamız üzücüdür.

passages.passage_text:
The human body is made up mainly of bone, muscle and fat. Some 639 different muscles make up about 45 per cent of the body weight. Each of these muscles has four different and measurable qualities. It can produce force which can be measured as strength of muscle. It can also store energy which permits it to work for extended periods of time independent of circulation. In addition, a muscle can shorten or be stretched. The combination of these four qualities of muscle is referred to as muscular power.

If muscles are to function efficiently, they must be continually supplied with energy fuel. This is accomplished by blood, which carries the energy fuels from the lungs and digestive system to the muscles. The blood is forced through the blood vessels by the heart. The combined capacity to supply energy fuels to the working muscles is called organic power.

The capacity and efficiency with which your body can function depend on the degree of development of both your muscular and organic powers through regular exercise. However, the level to which you can develop these powers is influenced by such factors as the type of body you have, the food you eat, presence or absence of disease, rest and sleep. You are physically fit only when you have developed your muscular and organic power.

Genetics and health determine the top limits to which your physical capacity can be developed. This is known as your 'potential physical capacity'. This potential capacity varies from individual to individual. Most of us, for example, could train for a lifetime and never come close to running a four-minute mile simply because we weren't built for it. The top level at which you can perform physically right now is called your 'acquired capacity' because it has been acquired or developed through physical activity in your daily routines.

You can avoid wastage of energy by acquiring a level of physical capacity well above the level required to perform your normal daily tasks. This can be done by supplementing your daily physical activity with a balanced exercise program performed regularly. Your capacity increases as you progressively increase the load on your muscular and organic systems.

İnsan Vücudunun Güçleri.

İnsan vücudu esas olarak kemik, kas ve yağdan oluşur. Yaklaşık 639 farklı kas, vücut ağırlığının aşağı yukarı yüzde 45'ini oluşturur. Kasların verimli bir şekilde çalışması için sürekli olarak enerji yakıtıyla beslenmeleri gerekir. Bu, enerji yakıtlarını akciğerlerden ve sindirim sisteminden kaslara taşıyan kan tarafından gerçekleştirilir. Kan, kalp tarafından kan damarlarının içine pompalanır. Çalışan kaslara enerji yakıtı sağlama yönündeki bu birleşik kapasiteye organik güç adı verilir.

Ancak bu güçleri geliştirebileceğiniz düzey; sahip olduğunuz vücut tipi, yediğiniz yiyecekler, hastalık olup olmaması, dinlenme ve uyku gibi etkenlerden etkilenir. Genetik ve sağlık, fiziksel kapasitenizin geliştirilebileceği en üst sınırları belirler. Bu, 'potansiyel fiziksel kapasiteniz' olarak bilinir. Bu potansiyel kapasite bireyden bireye değişir. Normal günlük işlerinizi yerine getirmek için gereken düzeyin oldukça üzerinde bir fiziksel kapasite kazanarak enerji israfını önleyebilirsiniz. passages.passage_text:
The successes and failures of scientific medicine came sharply into focus. New technology was available, but a more questioning attitude to drugs emerged.

On 25 July 1978, a girl called Louise Brown became the world's first 'test-tube baby'. An egg from her mother's body had been successfully fertilized in a laboratory. For childless couples, the technique invoked new hope. Was it possible to manipulate human reproduction even more dramatically? Scientists developed 'cloning' in the seventies. It means reproducing several identical living things from a single original. Gardeners have practised it for centuries by taking cuttings from one plant to produce others. Scientists managed to clone frogs, and people suggested that it might be possible to clone humans, too. Ira Levin examined the idea in his novel The Boys from Brazil. In it, cells from Hitler's body are implanted in women around the world to create a whole race of Hitlers. This was a terrible fantasy. But despite its possibility, most scientists rejected the idea that a complex organism such as the human body could ever be cloned.

In 1979, Dr. Geoffrey Hounsfield won the Nobel Prize for physiology by developing the body scanner. This revolutionized X-ray techniques by scanning the body from all angles in three-dimensional sections. Drugs came under careful scrutiny. The morning sickness drug, Thalidomide, was found to produce deformed children, and the drug company was forced to pay millions of pounds in compensation. Doubts also grew about the contraceptive pill. Women over 35 who were heavy smokers were advised not to use it because of its dangerous side effects. In contrast, natural medicine became hugely popular, especially acupuncture, an ancient Chinese method of anaesthetizing patients by sticking pins into points in the nervous system.

passages.passage_text:
Dr. E. Clark is a famous biologist and professor of zoology at the University of Maryland. In this article, she has described her research on sharks.

My early experiments with shark behaviour at Cape Haze surprised a great many scientists - including, I must admit, myself. The experiments showed how easily many types of sharks learned to distinguish between right and wrong targets, which is a skill they developed as quickly as laboratory white rats.

More recent studies of sharks' brains, sensory systems, and types of behaviour contradict popular misconceptions of sharks as stupid, unpredictable eating machines, with nothing more than primitive brains and a good sense of smell. In fact, sharks are as predictable as any animal - even one's wife or husband - if one takes time to study and get to know them. Those of us who have had an opportunity to dive frequently with sharks do so, knowing that it is far safer to swim with these animals than to drive on an average city street or highway.

The last few years have produced exciting new knowledge about sharks. Barely a decade ago, there were only 250 accepted species; today, that number has climbed by a hundred. Sharks are a great deal more sophisticated than we once thought, and we now know that they have a higher sensitivity to electric fields than any animal ever studied. They have also been shown to orient to Earth's magnetic field. Sharks can match laboratory white rats in certain learning tests, and they have a surprisingly long retention span. Thus, they are hardly the primitive and senseless creatures that man has mistaken them for.

For the most part, the normal shark diet consists of fishes, mollusks, and crustaceans. Few sharks actually hunt or feed on marine mammals. No shark normally feeds on man. Most shark attacks on humans are bite-and-release or slashing types of actions that suggest warnings rather than attempts to kill. We accept the fact that a dog bites a stranger if the latter invades its territory. Are the rare shark attacks on humans caused by the similar invasion of what the shark considers its territory?

When we consider the rarity of shark attacks among hundreds of millions of swimmers each year, we should ask ourselves a moral question: Because we like to swim and dive in an environment unnatural to our species, is it right for us to kill off tens of thousands of harmless inhabitants of that environment to ensure our peace of mind? We have invented many sports that are more hazardous than going into the sea. When we kill ourselves at these, we blame no one else and simply accept the risks. But when it comes to sharing the sea, we insist that sharks take all the risks. With further research we may one day be able to predict sharks' behaviour with great accuracy. When that day comes, I feel certain we will recognize that sharks present no threat to mankind.

To suggest that rare shark bites may be defensive reactions to entering their space
To argue that swimmers should behave as cautiously in the sea as around wild dogs

passages.title: Sharks: Magnificent and Misunderstood
passages.tts_script:
Sharks: Magnificent and Misunderstood.

Dr. E. Clark is a famous biologist and professor of zoology at the University of Maryland. In this article, she has described her research on sharks.

My early experiments with shark behaviour at Cape Haze surprised a great many scientists - including, I must admit, myself. The experiments showed how easily many types of sharks learned to distinguish between right and wrong targets, which is a skill they developed as quickly as laboratory white rats.

More recent studies of sharks' brains, sensory systems, and types of behaviour contradict popular misconceptions of sharks as stupid, unpredictable eating machines, with nothing more than primitive brains and a good sense of smell. In fact, sharks are as predictable as any animal - even one's wife or husband - if one takes time to study and get to know them. Those of us who have had an opportunity to dive frequently with sharks do so, knowing that it is far safer to swim with these animals than to drive on an average city street or highway.

The last few years have produced exciting new knowledge about sharks. Barely a decade ago, there were only 250 accepted species; today, that number has climbed by a hundred. Sharks are a great deal more sophisticated than we once thought, and we now know that they have a higher sensitivity to electric fields than any animal ever studied. They have also been shown to orient to Earth's magnetic field. Sharks can match laboratory white rats in certain learning tests, and they have a surprisingly long retention span. Thus, they are hardly the primitive and senseless creatures that man has mistaken them for.

For the most part, the normal shark diet consists of fishes, mollusks, and crustaceans. Few sharks actually hunt or feed on marine mammals. No shark normally feeds on man. Most shark attacks on humans are bite-and-release or slashing types of actions that suggest warnings rather than attempts to kill. We accept the fact that a dog bites a stranger if the latter invades its territory. Are the rare shark attacks on humans caused by the similar invasion of what the shark considers its territory?

When we consider the rarity of shark attacks among hundreds of millions of swimmers each year, we should ask ourselves a moral question: Because we like to swim and dive in an environment unnatural to our species, is it right for us to kill off tens of thousands of harmless inhabitants of that environment to ensure our peace of mind? We have invented many sports that are more hazardous than going into the sea. When we kill ourselves at these, we blame no one else and simply accept the risks. But when it comes to sharing the sea, we insist that sharks take all the risks. With further research we may one day be able to predict sharks' behaviour with great accuracy. When that day comes, I feel certain we will recognize that sharks present no threat to mankind.

task2.model_answer:
Human beings often react with disproportionate fear toward wild animals they do not fully understand, frequently leading to unnecessary harm against marine and land ecosystems. As Dr. Clark points out in the case of sharks, sensationalized myths overshadow scientific facts, even though shark attacks are extremely rare compared to everyday dangers like driving or extreme sports.

Rather than trying to eliminate wild species to feel completely safe in nature, humans must recognize that oceans and forests are the natural habitats of other creatures. When people choose to swim, dive, or hike in wild environments, they voluntarily accept a small degree of risk. Protecting marine biodiversity requires public education based on scientific research rather than fear-driven culling. If societies invest in understanding animal behaviour and promoting respectful coexistence, we can enjoy natural spaces safely while preserving vital species that keep ecosystems balanced.

Köpekbalıkları: Muhteşem ve Yanlış Anlaşılmış.

Dr. E. Clark, Maryland Üniversitesi'nde ünlü bir biyolog ve zooloji profesörüdür. Bu makalede köpekbalıkları üzerine yaptığı araştırmasını anlatmıştır.

Cape Haze'de köpekbalığı davranışları üzerine yaptığım ilk deneyler pek çok bilim insanını ve itiraf etmeliyim ki beni de şaşırttı. Deneyler, birçok köpekbalığı türünün doğru ve yanlış hedefleri birbirinden ayırmayı ne kadar kolay öğrendiğini gösterdi; bu, laboratuvar beyaz fareleri kadar hızlı geliştirdikleri bir beceriydi.

Köpekbalıklarının beyinleri, duyu sistemleri ve davranış biçimleri üzerine yapılan daha yakın tarihli çalışmalar, onların yalnızca ilkel beyinlere ve iyi bir koku alma duyusuna sahip aptal, öngörülemez yeme makineleri olduğu yönündeki yaygın yanlış kanılarla çelişmektedir. Aslında, incelemek ve onları tanımak için zaman ayırırsanız, köpekbalıkları herhangi bir hayvan kadar — hatta insanın eşi kadar — öngörülebilirdir. Köpekbalıklarıyla sık sık dalış yapma fırsatı bulan bizler, bu hayvanlarla yüzmenin sıradan bir şehir caddesinde veya otoyolda araba kullanmaktan çok daha güvenli olduğunu bilerek dalarız.

Son birkaç yıl köpekbalıkları hakkında heyecan verici yeni bilgiler ortaya çıkardı. Daha on yıl kadar önce kabul edilen yalnızca 250 tür vardı; bugün bu sayı yüz adet daha arttı. Köpekbalıkları bir zamanlar düşündüğümüzden çok daha gelişmiştir ve artık elektrik alanlarına karşı şimdiye kadar incelenmiş tüm hayvanlardan daha yüksek bir duyarlılığa sahip olduklarını biliyoruz. Ayrıca Dünya'nın manyetik alanına göre yön bulabildikleri de gösterilmiştir. Köpekbalıkları belirli öğrenme testlerinde laboratuvar beyaz fareleriyle yarışabilir ve şaşırtıcı derecede uzun bir hafıza süresine sahiptir. Dolayısıyla, insanoğlunun onları sandığı gibi ilkel ve akılsız yaratıklar hiç değillerdir.

Köpekbalıklarının normal beslenmesi büyük ölçüde balıklar, yumuşakçalar ve kabuklulardan oluşur. Çok az köpekbalığı gerçekten deniz memelilerini avlar veya onlarla beslenir. Normal şartlarda hiçbir köpekbalığı insanla beslenmez. İnsanlara yönelik köpekbalığı saldırılarının çoğu, öldürme girişimlerinden ziyade uyarı niteliği taşıyan ısırıp bırakma veya darbe vurma türü eylemlerdir. Bir köpeğin, kendi bölgesine giren bir yabancıyı ısırmasını doğal karşılarız. İnsanlara yönelik nadir köpekbalığı saldırıları da köpekbalığının kendi bölgesi saydığı alana benzer bir şekilde girilmesinden mi kaynaklanmaktadır?

Her yıl yüz milyonlarca yüzücü arasında köpekbalığı saldırılarının ne kadar nadir olduğunu düşündüğümüzde, kendimize ahlaki bir soru sormalıyız: Türümüz için doğal olmayan bir ortamda yüzmeyi ve dalmayı seviyoruz diye, içimiz rahat etsin diye o ortamın on binlerce zararsız sakinini öldürmemiz doğru mu? Denize girmekten daha tehlikeli pek çok spor icat ettik. Bunları yaparken hayatımızı kaybettiğimizde kimseyi suçlamıyor ve riskleri basitçe kabulleniyoruz. Ancak konu denizi paylaşmaya gelince, tüm riski köpekbalıklarının almasında ısrar ediyoruz. Daha fazla araştırmayla bir gün köpekbalıklarının davranışlarını büyük bir doğrulukla öngörebiliriz. O gün geldiğinde, köpekbalıklarının insanlık için hiçbir tehdit oluşturmadığını fark edeceğimizden eminim.

passages.passage_text:
Most of us fear an electric shock, yet we know little about what is safe and what is not when we handle electricity. For example, most of the time we are cautious about handling electrical devices which seem to be complicated in structure, but do not worry about turning off the electricity with a wet hand. Maybe you don't mind placing your radio or the hair drier on the wet surface in the bathroom.

Body fluids are not as good conductors as metals. Their resistance is much higher. For example, a current of 20 microamperes flowing directly through the heart can bring about death. On the other hand, a current of 100 to 200 microamperes through electrodes on the chest triggers the regular beating of the heart, after the heart has stopped. The reason for such a big difference in the effects of the two values is that the first current is sent directly to the heart and the second has to pass through the fluids of the body, which have a greater resistance. As you can see, in an electric shock, it is the current that matters, not the voltage.

One thing about the injuries associated with electric shocks is that, most of the time, they arise from involuntary body movements in response to the current. For example, the current may cause you to lose your balance and to fall off a ladder. Sometimes, the victim freezes with the current, maybe because some muscles are paralyzed for a moment, and he cannot let go of the thing he is holding. As he keeps holding the object, there will be more current sent through the body.

One other thing about electric shocks is the burns they cause. When the skin burns, a low resistance path is established for the current and now the current can cause more damage.

Some electrical appliances require earthing. With these appliances, if the insulation becomes frayed, the leakage is carried to the ground, without doing any harm. Most of the time, people use extension cables without the earthing or make incorrect connections. It is not safe to do so. Always use the proper extensions and connections.

One other mistake made by most people is to wind thick wires around fuses, to prevent the fuse from blowing frequently. The fuses are there for safety, to prevent the overloading of the current. If they do not blow, then the excess current may cause damage to the electrical appliances or even cause a fire.

Briefly, it is not safe to play with electricity. Never forget that your body resistance is lowered greatly when it is wet. Always be careful with electricity, but never panic. If you see someone caught up in an electric shock, before you reach out to rescue him, go to the fuse box and shut off the circuit at the main inlet.

Modern households rely heavily on electrical appliances, yet many accidents still happen because people become overly comfortable with familiar devices. In my view, public safety education is just as important as building safer equipment.

First, clear warnings and practical training help people understand why simple habits matter. Many individuals know that damaged wires are dangerous, yet they still touch switches with wet hands or overload sockets because they do not realize how dramatically moisture lowers body resistance. When people understand the reasoning behind safety rules, such as why fuses must be allowed to blow, they are far less likely to take risky shortcuts.

Second, manufacturers and schools can work together to make safe behavior automatic. While modern circuit breakers and earthed plugs reduce hazards, no technology can protect users who ignore basic precautions or modify appliances improperly. Teaching children and adults how to respond calmly in emergencies, such as shutting off the main power supply before touching a victim, saves lives.

In conclusion, technology alone cannot eliminate electrical hazards. Raising everyday awareness through simple, practical education remains essential for preventing avoidable injuries at home.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Elektrik Çarpmaları.

Çoğumuz elektrik çarpmasından korkarız, ancak elektrikle uğraşırken neyin güvenli neyin güvensiz olduğu konusunda çok az şey biliriz. Örneğin, çoğu zaman yapısı karmaşık görünen elektrikli cihazları tutarken dikkatli davranırız ama elektriği ıslak elle kapatmaktan çekinmeyiz. Belki de radyonuzu ya da saç kurutma makinenizi banyodaki ıslak yüzeye koymayı umursamıyorsunuzdur.

Vücut sıvıları metaller kadar iyi iletken değildir. Dirençleri çok daha yüksektir. Örneğin, doğrudan kalpten geçen 20 mikroamperlik bir akım ölüme yol açabilir. Öte yandan, kalp durduktan sonra göğüsteki elektrotlar aracılığıyla verilen 100 ila 200 mikroamperlik bir akım kalbin düzenli atmasını tetikler. İki değerin etkileri arasındaki bu kadar büyük farkın nedeni, ilk akımın doğrudan kalbe gönderilmesi, ikincisinin ise daha yüksek bir dirence sahip olan vücut sıvılarından geçmek zorunda kalmasıdır. Gördüğünüz gibi, bir elektrik çarpmasında önemli olan voltaj değil, akımdır.

Elektrik çarpmalarıyla ilişkili yaralanmalarla ilgili bir husus da, bunların çoğu zaman akıma tepki olarak gelişen istemsiz vücut hareketlerinden kaynaklanmasıdır. Örneğin akım, dengenizi kaybedip bir merdivenden düşmenize neden olabilir. Bazen kazazede akımla birlikte kaskatı kesilir, belki de bazı kasları bir anlığına felç olduğu için elinde tuttuğu şeyi bırakamaz. Nesneyi tutmaya devam ettikçe vücudundan daha fazla akım geçecektir.

Elektrik çarpmalarıyla ilgili bir diğer husus ise neden oldukları yanıklardır. Deri yandığında, akım için düşük dirençli bir yol oluşur ve artık akım daha fazla hasara yol açabilir.

Bazı elektrikli cihazlar topraklama gerektirir. Bu cihazlarda yalıtım aşınırsa, elektrik kaçağı hiçbir zarar vermeden toprağa iletilir. Çoğu zaman insanlar topraklaması olmayan uzatma kabloları kullanır veya yanlış bağlantılar yapar. Bunu yapmak güvenli değildir. Her zaman uygun uzatma kablolarını ve bağlantıları kullanın.

Çoğu insanın yaptığı bir diğer hata da sigortanın sık sık atmasını önlemek için sigortaların etrafına kalın teller sarmaktır. Sigortalar güvenlik için, akımın aşırı yüklenmesini önlemek amacıyla oradadır. Eğer atmazlarsa, aşırı akım elektrikli cihazlara zarar verebilir ve hatta yangına bile neden olabilir.

Özetle, elektrikle oynamak güvenli değildir. Vücudunuz ıslakken vücut direncinizin büyük ölçüde düştüğünü asla unutmayın. Elektrik konusunda her zaman dikkatli olun ama asla paniğe kapılmayın. Elektrik çarpmasına maruz kalmış birini görürseniz, onu kurtarmak için uzanmadan önce sigorta kutusuna gidin ve ana girişten devreyi kapatın.

passages.passage_text:
Stress is considered to be a natural part of the contemporary world. Everybody is exposed to a certain amount of stress. Nonetheless, it should be made clear that stress doesn't occupy a greater place in our lives today than it did in the past. Although cavemen didn't have to worry about the stock market or the atomic bomb, they worried about being eaten by a bear while they were asleep or about dying of hunger - things that few people worry much about today. It's not that people suffer more stress today, it's just that they think they do. Everybody thinks that he or she is under the greatest stress. The truth is that everybody actually is under stress because if we really managed to avoid stress completely, we would be dead.

Stress is the response of the body to any demand. Stress is the state you are in, not the agent that produces it, which is called a stressor. Cold and heat are stressors. However, having a highly developed central nervous system, man most frequently suffers from stress due to emotional stressors. The thing for the average person to remember is that all the demands that you make - whether on your brain or on your liver or your muscles or your bones - cause stress. For example, stress can occur under deep anesthesia, when your emotions are not engaged, or in animals that have no nervous system, or even in plants.

There are two ways of telling when someone is under stress. One, not accessible to the public, is biochemical and neurological - measuring blood pressure, hormone levels, the electric activity of the brain and so on. Nevertheless, there are other indicators that anyone can judge. No two people react the same way, but the usual responses are an increase in pulse rate and an increased tendency to sweat. You will also become more irritable and will sometimes suffer insomnia, even long after the stressor agent is gone. You will usually become less capable of concentrating and you will have an increased desire to move about.

There are various causes of stress. They differ in various civilizations and historical time periods. At certain times, disease and hunger were the predominant causes. Another, now and then, is warfare or the fear of war. At the moment, the most frequent causes of distress in man are psychological, e.g., lack of adaptation or not having a code of behaviour.

The secret code to coping with stress is not to avoid stress but 'to do your own thing'. It implies doing what you like to do and not what you are forced to do. It is really a matter of learning how to live, how to behave in various situations, to decide: "Do I really want to take over my father's business or want to be a musician?" If you really want to be a musician, then be one.

task2.model_answer:
Many people believe that choosing a career based on personal passion reduces stress, whereas others argue that financial stability and family expectations matter more. In my opinion, following one's genuine interests is essential for long-term mental well-being, even though practical responsibilities cannot be ignored.

When individuals spend years in jobs they were pressured into taking, they often experience chronic dissatisfaction and psychological distress. Working toward goals that align with personal values creates motivation, making daily challenges feel meaningful rather than exhausting. As the passage suggests, stress itself is unavoidable, yet doing what you truly enjoy helps turn pressure into healthy engagement.

On the other hand, pursuing a passion without any realistic plan can create severe financial anxiety, which is also a powerful stressor. Therefore, the wisest approach is balancing personal fulfillment with practical preparation, such as building marketable skills within an area of interest.

In conclusion, while financial security provides necessary stability, forcing oneself into an unwanted path undermines happiness. Building a career around genuine interest, supported by sensible planning, offers the healthiest way to manage modern stress.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Stres.

Stres, çağdaş dünyanın doğal bir parçası olarak kabul edilmektedir. Herkes belirli bir miktar strese maruz kalır. Bununla birlikte, stresin bugün hayatımızda geçmişte olduğundan daha büyük bir yer kaplamadığı açıkça belirtilmelidir. Mağara insanları borsa ya da atom bombası konusunda endişelenmek zorunda kalmasalar da uyurken bir ayı tarafından yenme ya da açlıktan ölme konusunda endişeleniyorlardı ki bunlar bugün çok az insanın üzerinde durduğu şeylerdir. Bugün insanlar daha fazla stres çekiyor değil, sadece öyle olduklarını düşünüyorlar. Herkes en büyük stres altında olan kişinin kendisi olduğunu sanıyor. Gerçek şu ki aslında herkes stres altındadır; çünkü stresten tamamen kaçınmayı gerçekten başarabilseydik, ölmüş olurduk.

Stres, vücudun herhangi bir talebe verdiği tepkidir. Stres, onu üreten etken değil, içinde bulunduğunuz durumdur; o etkene stresör adı verilir. Soğuk ve sıcak birer stresördür. Ancak, son derece gelişmiş bir merkezi sinir sistemine sahip olan insan, en sık duygusal stresörlerden dolayı stres yaşar. Sıradan bir insanın hatırlaması gereken şey, ister beyninizden, ister karaciğerinizden, ister kaslarınızdan, ister kemiklerinizden olsun, vücudunuzdan istediğiniz tüm taleplerin strese yol açtığıdır. Örneğin stres, duygularınızın devrede olmadığı derin anestezi altında, sinir sistemi olmayan hayvanlarda ve hatta bitkilerde bile ortaya çıkabilir.

Birinin stres altında olduğunu anlamanın iki yolu vardır. Halkın erişimine açık olmayan ilki biyokimyasal ve nörolojik yöntemdir; kan basıncını, hormon seviyelerini, beynin elektriksel aktivitesini vb. ölçer. Yine de herkesin değerlendirebileceği başka göstergeler de vardır. İki insan aynı şekilde tepki vermez, ancak olağan tepkiler nabız hızında artış ve terleme eğiliminde artıştır. Ayrıca daha sinirli hale gelirsiniz ve stresör etken ortadan kalktıktan çok sonra bile bazen uykusuzluk çekebilirsiniz. Genellikle odaklanma beceriniz azalır ve yerinizde duramayıp hareket etme isteğiniz artar.

Stresin çeşitli nedenleri vardır. Bunlar farklı uygarlıklara ve tarihsel dönemlere göre değişiklik gösterir. Belirli dönemlerde hastalık ve açlık başlıca nedenlerdi. Zaman zaman ortaya çıkan bir diğer neden ise savaş veya savaş korkusudur. Günümüzde insanda sıkıntının en sık görülen nedenleri psikolojiktir; örneğin uyum sağlayamama veya bir davranış kuralına sahip olmama.

Stresle başa çıkmanın gizli şifresi stresten kaçmak değil, kendi istediğinizi yapmaktır. Bu, yapmaya zorlandığınız şeyi değil, yapmayı sevdiğiniz şeyi yapmak anlamına gelir. Bu aslında nasıl yaşanacağını, çeşitli durumlarda nasıl davranılacağını öğrenme ve şu kararı verme meselesidir: "Gerçekten babamın işini devralmak mı istiyorum, yoksa müzisyen mi olmak istiyorum?" Eğer gerçekten müzisyen olmak istiyorsanız, o zaman müzisyen olun.

passages.passage_text:
Few things are as insidious as bad water. It's dangerous for you and your children, but you usually can't tell if you have it. And if you do, you may not be able to find out where the problems are coming from. Water can carry some of our most serious diseases - typhoid, dysentery, hepatitis - yet still look clear in the glass. We may do battle over how we get our water and develop it, but we fear for its quality.

This issue is being dealt with currently. There is a necessity to prevent pollution by passing laws which will maintain safe drinking water. However, this is difficult because it has become increasingly apparent that the sources of pollution are not just institutions that can be controlled by specific laws. The burden of pollution belongs to all of us.

Water's nature itself is a part of these complications. This simple structure of hydrogen and oxygen has even been called the universal solvent. It takes into solution a vast number of substances, that is, dissolves them, but those it cannot dissolve are simply carried along.

Human beings have put this characteristic to work in thousands of ways. We wash with it; we flush with it; we mix it with chemicals to spray on our fields. We use it to make paint and plastic. We wash our workshop, garage and factory with it. But this remarkable utility also means that it's very hard to put anything out of water's reach. Consequently, a lot of things we don't want in water get there anyway. If you pour poison on the ground, even in the most barren desert, water will pick it up molecule by molecule, and because water is always going somewhere, it will take it away.

Technically, water pollution can be divided into two types: point-source pollution (waste dumped by factories or sewage plants) and nonpoint-source pollution. In many ways, the second is the larger problem.

Nonpoint-source pollution is what happens when you spill oil on the garage floor, then wash it down. It happens when a soybean field is sprayed with pesticides and then it rains. It happens when someone throws a dead battery into a valley. Water picks it all up and adds it to the system. Water is in serious jeopardy because we're not paying much attention to anything except pollution from a pipe.

All this shows that a change is coming - a fundamental change in the way we use and think about water. It's no use pointing fingers at industry. The only way to make progress is to have everyone realize that nonpoint-source pollution is the major cause of water pollution and to convince them that it is no longer possible to ignore fresh water.

passages.title: Bad Water
passages.tts_script:
Bad Water.

Few things are as insidious as bad water. It's dangerous for you and your children, but you usually can't tell if you have it. And if you do, you may not be able to find out where the problems are coming from. Water can carry some of our most serious diseases, such as typhoid, dysentery, and hepatitis, yet still look clear in the glass. We may do battle over how we get our water and develop it, but we fear for its quality.

This issue is being dealt with currently. There is a necessity to prevent pollution by passing laws which will maintain safe drinking water. However, this is difficult because it has become increasingly apparent that the sources of pollution are not just institutions that can be controlled by specific laws. The burden of pollution belongs to all of us.

Water's nature itself is a part of these complications. This simple structure of hydrogen and oxygen has even been called the universal solvent. It takes into solution a vast number of substances, that is, dissolves them, but those it cannot dissolve are simply carried along.

Human beings have put this characteristic to work in thousands of ways. We wash with it; we flush with it; we mix it with chemicals to spray on our fields. We use it to make paint and plastic. We wash our workshop, garage, and factory with it. But this remarkable utility also means that it's very hard to put anything out of water's reach. Consequently, a lot of things we don't want in water get there anyway. If you pour poison on the ground, even in the most barren desert, water will pick it up molecule by molecule, and because water is always going somewhere, it will take it away.

Technically, water pollution can be divided into two types: point-source pollution, meaning waste dumped by factories or sewage plants, and nonpoint-source pollution. In many ways, the second is the larger problem.

Nonpoint-source pollution is what happens when you spill oil on the garage floor, then wash it down. It happens when a soybean field is sprayed with pesticides and then it rains. It happens when someone throws a dead battery into a valley. Water picks it all up and adds it to the system. Water is in serious jeopardy because we're not paying much attention to anything except pollution from a pipe.

All this shows that a change is coming, a fundamental change in the way we use and think about water. It's no use pointing fingers at industry. The only way to make progress is to have everyone realize that nonpoint-source pollution is the major cause of water pollution and to convince them that it is no longer possible to ignore fresh water.

task1.model_answer: Contaminated water is a hidden threat because harmful diseases can be present even when water appears clear. Although laws aim to protect drinking water, legislation alone cannot solve the problem. Water acts as a universal solvent, dissolving or carrying away countless substances from daily human activities such as farming, cleaning, and manufacturing. Experts divide water pollution into point-source pollution from pipes and factories, and nonpoint-source pollution from everyday runoff like oil spills, pesticides, and discarded batteries. Because nonpoint-source pollution is the larger and more neglected problem, protecting fresh water requires a fundamental shift in public awareness rather than blaming industry alone.

task2.model_answer:
Many people assume that industrial factories are solely responsible for polluting rivers and lakes, yet individual citizens play an equally critical role in protecting water quality. While government regulations are necessary to control waste from industrial pipes, nonpoint-source pollution originates from everyday habits that laws cannot easily monitor.

First, ordinary household and agricultural practices directly affect local water systems. When motorists wash leaked motor oil off a driveway, dispose of batteries improperly, or overuse garden chemicals, rainfall eventually carries those toxins into the soil and groundwater. Because water dissolves and transports substances across wide distances, even small amounts of careless waste accumulate into serious contamination.

Second, shifting public behavior can create lasting environmental change. If communities educate residents about proper chemical disposal, encourage eco-friendly alternatives, and promote responsible water conservation, the burden on treatment facilities drops significantly.

In conclusion, although strict industrial laws remain vital, clean water ultimately depends on everyday responsibility. Only when individuals recognize their own impact can societies effectively safeguard fresh water for future generations.

passages.passage_text:
"We are determined to provide parents with the opportunity to choose quality family viewing instead of the crime and murder that dominates so much of TV aimed at children. Our new Children's Television department dynamically fulfills that commitment," says Gil Grosvenor from National Geographic Society, whose first home-video series for children - Really Wild Animals - is geared for youngsters between the ages of five and ten.

The series is hosted by Spin, a cartoon globe-on-the-go who introduces young viewers to the ways Earth's inhabitants live, use their environment, and care for one another. For instance, children see renowned scientist Jane Goodall studying the social structure of chimps and discover that these primates, just like humans, comfort their young.

Really Wild Animals begins with three video cassettes: Swinging Safari, Wonders Down Under, and Deep Sea Dive. Six more are scheduled. The videos are entertaining and educational, packed with animals - from African lions to Australia's spiny anteater.

Spin roams the world, speaking in the many voices of actor Dudley Moore. Spin presents a soap opera about colobus monkeys, a Western about sea horses, and a segment on lifestyles of the weird and little: about a fish called a mudskipper, a marsupial called a quoll, and a mammal that flies, the fruit bat. Each video includes mini-documentaries about animals. Original music accompanies the stories.

Andrew Wilk, executive producer and vice president for Children's Television, says: "We chose to start with a home-video series because we wanted involved viewers. When kids run VCRs themselves, they watch with concentration instead of zapping from channel to channel."

Children four and under will soon have their own home-video series in a format designed to appeal to that age. Called Geo Kids, the series will premiere in the fall of 1998.

"With this major new commitment, we hope to give children a running start toward a future where they can connect with the exciting, living world in all its variety and fullness."

task2.model_answer:
Today, children have access to countless cartoons and video platforms, which raises an important question about what makes screen time worthwhile. In my opinion, educational programs that combine entertainment with real-world knowledge are far more beneficial than purely fictional or violent shows.

First, mixing humor and storytelling with facts keeps young viewers engaged. When children enjoy characters, music, and creative formats—much like the animated globe in Really Wild Animals—they absorb information about science and nature effortlessly without feeling like they are sitting in a classroom.

Second, quality educational media encourages curiosity rather than passive watching. Shows that explore how animals live or highlight real researchers inspire kids to ask questions about the world around them and develop empathy for living creatures. By contrast, violent or fast-paced programs often overstimulate children without teaching useful skills.

In conclusion, while children certainly deserve to have fun when watching videos, entertainment does not have to be mindless. Combining lively storytelling with accurate facts helps young viewers enjoy their free time while building lasting knowledge.

passages.passage_text:
By Priit J. Vesilind

Fresh water, life itself, has never come easy in the Middle East. The rainfall only comes in winter, and drains quickly through the semiarid land, leaving the soil to bake and to thirst until next November. The region's accelerating population, expanding agriculture, industrialization, and higher living standards demand more fresh water. Drought and pollution limit its availability. War and mismanagement squander it.

Scarcity is only one element of the crisis. Inefficiency is another, as is the reluctance of some water-poor nations to change priorities from agriculture to less water-intensive enterprises. Some experts suggest that if nations would share both water technology and resources, they could satisfy the region's population, currently 159 million. But in this patchwork of ethnic and religious rivalries, water seldom stands alone as an issue. It is entangled in the politics that keep people from trusting and seeking help from one another. Here, where water, like truth, is precious, each nation tends to find its own water and supply its own truth.

My journey starts in spring-time, high in the Anti-Taurus Mountains of southern Turkey. The generous snows of the Turkish mountains have brought little wealth to the semiarid plains of the southeast. Without irrigation, they have yielded only one crop a year. But now Turkey has finally begun to harness its waters. I can see the Euphrates swelling with backup from the great Ataturk Dam. Soon its waters will rush through the world's two largest irrigation tunnels - 25 feet in diameter - to revitalize the Harran Plain 40 miles away. The 'Ataturk' will also generate nine billion kilowatt-hours of electricity a year. Eventually, 22 dams will impound the waters of the Euphrates and the Tigris, which also rises in eastern Turkey, all part of an ambitious and diverse development scheme called the Southeastern Anatolia Project.

On the Harran, now lush with spring grass, the mood is optimistic. At a government experimental farm at Koruklu, agronomists test patches of peaches, pecans, nectarines, pomegranates, and grapes as candidate crops for the coming waters. Local farmers attend irrigation classes with anticipation.

The massive 'Ataturk' sits 40 miles north of the city of Urfa. It is essentially an immense pile of rocks guarded by men with machine guns. With officials, I drive along its mile-long top. What looked like pebbles from a distance grow into car-size pieces of rock, each placed according to size, like a mosaic, by a machine with a monstrous arm. The blue-green Euphrates thunders below the dam with power that seems closer to electricity than water.

When nations share the same river, the upstream nation is under no legally binding obligation to provide water downstream. But the downstream nation can claim historical rights of use and press for fair treatment. In 1989, President Turgut Ozal alarmed Syria and Iraq by announcing that Turkey would hold back the flow of the Euphrates for a month to start filling the 'Ataturk'. To offset the loss, Turkey increased the flow for two months before the cutback, but even this did not prevent an outburst of criticism.

If seen as a commodity, water can be packaged, bought and sold, and may soon move between nations like wheat. But political mistrust hampers many promising schemes. In 1987, Turkey proposed a "peace pipeline" of water from two Turkish rivers - the Ceyhan and the Seyhan - that flow south into the Mediterranean. The dual pipelines would deliver potable water to millions in Syria, Jordan, Saudi Arabia, and other Arab Gulf states. Nevertheless, few nations were receptive, and the concept sits in limbo.

"In this region," Turkish Foreign Ministry official Burhan Ant told me in Ankara, "interdependence is understood as the opposite of independence. Every country here seeks a kind of self-sufficiency in every field because they don't trust the others."

passages.title: Middle East Water: Critical Resource
passages.tts_script:
Middle East Water: Critical Resource.

By Priit J. Vesilind.

Fresh water, life itself, has never come easy in the Middle East. The rainfall only comes in winter, and drains quickly through the semiarid land, leaving the soil to bake and to thirst until next November. The region's accelerating population, expanding agriculture, industrialization, and higher living standards demand more fresh water. Drought and pollution limit its availability. War and mismanagement squander it.

Scarcity is only one element of the crisis. Inefficiency is another, as is the reluctance of some water-poor nations to change priorities from agriculture to less water-intensive enterprises. Some experts suggest that if nations would share both water technology and resources, they could satisfy the region's population, currently 159 million. But in this patchwork of ethnic and religious rivalries, water seldom stands alone as an issue. It is entangled in the politics that keep people from trusting and seeking help from one another. Here, where water, like truth, is precious, each nation tends to find its own water and supply its own truth.

My journey starts in springtime, high in the Anti-Taurus Mountains of southern Turkey. The generous snows of the Turkish mountains have brought little wealth to the semiarid plains of the southeast. Without irrigation, they have yielded only one crop a year. But now Turkey has finally begun to harness its waters. I can see the Euphrates swelling with backup from the great Ataturk Dam. Soon its waters will rush through the world's two largest irrigation tunnels, 25 feet in diameter, to revitalize the Harran Plain 40 miles away. The Ataturk will also generate nine billion kilowatt-hours of electricity a year. Eventually, 22 dams will impound the waters of the Euphrates and the Tigris, which also rises in eastern Turkey, all part of an ambitious and diverse development scheme called the Southeastern Anatolia Project.

On the Harran, now lush with spring grass, the mood is optimistic. At a government experimental farm at Koruklu, agronomists test patches of peaches, pecans, nectarines, pomegranates, and grapes as candidate crops for the coming waters. Local farmers attend irrigation classes with anticipation.

The massive Ataturk sits 40 miles north of the city of Urfa. It is essentially an immense pile of rocks guarded by men with machine guns. With officials, I drive along its mile-long top. What looked like pebbles from a distance grow into car-size pieces of rock, each placed according to size, like a mosaic, by a machine with a monstrous arm. The blue-green Euphrates thunders below the dam with power that seems closer to electricity than water.

When nations share the same river, the upstream nation is under no legally binding obligation to provide water downstream. But the downstream nation can claim historical rights of use and press for fair treatment. In 1989, President Turgut Ozal alarmed Syria and Iraq by announcing that Turkey would hold back the flow of the Euphrates for a month to start filling the Ataturk. To offset the loss, Turkey increased the flow for two months before the cutback, but even this did not prevent an outburst of criticism.

If seen as a commodity, water can be packaged, bought and sold, and may soon move between nations like wheat. But political mistrust hampers many promising schemes. In 1987, Turkey proposed a peace pipeline of water from two Turkish rivers, the Ceyhan and the Seyhan, that flow south into the Mediterranean. The dual pipelines would deliver potable water to millions in Syria, Jordan, Saudi Arabia, and other Arab Gulf states. Nevertheless, few nations were receptive, and the concept sits in limbo.

"In this region," Turkish Foreign Ministry official Burhan Ant told me in Ankara, "interdependence is understood as the opposite of independence. Every country here seeks a kind of self-sufficiency in every field because they don't trust the others."

task1.model_answer: In the Middle East, rapid population growth, agriculture, drought, and political rivalries make fresh water increasingly scarce. To harness its own rivers, Turkey launched the Southeastern Anatolia Project, anchored by the massive Ataturk Dam, to irrigate the Harran Plain and generate electricity. task2.model_answer:
Whether shared rivers should be treated as national property or a collective regional resource is a complex geopolitical dilemma. On one hand, upstream countries invest heavily in infrastructure such as dams and irrigation networks to boost domestic agriculture and energy security. Without legal obligations restricting them, governments naturally prioritize the economic welfare of their own citizens.

On the other hand, downstream nations depend on continuous river flows for drinking water, farming, and basic survival. If an upstream state unilaterally reduces the flow, the consequences for downstream populations can be severe, fueling hostility and diplomatic crises. Furthermore, refusing to cooperate prevents promising regional initiatives, such as cross-border water pipelines, from succeeding.

In conclusion, while sovereign nations have the right to develop their natural resources, shared rivers require transparent agreements. Establishing fair, mutually binding water-sharing treaties is the only sustainable way to build trust and ensure stability across arid regions.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Orta Doğu'da Su: Kritik Kaynak.

Yazan: Priit J. Vesilind.

Hayatın ta kendisi olan tatlı su, Orta Doğu'da hiçbir zaman kolay elde edilmemiştir. Yağmur sadece kışın yağar ve yarı kurak topraktan hızla süzülüp gider; toprağı gelecek kasıma kadar kavrulmaya ve susuzluğa terk eder. Bölgenin hızla artan nüfusu, genişleyen tarımı, sanayileşmesi ve yükselen yaşam standartları daha fazla tatlı su talep etmektedir. Kuraklık ve kirlilik suyun bulunabilirliğini sınırlar. Savaş ve kötü yönetim ise onu israf eder.

Kıtlık, krizin yalnızca bir unsurudur. Verimsizlik bir diğeridir; tıpkı su fakiri bazı ülkelerin önceliklerini tarımdan daha az su gerektiren sektörlere kaydırma konusundaki isteksizliği gibi. Bazı uzmanlar, ülkelerin hem su teknolojisini hem de kaynakları paylaşmaları halinde bölgenin şu an 159 milyon olan nüfusuna yetebileceklerini öne sürüyor. Ancak etnik ve dini rekabetlerden oluşan bu yamalı bohçada su nadiren tek başına bir mesele olarak kalır. İnsanların birbirine güvenmesini ve birbirinden yardım istemesini engelleyen siyasetin içine dolanmıştır. Suyun da tıpkı gerçek gibi kıymetli olduğu bu yerde, her ülke kendi suyunu bulma ve kendi gerçeğini sunma eğilimindedir.

Yolculuğum ilkbaharda, Türkiye'nin güneyindeki Anti-Toros Dağları'nın yükseklerinde başlıyor. Türkiye dağlarının cömert karları, güneydoğunun yarı kurak ovalarına çok az zenginlik getirmiştir. Sulama olmadan yılda yalnızca bir ürün verebilmişlerdir. Ancak şimdi Türkiye nihayet sularını kontrol altına almaya başladı. Fırat'ın devasa Atatürk Barajı'nın arkasında birikerek kabardığını görebiliyorum. Yakında suları, 40 mil uzaklıktaki Harran Ovası'nı yeniden canlandırmak için dünyanın en büyük iki sulama tünelinden, 25 fit çapındaki tünellerden gürül gürül akacak. Atatürk Barajı ayrıca yılda dokuz milyar kilovatsaat elektrik üretecek. Nihayetinde, doğu Türkiye'den de doğan Fırat ve Dicle'nin sularını 22 baraj tutacak; bunların hepsi Güneydoğu Anadolu Projesi adı verilen iddialı ve çok yönlü bir kalkınma planının parçası.

Şimdi bahar çimleriyle yemyeşil olan Harran'da hava iyimser. Koruklu'daki devlete ait bir deneme çiftliğinde ziraat mühendisleri, gelecek sular için aday ürünler olarak şeftali, pekan cevizi, nektarin, nar ve üzüm parsellerini test ediyor. Yerel çiftçiler beklenti içinde sulama derslerine katılıyor.

Devasa Atatürk Barajı, Urfa şehrinin 40 mil kuzeyinde yer alıyor. Aslında makineli tüfekli adamlar tarafından korunan muazzam bir kaya yığını. Yetkililerle birlikte bir mil uzunluğundaki tepesi boyunca araba sürüyorum. Uzaktan çakıl taşı gibi görünen şeyler, yaklaştıkça her biri devasa kollu bir makine tarafından bir mozaik gibi boyutuna göre yerleştirilmiş araba büyüklüğünde kaya parçalarına dönüşüyor. Mavi-yeşil Fırat, barajın altında sudan çok elektriğe benzeyen bir güçle gürlüyor.

Ülkeler aynı nehri paylaştığında, yukarı havzadaki ülkenin aşağı havzaya su sağlama konusunda hukuken bağlayıcı bir yükümlülüğü yoktur. Ancak aşağı havzadaki ülke tarihsel kullanım hakları iddia edebilir ve adil muamele için baskı yapabilir. 1989'da Cumhurbaşkanı Turgut Özal, Türkiye'nin Atatürk Barajı'nı doldurmaya başlamak için Fırat'ın akışını bir ay boyunca tutacağını açıklayarak Suriye ve Irak'ı telaşlandırdı. Kaybı telafi etmek için Türkiye kesintiden önce iki ay boyunca akışı artırdı, ancak bu bile eleştiri patlamasını önleyemedi.

Bir ticari mal olarak görülürse su paketlenebilir, alınıp satılabilir ve yakında buğday gibi ülkeler arasında taşınabilir. Ancak siyasi güvensizlik birçok umut verici planı engelliyor. 1987'de Türkiye, güneye doğru Akdeniz'e akan iki Türk nehri olan Ceyhan ve Seyhan'dan bir barış suyu boru hattı önerdi. Çift boru hattı Suriye, Ürdün, Suudi Arabistan ve diğer Arap Körfez ülkelerindeki milyonlarca insana içme suyu ulaştıracaktı. Yine de çok az ülke buna sıcak baktı ve fikir askıda kaldı.

"Bu bölgede," dedi Ankara'da Türkiye Dışişleri Bakanlığı yetkilisi Burhan Ant bana, "karşılıklı bağımlılık, bağımsızlığın zıddı olarak anlaşılıyor. Buradaki her ülke başkalarına güvenmediği için her alanda bir tür kendi kendine yeterlilik arayışında."

passages.passage_text:
Around 1975, a number of books were written about strange things which occurred in the Bermuda Triangle, a part of the Atlantic Ocean off the southeast coast of the U.S. They told the stories of planes and ships that disappeared for no understandable reason and were never found again. They told about ships which were found undamaged but with no one on them. According to these books, more than 1,000 people disappeared in the Triangle from 1945 to 1975.

According to some writers, there were no natural explanations for many of the disappearances, so they suggested other explanations. For example, according to one writer, some strange and terrible power exists in the Triangle. According to another writer, people from space are living at the bottom of the Atlantic, and sometimes they need human sailors and airmen for their research. These ideas were not scientific, but they were good advertisements, which made the books about the Bermuda Triangle immediate successes.

However, the books give little evidence to support their unusual ideas. In addition, these books ignore at least three important facts that suggest natural reasons for many of the occurrences. First, messages from some of the ships and aircraft which later disappeared give us evidence of problems with navigational instruments. Similar stories are told by officers who were on duty on planes and ships which finally managed to come through the Triangle without disaster.

Second, the weather in this part of the Atlantic Ocean is very unpredictable. Dangerous storms that can cause problems even for experienced pilots and sailors can begin suddenly and without warning. Finally, the Bermuda Triangle is very large, and many people, both experienced and inexperienced, sail and fly through it. Perhaps the figure of 1,000 deaths in thirty years shocks some people, but, in fact, the figure is not unusual for an area of ocean that is so large and that is crossed by so many ships.

The evidence which exists, therefore, supports one conclusion about the Bermuda Triangle: we do not need stories about people from space or strange unnatural powers to explain the disappearances.

task2.model_answer:
Many people enjoy reading books and watching documentaries about mysteries such as the Bermuda Triangle, even when scientists offer clear natural explanations. There are two main reasons why supernatural theories remain so popular.

First, dramatic stories about alien abductions or hidden ocean powers are far more exciting than ordinary facts about compass errors or sudden storms. As the passage points out, unusual ideas act as great advertisements that capture public imagination and sell books. Second, human beings naturally feel uncomfortable when events lack simple answers. When a ship vanishes without leaving clear wreckage, mystery stories seem to fill that gap in knowledge.

However, relying on unscientific myths can be misleading because it ignores real safety lessons, such as preparing for unpredictable weather and improving navigation technology. In short, while mystery stories are entertaining, critical thinking and scientific evidence remain essential for understanding the real world.

1975 civarında, Amerika Birleşik Devletleri'nin güneydoğu kıyısı açıklarındaki Atlas Okyanusu'nun bir bölümü olan Bermuda Şeytan Üçgeni'nde meydana gelen tuhaf olaylar hakkında bir dizi kitap yazıldı. Bu kitaplar, anlaşılabilir bir sebep olmaksızın kaybolan ve bir daha asla bulunamayan uçakların ve gemilerin hikayelerini anlatıyordu. Hasarsız ancak içinde kimse olmadan bulunan gemilerden bahsediyorlardı. Bu kitaplara göre, 1945'ten 1975'e kadar Üçgen'de 1.000'den fazla kişi kayboldu.

Bazı yazarlara göre kaybolmaların birçoğunun doğal bir açıklaması yoktu, bu yüzden başka açıklamalar öne sürdüler. Örneğin bir yazara göre, Üçgen'de tuhaf ve korkunç bir güç vardır. Başka bir yazara göre ise uzaydan gelen insanlar Atlas Okyanusu'nun dibinde yaşamaktadır ve bazen araştırmaları için insan denizcilere ve havacılara ihtiyaç duyarlar. Bu fikirler bilimsel değildi ancak iyi birer reklamdı; bu da Bermuda Şeytan Üçgeni hakkındaki kitapları anında başarıya ulaştırdı.

Ancak kitaplar, sıra dışı fikirlerini desteklemek için çok az kanıt sunmaktadır. Ayrıca bu kitaplar, olayların birçoğu için doğal nedenlere işaret eden en az üç önemli gerçeği görmezden gelmektedir. İlk olarak, daha sonra kaybolan bazı gemi ve uçaklardan gelen mesajlar, bize seyrüsefer aletlerinde sorunlar yaşandığına dair kanıt sunmaktadır. Benzer hikayeler, Üçgen'den nihayetinde felaket yaşamadan geçmeyi başaran uçak ve gemilerde görevli subaylar tarafından da anlatılmaktadır.

İkinci olarak, Atlas Okyanusu'nun bu kısmında hava durumu çok öngörülemezdir. Deneyimli pilotlar ve denizciler için bile sorunlara yol açabilecek tehlikeli fırtınalar aniden ve hiçbir uyarı olmadan başlayabilir. Son olarak, Bermuda Şeytan Üçgeni çok büyüktür ve hem deneyimli hem de deneyimsiz birçok insan buradan gemiyle geçer ve uçar. Belki otuz yılda 1.000 ölüm rakamı bazı insanları şok etmektedir, ancak aslında bu rakam bu kadar büyük ve bu kadar çok geminin geçtiği bir okyanus alanı için olağan dışı değildir.

Dolayısıyla eldeki kanıtlar Bermuda Şeytan Üçgeni hakkında tek bir sonucu desteklemektedir: kaybolmaları açıklamak için uzaydan gelen insanlar veya tuhaf doğaüstü güçler hakkındaki hikayelere ihtiyacımız yoktur.

passages.passage_text:
The Bermuda Triangle, which is sometimes called 'The Graveyard of the Atlantic', is one of the greatest mysteries of the world. This is an area of the western Atlantic between Bermuda and Florida, almost triangular in shape, where at least a hundred ships and planes and over a thousand people have disappeared since 1945. No wreckage has ever been discovered in the area; that is, no bodies, life boats, or any other evidence of disaster have been found. It is as if these planes, ships and people had never existed. In some cases, a normal radio message was sent from the airplane reporting that everything was fine. Then, a few minutes later, the radio seemed to break down. In others, a weak S.O.S. message was received but the airplane disappeared before ships or other airplanes could be sent to help. Sometimes in perfect weather, there were strange references to fog and loss of direction. In the extraordinary case of five U.S. navy planes which disappeared on a regular flight from Florida, the rescue plane sent to find them also disappeared. A strange white light is a characteristic of the sea in this area. It is interesting to know that not only was this light observed by the astronauts on their way to space, but it was also seen by Columbus over four hundred years ago. It is not yet known if this light has any connection with the strange disappearances.

Many theories have been suggested to explain all these mysterious happenings in the Bermuda Triangle. Some people believe that they are caused by activity from outer space. Others think that they are caused by some undiscovered source of energy or by some dimension of time or space which is not known by man. There is no answer yet, but scientists are working hard to find one.

task2.model_answer:
Stories like the Bermuda Triangle continue to fascinate people because human beings are naturally drawn to unsolved mysteries. When ships and planes vanish without leaving wreckage or survivors, our imagination tries to fill in the missing details. Furthermore, dramatic nicknames such as 'The Graveyard of the Atlantic' and unusual reports of white lights or sudden fog make these events sound almost supernatural, which keeps public interest alive across generations.

In my view, scientific investigation is far more convincing than supernatural explanations. While ideas about outer space or hidden dimensions are entertaining in films and books, most maritime and aviation accidents have natural causes, such as sudden storms, magnetic anomalies, strong ocean currents, or human error. Because modern technology like GPS and satellite tracking has dramatically improved navigation, fewer unexplained incidents occur today. Ultimately, seeking evidence-based answers helps us learn and stay safe, even if mystery stories remain enjoyable.

Bazen 'Atlantik'in Mezarlığı' olarak da adlandırılan Bermuda Şeytan Üçgeni, dünyanın en büyük gizemlerinden biridir. Burası, Bermuda ile Florida arasında yer alan, neredeyse üçgen şeklindeki batı Atlantik bölgesidir ve 1945'ten bu yana burada en az yüz gemi ve uçak ile binden fazla insan ortadan kaybolmuştur. Bölgede hiçbir zaman enkaz keşfedilmemiştir; yani hiçbir ceset, cankurtaran filikası ya da başka bir felaket kanıtı bulunamamıştır. Sanki bu uçaklar, gemiler ve insanlar hiç var olmamış gibidir. Bazı durumlarda, uçaktan her şeyin yolunda olduğunu bildiren normal bir telsiz mesajı gönderilmiştir. Ardından birkaç dakika sonra telsiz bozulmuş gibi görünmüştür. Diğer durumlarda zayıf bir S.O.S. mesajı alınmış, ancak yardıma gemiler veya başka uçaklar gönderilemeden uçak ortadan kaybolmuştur. Bazen mükemmel hava koşullarında bile sise ve yön kaybına dair tuhaf ifadeler yer almıştır. Florida'dan rutin bir uçuş sırasında kaybolan beş ABD donanma uçağının olağanüstü vakasında, onları bulmak için gönderilen kurtarma uçağı da ortadan kaybolmuştur. Tuhaf bir beyaz ışık, bu bölgedeki denizin belirgin bir özelliğidir. Bu ışığın yalnızca uzaya giden astronotlar tarafından gözlemlenmekle kalmayıp, dört yüz yılı aşkın bir süre önce Kolomb tarafından da görülmüş olması ilginçtir. Bu ışığın tuhaf kaybolmalarla herhangi bir bağlantısı olup olmadığı henüz bilinmemektedir.

Bermuda Şeytan Üçgeni'ndeki tüm bu gizemli olayları açıklamak için birçok teori öne sürülmüştür. Bazı insanlar bunların uzaydan gelen faaliyetlerden kaynaklandığına inanmaktadır. Diğerleri ise bunların henüz keşfedilmemiş bir enerji kaynağından ya da insanoğlunun bilmediği bir zaman veya uzay boyutundan kaynaklandığını düşünmektedir. Henüz bir yanıt yoktur, ancak bilim insanları bir yanıt bulmak için yoğun şekilde çalışmaktadır.

Americans these days are very concerned with the economy. It seems more people are having to learn to spend less and to spend wisely due to the hard times we are experiencing. However, people's attitudes towards money differ.

The misers accumulate money in banks if their income is large, or in the house stuffed in mattresses or under the living room rug if they are low income people. They seem almost obsessed with the idea of saving. The misers deprive themselves of many things and most live miserably in order to hoard their wealth. My 90-year-old neighbor, having gained the sympathy of the neighbors, often collected groceries and money from them. She dressed shabbily and lived in a deteriorated house. After her death, it was discovered that this old woman had left thousands of dollars to the church and other organizations. She left nothing to her family.

The spenders are people who cannot seem to hold on to their money. They have a tendency to spend too much on too many unnecessary things. They are often too generous, buying elaborate gifts for friends and family. Credit cards in some spenders' hands are often dangerous weapons. They become addicted to using them only to regret it later when the bills come in and they are unable to pay. Other spenders like to gamble and this can also be destructive if it turns into a vice. Many spenders do not necessarily throw their money away but give it to charities for good causes, simply because they enjoy giving. My Uncle Mario is a big spender. He makes over $25,000 a year, but he never has any money in his savings account because he spends his entire paycheck each week on necessities and luxuries. Last week he spent $500 on a new moped, not because he needed one, but because he thought it would be fun to own one. As a result of his spending, every year in April he has to borrow money to pay his taxes because he has spent it all.

task2.model_answer:
Both extreme saving and uncontrolled spending can harm a person's quality of life, so finding a balanced approach to personal finance is essential. People who behave like misers often sacrifice their daily comfort, health, and relationships simply to watch their bank accounts grow. Money is meant to support a good life, and hoarding it without enjoying basic pleasures defeats its true purpose.

On the other hand, chronic spenders face constant financial stress because they fail to prepare for emergencies or routine obligations such as taxes and medical bills. Relying heavily on credit cards or impulsive purchases may bring temporary excitement, yet it frequently leads to debt and regret. A healthy financial habit lies between these two extremes: setting aside a fixed percentage of income for savings and emergencies while budgeting responsibly for everyday needs, hobbies, and occasional generosity. By planning ahead, individuals can enjoy the present without endangering their future security.

Amerikalılar bugünlerde ekonomi konusunda oldukça endişeliler. Görünüşe göre yaşadığımız zor zamanlar nedeniyle daha fazla insan daha az harcamayı ve akıllıca harcamayı öğrenmek zorunda kalıyor. Ancak insanların paraya yönelik tutumları farklılık gösteriyor.

Cimriler, gelirleri yüksekse paralarını bankalarda; düşük gelirli kişilerse evde şiltelerin içine tıkıştırarak ya da oturma odasındaki halının altında biriktirirler. Para biriktirme fikrine neredeyse takıntılı gibidirler. Cimriler kendilerini birçok şeyden mahrum bırakırlar ve çoğu, servetlerini istiflemek uğruna sefil bir hayat sürer. 90 yaşındaki komşum, komşuların sempatisini kazanarak sık sık onlardan erzak ve para toplardı. Eski püskü giyinir ve harap bir evde yaşardı. Ölümünden sonra, bu yaşlı kadının kiliseye ve diğer kuruluşlara binlerce dolar bıraktığı ortaya çıktı. Ailesine ise hiçbir şey bırakmadı.

Savurganlar ise paralarını bir türlü ellerinde tutamayan insanlardır. Çok fazla gereksiz şeye aşırı para harcama eğilimindedirler. Genellikle aşırı cömerttirler; arkadaşları ve aileleri için özenli ve gösterişli hediyeler alırlar. Kredi kartları bazı savurganların elinde çoğu zaman tehlikeli silahlardır. Onları kullanmaya bağımlı hale gelirler, ancak daha sonra faturalar geldiğinde ve ödeyemediklerinde bundan pişmanlık duyarlar. Diğer savurganlar kumar oynamayı severler ve bu da kötü bir alışkanlığa dönüşürse yıkıcı olabilir. Birçok savurgan parasını mutlaka çöpe atmaz; sırf vermekten keyif aldığı için hayır kurumlarına iyi amaçlar uğruna bağışlar. Mario Amcam tam bir savurgandır. Yılda 25.000 doların üzerinde kazanır ama tasarruf hesabında hiç parası yoktur; çünkü her hafta tüm maaşını zorunlu ihtiyaçlara ve lükslere harcar. Geçen hafta yeni bir moped için 500 dolar harcadı; ihtiyacı olduğundan değil, bir tanesine sahip olmanın eğlenceli olacağını düşündüğü için. Bu harcamalarının sonucunda, her yıl Nisan ayında tüm parasını harcamış olduğu için vergilerini ödemek üzere borç para almak zorunda kalıyor.

passages.passage_text:
Hearing specialists used to worry about loud noise as a cause of deafness only in industrial and military situations. They knew that eight hours of daily exposure, year in and year out, to the noise of the proverbial boiler factory would eventually result in permanent, or irreversible, hearing loss. People who used drills were particularly susceptible. Then they learned that the same thing happened to aviators. And after jets came into existence, the hazard applied to ground crews at airports and flight-deck personnel aboard aircraft carriers - hence came the introduction of insulated, noise-absorbing plastic earmuffs.

In discotheques and rock 'n' roll joints, the trouble is not so much in the instruments themselves, or the small area. The blame goes to the electronic amplifiers. An old-fashioned military band, playing a march in Central Park, generated as much sound. However, the sound was not amplified, but was dissipated in the open air. A trombonist sitting in front of a tuba player might be a bit deaf for an hour or so after a concert; then his hearing returned to normal. A microphone hooked up to a public address system intensified the sound but did not appreciably increase the hearing hazard. What did was multiple mikes and speakers, and the installation of internal mikes in such instruments as guitars and bousoukis.

The man who had the problem closest to home, and studied it there, was George T. Singleton, an ear, nose and throat man at the University of Florida. He noticed that, when he picked up his teenage daughter Marsha after a dance, she couldn't hear what he said in the car on the way home. Singleton recruited a research team and tested the hearing of ten fourteen-year-old ninth-graders an hour before a dance. Then, the investigators went to the dance hall, and found the average sound intensity to be very high in the middle of the dance floor. Directly in front of the band, it peaked to extremely high levels. The test crew had to move forty feet outside the building before the level dropped to a safe, but still uncomfortable, level.

After the dance, the kids' hearing was tested again. Despite the youthful resiliency of their inner ears, all had suffered at least temporary hearing impairment. The greatest damage was in the high-frequency speech range, involving consonantal sounds, similar to the loss felt by oldsters who complain that "everybody mumbles nowadays."

Why do the youngsters immerse themselves in noise that is so uncomfortable to their elders? A Florida teenager explained: "The sounds embalm you. They numb you like tranquilizers. You don't want to hear others talk. You don't want to talk. You don't know what to say to each other, anyway." So, why listen? And, eventually, how?
