task1.model_answer: In "Over-Amplification," the author explains that noise-induced hearing loss, once associated mainly with factories, drills, and military jets, has become a serious risk at rock venues and dances due to electronic amplification. Unlike unamplified outdoor concerts where sound naturally dissipates, multiple microphones, speakers, and internal instrument pickups create dangerously high noise levels. Inspired by his daughter's temporary hearing difficulty after a dance, Dr. George T. Singleton tested ten ninth-graders before and after a school dance. Although the students had young, resilient ears, every participant experienced at least temporary impairment, particularly in high-frequency consonant sounds. Ironically, many teenagers welcome this overwhelming volume because it numbs them and removes the pressure to talk.
task1.prompt: Summarize the causes of hearing damage at modern music venues and the findings of Dr. George T. Singleton's study in your own words.
task1.title: Summary of Over-Amplification

task2.model_answer:
Many young people regularly listen to music at high volumes through headphones or at concerts without realizing that hearing damage accumulates silently over time. While a single loud event may cause only temporary ringing or muffled speech, repeated exposure gradually destroys delicate inner-ear structures, leading to permanent impairment in high-frequency sounds that cannot be reversed.

Because young listeners often view loud volume as immersive or stress-relieving, public awareness alone is rarely enough. Schools and music venues should take practical preventive measures. Venues can display decibel levels and provide affordable earplugs, while schools can include short workshops on hearing conservation in health classes. Furthermore, smartphone makers already include volume warnings, and encouraging young people to enable safe-listening limits is a realistic step.

In conclusion, protecting young people's hearing does not require giving up music. By combining sensible volume limits with accessible ear protection and education, society can help teenagers enjoy music safely for decades to come.
task2.prompt: Today, many young people expose their ears to dangerously loud music at concerts and through personal headphones. Why is this a serious problem, and what practical steps can be taken to protect young people's hearing? Give reasons and examples.
task2.title: Protecting Youth Hearing from Loud Music

passages.tts_script_tr:
Aşırı Ses Yükseltme.

İşitme uzmanları eskiden sağırlık nedeni olarak yüksek gürültüden yalnızca endüstriyel ve askeri ortamlarda endişe duyarlardı. Yıllar boyunca günde sekiz saat o meşhur kazan fabrikası gürültüsüne maruz kalmanın eninde sonunda kalıcı, yani geri döndürülemez işitme kaybıyla sonuçlanacağını biliyorlardı. Matkap kullanan kişiler özellikle hassastı. Sonra aynı durumun havacıların da başına geldiğini öğrendiler. Ve jetlerin ortaya çıkmasından sonra bu tehlike havalimanlarındaki yer ekiplerini ve uçak gemilerindeki uçuş güvertesi personelini de kapsar hale geldi; bu nedenle yalıtımlı, gürültü emici plastik kulak koruyucular kullanıma sunuldu.

Diskoteklerde ve rock 'n' roll mekanlarında sorun, pek de enstrümanların kendisinde veya alanın küçüklüğünde değildir. Suç, elektronik amfilerdedir. Central Park'ta marş çalan eski usul bir askeri bando da aynı miktarda ses üretirdi. Ancak ses yükseltilmez, açık havada dağılırdı. Bir tuba çalgıcısının önünde oturan bir tromboncu, konserden sonra bir saat kadar biraz sağır kalabilirdi; ardından işitmesi normale dönerdi. Genel seslendirme sistemine bağlı bir mikrofon sesi yoğunlaştırdı ama işitme tehlikesini kayda değer ölçüde artırmadı. Bunu yapan şey ise çoklu mikrofonlar ve hoparlörler ile gitar ve buzuki gibi enstrümanların içine dahili mikrofonlar yerleştirilmesiydi.

Sorunu en yakından, kendi evinde yaşayan ve orada inceleyen kişi, Florida Üniversitesi'nde kulak burun boğaz uzmanı olan George T. Singleton'dı. Ergenlik çağındaki kızı Marsha'yı bir dans partisinden aldıktan sonra eve dönüş yolunda arabada söylediklerini kızının duyamadığını fark etti. Singleton bir araştırma ekibi kurdu ve bir dans partisinden bir saat önce on dört yaşındaki on dokuzuncu sınıf öğrencisinin işitmesini test etti. Ardından araştırmacılar dans salonuna gittiler ve dans pistinin ortasındaki ortalama ses şiddetinin çok yüksek olduğunu gördüler. Doğrudan müzik grubunun önünde ses son derece yüksek seviyelere ulaşıyordu. Test ekibi, ses seviyesinin güvenli ama yine de rahatsız edici bir düzeye düşmesi için binanın kırk fit dışına çıkmak zorunda kaldı.

Dans partisinden sonra çocukların işitmesi yeniden test edildi. İç kulaklarının gençlikten gelen esnekliğine rağmen hepsi en azından geçici işitme bozukluğu yaşamıştı. En büyük hasar, ünsüz sesleri içeren yüksek frekanslı konuşma aralığındaydı; bu da günümüzde herkesin ağzında geveleyerek konuştuğundan şikayet eden yaşlıların yaşadığı kayba benziyordu.

Gençler kendilerini büyükleri için bu kadar rahatsız edici olan bir gürültünün içine neden bırakıyorlar? Floridalı bir genç şöyle açıkladı: Sesler sizi mumyalıyor. Sakinleştiriciler gibi sizi uyuşturuyorlar. Başkalarının konuştuğunu duymak istemiyorsunuz. Konuşmak istemiyorsunuz. Zaten birbirinize ne söyleyeceğinizi de bilmiyorsunuz. O halde neden dinleyesiniz ki? Ve eninde sonunda, nasıl?

passages.passage_text:
At the center of the cyclamate discussion is Dr. Jacqueline Verrett, a Food and Drug Administration research scientist for many years who, since 1966, has been testing cyclamate on chicken embryos. Of a total of 4,000 embryos injected, some have shown deformities: feet attached directly to the hip, toes fused together, 'flipper' legs, malformed spines and missing pelvises. An earlier FDA test had shown chromosome breakage in rats that were injected with cyclohexylamine, a metabolic product of cyclamate. Concluded Dr. Verrett, "I don't recommend cyclamate for chicks, and I don't recommend it for people." After discussing the results of her work on a television program, she drew an immediate rebuttal from the FDA Commissioner Dr. Herbert Ley. "Cyclamates are safe within the present state of knowledge and scientific opinion available to me," he said.

There have been other warnings about the widely used sweetener. Last November, the FDA was advised by the National Academy of Sciences, National Research Council, that use of cyclamates should be restricted. As a result, the agency last April began considering new labeling requirements for artificially sweetened foods and beverages. The labels would indicate cyclamate content in milligrams and would recommend a maximum daily intake of 3,500 mg for adults and 1,200 for children. But the FDA has not yet given any indication about when, or if, it will establish the requirements.

The ban on cyclamates, ordered by the Health Education and Welfare Secretary Robert Finch last week, might hit millions of weight-watchers in the waistline, but it is a real disappointment to the rich diet-food industry. In the 20 years since cyclamates were discovered, sales of products containing the non-nutritive sweeteners have risen to $1 billion annually.

Worst hit will be the processors of foods containing the sweetener. Most of the cyclamate supply now goes into diet drinks, which have gained at least a share of the market for soft drinks. There is some question whether diet drinkers will switch back to sugar-sweetened drinks or just give it all up in favor of water. Cyclamates are also used in puddings, gelatins, salad dressing, jams and jellies, ice cream and practically all diet foods. The producers of 'cured' bacon commonly use cyclamates, which are cheaper than sugar. Cyclamates even go into the making of children's flavored vitamins, pickles and dog food.

Diet drinks containing cyclamates must be removed from shelves by January 1st. The announcement took some producers unawares. Instead of trying to fight the ban, Coca-Cola officials say that they are experimenting with other formulae for their diet drinks, and will probably switch to some other low-calorie sweetener. PepsiCo, which was obviously not caught napping, immediately announced that it will begin marketing within a few weeks cyclamate-free Diet Pepsi-Cola 'with a touch of real sugar'.

passages.title: The Cyclamate Controversy
passages.tts_script:
The Cyclamate Controversy.

At the center of the cyclamate discussion is Dr. Jacqueline Verrett, a Food and Drug Administration research scientist for many years who, since 1966, has been testing cyclamate on chicken embryos. Of a total of 4,000 embryos injected, some have shown deformities: feet attached directly to the hip, toes fused together, flipper legs, malformed spines, and missing pelvises. An earlier FDA test had shown chromosome breakage in rats that were injected with cyclohexylamine, a metabolic product of cyclamate. Concluded Dr. Verrett, "I don't recommend cyclamate for chicks, and I don't recommend it for people." After discussing the results of her work on a television program, she drew an immediate rebuttal from the FDA Commissioner Dr. Herbert Ley. "Cyclamates are safe within the present state of knowledge and scientific opinion available to me," he said.

There have been other warnings about the widely used sweetener. Last November, the FDA was advised by the National Academy of Sciences, National Research Council, that use of cyclamates should be restricted. As a result, the agency last April began considering new labeling requirements for artificially sweetened foods and beverages. The labels would indicate cyclamate content in milligrams and would recommend a maximum daily intake of 3,500 milligrams for adults and 1,200 milligrams for children. But the FDA has not yet given any indication about when, or if, it will establish the requirements.

The ban on cyclamates, ordered by the Health Education and Welfare Secretary Robert Finch last week, might hit millions of weight-watchers in the waistline, but it is a real disappointment to the rich diet-food industry. In the 20 years since cyclamates were discovered, sales of products containing the non-nutritive sweeteners have risen to one billion dollars annually.

Worst hit will be the processors of foods containing the sweetener. Most of the cyclamate supply now goes into diet drinks, which have gained at least a share of the market for soft drinks. There is some question whether diet drinkers will switch back to sugar-sweetened drinks or just give it all up in favor of water. Cyclamates are also used in puddings, gelatins, salad dressing, jams and jellies, ice cream, and practically all diet foods. The producers of cured bacon commonly use cyclamates, which are cheaper than sugar. Cyclamates even go into the making of children's flavored vitamins, pickles, and dog food.

Diet drinks containing cyclamates must be removed from shelves by January first. The announcement took some producers unawares. Instead of trying to fight the ban, Coca-Cola officials say that they are experimenting with other formulae for their diet drinks, and will probably switch to some other low-calorie sweetener. PepsiCo, which was obviously not caught napping, immediately announced that it will begin marketing within a few weeks cyclamate-free Diet Pepsi-Cola, with a touch of real sugar.

task2.model_answer:
When scientific studies raise credible concerns about a widely consumed food additive, governments must balance consumer safety against economic disruption. In my view, public health should always take priority, even when decisive action hurts major industries.

First, food additives such as artificial sweeteners are consumed daily by millions of people, including children who may be especially vulnerable. Waiting years for absolute scientific certainty can expose the public to avoidable long-term harm. Applying the precautionary principle through clear labeling, intake limits, or targeted bans protects consumers before irreversible health problems occur.

Admittedly, sudden bans can impose heavy costs on food processors and disappoint consumers who rely on diet products. However, competitive industries are capable of adapting quickly when rules are clear. As seen in the cyclamate case, prepared companies can reformulate recipes using safer alternatives or modest amounts of natural ingredients.

In conclusion, regulatory agencies should act promptly on credible scientific warnings rather than delaying for commercial convenience. Prioritizing consumer safety encourages healthier innovation across the food industry.

Siklamat Tartışması.

Siklamat tartışmasının merkezinde, uzun yıllardır Gıda ve İlaç Dairesi'nde (FDA) araştırmacı bilim insanı olarak çalışan ve 1966'dan beri tavuk embriyoları üzerinde siklamat testi yapan Dr. Jacqueline Verrett yer alıyor. Enjeksiyon yapılan toplam 4.000 embriyodan bazılarında şekil bozuklukları görüldü: doğrudan kalçaya yapışık ayaklar, birbirine kaynaşmış ayak parmakları, yüzgeç şeklinde bacaklar, kusurlu omurgalar ve eksik leğen kemikleri. Bunun sonucunda kurum, geçen Nisan ayında yapay olarak tatlandırılmış yiyecek ve içecekler için yeni etiketleme zorunluluklarını değerlendirmeye başladı. En ağır darbeyi bu tatlandırıcıyı içeren gıdaların işleyicileri alacak. Siklamat arzının büyük kısmı şu anda meşrubat pazarında en azından belirli bir pay edinmiş olan diyet içeceklere gidiyor. Siklamatlar ayrıca pudinglerde, jölelerde, salata soslarında, reçel ve marmelatlarda, dondurmada ve neredeyse tüm diyet yiyeceklerde kullanılıyor. Kürlenmiş domuz pastırması üreticileri, şekerden daha ucuz olduğu için yaygın olarak siklamat kullanıyor. Siklamatlar çocuklara yönelik aromalı vitaminlerin, turşuların ve köpek mamalarının yapımına bile giriyor.

Siklamat içeren diyet içecekler 1 Ocak'a kadar raflardan kaldırılmalıdır. Bu duyuru bazı üreticileri hazırlıksız yakaladı. Coca-Cola yetkilileri, yasağa karşı mücadele etmeye çalışmak yerine diyet içecekleri için başka formüller denediklerini ve muhtemelen başka bir düşük kalorili tatlandırıcıya geçeceklerini söylüyor. Gafil avlanmadığı açıkça belli olan PepsiCo ise birkaç hafta içinde, içinde az miktarda gerçek şeker bulunan siklamatsız Diet Pepsi-Cola'yı pazarlamaya başlayacağını derhal duyurdu.

passages.passage_text:
The people of the Caucasus Mountains of southern Russia have long been famous for attaining extremely old ages. Arab and Persian chronicles from centuries ago noted the existence of these longevous peoples. The latest Soviet census reports that 70 per cent of all people reaching 110 years or more live in the Caucasus region. An anthropologist described meeting a woman of 139 years. This does not seem old at all, however, compared to her first cousin, who reached 146 and her great-grandfather, who lived to be 160. When we consider that most people in the United States expect to live only half that long and that people in some parts of the developing world will live only one third that long, we cannot help wondering what the causes of such long life are. Is it exercise, diet, physical environment, cultural environment, or what? Anthropologists have concluded that exercise and diet are not as important as a steady way of life with certain cultural expectations and roles.

The people in most of the region of the Caucasus Mountains have a slow, regular, rhythmic lifestyle. There is continuity in all of the physical aspects of their life. First, most of the Caucasians live in mountain villages in a pastoral setting. They work as farmers, herders, or gardeners. Their lives are regulated by the rising of the sun, the steady rhythm of the growing cycle, the harvest, and the setting sun. Most of the longevous people have always held the same jobs. They learned their jobs young, and have continued in the same job until they are well past 100, some working until they are 120 or 130. The outdoor work and the mountainous terrain provide a good deal of exercise. Anthropologists feel that while exercise contributes to longevity, the rhythmic lifestyle is more important. There is also continuity in diet. The people of the Caucasus very much enjoy their traditional food and have no inclination to change it. They have eaten the same lean meat, grains, fruits, and vegetables from childhood to old age. Traditionally, Caucasians are lean people who do not overeat. Like exercise, anthropologists conclude that it is not the diet itself that is the secret for long life, although it does contribute. The real secret is the continuity in diet from birth to death. The consistent, unchanged diet and regular dietary rhythm allow the body and its digestive system to become entirely adjusted. Therefore, physiological stress on the digestive system is at a minimum. The overall evenness of pace in the Caucasian way of life makes for a feeling of well-being and encourages longevity.

Another important cause of longevity among the Caucasians is a stable cultural environment with certain expectations. First, the goals of the Caucasians do not overreach the possibilities of attainment. Unlike many Americans who want to be chairmen of the boards or presidents of the companies, goals which they can never attain, the goals of the Caucasians tend to be realistic and attainable within their cultural milieu. Their goals are more people-oriented. They concentrate on being hospitable and generous towards others, goals which are not only attainable, but also contribute to the overall well-being of the social group. Because the goals of the Caucasians are realistic and attainable, emotional tensions are reduced. This contributes to long life. Second, the normal expectation within the region is for long life. Individuals expect to live far beyond the age of 100. On the other hand, the cultural expectation of people in the United States is for a maximum life span of about 80 years. These cultural expectations become self-fulfilling prophecies. Further, the Caucasians do not expect the old people to sit idly by, but to participate actively in all phases of life. A stable environment with realistic goals and expectations is a second cause for longevity among the Caucasians.

Finally, longevity is also encouraged by the role of old people in the family and in the community. The Caucasians have large extended families of maybe 300 people or more. This provides a large network of people with mutual rights and obligations. The aged are respected as heads of the family. They make decisions about money, marriages, land sales, and other matters. They are also expected to be affectionate toward their grandchildren. The old people are also respected in the community. They continue to vote, hold office and so make decisions which will affect the future of the entire community. Because of their important place in the family and in the community, the aged retain a feeling of individual self-worth and importance. Retaining a positive self-image reduces physical and mental problems, thus encouraging a longer life.

First, residents follow a calm, rhythmic lifestyle in rural mountain villages, maintaining the same outdoor occupations and traditional diet from childhood into advanced old age, which minimizes physical stress. task2.model_answer:
In many modern societies, aging is frequently associated with withdrawal from public life, which can negatively affect both mental and physical health. In contrast, communities where older adults remain socially active demonstrate that meaningful participation plays a crucial role in healthy aging.

When elderly individuals continue to contribute to family and community decisions, they maintain a clear sense of purpose and belonging. Feeling valued reduces loneliness and depression, two major risk factors for cognitive and physical decline in old age. Moreover, regular social interaction keeps the mind engaged and encourages daily physical movement. On the other hand, societies that push older citizens to the margins often unintentionally accelerate their loss of independence.

Of course, older people should not be forced to carry heavy physical burdens beyond their strength. Instead, communities should offer flexible ways for them to share their experience, mentor younger generations, and take part in civic life. Ultimately, respecting and involving the elderly benefits everyone by strengthening social cohesion and promoting longer, healthier lives.

İyi Bir Yaşam.

Güney Rusya'daki Kafkas Dağları'nın insanları, çok ileri yaşlara ulaşmalarıyla uzun zamandır ünlüdür. Yüzyıllar öncesine ait Arap ve Fars kronikleri bu uzun ömürlü halkların varlığını kaydetmiştir. Son Sovyet nüfus sayımı, 110 yaş ve üzerine ulaşan tüm insanların yüzde 70'inin Kafkasya bölgesinde yaşadığını bildirmektedir. Bir antropolog, 139 yaşında bir kadınla tanıştığını anlatmıştır. Ancak bu durum, 146 yaşına ulaşan birinci dereceden kuzeni ve 160 yaşına kadar yaşayan büyük büyükbabasıyla karşılaştırıldığında hiç de yaşlı görünmemektedir. Amerika Birleşik Devletleri'ndeki çoğu insanın bunun yalnızca yarısı kadar yaşamayı beklediğini ve gelişmekte olan dünyanın bazı bölgelerindeki insanların bunun yalnızca üçte biri kadar yaşayacağını düşündüğümüzde, böylesine uzun bir yaşamın nedenlerinin ne olduğunu merak etmekten kendimizi alamayız. Egzersiz mi, beslenme mi, fiziksel çevre mi, kültürel çevre mi, yoksa başka bir şey mi? Antropologlar, egzersiz ve beslenmenin, belirli kültürel beklentilere ve rollere sahip istikrarlı bir yaşam tarzı kadar önemli olmadığı sonucuna varmıştır.

Kafkas Dağları bölgesinin büyük bir kısmındaki insanlar yavaş, düzenli ve ritmik bir yaşam tarzına sahiptir. Yaşamlarının tüm fiziksel yönlerinde bir süreklilik vardır. İlk olarak, Kafkasyalıların çoğu kırsal bir ortamda, dağ köylerinde yaşar. Çiftçi, çoban veya bahçıvan olarak çalışırlar. Yaşamları güneşin doğuşu, büyüme döngüsünün istikrarlı ritmi, hasat ve güneşin batışı ile düzenlenir. Uzun ömürlü insanların çoğu her zaman aynı işlerde çalışmıştır. İşlerini genç yaşta öğrenmişler ve 100 yaşını epey geçene kadar aynı işte çalışmaya devam etmişlerdir; bazıları 120 veya 130 yaşına kadar çalışmaktadır. Açık havada yapılan işler ve dağlık arazi, bol miktarda egzersiz sağlar. Antropologlar, egzersizin uzun ömre katkıda bulunmakla birlikte, ritmik yaşam tarzının daha önemli olduğunu düşünmektedir. Beslenmede de bir süreklilik vardır. Kafkasya halkı geleneksel yemeklerinden çok keyif alır ve onları değiştirmeye hiç niyeti yoktur. Çocukluktan yaşlılığa kadar aynı yağsız eti, tahılları, meyveleri ve sebzeleri yemişlerdir. Geleneksel olarak Kafkasyalılar, aşırı yemek yemeyen zayıf insanlardır. Antropologlar, tıpkı egzersizde olduğu gibi, katkıda bulunmasına rağmen uzun yaşamın sırrının beslenmenin kendisi olmadığı sonucuna varmaktadır. Gerçek sır, doğumdan ölüme kadar beslenmedeki sürekliliktir. Tutarlı, değişmeyen beslenme düzeni ve düzenli beslenme ritmi, vücudun ve sindirim sisteminin tamamen uyum sağlamasına olanak tanır. Bu nedenle, sindirim sistemi üzerindeki fizyolojik stres en aza iner. Kafkas yaşam tarzındaki genel tempo dengesi, bir esenlik duygusu yaratır ve uzun ömrü teşvik eder.

Kafkasyalılar arasındaki uzun ömrün bir diğer önemli nedeni, belirli beklentilere sahip istikrarlı bir kültürel çevredir. İlk olarak, Kafkasyalıların hedefleri ulaşılabilirlik sınırlarını aşmaz. Asla ulaşamayacakları yönetim kurulu başkanı veya şirket başkanı olma hedefleri güden birçok Amerikalının aksine, Kafkasyalıların hedefleri kendi kültürel ortamları içinde gerçekçi ve ulaşılabilir olma eğilimindedir. Hedefleri daha çok insan odaklıdır. Başkalarına karşı misafirperver ve cömert olmaya odaklanırlar; bu hedefler yalnızca ulaşılabilir olmakla kalmaz, aynı zamanda sosyal grubun genel refahına da katkıda bulunur. Kafkasyalıların hedefleri gerçekçi ve ulaşılabilir olduğu için duygusal gerilimler azalır. Bu da uzun yaşama katkıda bulunur. İkinci olarak, bölge içindeki olağan beklenti uzun bir yaşam yönündedir. Bireyler 100 yaşının çok ötesinde yaşamayı beklerler. Öte yandan, Amerika Birleşik Devletleri'ndeki insanların kültürel beklentisi yaklaşık 80 yıllık azami bir yaşam süresidir. Bu kültürel beklentiler kendi kendini gerçekleştiren kehanetlere dönüşür. Ayrıca Kafkasyalılar, yaşlılardan kenarda boş oturmalarını değil, yaşamın tüm evrelerine aktif olarak katılmalarını beklerler. Gerçekçi hedeflere ve beklentilere sahip istikrarlı bir çevre, Kafkasyalılar arasındaki uzun ömrün ikinci nedenidir.

Son olarak, uzun ömür yaşlıların ailedeki ve toplumdaki rolüyle de teşvik edilir. Kafkasyalıların belki 300 veya daha fazla kişiden oluşan büyük geniş aileleri vardır. Bu, karşılıklı haklara ve yükümlülüklere sahip geniş bir insan ağı sağlar. Yaşlılara ailenin reisi olarak saygı duyulur. Para, evlilikler, arazi satışları ve diğer konular hakkında kararlar verirler. Ayrıca torunlarına karşı şefkatli olmaları beklenir. Yaşlılara toplum içinde de saygı duyulur. Oy kullanmaya, görev üstlenmeye ve böylece tüm toplumun geleceğini etkileyecek kararlar almaya devam ederler. Ailedeki ve toplumdaki önemli yerleri nedeniyle yaşlılar, bireysel öz değer ve önem duygusunu korurlar. Olumlu bir benlik imajını korumak fiziksel ve zihinsel sorunları azaltır ve böylece daha uzun bir yaşamı teşvik eder.

passages.passage_text:
Sleep is broken into five distinct parts - Stages 1 through 4, plus REM, an acronym for rapid eye movement. REM and non-REM sleep are quite different, as different from each other as each is from being awake. Much remains unknown about each of the five sleep stages. Most dreaming occurs during REM sleep, a period when the eyeballs move rapidly beneath the closed lids. And whether they remember or not, all adults dream, usually four to six times a night.

Three types of mood are strongly related to some specific stage of sleep. Our friendly, aggressive, and sleepy feelings all relate to Stage 2 sleep, which accounts for most of our total sleep hours. Our friendly and sleepy feelings, but not our aggressive feelings, are affected as well by Stages 3 and 4, and by how long it takes us to fall asleep.

This means that if you get less sleep than normal - and people vary a great deal in how much sleep they normally require - you awake more friendly, more aggressive, but less sleepy. Researchers knew from their earlier work that sleep determines if people feel happier. Yet, when they studied the various sleep stages, they found no correlation between sleep physiology and the unhappy mood. They were puzzled by this. Clearly sleep made a difference, but that difference didn't relate to how much time one spent in each of the various sleep stages.

The researchers decided the key to whether we feel happy or unhappy after sleep must lie in sleep's psychological component - our dreams. So, they began studying dream content - what dreamers dreamed and who appeared in their dreams - to see how it affected mood.

These findings have emerged from eight years of sleep and dream research at the Veterans Administration Hospital in Cincinnati, Ohio:
- While sleep affects how sleepy, friendly, aggressive, and unhappy we feel after awakening, feelings of happiness or unhappiness depend most strongly on our dreams.
- Each of us has a special dream character, a type of person whose appearance in our dreams makes us feel happier when we awake.
- What we dream at night isn't as important to how we feel in the morning as the number of people who populate our dreams. The more people we see, the better we feel.

Our sleep influences our mood. Our mood, in turn, affects our performance. And throughout the day, our levels of mood and performance remain closely linked.

Research shows that specific sleep stages influence friendly, aggressive, and sleepy moods; for instance, Stage 2 affects all three, while Stages 3 and 4 also influence friendliness and sleepiness. task2.model_answer:
Although sleep is often treated as a luxury in busy modern schedules, scientific evidence shows that adequate rest is essential for both emotional balance and daily performance. Without sufficient sleep, people wake up with altered moods that directly affect how well they work or study.

When individuals get less sleep than they need, their emotional control weakens. As research indicates, sleep deprivation can make people feel more aggressive and less emotionally steady, even if they temporarily feel less sleepy. Because mood and performance remain closely connected throughout the day, a poor mood caused by bad sleep reduces concentration, decision-making quality, and cooperation with colleagues or classmates. Over time, chronic sleep loss harms both productivity and mental health.

To prevent these negative effects, people should treat regular sleep as a core health priority. Maintaining a consistent bedtime, limiting screen exposure late at night, and protecting enough hours for full sleep cycles allow both the body and mind to recover. In the long run, sleeping well is not wasted time; it is the foundation of effective daytime performance.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Uyumak, Belki de Rüya Görmek.

Uyku beş ayrı bölüme ayrılır: 1'den 4'e kadar olan Evreler ve "rapid eye movement" (hızlı göz hareketi) ifadesinin kısaltması olan REM. REM ve REM dışı uyku birbirinden oldukça farklıdır; her birinin uyanık olmaktan farklı olduğu kadar birbirlerinden de farklıdırlar. Beş uyku evresinin her biri hakkında hâlâ bilinmeyen çok şey vardır. Çoğu rüya, göz kürelerinin kapalı göz kapaklarının altında hızla hareket ettiği bir dönem olan REM uykusu sırasında görülür. Hatırlasalar da hatırlamasalar da tüm yetişkinler genellikle gecede dört ila altı kez rüya görürler.

Üç ruh hâli türü, uykunun belirli bir evresiyle güçlü bir şekilde ilişkilidir. Dostane, agresif ve uykulu hissetmemizin tümü, toplam uyku saatlerimizin çoğunu oluşturan Evre 2 uykusuyla ilgilidir. Dostane ve uykulu hislerimiz, ancak agresif hislerimiz değil, Evre 3 ve 4'ten ve uykuya dalmamızın ne kadar sürdüğünden de etkilenir.

Bu, normalden daha az uyursanız — ki insanlar normalde ne kadar uykuya ihtiyaç duydukları konusunda büyük farklılıklar gösterir — daha dostane, daha agresif, ancak daha az uykulu uyanacağınız anlamına gelir. Araştırmacılar daha önceki çalışmalarından uykunun insanların kendilerini daha mutlu hissedip hissetmediklerini belirlediğini biliyorlardı. Yine de çeşitli uyku evrelerini incelediklerinde, uyku fizyolojisi ile mutsuz ruh hâli arasında hiçbir ilişki bulamadılar. Bu durum kafalarını karıştırdı. Açıkça görülüyordu ki uyku bir fark yaratıyordu, ancak bu fark kişinin çeşitli uyku evrelerinin her birinde ne kadar zaman geçirdiğiyle ilgili değildi.

Araştırmacılar, uykudan sonra mutlu mu yoksa mutsuz mu hissedeceğimizin anahtarının uykunun psikolojik bileşeninde, yani rüyalarımızda yatıyor olması gerektiğine karar verdiler. Bu yüzden, ruh hâlini nasıl etkilediğini görmek için rüya içeriğini, yani rüya görenlerin ne gördüğünü ve rüyalarında kimlerin belirdiğini incelemeye başladılar.

Bu bulgular, Ohio, Cincinnati'deki Veterans Administration Hastanesi'nde sekiz yıl süren uyku ve rüya araştırmalarından ortaya çıkmıştır. İlk olarak, uyku uyandıktan sonra kendimizi ne kadar uykulu, dostane, agresif ve mutsuz hissettiğimizi etkilerken, mutluluk veya mutsuzluk duyguları en güçlü şekilde rüyalarımıza bağlıdır. İkinci olarak, her birimizin özel bir rüya karakteri vardır; rüyalarımızda görünmesi uyandığımızda kendimizi daha mutlu hissetmemizi sağlayan bir insan tipi. Üçüncü olarak, gece ne rüya gördüğümüz, sabah nasıl hissettiğimiz açısından rüyalarımızı dolduran insan sayısı kadar önemli değildir. Ne kadar çok insan görürsek, kendimizi o kadar iyi hissederiz.

Uykumuz ruh hâlimizi etkiler. Ruh hâlimiz de karşılığında performansımızı etkiler. Ve gün boyunca ruh hâli ve performans düzeylerimiz yakından bağlantılı kalır.

passages.passage_text:
There are over 100 elements in nature. Each element is composed of an innumerable group of atoms which are identical with one another and different from the atoms that make up the other elements. Normally they are found in pairs or in combinations with other kinds of atoms. We call these arrangements of atoms 'molecules'.

Why do some atoms combine while others do not? What determines the manner in which atoms combine? The answers have to do with the electrons that circle the nucleus of the atom. As we know, an atom is composed of three kinds of particles: protons and neutrons, which are found in a very small region at the center of the atom, and electrons, which orbit the nucleus. The number of electrons in an atom is the same as the number of protons, and this number determines the chemical properties of the element. The number of neutrons in the atoms of a given element is not constant, though it is usually slightly greater than the number of protons. The orbits of the electrons about the nucleus are something like the orbits of the planets in our solar system about the sun, except that each atomic orbital can contain only a certain maximum number of electrons. For example, the first atomic orbital, corresponding to the planet Mercury, can contain as many as two electrons, no more; the second atomic orbital, corresponding to the planet Venus, can contain as many as eight electrons, no more; and so on. The inner orbitals of atoms are the first to take electrons, and because of certain factors that depend upon energy, atoms like to have their last, outer orbital full. The inert gases - Helium, Neon, Argon, Krypton, Xenon, and Radon - are elements whose atoms have full electron orbitals. Consequently, these elements do not combine with other elements; they are chemically inactive, inert. The atoms of all other elements tend to combine with other atoms so as to fill up their electron orbitals.

Hydrogen atoms always have a single electron and a single proton, so their electron shell (orbital) is one electron short of being full. In the gaseous state, two hydrogen atoms are combined to form a single molecule (H2). Each electron circling about both nuclei makes it appear as if there were only one electronic orbital.

Oxygen atoms have eight electrons, two of which fill the first orbital; the remaining six are contained in the second orbital, leaving the second orbital two short of the preferred number eight. Often in nature we find a molecule where two hydrogen atoms have given their electrons to a single oxygen atom, which fills the second orbital of the oxygen atom. This arrangement of oxygen and hydrogen is very stable. This molecule is called 'water'.

The carbon atom has four of its six electrons in its outer orbital. Depending upon how you look at it, it has either four too few or four too many electrons in its outer orbital. It is willing either to borrow or to lend four electrons. When carbon combines with oxygen, the carbon atom gives two electrons to each of two oxygen atoms; the result is the gas carbon dioxide (CO2), which is quite common in nature.

Chemical reactions are simply the arrangements and rearrangements atoms and molecules go through to have full electron orbitals. Any destruction or creation of molecules is a chemical reaction.

As we know, an atom is composed of three kinds of particles: protons and neutrons, which are found in a very small region at the center of the atom, and electrons, which orbit the nucleus. The number of electrons in an atom is the same as the number of protons, and this number determines the chemical properties of the element. The number of neutrons in the atoms of a given element is not constant, though it is usually slightly greater than the number of protons. The orbits of the electrons about the nucleus are something like the orbits of the planets in our solar system about the sun, except that each atomic orbital can contain only a certain maximum number of electrons. For example, the first atomic orbital, corresponding to the planet Mercury, can contain as many as two electrons, no more; the second atomic orbital, corresponding to the planet Venus, can contain as many as eight electrons, no more; and so on. The inner orbitals of atoms are the first to take electrons, and because of certain factors that depend upon energy, atoms like to have their last, outer orbital full. The inert gases, Helium, Neon, Argon, Krypton, Xenon, and Radon, are elements whose atoms have full electron orbitals. Consequently, these elements do not combine with other elements; they are chemically inactive, inert. The atoms of all other elements tend to combine with other atoms so as to fill up their electron orbitals.

Hydrogen atoms always have a single electron and a single proton, so their electron shell, or orbital, is one electron short of being full. In the gaseous state, two hydrogen atoms are combined to form a single molecule, H 2. Each electron circling about both nuclei makes it appear as if there were only one electronic orbital.

Oxygen atoms have eight electrons, two of which fill the first orbital; the remaining six are contained in the second orbital, leaving the second orbital two short of the preferred number eight. Often in nature we find a molecule where two hydrogen atoms have given their electrons to a single oxygen atom, which fills the second orbital of the oxygen atom. This arrangement of oxygen and hydrogen is very stable. This molecule is called water.

The carbon atom has four of its six electrons in its outer orbital. Depending upon how you look at it, it has either four too few or four too many electrons in its outer orbital. It is willing either to borrow or to lend four electrons. When carbon combines with oxygen, the carbon atom gives two electrons to each of two oxygen atoms; the result is the gas carbon dioxide, C O 2, which is quite common in nature.

Chemical reactions are simply the arrangements and rearrangements atoms and molecules go through to have full electron orbitals. Any destruction or creation of molecules is a chemical reaction.

While protons and neutrons sit in the nucleus, electrons orbit in layers that hold fixed capacities, such as two in the first orbital and eight in the second. Because atoms seek full outer orbitals, elements with incomplete shells—like hydrogen, oxygen, and carbon—share or transfer electrons to create stable molecules such as water and carbon dioxide. In contrast, inert gases already possess full orbitals and remain chemically inactive. Thus, chemical reactions are essentially atomic rearrangements aimed at achieving full electron orbitals.

Learning basic chemistry is essential for everyone, not only for professional scientists. Everything we interact with daily—from the water we drink to the air we breathe and the fuels we use—consists of molecules formed through simple atomic rules. Without basic chemical literacy, people are more likely to misunderstand news about climate change, nutrition, or medical treatments.

Although specialized careers require deeper mathematical study, grasping foundational concepts such as elements, atoms, and chemical reactions empowers all students to interpret the physical world logically. Therefore, introductory chemistry should remain a core part of general education.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Elementler.

Doğada 100'ün üzerinde element vardır. Her element, birbirinin tıpatıp aynısı olan ve diğer elementleri oluşturan atomlardan farklı olan sayısız atom grubundan oluşur. Normalde çiftler hâlinde veya diğer atom türleriyle birleşimler hâlinde bulunurlar. Atomların bu düzenlenişlerine molekül adını veririz.

Bazı atomlar birleşirken diğerleri neden birleşmez? Atomların birleşme biçimini ne belirler? Yanıtlar, atomun çekirdeği etrafında dönen elektronlarla ilgilidir. Bildiğimiz gibi bir atom üç tür parçacıktan oluşur: atomun merkezindeki çok küçük bir bölgede bulunan protonlar ve nötronlar ile çekirdeğin yörüngesinde dönen elektronlar. Bir atomdaki elektron sayısı proton sayısıyla aynıdır ve bu sayı elementin kimyasal özelliklerini belirler. Belirli bir elementin atomlarındaki nötron sayısı sabit değildir, ancak genellikle proton sayısından biraz daha fazladır. Elektronların çekirdek etrafındaki yörüngeleri, güneş sistemimizdeki gezegenlerin güneş etrafındaki yörüngelerine biraz benzer; tek fark, her atomik yörüngenin yalnızca belirli bir azami elektron sayısını barındırabilmesidir. Örneğin, Merkür gezegenine karşılık gelen birinci atomik yörünge en fazla iki elektron barındırabilir, daha fazlasını değil; Venüs gezegenine karşılık gelen ikinci atomik yörünge en fazla sekiz elektron barındırabilir, daha fazlasını değil; ve bu şekilde devam eder. Atomların iç yörüngeleri elektronları ilk alan yörüngelerdir ve enerjiye bağlı belirli faktörler nedeniyle atomlar son, yani en dış yörüngelerinin dolu olmasını severler. Soy gazlar — Helyum, Neon, Argon, Kripton, Ksenon ve Radon — atomları dolu elektron yörüngelerine sahip olan elementlerdir. Sonuç olarak bu elementler başka elementlerle birleşmezler; kimyasal olarak etkisiz, yani inerttirler. Diğer tüm elementlerin atomları, elektron yörüngelerini doldurmak amacıyla başka atomlarla birleşme eğilimindedir.

Hidrojen atomlarının her zaman tek bir elektronu ve tek bir protonu vardır, bu nedenle elektron kabukları ya da yörüngeleri dolmaktan bir elektron eksiktir. Gaz hâlinde iki hidrojen atomu tek bir molekül olan H 2'yi oluşturmak üzere birleşir. Her iki çekirdeğin etrafında dönen her bir elektron, sanki yalnızca tek bir elektron yörüngesi varmış gibi görünmesine neden olur.

Oksijen atomlarının sekiz elektronu vardır; bunların ikisi birinci yörüngeyi doldurur, kalan altısı ise ikinci yörüngede bulunur ve bu da ikinci yörüngeyi tercih edilen sekiz sayısından iki eksik bırakır. Doğada sıklıkla, iki hidrojen atomunun elektronlarını tek bir oksijen atomuna verdiği ve bunun da oksijen atomunun ikinci yörüngesini doldurduğu bir molekülle karşılaşırız. Oksijen ve hidrojenin bu düzenlenişi çok kararlıdır. Bu moleküle su denir.

Karbon atomunun altı elektronundan dördü dış yörüngesindedir. Duruma nasıl baktığınıza bağlı olarak, dış yörüngesinde ya dört elektron eksiktir ya da dört elektron fazladır. Dört elektron ödünç almaya ya da ödünç vermeye isteklidir. Karbon oksijenle birleştiğinde, karbon atomu iki oksijen atomunun her birine ikişer elektron verir; sonuç, doğada oldukça yaygın olan karbondioksit gazı, yani C O 2'dir.

Kimyasal tepkimeler, atomların ve moleküllerin dolu elektron yörüngelerine sahip olmak için geçirdikleri düzenleniş ve yeniden düzenlenişlerden ibarettir. Moleküllerin her türlü yıkımı veya oluşumu bir kimyasal tepkimedir.

passages.passage_text:
Polystyrene foam is one of the great success stories of modern industry. Light, shock-resistant, insulating and cheap to make, it shows up everywhere: in disposable coffee cups, in boxes that hold fast-food hamburgers, as packing 'peanuts' for safe shipping. But the stuff has a serious downside as well. Polystyrene is bulky, taking up space in landfills; as a plastic, it takes decades to decompose; its manufacture causes the release of hazardous chemicals; and the market for recycling it is hopelessly limited. Environmentalists have argued for years that the foam should simply be banned.

They now have an unlikely ally: McDonald's. America's largest fast-food chain and frequent target of environmental protests announced last week that it would begin phasing out foam packaging within 60 days at its 8,500 U.S. restaurants. The move came as a surprise. The company has long said the containers were not necessarily a problem and had planned a $100 million campaign to recycle them. But ecology-minded customers were increasingly unhappy with the packages. As a result, McDonald's is making the phaseout part of a broad pro-environment initiative that the company is developing in partnership with the Washington-based Environmental Defense Fund.

McDonald's will probably replace its foam hamburger boxes with material similar to the thin paper used to wrap its smallest sandwiches. That is not a perfect solution either. The paper is not yet recyclable, and while it does break down in landfills, its production requires cutting down trees. But it takes up 90% less space than foam when discarded, and McDonald's is testing a paper-recycling technique in some of its California stores. If it can find alternatives, the chain may also replace its polystyrene plates and coffee cups.

One possible substitute for some uses of polystyrene comes straight from nature. To replace the plastic-foam pellets that are used to protect delicate merchandise during shipping, at least two companies in California are trying to market a biodegradable, in fact, edible, alternative: popcorn. The drawbacks are that it is more expensive to produce than polystyrene pellets and tends to attract rodents and insects. Nonetheless, a handful of mail-order companies and other shippers in the U.S., Canada and Europe have begun packing with popcorn (butter and salt not included). Such small innovations, along with dramatic shifts by companies like McDonald's, may someday eliminate a major insult to the environment.

task2.model_answer:
Businesses play a decisive role in reducing plastic pollution, and consumer pressure is often the strongest force pushing them to change. When major corporations replace harmful packaging, the positive impact is far greater than individual recycling habits alone can achieve.

First, large companies control massive supply chains. As shown by McDonald's decision to abandon foam boxes at thousands of outlets, one corporate policy shift can instantly remove huge volumes of non-biodegradable waste from landfills. Second, customers have real power through their purchasing choices. When shoppers demand greener practices or boycott wasteful products, businesses realize that ignoring environmental concerns threatens their profits and reputation.

However, alternative materials often involve new trade-offs, such as higher costs or tree consumption. Therefore, companies must invest in research alongside customer feedback to develop truly sustainable packaging rather than relying on temporary fixes.

Polistiren köpük, modern endüstrinin en büyük başarı hikâyelerinden biridir. Hafif, darbeye dayanıklı, yalıtkan ve üretimi ucuz olan bu malzeme her yerde karşımıza çıkar: tek kullanımlık kahve bardaklarında, fast-food hamburgerlerin konduğu kutularda ve güvenli kargo taşımacılığı için kullanılan dolgu köpüklerinde. Ancak bu maddenin ciddi bir olumsuz yönü de vardır. Polistiren çok yer kaplar ve çöp sahalarında büyük alan işgal eder; bir plastik türü olduğu için doğada çözünmesi on yıllar alır; üretimi tehlikeli kimyasalların salınımına yol açar ve geri dönüşüm pazarı umutsuzca sınırlıdır. Çevreciler yıllardır bu köpüğün tamamen yasaklanması gerektiğini savunmaktadır.

Artık beklenmedik bir müttefikleri var: McDonald's. Amerika'nın en büyük fast-food zinciri ve çevre protestolarının sıkça hedefi olan şirket, geçen hafta ABD'deki 8.500 restoranında 60 gün içinde köpük ambalajları aşamalı olarak kullanımdan kaldırmaya başlayacağını duyurdu. Bu hamle sürpriz oldu. Şirket uzun süredir bu kapların mutlaka bir sorun teşkil etmediğini savunuyor ve bunları geri dönüştürmek için 100 milyon dolarlık bir kampanya planlıyordu. Ancak çevre bilincine sahip müşteriler bu ambalajlardan giderek daha fazla rahatsızlık duyuyordu. Sonuç olarak McDonald's, bu aşamalı kaldırma sürecini, Washington merkezli Çevre Savunma Fonu ile ortaklaşa geliştirdiği kapsamlı bir çevre dostu girişimin parçası haline getiriyor.

McDonald's, köpük hamburger kutularını muhtemelen en küçük sandviçlerini sarmak için kullandığı ince kağıda benzer bir malzemeyle değiştirecek. Bu da kusursuz bir çözüm değil. Söz konusu kağıt henüz geri dönüştürülebilir değil ve çöp sahalarında çözünse de üretimi ağaçların kesilmesini gerektiriyor. Yine de atıldığında köpüğe kıyasla yüzde 90 daha az yer kaplıyor ve McDonald's Kaliforniya'daki bazı şubelerinde bir kağıt geri dönüşüm tekniğini test ediyor. Eğer alternatifler bulabilirse zincir, polistiren tabaklarını ve kahve bardaklarını da değiştirebilir.

Polistirenin bazı kullanım alanları için olası bir ikame ise doğrudan doğadan geliyor. Hassas ürünleri nakliye sırasında korumak amacıyla kullanılan plastik köpük parçacıklarının yerini alması için Kaliforniya'daki en az iki şirket, biyolojik olarak parçalanabilen, hatta yenilebilen bir alternatifi pazarlamaya çalışıyor: patlamış mısır. Bunun dezavantajları, üretiminin polistiren parçacıklara göre daha pahalı olması ve kemirgenler ile böcekleri çekme eğilimi göstermesidir. Yine de ABD, Kanada ve Avrupa'daki birkaç posta siparişi şirketi ve diğer göndericiler, tereyağı ve tuz hariç olmak üzere patlamış mısırla paketleme yapmaya başladı. Bu tür küçük yenilikler, McDonald's gibi şirketlerin attığı çarpıcı adımlarla birleştiğinde, bir gün çevreye verilen büyük bir zararı ortadan kaldırabilir.

passages.passage_text:
Some time ago, I discovered that one of the chairs in my front hall had a broken leg. I didn't foresee any great difficulty in getting it mended, as there are a whole lot of antique shops in Pimlico Road, which is three minutes' walk from my flat. So, I set forth one morning carrying the chair with me. I went into the first shop confidently expecting a friendly reception, with a kindly man saying: "What a charming chair. Yes, that's quite a simple job. When would you want it back?"

I was quite wrong. The man I approached wouldn't even look at it. I wasn't too concerned; after all, it was only the first try and there are many more shops on both sides of the road.

The reaction at the second shop, though slightly politer, was just the same, and at the third and the fourth, so I decided that my approach must be wrong.

I entered the fifth shop with some confidence because I had concocted a plan. I placed the chair gently on the floor so as not to disturb the damaged leg and said "Would you like to buy a chair?" The rather fierce proprietor looked it over carefully and said, "Yes, not a bad little chair. How much do you want for it?" "£20," I said. "OK," he said, "I'll give you £20." "It's got a slightly broken leg," I said. "Yes, I saw that; it's nothing. Don't worry about it."

Everything was going to plan and I was getting excited. "What will you do with it?" I asked. "Oh, it will be very saleable once the repair is done. I like the bit of old green velvet on the top. I shall leave that - yes, very saleable." "I'll buy it," I said. "What d'ye mean? You've just sold it to me," he said. "Yes I know, but I've changed my mind. As a matter of fact, it is just what I'm looking for - I've got its pair at home. I'll give you 27 quid for it." "You must be crazy," he said. Then suddenly the penny dropped and he smiled and said, "I know what you want. You want me to mend your chair, don't you?" "You're plumb right," I said.

"And what would you have done if I had walked in and said, 'Would you mend this chair for me?' Would you have repaired it?" "No, I wouldn't have done it," he said. "We don't do repairs - not enough money in it and too much of a nuisance. However, I'll mend this chair for you - shall we say a fiver?" He was a very nice man and thought the whole episode rather funny.

passages.title: Antiques Repairs
passages.tts_script:
Antiques Repairs.

Some time ago, I discovered that one of the chairs in my front hall had a broken leg. I didn't foresee any great difficulty in getting it mended, as there are a whole lot of antique shops in Pimlico Road, which is three minutes' walk from my flat. So, I set forth one morning carrying the chair with me. I went into the first shop confidently expecting a friendly reception, with a kindly man saying: "What a charming chair. Yes, that's quite a simple job. When would you want it back?"

I was quite wrong. The man I approached wouldn't even look at it. I wasn't too concerned; after all, it was only the first try and there are many more shops on both sides of the road.

The reaction at the second shop, though slightly politer, was just the same, and at the third and the fourth, so I decided that my approach must be wrong.

I entered the fifth shop with some confidence because I had concocted a plan. I placed the chair gently on the floor so as not to disturb the damaged leg and said, "Would you like to buy a chair?" The rather fierce proprietor looked it over carefully and said, "Yes, not a bad little chair. How much do you want for it?" "20 pounds," I said. "OK," he said, "I'll give you 20 pounds." "It's got a slightly broken leg," I said. "Yes, I saw that; it's nothing. Don't worry about it."

Everything was going to plan and I was getting excited. "What will you do with it?" I asked. "Oh, it will be very saleable once the repair is done. I like the bit of old green velvet on the top. I shall leave that, yes, very saleable." "I'll buy it," I said. "What do you mean? You've just sold it to me," he said. "Yes, I know, but I've changed my mind. As a matter of fact, it is just what I'm looking for. I've got its pair at home. I'll give you 27 quid for it." "You must be crazy," he said. Then suddenly the penny dropped and he smiled and said, "I know what you want. You want me to mend your chair, don't you?" "You're plumb right," I said.

"And what would you have done if I had walked in and said, 'Would you mend this chair for me?' Would you have repaired it?" "No, I wouldn't have done it," he said. "We don't do repairs - not enough money in it and too much of a nuisance. However, I'll mend this chair for you - shall we say a fiver?" He was a very nice man and thought the whole episode rather funny.

task2.model_answer:
In everyday situations, direct requests do not always work, and clever persuasion can sometimes open doors that strict rules keep closed. When people refuse a request because they see only inconvenience, reframing the situation can highlight mutual benefit or break the ice with humor.

In the story, the narrator could not persuade antique dealers to fix his chair because repair work was unprofitable. By staging a playful sale and repurchase, he demonstrated both the chair's value and his willingness to pay, turning a grumpy refusal into a friendly agreement. Similar creativity helps in daily life, such as negotiating freelance work or resolving customer service disputes.

Of course, indirect tactics must remain honest and lighthearted; manipulation that deceives someone into financial loss is unacceptable. When used respectfully, however, wit and creative problem-solving are valuable communication skills.

passages.passage_text:
In 334 B.C., with an army of 35,000 men, Alexander crossed into Asia Minor. In addition to soldiers, the former student of Aristotle brought along scientists to study plant and animal life and to chart the terrain. After capturing the coast of Asia Minor, Alexander marched into Syria and defeated the Persian army at the battle of Issus. Rather than pursuing the fleeing Persian king, Darius III, Alexander stayed with his master plan, which included the capture of coastal ports in order to crush the Persian navy. He captured Tyre, thought to be an impregnable city, and advanced into Egypt. Grateful to Alexander for having liberated them from Persian rule, the Egyptians made him pharaoh. Alexander appointed officials to administer the country and founded a new city, Alexandria.

Having destroyed or captured the Persian fleet, Alexander moved into Mesopotamia in pursuit of Darius in 331 B.C. The Macedonians defeated the numerically superior Persians at Gaugamela, just east of the Tigris River, but Darius escaped. After stopovers at Babylon and at Persepolis, which he burned in revenge for Xerxes' destruction of Athens more than 150 years earlier, Alexander resumed the chase. When he finally caught up with Darius, the Persian king was already dead, killed by Persian conspirators.

Alexander relentlessly pushed deeper into Asia, crossing from Afghanistan into north India, where he defeated the king of Pontus in a costly battle. When Alexander announced plans to push deeper into India, his troops, exhausted and far from home in a strange land, resisted. Yielding to their wishes, Alexander returned to Babylon in 324 B.C. In these campaigns, Alexander proved himself to be a superb strategist and leader of men. Winning every battle, Alexander's army had carved an empire that stretched from Greece to India. Future conquerors, including Caesar and Napoleon, would read of Alexander's career with fascination and longing.

Beginning with 35,000 soldiers and scientists, he conquered Asia Minor, Syria, and Egypt, prioritizing coastal ports like Tyre to cripple the Persian fleet rather than immediately chasing King Darius III. After destroying Persia's naval power, Alexander defeated a larger Persian force at Gaugamela, burned Persepolis in retaliation for Athens' earlier destruction, and pursued Darius until discovering he had been murdered by conspirators. Alexander then pushed into Afghanistan and northern India, defeating local forces before his exhausted troops forced him to turn back to Babylon, cementing his legacy as a brilliant strategist.

task2.model_answer:
Alexander the Great's campaigns show that military success relies as much on careful planning and leadership as on bravery in battle. By securing coastal ports to destroy the Persian navy before advancing inland, Alexander prevented his supply lines from being cut off and demonstrated remarkable strategic foresight. Furthermore, bringing scientists to chart the terrain and study local ecosystems proved that knowledge of unfamiliar lands is a powerful asset during expansion.

However, Alexander's eventual retreat from India highlights an essential limit of leadership: even the most brilliant commander depends on the endurance and morale of his soldiers. Although Alexander won every battle, his troops' exhaustion after years away from home forced him to compromise and return to Babylon. In conclusion, lasting success requires balancing ambitious goals with practical strategy and respect for the limits of the people carrying them out.

Büyük İskender.

MÖ 334 yılında İskender, 35.000 kişilik bir orduyla Küçük Asya'ya geçti. Aristoteles'in eski öğrencisi olan İskender, askerlerin yanı sıra bitki ve hayvan yaşamını incelemek ve arazi haritasını çıkarmak için bilim insanlarını da yanında getirdi. Küçük Asya kıyılarını ele geçirdikten sonra Suriye'ye yürüdü ve İssos Savaşı'nda Pers ordusunu mağlup etti. Kaçan Pers kralı III. Darius'un peşine düşmek yerine, Pers donanmasını ezmek amacıyla kıyı limanlarını ele geçirmeyi de içeren ana planına sadık kaldı. Ele geçirilmesi imkansız sanılan Sur şehrini fethetti ve Mısır'a doğru ilerledi. Kendilerini Pers yönetiminden kurtardığı için İskender'e minnettar olan Mısırlılar onu firavun ilan etti. İskender ülkeyi yönetmeleri için memurlar atadı ve İskenderiye adında yeni bir şehir kurdu.

Pers donanmasını yok ettikten veya ele geçirdikten sonra İskender, MÖ 331'de Darius'un peşinden Mezopotamya'ya girdi. Makedonlar, Dicle Nehri'nin hemen doğusundaki Gaugamela'da sayıca üstün olan Persleri yendi ancak Darius kaçmayı başardı. Babil'de ve 150 yılı aşkın bir süre önce Kserkses'in Atina'yı yerle bir etmesinin intikamını almak için yaktığı Persepolis'te verdiği molaların ardından İskender takibe devam etti. Sonunda Darius'a yetiştiğinde Pers kralı, Pers komplocular tarafından öldürülmüş halde çoktan can vermişti.

İskender durmaksızın Asya'nın derinliklerine ilerledi; Afganistan'dan kuzey Hindistan'a geçerek çetin bir savaşta Pontus kralını yendi. İskender Hindistan'ın daha da içlerine ilerleme planlarını açıkladığında, bitkin düşmüş ve evlerinden uzakta yabancı bir diyarda bulunan askerleri direndi. Onların isteklerine boyun eğen İskender, MÖ 324'te Babil'e geri döndü. Bu seferlerde İskender kendisinin muhteşem bir stratejist ve insanları yöneten bir lider olduğunu kanıtladı. Her savaşı kazanan İskender'in ordusu, Yunanistan'dan Hindistan'a uzanan bir imparatorluk kurmuştu. Sezar ve Napolyon da dahil olmak üzere gelecekteki fatihler, İskender'in kariyerini hayranlık ve özlemle okuyacaktı.

passages.passage_text:
In the late Middle Ages, Latin Christendom was afflicted with severe economic problems. The earlier increases in agricultural production did not continue. Limited use of fertilizers and limited knowledge of conservation exhausted the topsoil. As more grazing lands were converted to the cultivation of cereals, animal husbandry decreased, causing a serious shortage of manure needed for arable land. Intermittent bouts of prolonged heavy rains and frost also hampered agriculture. From 1301 to 1314, there was a general shortage of food, and from 1315 to 1317, famine struck Europe. Throughout the century, starvation and malnutrition were widespread.

Other economic problems abounded. A silver shortage, caused by technical problems in sinking deeper shafts in the mines, led to the debasement of coins and spiraling inflation, which hurt the feudal nobility in particular. Prices for manufactured luxury goods, which the nobility craved, rose rapidly. At the same time, the dues that the nobility collected from peasants diminished. To replace their revenues, lords and knights turned to plunder and warfare.

Compounding the economic crisis was the Black Death, or bubonic plague. This disease was carried by the fleas on brown rats, and probably first struck Mongolia in 1331-32. From there it crossed into Russia. Carried back from Black Sea ports, the plague reached Sicily in 1347. Spreading swiftly throughout much of Europe, the plague attacked an already declining and undernourished population. The first crisis lasted until 1351, and other serious outbreaks occurred in later decades. The crowded cities and towns had the highest mortalities. Perhaps twenty million people - about one-quarter to one-third of the European population - perished in the worst human disaster in recorded history.

Deprived of many of their intellectual and spiritual leaders, the panic-stricken masses drifted into immorality and hysteria. Frenzied forms of religious life and superstitious practices became popular. Flagellants marched from region to region beating each other with sticks and whips in a desperate effort to please God, who they believed had cursed them with the plague. In addition to flagellation and superstition, black magic, witchcraft, and sexual immorality found eager supporters. Dress became increasingly ostentatious and bizarre. Art forms concentrated on morbid scenes of decaying flesh, dances of death, and the torments of Hell. Sometimes this hysteria was directed against the Jews, who were accused of causing the plague by poisoning the wells. Terrible massacres of Jews occurred despite the pleas of the papacy.

passages.title: The Middle Ages in Europe
passages.tts_script:
The Middle Ages in Europe.

In the late Middle Ages, Latin Christendom was afflicted with severe economic problems. The earlier increases in agricultural production did not continue. Limited use of fertilizers and limited knowledge of conservation exhausted the topsoil. As more grazing lands were converted to the cultivation of cereals, animal husbandry decreased, causing a serious shortage of manure needed for arable land. Intermittent bouts of prolonged heavy rains and frost also hampered agriculture. From 1301 to 1314, there was a general shortage of food, and from 1315 to 1317, famine struck Europe. Throughout the century, starvation and malnutrition were widespread.

Other economic problems abounded. A silver shortage, caused by technical problems in sinking deeper shafts in the mines, led to the debasement of coins and spiraling inflation, which hurt the feudal nobility in particular. Prices for manufactured luxury goods, which the nobility craved, rose rapidly. At the same time, the dues that the nobility collected from peasants diminished. To replace their revenues, lords and knights turned to plunder and warfare.

Compounding the economic crisis was the Black Death, or bubonic plague. This disease was carried by the fleas on brown rats, and probably first struck Mongolia in 1331 to 1332. From there it crossed into Russia. Carried back from Black Sea ports, the plague reached Sicily in 1347. Spreading swiftly throughout much of Europe, the plague attacked an already declining and undernourished population. The first crisis lasted until 1351, and other serious outbreaks occurred in later decades. The crowded cities and towns had the highest mortalities. Perhaps twenty million people, about one-quarter to one-third of the European population, perished in the worst human disaster in recorded history.

Deprived of many of their intellectual and spiritual leaders, the panic-stricken masses drifted into immorality and hysteria. Frenzied forms of religious life and superstitious practices became popular. Flagellants marched from region to region beating each other with sticks and whips in a desperate effort to please God, who they believed had cursed them with the plague. In addition to flagellation and superstition, black magic, witchcraft, and sexual immorality found eager supporters. Dress became increasingly ostentatious and bizarre. Art forms concentrated on morbid scenes of decaying flesh, dances of death, and the torments of Hell. Sometimes this hysteria was directed against the Jews, who were accused of causing the plague by poisoning the wells. Terrible massacres of Jews occurred despite the pleas of the papacy.

task1.model_answer: In the late Middle Ages, Europe suffered from overlapping agricultural, financial, and medical catastrophes. Soil exhaustion, reduced livestock manure, and harsh weather caused prolonged food shortages and famine between 1301 and 1317, leaving the population malnourished. Simultaneously, mining difficulties created a silver shortage that led to debased coins and severe inflation, driving impoverished nobles to warfare and plunder. Into this weakened society arrived the Black Death in 1347, carried by fleas on brown rats. Killing roughly one-quarter to one-third of Europe's population—especially in crowded cities—the plague also destroyed intellectual and spiritual leadership, triggering widespread superstition, flagellation, bizarre fashion, morbid art, and violent persecution of Jewish communities.
task1.prompt: Summarize the causes and major social consequences of the economic and public health crises in late medieval Europe.
task1.title: Summary of Late Medieval Crises

task2.model_answer:
Severe economic instability and widespread disease often undermine social order because they erode the institutions and security that societies rely on. In late medieval Europe, years of famine and inflation had already strained daily life before the Black Death struck. When the plague killed up to a third of the population, including many intellectual and religious leaders, communities lost both practical guidance and moral stability.

Under intense fear and uncertainty, people often search for immediate explanations or scapegoats rather than accepting complex realities. In medieval Europe, this panic fueled extreme rituals like flagellation, bizarre trends in art and clothing, and false accusations against minorities such as Jewish communities. Even in modern crises, economic hardship and pandemics can increase social tension, misinformation, and distrust. Therefore, maintaining strong public leadership, accurate information, and mutual support is vital to prevent fear from turning into collective hysteria.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Avrupa'da Orta Çağ.

Geç Orta Çağ'da Latin Hristiyan dünyası ciddi ekonomik sorunlarla boğuşuyordu. Tarımsal üretimde daha önce görülen artışlar devam etmedi. Gübrenin sınırlı kullanımı ve toprak koruma konusundaki yetersiz bilgi, üst toprağı verimsizleştirdi. Daha fazla otlak alan tahıl ekimine dönüştürüldükçe hayvancılık azaldı ve bu durum ekilebilir araziler için gereken gübrede ciddi bir kıtlığa yol açtı. Zaman zaman ortaya çıkan uzun süreli şiddetli yağmurlar ve don olayları da tarımı sekteye uğrattı. 1301'den 1314'e kadar genel bir gıda sıkıntısı yaşandı ve 1315'ten 1317'ye kadar Avrupa'yı kıtlık vurdu. Yüzyıl boyunca açlık ve yetersiz beslenme yaygın olarak görüldü.

Başka ekonomik sorunlar da baş göstermişti. Madenlerde daha derin kuyular açılmasındaki teknik sorunların yol açtığı gümüş kıtlığı, sikkelerin ayarının düşürülmesine ve özellikle feodal soylulara zarar veren hızla artan bir enflasyona neden oldu. Soyluların çok arzuladığı imal edilmiş lüks malların fiyatları hızla yükseldi. Aynı zamanda soyluların köylülerden topladığı vergiler azaldı. Gelirlerini telafi etmek için lordlar ve şövalyeler yağma ve savaşa yöneldi.

Ekonomik krizi daha da ağırlaştıran şey ise Kara Ölüm ya da diğer adıyla hıyarcıklı veba oldu. Bu hastalık kahverengi sıçanların üzerindeki pireler tarafından taşınıyordu ve muhtemelen ilk olarak 1331-1332 yıllarında Moğolistan'da ortaya çıktı. Oradan Rusya'ya geçti. Karadeniz limanlarından geri taşınan veba, 1347'de Sicilya'ya ulaştı. Avrupa'nın büyük bir bölümüne hızla yayılan veba, nüfusu zaten azalmakta olan ve yetersiz beslenen bir topluluğa saldırdı. İlk kriz 1351'e kadar sürdü ve sonraki on yıllarda başka ciddi salgınlar da meydana geldi. Kalabalık şehirler ve kasabalar en yüksek ölüm oranlarına sahne oldu. Kayıtlı tarihteki bu en büyük insanlık felaketinde Avrupa nüfusunun yaklaşık dörtte biri ila üçte birine karşılık gelen belki de yirmi milyon insan hayatını kaybetti.

Entelektüel ve ruhani liderlerinin çoğundan yoksun kalan panik halindeki kitleler, ahlaksızlığa ve histeriye sürüklendi. Dini yaşamın çılgınca biçimleri ve batıl inanç uygulamaları yaygınlaştı. Kamçıcılar, kendilerini veba ile lanetlediğine inandıkları Tanrı'yı hoşnut etmek için umutsuz bir çabayla birbirlerini sopa ve kırbaçlarla döverek bölgeden bölgeye yürüdü. Kendini kırbaçlama ve batıl inançların yanı sıra kara büyü, cadılık ve cinsel ahlaksızlık da hevesli destekçiler buldu. Giyim giderek daha gösterişli ve tuhaf bir hal aldı. Sanat biçimleri çürüyen etlerin hastalıklı sahnelerine, ölüm danslarına ve Cehennem azaplarına odaklandı. Bazen bu histeri, kuyuları zehirleyerek vebaya yol açmakla suçlanan Yahudilere yöneldi. Papalığın yakarışlarına rağmen korkunç Yahudi katliamları yaşandı.

passages.passage_text:
Disillusionment with one's parents, however good and adequate they may be both as parents and as individuals, is to some degree inevitable. Most children have a very high ideal of their parents that can hardly stand up to realistic evaluation unless the parents themselves have been unsatisfactory. Parents would be greatly surprised and deeply touched if they realised how much belief their children usually have in their character and infallibility, and how much this faith means to a child. If parents were prepared for this adolescent reaction, and realised that it was a sign that the child was growing up and developing valuable powers of observation and independent judgement, they would not be very hurt, so they would not drive the child into opposition by resenting and resisting it.

The adolescent, with his passion for sincerity, always respects a parent who admits that he is wrong, or ignorant, or even that he has been unfair or unjust. What the child cannot forgive is the parents' refusal to admit these charges if the child knows them to be true.

Victorian parents believed that they kept their dignity by retreating behind an unreasoning authoritarian attitude; in fact, they did nothing of the kind, but children were then too cowed to let them know how they really felt. Today, we tend to go to the other extreme, but, on the whole, this is a healthier attitude both for the child and the parent. It is always wiser and safer to face up to reality, however painful it may be at the moment.

task1.model_answer: Children naturally admire their parents and view them as infallible, so experiencing some disillusionment during adolescence is unavoidable. Rather than taking this shift personally, parents should recognize it as healthy evidence of growing observation and independent judgement. Teenagers value honesty above all; they respect parents who openly admit being wrong, ignorant, or unfair, whereas denying obvious faults damages trust. Unlike Victorian parents, who hid behind strict authority while intimidating children into silence, modern parents tend toward greater openness. Even if taken far, facing reality honestly is ultimately healthier and safer for both parents and children.

task2.model_answer:
Openness and honesty between parents and teenagers build far stronger relationships than rigid authority ever could. As the passage highlights, adolescents naturally begin evaluating their parents realistically, not out of disrespect, but because they are developing independent judgement. When parents pretend to be infallible or hide behind strict rules, teenagers recognize the dishonesty and may become resentful or distant.

In contrast, a parent who admits mistakes models maturity and sincerity. Acknowledging an unfair decision or an error does not weaken parental authority; instead, it earns genuine respect and teaches young people how to handle their own mistakes responsibly. Of course, parents still need to set reasonable boundaries and guide their children with care. Nevertheless, authority rooted in mutual respect and truth is far more durable than obedience driven by fear. Ultimately, honest communication helps adolescents transition into confident, fair-minded adults.

Ebeveyn Otoritesi.

Anne ve babalar hem ebeveyn hem de birey olarak ne kadar iyi ve yeterli olurlarsa olsunlar, onlara karşı hayal kırıklığı yaşamak bir dereceye kadar kaçınılmazdır. Çoğu çocuğun anne ve babasına dair çok yüksek bir ideali vardır ve ebeveynlerin kendileri yetersiz olmadıkça bu ideal gerçekçi bir değerlendirmeye pek dayanamaz. Ebeveynler, çocuklarının onların karakterine ve yanılmazlığına genellikle ne kadar çok inandığını ve bu inancın bir çocuk için ne kadar büyük bir anlam taşıdığını fark etselerdi çok şaşırır ve derinden duygulanırlardı. Eğer ebeveynler bu ergenlik tepkisine hazırlıklı olsalardı ve bunun çocuğun büyüdüğünün, değerli gözlem ve bağımsız yargı yetenekleri geliştirdiğinin bir işareti olduğunu anlasalardı, bu kadar incinmezler ve buna içerleyip direnerek çocuğu karşıt bir tutuma itmezlerdi.

Ergen, samimiyete duyduğu tutkuyla, hatalı olduğunu, bilmediğini, hatta haksızlık veya adaletsizlik yaptığını kabul eden bir ebeveyne her zaman saygı duyar. Çocuğun affedemediği şey ise, kendisi doğru olduğunu bildiği halde ebeveynlerin bu suçlamaları kabul etmeyi reddetmesidir.

Viktorya dönemi ebeveynleri, mantıksız ve otoriter bir tavrın arkasına sığınarak saygınlıklarını koruduklarına inanırlardı; aslında böyle bir şey yaptıkları yoktu, ancak çocuklar o zamanlar gerçekte ne hissettiklerini belli edemeyecek kadar sindirilmişlerdi. Bugün ise diğer uca gitme eğilimindeyiz, ancak genel olarak bu, hem çocuk hem de ebeveyn için daha sağlıklı bir tutumdur. O an için ne kadar acı verici olursa olsun, gerçekle yüzleşmek her zaman daha akıllıca ve daha güvenlidir.

passages.passage_text:
The increasing divorce rate can be seen as a 'product of conflict between the changing economic system and its social and ideological superstructure (notably the family)'. In advanced capitalist industrial societies, there is an increasing demand for cheap female wage labour. Wives are encouraged to take up paid employment not only because there is a demand for their services, but also because the capitalist controlled media has raised 'material aspirations' which regulate the demand for desirable goods. These material aspirations can only be satisfied by both spouses working as wage earners. However, conflict results from the contradiction between female wage labour and the normative expectations which surround married life. 'Working wives' are still expected to be primarily responsible for housework and raising children. In addition, they are still expected, to some degree, to play a subservient role to the male head of the household. These normative expectations contradict the wife's role as a wage earner since she is now sharing the economic burden with her husband. Conflict between the spouses can result from this contradiction, and conflict can lead to marital breakdown.

While laws and procedures regulating divorce were altered, the divorce rate tended to increase quickly and since each new piece of legislation made divorce more readily available, the rate rose rapidly for a time before leveling off. Today there is one divorce in Britain for every three marriages. (In the USA the rate is one in two.) Many people have suggested that the higher divorce rates reflect an underlying increase in marital instability; the problem with this argument is that we have no way of knowing how many 'unstable' or 'unhappy' marriages existed before legislation made it possible to dissolve them in a public (and recordable) form. Some commentators have gone further and argued that more permissive divorce laws in themselves cause marital breakdown. But we can certainly be sceptical of such a view, suggesting as it does that happily married couples can suddenly be persuaded to abandon their relationship, propelled by the attraction of a new divorce law. A more plausible explanation for rises in the divorce rate after the passage of a law is that unhappily married couples were for the first time given access to a legal solution to pre-existent marital problems; in other words, changes in divorce laws are less likely to cause marital breakdown than to provide new types of solutions where breakdown has already occurred.
