passages.title: Two Views of Divorce
passages.tts_script:
Two Views of Divorce.

The increasing divorce rate can be seen as a product of conflict between the changing economic system and its social and ideological superstructure, notably the family. In advanced capitalist industrial societies, there is an increasing demand for cheap female wage labour. Wives are encouraged to take up paid employment not only because there is a demand for their services, but also because the capitalist controlled media has raised material aspirations which regulate the demand for desirable goods. These material aspirations can only be satisfied by both spouses working as wage earners. However, conflict results from the contradiction between female wage labour and the normative expectations which surround married life. Working wives are still expected to be primarily responsible for housework and raising children. In addition, they are still expected, to some degree, to play a subservient role to the male head of the household. These normative expectations contradict the wife's role as a wage earner since she is now sharing the economic burden with her husband. Conflict between the spouses can result from this contradiction, and conflict can lead to marital breakdown.

While laws and procedures regulating divorce were altered, the divorce rate tended to increase quickly, and since each new piece of legislation made divorce more readily available, the rate rose rapidly for a time before leveling off. Today there is one divorce in Britain for every three marriages. In the USA the rate is one in two. Many people have suggested that the higher divorce rates reflect an underlying increase in marital instability; the problem with this argument is that we have no way of knowing how many unstable or unhappy marriages existed before legislation made it possible to dissolve them in a public and recordable form. Some commentators have gone further and argued that more permissive divorce laws in themselves cause marital breakdown. But we can certainly be sceptical of such a view, suggesting as it does that happily married couples can suddenly be persuaded to abandon their relationship, propelled by the attraction of a new divorce law. A more plausible explanation for rises in the divorce rate after the passage of a law is that unhappily married couples were for the first time given access to a legal solution to pre-existent marital problems; in other words, changes in divorce laws are less likely to cause marital breakdown than to provide new types of solutions where breakdown has already occurred.

The first view focuses on economic and social pressures: as capitalist societies demand cheap female labour and promote higher material aspirations, both spouses must earn wages. However, working wives are still expected to handle housework, childcare, and a subordinate domestic role, creating conflict that can end marriages. The second view examines legal reform. Rather than causing marital breakdown or proving greater instability, more accessible divorce laws simply give unhappily married couples a formal legal solution to problems that already existed before divorce became widely available.

task2.model_answer:
Rising divorce rates are often blamed on modern legal reforms, yet deeper social and economic shifts play a far greater role. As the passage suggests, easier access to divorce does not break apart happy marriages; instead, it allows couples in already troubled relationships to separate legally and safely.

More importantly, changing gender roles inside the household create genuine strain when social expectations fail to keep pace with economic reality. When both partners work full-time to meet rising living costs, expecting one spouse to shoulder almost all domestic chores and childcare inevitably generates resentment. Without a fair division of unpaid labour and mutual respect, financial partnership alone cannot sustain a marriage.

Ultimately, reducing marital breakdown requires addressing workplace pressures and unequal household expectations rather than restricting legal rights. Societies that support balanced family responsibilities give marriages a much stronger foundation to endure.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Boşanmaya İki Farklı Bakış.

Artan boşanma oranı, değişen ekonomik sistem ile başta aile olmak üzere onun toplumsal ve ideolojik üstyapısı arasındaki çatışmanın bir ürünü olarak görülebilir. Gelişmiş kapitalist sanayi toplumlarında, ucuz kadın ücretli emeğine yönelik artan bir talep vardır. Evli kadınlar yalnızca hizmetlerine talep olduğu için değil, aynı zamanda kapitalistlerin kontrolündeki medyanın arzu edilen mallara olan talebi düzenleyen maddi beklentileri yükseltmesi nedeniyle de ücretli bir işte çalışmaya teşvik edilmektedir. Bu maddi beklentiler ancak her iki eşin de ücretli çalışan olarak çalışmasıyla karşılanabilir. Ancak, kadınların ücretli çalışması ile evlilik hayatını çevreleyen normatif beklentiler arasındaki çelişkiden bir çatışma doğar. Çalışan kadınlardan hâlâ ev işlerinden ve çocuk yetiştirmekten birincil derecede sorumlu olmaları beklenmektedir. Buna ek olarak, bir ölçüde evin reisi olan erkeğe karşı hâlâ itaatkâr bir rol oynamaları beklenmektedir. Bu normatif beklentiler, kadının artık ekonomik yükü kocasıyla paylaştığı düşünüldüğünde ücretli çalışan rolüyle çelişmektedir. Bu çelişkiden eşler arasında çatışma doğabilir ve çatışma da evliliğin yıkılmasına yol açabilir.

Boşanmayı düzenleyen yasalar ve prosedürler değiştirildikçe boşanma oranı hızla artma eğilimi göstermiştir ve her yeni yasal düzenleme boşanmayı daha kolay erişilebilir kıldığından, bu oran bir süre hızla yükseldikten sonra dengelenmiştir. Bugün Britanya'da her üç evliliğe karşılık bir boşanma gerçekleşmektedir. ABD'de ise bu oran ikide birdir. Pek çok kişi, yüksek boşanma oranlarının evlilikteki istikrarsızlığın altında yatan bir artışı yansıttığını öne sürmüştür; bu argümanın sorunu, yasalar evlilikleri kamuya açık ve kayıt altına alınabilir bir biçimde sonlandırmayı mümkün kılmadan önce ne kadar istikrarsız veya mutsuz evlilik olduğunu bilmemizin hiçbir yolu olmamasıdır. Bazı yorumcular daha da ileri giderek, daha esnek boşanma yasalarının kendi başlarına evliliklerin yıkılmasına yol açtığını savunmuşlardır. Ancak, yeni bir boşanma yasasının cazibesine kapılan mutlu evli çiftlerin ilişkilerini terk etmeye aniden ikna edilebileceğini öne süren böyle bir görüşe elbette şüpheyle yaklaşabiliriz. Bir yasanın kabul edilmesinden sonra boşanma oranlarında görülen artışlar için daha makul bir açıklama, mutsuz evli çiftlere önceden var olan evlilik sorunlarına karşı ilk kez yasal bir çözüme erişim imkânı verilmiş olmasıdır; başka bir deyişle, boşanma yasalarındaki değişikliklerin evliliğin yıkılmasına neden olma ihtimali, yıkımın zaten gerçekleştiği durumlarda yeni çözüm yolları sunma ihtimalinden daha düşüktür.

passages.passage_text:
In our culture, success in itself implies no superior virtue. A book is not necessarily a superior one because it makes the best seller lists. Most books that achieve this distinction appeal to the mass market and are generally supported by extensive publicity. While success in the business world may require a high degree of business acumen, this quality has never before been considered a personal virtue. Today it is the achievement that counts, not the personal qualities of the individual. Sometimes success is achieved by qualities that are anything but virtuous. Until his downfall, Hitler was considered a success by a great many people throughout the world. Of course, success may attend the individual with superior abilities; however, what is acknowledged is not the personal virtue of the individual but his achievement.

The actual accomplishment is often relatively unimportant. The author of six good books may be less of a success than the writer of one best seller. What does count is the recognition. Without recognition one cannot be considered a public success.

To achieve success means to rise above the crowd, to stand out from the mass of people and be recognized as an individual. For the writer, it means that what he says or writes is now regarded as important. "He counts" is the way one successful author was described. Before his success, he didn't 'count' although what he wrote before his success may have had greater value than his subsequent work. Through success he had become important. We see this all the time. As soon as a person becomes successful, he is listened to with respect. Since he has 'made it,' his words may tell the rest of us who are still struggling the secret of his good fortune. The successful person is important to all who wish to be successful.

task2.model_answer:
In today's media-driven society, public recognition often overshadows genuine merit, yet true success should still be measured by the value of a person's contribution rather than fame alone. passages.tts_script_tr:
Başarı.

Kültürümüzde başarı, tek başına üstün bir erdem anlamına gelmez. Bir kitabın çok satanlar listesine girmesi, onun mutlaka üstün bir kitap olduğu anlamına gelmez. Bu ayrıcalığa ulaşan kitapların çoğu kitle pazarına hitap eder ve genellikle kapsamlı tanıtım kampanyalarıyla desteklenir. İş dünyasında başarı yüksek düzeyde bir ticari zekâ gerektirse de, bu nitelik daha önce hiçbir zaman kişisel bir erdem olarak görülmemiştir. Bugün önemli olan bireyin kişisel nitelikleri değil, elde ettiği başarıdır. Bazen başarıya, erdemli olmaktan çok uzak niteliklerle ulaşılır. Çöküşüne kadar Hitler, dünya çapında pek çok insan tarafından başarılı biri olarak görülüyordu. Elbette başarı, üstün yeteneklere sahip bireyin yanında olabilir; ancak takdir edilen şey bireyin kişisel erdemi değil, başarısıdır.

Asıl elde edilen eser ya da icraat genellikle görece önemsizdir. Altı iyi kitabın yazarı, tek bir çok satan kitabın yazarından daha az başarılı sayılabilir. Asıl önemli olan tanınmaktır. Tanınma olmadan kişi toplum nezdinde başarılı sayılamaz.

Başarıya ulaşmak, kalabalığın üzerine çıkmak, insan yığınından sıyrılmak ve bir birey olarak tanınmak demektir. Yazar için bu, söylediklerinin veya yazdıklarının artık önemli görüldüğü anlamına gelir. Başarılı bir yazar, "O önemli biri" sözleriyle tanımlanmıştı. Başarısından önce, o dönemde yazdıkları sonraki eserlerinden daha büyük bir değere sahip olsa bile 'önemli' sayılmıyordu. Başarı sayesinde önemli hale gelmişti. Bunu her zaman görürüz. Bir kişi başarılı olur olmaz saygıyla dinlenir. Artık 'başardığı' için, sözleri hâlâ mücadele eden geri kalanlarımıza bu şansının sırrını anlatabilir. Başarılı kişi, başarılı olmak isteyen herkes için önemlidir.

task2.model_answer:
Restricting contact with the outside world may give rulers short-term political stability, yet in the long run it harms a society far more than it helps. When governments ban foreign books, limit travel, and block international trade, they also cut off the flow of new scientific ideas, technologies, and cultural perspectives. Engaging cautiously with other nations allows a country to preserve its own traditions while still benefiting from global knowledge and commerce.

passages.passage_text:
For the past two years, I have been studying cancer survivors at UCLA, trying to find out why it is that some people respond much better to their treatment than do others. At first, I thought that some patients did well because their illnesses were not as severe as the illnesses of others. On closer scrutiny, however, I discovered that severity of the illness was only one of a number of factors that accounted for the difference between those who get well and those who don't. The patients I am talking about here received, upon diagnosis, whatever therapy - medication, radiation, surgery - their individual cases demanded. Yet, the response to such treatments was hardly uniform. Some patients fared much better in their therapies than others.

What was it, then, that was different? Was there any one thing that all survivors had in common? Yes. I have found that the major characteristics of these survivors were very similar. Among the similarities are:
- They all had a strong will to live.
- They were not panicky about their illness.
- They had confidence in their ability to persevere.
- Despite all the forecasts to the contrary, they believed they could make it.
- They were capable of joyous response.
- They were convinced that their treatment would work.

The Placebo Effect

The mind-body effect should not be surprising in view of the experience over the years with placebos. The term 'placebo' is used to describe a 'pill' that contains no medical ingredients but that often produces the same effect as genuine medication. Placebos provide ample proof that expectations can have an effect on body chemistry. According to a recent article on placebos in Medical World News, studies conducted over the past 25 years have shown that placebos satisfactorily relieved symptoms in an average of 35 per cent of patients tested. These symptoms include: fever, severe post-operative pain, anginal pain, headache, and anxiety, among other complaints. The explanation for this strange phenomenon is that the human mind can create actual changes in body chemistry as a result of what it believes. If, for example, a person believes that a certain medication contains a substance that can accomplish a specific need, the body tends to move in that direction.

An increasing number of scientists now contend that the body's healing system and its belief system are closely related. That is why hope, faith, and the will to live can be vital factors in the struggle against disease. The belief system converts positive expectations into plus factors in any contest against illness.

Modern medicine relies heavily on surgery, medication, and advanced technology, yet a patient's mindset should also receive serious attention during treatment. İnancın İyileştirici Gücü.

Son iki yıldır UCLA'da kanseri yenen hastalar üzerinde çalışıyor, bazı insanların tedavilerine neden diğerlerinden çok daha iyi yanıt verdiğini anlamaya çalışıyorum. Başlangıçta, bazı hastaların hastalıkları diğerlerininki kadar ağır olmadığı için iyiye gittiğini düşünmüştüm. Ancak daha yakından incelediğimde, hastalığın şiddetinin iyileşenlerle iyileşemeyenler arasındaki farkı açıklayan pek çok etmenden yalnızca biri olduğunu keşfettim. Burada sözünü ettiğim hastalar, teşhis konulduktan sonra kendi özel durumlarının gerektirdiği her türlü terapi, ilaç, radyasyon veya cerrahi tedaviyi aldılar. Yine de bu tedavilere verilen yanıt hiç de tekdüze değildi. Bazı hastalar tedavilerinde diğerlerinden çok daha iyi sonuçlar aldı.

Öyleyse farklı olan neydi? Hayatta kalanların hepsinin ortak bir noktası var mıydı? Evet. Bu iyileşen kişilerin başlıca özelliklerinin birbirine çok benzediğini gördüm. Benzerlikler şunları içeriyor:
Hepsinin güçlü bir yaşama arzusu vardı.
Hastalıkları konusunda paniğe kapılmamışlardı.
Azimle direnme yeteneklerine güveniyorlardı.
Aksini söyleyen tüm tahminlere rağmen başarabileceklerine inanıyorlardı.
Neşeyle karşılık verebiliyorlardı.
Tedavilerinin işe yarayacağına ikna olmuşlardı.

Plasebo Etkisi.

Yıllar boyunca plasebolarla edinilen deneyimler göz önüne alındığında, zihin-beden etkisi şaşırtıcı olmamalıdır. 'Plasebo' terimi, hiçbir tıbbi etken madde içermeyen ancak çoğu zaman gerçek bir ilaçla aynı etkiyi yaratan bir 'hapı' tanımlamak için kullanılır. Plasebolar, beklentilerin vücut kimyası üzerinde bir etkiye sahip olabileceğine dair bolca kanıt sunar. Medical World News'da plasebolar üzerine yayımlanan yakın tarihli bir makaleye göre, son 25 yılda yapılan araştırmalar, plaseboların test edilen hastaların ortalama yüzde 35'inde belirtileri tatmin edici düzeyde hafiflettiğini göstermiştir. Bu belirtiler arasında ateş, şiddetli ameliyat sonrası ağrı, anjina ağrısı, baş ağrısı, kaygı ve diğer şikâyetler yer almaktadır. Bu tuhaf olgunun açıklaması, insan zihninin inandığı şeyler sonucunda vücut kimyasında gerçek değişiklikler yaratabilmesidir. Örneğin bir kişi, belirli bir ilacın özel bir ihtiyacı karşılayabilecek bir madde içerdiğine inanırsa, vücut o yönde tepki verme eğilimi gösterir.

Artan sayıda bilim insanı artık vücudun iyileşme sistemi ile inanç sisteminin yakından ilişkili olduğunu savunmaktadır. İşte bu yüzden umut, inanç ve yaşama arzusu hastalığa karşı mücadelede hayati etkenler olabilir. İnanç sistemi, hastalığa karşı verilen her mücadelede olumlu beklentileri artı değerlere dönüştürür.

passages.passage_text:
Memory, like sweatshirts, comes in three sizes. There is a sensory storage system which can hold information for only a very brief time period. Next is a short-term storage which can hold a small amount of information. Finally, you have a long-term storage system which holds vast amounts of information.

What psychological processes are involved in remembering a stimulus which is briefly perceived, such as the license number of a car? Psychologists have discovered that a stimulus is maintained in a sensory storage system which holds information for less than a second. The sensory storage system is called iconic memory if visual stimuli are involved or echoic memory if the stimulation is auditory.

Your sensory storage system appears to operate in a fairly automatic way. There seems to be no voluntary action you can take to prolong the life of information from sensory storage without using the next stage of memory, called short-term memory (STM), or primary memory.

Information can be recycled in short-term memory by a process called rehearsal. When rehearsal is prevented or disrupted, information in short-term memory is lost and so cannot enter long-term memory (LTM). However, once information has entered long-term memory, rehearsal is no longer necessary to guarantee that information is not forgotten. While preventing items from being forgotten is the major difficulty in short-term memory, long-term memory suffers from the opposite problem. There is so much information contained in long-term memory that locating and retrieving this information can be quite difficult. Indeed, psychologists distinguish between information which is available in long-term memory and that which is accessible. All information in long-term memory is considered available; that is, it can be remembered under the proper circumstances. But only that information which actually is remembered is accessible. Thus, accessible information is always available, but available information cannot always be accessible. The process of obtaining memory information from wherever it is stored is called retrieval. In order for information to be accessible, it must first be retrieved. Retrieval of information from long-term memory is a difficult process and is not always successful. Retrieval from short-term memory is considerably easier, and many models of short-term memory assume that if an item is available in short-term memory, it is automatically accessible.

While information in short-term memory is coded primarily by acoustic features (how the words sound when spoken), information in long-term memory is organized primarily according to what the words mean. While interference in short-term memory is based upon acoustic relationships, interference in long-term memory occurs among semantically related words.

The most dramatic distinction between short and long-term memory systems lies in their respective capacities - the number of items each system can store. Short-term memory has a very limited capacity compared to the almost unlimited storage capacity of long-term memory.

passages.title: Memory
passages.tts_script:
Memory.

Memory, like sweatshirts, comes in three sizes. There is a sensory storage system which can hold information for only a very brief time period. Next is a short-term storage which can hold a small amount of information. Finally, you have a long-term storage system which holds vast amounts of information.

What psychological processes are involved in remembering a stimulus which is briefly perceived, such as the license number of a car? Psychologists have discovered that a stimulus is maintained in a sensory storage system which holds information for less than a second. The sensory storage system is called iconic memory if visual stimuli are involved, or echoic memory if the stimulation is auditory.

Your sensory storage system appears to operate in a fairly automatic way. There seems to be no voluntary action you can take to prolong the life of information from sensory storage without using the next stage of memory, called short-term memory, or STM, or primary memory.

Information can be recycled in short-term memory by a process called rehearsal. When rehearsal is prevented or disrupted, information in short-term memory is lost and so cannot enter long-term memory, or LTM. However, once information has entered long-term memory, rehearsal is no longer necessary to guarantee that information is not forgotten. While preventing items from being forgotten is the major difficulty in short-term memory, long-term memory suffers from the opposite problem. There is so much information contained in long-term memory that locating and retrieving this information can be quite difficult. Indeed, psychologists distinguish between information which is available in long-term memory and that which is accessible. All information in long-term memory is considered available; that is, it can be remembered under the proper circumstances. But only that information which actually is remembered is accessible. Thus, accessible information is always available, but available information cannot always be accessible. The process of obtaining memory information from wherever it is stored is called retrieval. In order for information to be accessible, it must first be retrieved. Retrieval of information from long-term memory is a difficult process and is not always successful. Retrieval from short-term memory is considerably easier, and many models of short-term memory assume that if an item is available in short-term memory, it is automatically accessible.

While information in short-term memory is coded primarily by acoustic features, meaning how the words sound when spoken, information in long-term memory is organized primarily according to what the words mean. While interference in short-term memory is based upon acoustic relationships, interference in long-term memory occurs among semantically related words.

The most dramatic distinction between short and long-term memory systems lies in their respective capacities, the number of items each system can store. Short-term memory has a very limited capacity compared to the almost unlimited storage capacity of long-term memory.

task1.model_answer: Psychologists divide human memory into three storage systems: sensory, short-term, and long-term memory. Sensory storage holds visual (iconic) or auditory (echoic) stimuli automatically for less than a second. To keep this information longer, it must move to short-term memory (STM), which has a very limited capacity and encodes information primarily by sound. Through rehearsal, items in STM can be transferred to long-term memory (LTM), an almost unlimited system organized by meaning. While STM's main challenge is preventing rapid forgetting, LTM's difficulty lies in retrieval: although stored information remains available, locating and making it accessible is not always successful.

task2.model_answer:
Understanding how human memory works can significantly improve the way students study for exams. Because short-term memory has a very limited capacity and loses information quickly when rehearsal is interrupted, simply reading notes once is rarely effective. Instead, learners should minimize distractions and actively rehearse key points so that information can successfully enter long-term memory.

Furthermore, knowing that long-term memory organizes information by meaning rather than sound suggests that rote memorization is less useful than deep understanding. When students connect new vocabulary or concepts to ideas they already know, they build stronger semantic networks. Although long-term memory holds vast amounts of information, retrieval can still fail if material is poorly organized. Practicing active recall—testing oneself without looking at notes—trains the brain to retrieve stored knowledge reliably. By aligning study habits with how memory actually functions, students can retain information longer and access it more easily under exam pressure.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Hafıza.

Hafıza da tıpkı sweatshirtler gibi üç boyutta gelir. Bilgiyi yalnızca çok kısa bir süre tutabilen bir duyusal depolama sistemi vardır. Ardından, az miktarda bilgi tutabilen kısa süreli depolama gelir. Son olarak, çok büyük miktarda bilgiyi barındıran uzun süreli depolama sistemi bulunur.

Bir arabanın plaka numarası gibi kısa süreliğine algılanan bir uyaranı hatırlamada hangi psikolojik süreçler rol oynar? Psikologlar, bir uyaranın bilgiyi bir saniyeden kısa bir süre tutan duyusal bir depolama sisteminde muhafaza edildiğini keşfetmişlerdir. Duyusal depolama sistemi, görsel uyaranlar söz konusu olduğunda ikonik bellek, uyarım işitsel olduğunda ise ekoik bellek olarak adlandırılır.

Duyusal depolama sisteminiz oldukça otomatik bir şekilde çalışıyor gibi görünmektedir. Kısa süreli bellek (STM) ya da birincil bellek olarak adlandırılan bir sonraki bellek aşamasını kullanmadan, duyusal depodaki bilginin ömrünü uzatmak için yapabileceğiniz gönüllü bir eylem yok gibi görünmektedir.

Bilgi, tekrarlama adı verilen bir süreçle kısa süreli bellekte yeniden döndürülebilir. Tekrarlama engellendiğinde veya kesintiye uğradığında, kısa süreli bellekteki bilgi kaybolur ve bu nedenle uzun süreli belleğe (LTM) giremez. Ancak bilgi bir kez uzun süreli belleğe girdikten sonra, bilginin unutulmamasını sağlamak için artık tekrarlama gerekli değildir. Öğelerin unutulmasını önlemek kısa süreli bellekteki en büyük zorlukken, uzun süreli bellek bunun tam tersi bir sorundan muzdariptir. Uzun süreli bellekte o kadar çok bilgi vardır ki, bu bilgiyi bulmak ve geri çağırmak oldukça zor olabilir. Nitekim psikologlar, uzun süreli bellekte mevcut olan bilgi ile erişilebilir olan bilgi arasında ayrım yaparlar. Uzun süreli bellekteki tüm bilgiler mevcut kabul edilir; yani uygun koşullar altında hatırlanabilir. Ancak yalnızca gerçekten hatırlanan bilgiler erişilebilirdir. Dolayısıyla erişilebilir bilgi her zaman mevcuttur, fakat mevcut bilgi her zaman erişilebilir olmayabilir. Bellek bilgisini depolandığı yerden alma sürecine geri çağırma denir. Bilginin erişilebilir olması için önce geri çağrılması gerekir. Uzun süreli bellekten bilgi geri çağırma zor bir süreçtir ve her zaman başarılı olmaz. Kısa süreli bellekten geri çağırma ise oldukça kolaydır ve kısa süreli belleğe dair birçok model, bir öğe kısa süreli bellekte mevcutsa otomatik olarak erişilebilir olduğunu varsayar.

Kısa süreli bellekteki bilgi öncelikli olarak akustik özelliklere, yani kelimelerin söylendiğinde nasıl ses çıkardığına göre kodlanırken; uzun süreli bellekteki bilgi öncelikli olarak kelimelerin ne anlama geldiğine göre düzenlenir. Kısa süreli bellekteki karışma akustik ilişkilere dayanırken, uzun süreli bellekteki karışma anlamsal olarak ilişkili kelimeler arasında gerçekleşir.

Kısa ve uzun süreli bellek sistemleri arasındaki en çarpıcı fark, her bir sistemin depolayabileceği öğe sayısı olan kendi kapasitelerinde yatar. Kısa süreli bellek, uzun süreli belleğin neredeyse sınırsız depolama kapasitesine kıyasla çok sınırlı bir kapasiteye sahiptir.

passages.passage_text:
Education in Britain is primarily the responsibility of local educational authorities although the central government lays down guidelines and provides or withholds money. From the end of the Second World War until the 1960's, education under State control depended on the '11-plus' examination, taken by all pupils between the ages of eleven and twelve. The most successful went to grammar schools or direct-grant schools, while the rest went to secondary modern schools. Since the 1960's, almost all local authorities have introduced comprehensive schools, where all pupils attend the same school, even though there is usually an attempt to separate them according to ability once they are there. Local authorities where the Labour Party is usually in control tend, by now, to be almost completely comprehensive; those where the Conservatives hold power have been more resistant to the change.

Throughout this period, the public schools, which are private in all except name, have continued to exist, independent of the State system. Some became direct-grant schools, accepting students who had passed the 11-plus examination and were paid for by local authorities, but this system came to an end in many cases when a Labour-controlled local authority refused to go on paying the grants because of its commitment to comprehensive education.

The public debate in England and Wales between the supporters of comprehensive schools and those who want to retain or revive grammar schools continues unabated. Every year statistics are produced to demonstrate that comprehensive schools provide better education than grammar schools (and in some cases, better than the prestigious private sector). These statistics are immediately contradicted by others proving the opposite. The local authorities have, on the whole, been converted to the comprehensive system, in some cases with enthusiasm, in others with marked reluctance. Yet, the real complication of the debate stems from the fact that although arguments are usually stated in educational terms, almost all of them are based on political opinions.

It is clear that those local authorities that have abolished grammar schools completely were determined that their experiment should succeed because of their belief that it is just as wrong to separate children by intelligence as by social class. Such authorities tend to associate grammar schools with the private sector they would also like to abolish if they had the opportunity. In their view, any system that differentiates between children strengthens class barriers, and the fact that more upper-class children tend to go to university is not evidence that comprehensive schools are inferior; it is merely further evidence of the discrimination that already exists in society.

The defenders of grammar schools use examination results to show that children reach their maximum potential when placed with others of similar intelligence and point out that even in comprehensive schools they are put in different classes according to ability. It is difficult to believe, however, that this defence is inspired purely by a desire for academic excellence.

task1.model_answer: Following the Second World War, state education in Britain relied on the 11-plus examination, which divided eleven- and twelve-year-olds into grammar, direct-grant, or secondary modern schools. Since the 1960's, however, most local authorities have replaced this system with comprehensive schools attended by all pupils, although students are often grouped by ability inside them. Meanwhile, private "public" schools have remained outside the state system. The shift toward comprehensive schooling sparked an ongoing debate, particularly between Labour and Conservative local authorities. While supporters of comprehensive schools argue against reinforcing class divisions and separating children by intelligence, defenders of grammar schools claim students perform best alongside peers of similar ability. Ultimately, the passage suggests that this educational debate is driven mainly by political beliefs.

task2.model_answer:
Whether schools should group students by academic ability or teach everyone together in mixed-ability classes remains a central question in education policy. Both approaches offer distinct advantages and drawbacks.

Supporters of ability grouping argue that tailored instruction allows high-achieving students to move at a faster pace while giving struggling learners the targeted support they need. When students share similar skill levels, teachers can design lessons that match their pace without leaving anyone behind or holding others back.

On the other hand, critics warn that separating students early can damage motivation and widen social inequality. As noted in the British debate over grammar and comprehensive schools, academic selection often mirrors existing social advantages. Mixed-ability environments encourage peer learning, foster mutual respect, and avoid labeling young children as academic failures at an early age.

In my view, schools should keep students together in comprehensive settings during core years while offering flexible, subject-specific support rather than rigid selection. This balances academic growth with social fairness.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Britanya'da Eğitim.

Britanya'da eğitim, merkezi hükümet yönergeler belirleyip ödenek sağlasa veya kesebilse de, öncelikli olarak yerel eğitim idarelerinin sorumluluğundadır. İkinci Dünya Savaşı'nın sonundan 1960'lara kadar devlet kontrolündeki eğitim, on bir ila on iki yaş arasındaki tüm öğrencilerin girdiği "11-plus" sınavına dayanıyordu. En başarılı öğrenciler grammar school olarak bilinen akademik devlet liselerine ya da doğrudan ödenekli okullara (direct-grant schools) giderken, geri kalanlar genel ortaöğretim okullarına (secondary modern schools) gidiyordu. 1960'lardan bu yana neredeyse tüm yerel idareler, öğrencilerin okula girdikten sonra genellikle yeteneklerine göre ayrılmasına çalışılsa da, tüm öğrencilerin aynı okula devam ettiği kapsamlı okulları (comprehensive schools) uygulamaya koymuştur. Genellikle İşçi Partisi'nin kontrolünde olan yerel idareler artık neredeyse tamamen kapsamlı okul sistemine geçmiş durumdayken, Muhafazakârların iktidarda olduğu bölgeler bu değişime karşı daha dirençli olmuştur.

Bu dönem boyunca, adı dışında her şeyiyle özel olan "public school" adlı köklü özel okullar, devlet sisteminden bağımsız olarak varlığını sürdürmüştür. Bunlardan bazıları, 11-plus sınavını geçen ve öğrenim ücretleri yerel idareler tarafından ödenen öğrencileri kabul eden doğrudan ödenekli okullara dönüştü; ancak İşçi Partisi kontrolündeki bir yerel idare kapsamlı eğitime olan bağlılığı nedeniyle ödenekleri ödemeyi sürdürmeyi reddettiğinde, bu sistem pek çok durumda sona erdi.

İngiltere ve Galler'de kapsamlı okulların destekçileri ile grammar school okullarını korumak veya yeniden canlandırmak isteyenler arasındaki kamuoyu tartışması hız kesmeden devam etmektedir. Her yıl, kapsamlı okulların grammar school okullarından (ve bazı durumlarda prestijli özel sektör okullarından bile) daha iyi eğitim verdiğini gösteren istatistikler yayımlanmaktadır. Bu istatistikler, tam tersini kanıtlayan başka verilerle derhal çürütülmektedir. Yerel idareler genel olarak, kimisi büyük bir hevesle kimisi ise belirgin bir isteksizlikle de olsa kapsamlı okul sistemine geçmiştir. Ancak tartışmanın asıl karmaşıklığı, argümanların genellikle eğitim terimleriyle ifade edilmesine rağmen neredeyse tamamının siyasi görüşlere dayanmasından kaynaklanmaktadır.

Grammar school okullarını tamamen kaldıran yerel idarelerin, çocukları zekâya göre ayırmanın sosyal sınıfa göre ayırmak kadar yanlış olduğuna inandıkları için bu deneylerinin başarılı olmasını sağlamaya kararlı oldukları açıktır. passages.passage_text:
Organisms exhibit biological rhythms. Some are short and can be measured in minutes or hours. Others last days or months. The idea that our bodies are in constant flux is fairly new and goes against traditional medical training. In the past, many doctors were taught to believe the body has a relatively stable, or homeostatic, internal environment. Any fluctuations were considered random and not meaningful enough to be studied.

As early as the 1940's, however, some scientists questioned the homeostatic view of the body. Franz Halberg, a young European scientist working in the United States, conducted a series of experiments on mice and noticed that the number of white blood cells in these animals was dramatically higher and lower at different times of the day. Gradually, such research spread to the study of biological rhythms in human beings, and the findings were sometimes startling. For example, the time of day when a person receives X-ray or drug treatment for cancer can affect treatment benefits and ultimately mean the difference between life and death.

This new science, the study of biological rhythms in human beings, is called chronobiology, and the evidence supporting it has become increasingly persuasive. Along the way, the scientific and medical communities are beginning to rethink their ideas about how the human body works, and gradually what had been considered a minor science just a few years ago is being studied in major universities and medical centers around the world.

With their new findings, they are teaching us things that can literally change our lives - by helping us organize ourselves so we can work with our natural rhythms rather than against them. This can enhance our outlook on life as well as our performance at work.

Because they are easy to detect and measure, more is known of daily - or circadian (Latin for 'about a day') - rhythms than other types. The most obvious daily rhythm is the sleep / wake cycle. But there are other daily cycles as well: temperature, blood pressure, hormone levels. Amid these and the body's other changing rhythms, you are simply a different person at 9 a.m. than you are at 3 p.m. How you feel, how well you work, your level of alertness, your sensitivity to taste and smell, the degree with which you enjoy food or take pleasure in music - all are changing throughout the day. Most of us seem to reach our peak of alertness around noon. Soon after that, alertness declines, and sleepiness may set in by mid-afternoon.

Your short-term memory is best during the morning - in fact, about 15 per cent more efficient than at any other time of day. So, students, take heed: when faced with a morning exam, it really does pay to review your notes right before the test is given.

Long-term memory is different. Afternoon is the best time for learning material that you want to recall days, weeks or months later. Politicians, business executives or others who must learn speeches would be smart to do their memorizing during that time of day. If you are a student, it would be better for you to schedule your more difficult classes in the afternoon, rather than in the morning. You should also try to do most of your studying in the afternoon, rather than late at night. Many students believe they memorize better while burning the midnight oil because their short-term recall is better during the wee hours of the morning than in the afternoon. But short-term memory won't help them much several days later, when they face the exam.

task1.model_answer: Chronobiology, the study of biological rhythms in humans, challenges the older medical belief that the body maintains a static internal state. Beginning with 1940s experiments on mice by Franz Halberg, researchers discovered that physiological markers such as white blood cells, body temperature, blood pressure, and hormone levels follow predictable cycles. In medicine, this discovery is vital because even the timing of cancer treatment can influence survival. In daily life, understanding circadian rhythms helps people work more effectively. Alertness typically peaks around noon before dropping in the mid-afternoon. Furthermore, memory varies by time of day: short-term memory is strongest in the morning, making last-minute review useful before a morning test, whereas afternoon studying is superior for long-term retention.

task2.model_answer:
Many schools and workplaces still follow rigid morning schedules without considering how human energy and memory fluctuate across the day. Adjusting daily timetables to reflect circadian rhythms could improve both learning and productivity.

Research shows that alertness peaks around noon and declines in the afternoon, while short-term and long-term memory operate best at different hours. If schools scheduled demanding subjects requiring deep long-term understanding in the afternoon rather than early morning, students might retain complex material more effectively. Similarly, flexible office hours would allow employees to tackle analytical tasks when they are most alert.

However, completely redesigning societal schedules has practical obstacles. Coordinated hours are necessary for teamwork, public transportation, and family routines, and not every individual shares the exact same biological clock.

Overall, while society cannot abandon standard schedules entirely, offering greater flexibility and placing demanding classes or tasks in line with natural cognitive peaks is a practical step toward better performance and well-being.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Günün En Verimli Saatiniz Hangisi?

Canlılar biyolojik ritimler sergiler. Bunlardan bazıları kısadır ve dakikalar ya da saatlerle ölçülebilir. Diğerleri ise günler veya aylar sürer. Vücudumuzun sürekli bir değişim ve akış içinde olduğu fikri oldukça yenidir ve geleneksel tıp eğitimine ters düşer. Geçmişte birçok doktora, vücudun nispeten sabit, yani homeostatik bir iç ortama sahip olduğu öğretilirdi. Her türlü dalgalanma rastgele görülür ve incelenmeye değer bulunmazdı.

Ancak daha 1940'larda bazı bilim insanları vücuda ilişkin bu homeostatik görüşü sorguladı. Amerika Birleşik Devletleri'nde çalışan genç Avrupalı bilim insanı Franz Halberg, fareler üzerinde bir dizi deney yürüttü ve bu hayvanlardaki beyaz kan hücresi sayısının günün farklı saatlerinde çarpıcı biçimde yükselip alçaldığını fark etti. Zamanla bu tür araştırmalar insanlardaki biyolojik ritimlerin incelenmesine kadar yayıldı ve bulgular zaman zaman şaşırtıcı oldu. Örneğin, bir kişinin kanser için röntgen veya ilaç tedavisi aldığı günün saati, tedavinin yararlarını etkileyebilir ve nihayetinde yaşam ile ölüm arasındaki farkı belirleyebilir.

İnsanlardaki biyolojik ritimleri inceleyen bu yeni bilim dalına kronobiyoloji adı verilmektedir ve onu destekleyen kanıtlar giderek daha ikna edici hale gelmiştir. Bu süreçte bilim ve tıp camiaları insan vücudunun nasıl çalıştığına dair fikirlerini yeniden gözden geçirmeye başlamış ve daha birkaç yıl önce önemsiz bir bilim dalı olarak görülen bu alan, dünyanın dört bir yanındaki büyük üniversitelerde ve tıp merkezlerinde giderek daha fazla araştırılmaya başlanmıştır.

Yeni bulgularıyla bize hayatımızı kelimenin tam anlamıyla değiştirebilecek şeyler öğretiyorlar; bunu da doğal ritimlerimize karşı koymak yerine onlarla uyum içinde çalışabilmemiz için kendimizi düzenlememize yardımcı olarak yapıyorlar. Bu durum hem hayata bakış açımızı hem de iş yerindeki performansımızı iyileştirebilir.

Tespit edilmeleri ve ölçülmeleri kolay olduğu için, günlük – ya da Latincede "yaklaşık bir gün" anlamına gelen sirkadiyen – ritimler hakkında diğer türlere kıyasla daha fazla şey bilinmektedir. En belirgin günlük ritim uyku-uyanıklık döngüsüdür. Ancak başka günlük döngüler de vardır: vücut ısısı, kan basıncı, hormon düzeyleri. Tüm bu ve vücudun diğer değişen ritimlerinin ortasında, sabah saat 9'da öğleden sonra saat 3'tekinden bambaşka bir insansınızdır. Nasıl hissettiğiniz, ne kadar iyi çalıştığınız, uyanıklık düzeyiniz, tat ve kokuya karşı duyarlılığınız, yemekten aldığınız keyif veya müzikten duyduğunuz haz; bunların hepsi gün boyunca değişir. Çoğumuz uyanıklık zirvemize öğle saatleri civarında ulaşırız. Bundan kısa bir süre sonra uyanıklık azalır ve öğleden sonra ortasına doğru uyku hali başlayabilir.

Kısa süreli belleğiniz en iyi sabah saatlerinde çalışır; hatta günün diğer herhangi bir saatine göre yaklaşık yüzde 15 daha verimlidir. Bu yüzden öğrenciler, kulak verin: sabah bir sınavla karşı karşıya olduğunuzda, notlarınızı sınav verilmeden hemen önce gözden geçirmek gerçekten de işe yarar.

Uzun süreli bellek ise farklıdır. Günler, haftalar ya da aylar sonra hatırlamak istediğiniz bilgileri öğrenmek için en uygun zaman öğleden sonradır. Konuşma ezberlemesi gereken politikacılar, şirket yöneticileri veya diğer kişiler ezberlerini günün bu saatinde yaparlarsa akıllıca davranmış olurlar. Eğer bir öğrenciyseniz, daha zor derslerinizi sabah yerine öğleden sonraya programlamanız daha iyi olur. Ayrıca ders çalışmanızın büyük bölümünü gece geç saatler yerine öğleden sonra yapmaya çalışmalısınız. Birçok öğrenci gece geç saatlere kadar uyanık kalıp çalışırken daha iyi ezberlediğine inanır; çünkü sabaha karşı erken saatlerde kısa süreli hatırlamaları öğleden sonraya göre daha iyidir. Ancak sınava birkaç gün sonra girdiklerinde kısa süreli bellek onlara pek yardımcı olmayacaktır.

passages.passage_text:
Over the past several years, researchers have dug deep into Atlantic sea-floor sediments and Greenland glaciers to study the chemistry of ancient mud and ice, and they are increasingly convinced that climate change is anything but smooth. "The transition from warm to frigid can come in a decade or two - a geological snap of the fingers", says Gerard Bond, a geophysicist at Columbia University's Lamont-Doherty Observatory: "The data have been coming out of Greenland for maybe two or three decades. But the first results were really so surprising that people weren't ready to believe them."

There is a growing understanding as well that ice ages are not uniformly icy, nor interglacial periods, i.e., periods between ice ages, unchangingly warm. About 40,000 years ago, for example, right in the middle of the last ice age, the world warmed briefly, forcing glaciers to retreat. And while the current interglacial period has been stably temperate, the previous one, according to at least one study, was evidently interrupted by frigid spells lasting hundreds of years. If that period was more typical than the present one, humanity's invention of agriculture, and thus civilization, may have been possible only because of a highly unusual period of stable temperature - a fluke.

Just 150 years ago, the notion that much of the Northern Hemisphere had once been covered by thick sheets of ice was both new and highly controversial. Within a few decades, though, most scientists were convinced and began looking for explanations. Several suggested that astronomical cycles were involved, and by the 1930's the Yugoslav astronomer Milutin Milankovitch had constructed a coherent theory. The ice ages, he argued, were triggered by changes in the shape of the earth's slightly oval orbit around the sun and in the planet's axis of rotation. Studies of the chemical composition of ocean-floor sediments, which depend on climatic conditions when the material was laid down, more or less supported Milankovitch's predicted schedule of global glaciation.

According to Milankovitch's cycles, an ice age could start sometime within the next 1,000 or 2,000 years. But geophysicists have realized for years that while the cycles are real and influence climate, they alone cannot explain ice ages. For one thing, Milankovitch's timing of glaciation may be broadly correct, but major glacial episodes happen when his cycles call for minor ones, and vice versa.

Several suggested that astronomical cycles were involved, and by the 1930s the Yugoslav astronomer Milutin Milankovitch had constructed a coherent theory. The ice ages, he argued, were triggered by changes in the shape of the earth's slightly oval orbit around the sun and in the planet's axis of rotation. Studies of the chemical composition of ocean-floor sediments, which depend on climatic conditions when the material was laid down, more or less supported Milankovitch's predicted schedule of global glaciation.

According to Milankovitch's cycles, an ice age could start sometime within the next 1,000 or 2,000 years. But geophysicists have realized for years that while the cycles are real and influence climate, they alone cannot explain ice ages. For one thing, Milankovitch's timing of glaciation may be broadly correct, but major glacial episodes happen when his cycles call for minor ones, and vice versa.

Throughout history, human societies have relied heavily on relatively stable and predictable weather patterns. task2.model_answer:
Whenever an unusually severe winter hits, some commentators point to freezing temperatures as proof that global warming is exaggerated. However, confusing a single cold spell with long-term climate change overlooks an important scientific distinction between weather and climate.

Weather refers to short-term atmospheric conditions in a specific place, such as a week-long arctic freeze in the eastern United States. Climate, on the other hand, describes average temperature and precipitation patterns across the entire planet over decades or centuries. In fact, a warming planet can disrupt polar jet streams, occasionally pushing frigid arctic air farther south and producing harsher local winter storms even as global average temperatures continue to rise.

Therefore, isolated cold waves do not disprove long-term warming trends. Rather than dismissing scientific models because of one bitter winter, societies should prepare for all forms of extreme weather—both intense heat waves and unexpected freezes—by strengthening infrastructure and reducing greenhouse gas emissions.

passages.passage_text:
Does a drink a day keep heart attacks away? Over the past 20 years, numerous studies have found that moderate alcohol consumption - say, one or two beers, glasses of wine or cocktails daily - helps to prevent coronary heart disease. Last week a report in the New England Journal of Medicine added strong new evidence in support of that theory. More importantly, the work provided the first solid indication of how alcohol works to protect the heart.

In the study, researchers from Boston's Brigham and Women's Hospitals and Harvard Medical School compared the drinking habits of 340 men and women who had suffered recent heart attacks with those of healthy people of the same age and sex. The scientists found that people who sip one to three drinks a day are about half as likely to suffer heart attacks as nondrinkers are. The apparent source of the protection: those who drank alcohol had higher blood levels of high-density lipoproteins, or HDL's, the so-called good cholesterol, which is known to ward off heart disease.

As evidence has mounted, some doctors have begun recommending a daily drink for cardiac patients. But most physicians are not ready to recommend a ritual happy hour for everyone. The risks of teetotaling are nothing compared with the dangers of too much alcohol, including high blood pressure, strokes and cirrhosis of the liver - not to mention violent behaviour and traffic accidents. Moreover, some studies suggest that even moderate drinking may increase the incidence of breast and colon cancer. Until there is evidence that the benefits of a daily dose of alcohol outweigh the risks, most people won't be able to take a doctor's prescription to the neighbourhood bar or liquor store.

task2.model_answer:
Public health headlines often highlight studies showing that a particular food or drink, such as red wine or coffee, may protect against certain illnesses. While such findings are worth investigating, doctors are right to remain cautious before turning preliminary results into universal lifestyle advice.

First, human health is influenced by a complex mix of genetics, diet, and daily habits, making it risky to focus on a single substance. As the passage illustrates, even if moderate alcohol intake raises good cholesterol, it may simultaneously increase the risk of breast and colon cancer. Second, general recommendations can easily be misunderstood or taken to extremes. Advising the public to drink daily could unintentionally encourage heavy consumption among people vulnerable to addiction, leading to far greater harm than benefit.

In conclusion, medical advice should always weigh overall risks against potential rewards. For most individuals, proven habits such as regular exercise and a balanced diet remain far safer ways to protect long-term health.

Kalp Krizine Karşı Kanıt.

Günde bir kadeh içki kalp krizini uzak tutar mı? Son 20 yılda yapılan çok sayıda araştırma, örneğin günde bir veya iki bira, bir iki kadeh şarap ya da kokteyl gibi ölçülü alkol tüketiminin koroner kalp hastalığını önlemeye yardımcı olduğunu ortaya koydu. Geçen hafta New England Journal of Medicine dergisinde yayımlanan bir rapor, bu teoriyi destekleyen güçlü yeni kanıtlar sundu. Daha da önemlisi, çalışma alkolün kalbi korumak için nasıl etki ettiğine dair ilk somut göstergeyi sağladı.

Çalışmada, Boston'daki Brigham ve Kadın Hastaneleri ile Harvard Tıp Fakültesi'nden araştırmacılar, yakın zamanda kalp krizi geçirmiş 340 erkek ve kadının içki içme alışkanlıklarını aynı yaş ve cinsiyetteki sağlıklı kişilerin alışkanlıklarıyla karşılaştırdı. Bilim insanları, günde bir ila üç kadeh içki içen kişilerin kalp krizi geçirme olasılığının hiç içki içmeyenlere göre yaklaşık yarı yarıya daha düşük olduğunu buldu. Korumanın görünürdeki kaynağı ise şuydu: Alkol tüketenlerin kanlarında, kalp hastalığını önlediği bilinen ve sözde iyi kolesterol olarak adlandırılan yüksek yoğunluklu lipoproteinlerin, yani HDL'lerin düzeyi daha yüksekti.

Kanıtlar arttıkça bazı doktorlar kalp hastalarına günde bir kadeh içki önermeye başladı. Ancak çoğu hekim herkese düzenli bir içki saati tavsiye etmeye henüz hazır değil. Hiç alkol almamanın riskleri; yüksek tansiyon, felç ve karaciğer sirozunun yanı sıra şiddet davranışları ve trafik kazaları da dahil olmak üzere aşırı alkolün tehlikeleriyle kıyaslanamaz bile. Dahası, bazı araştırmalar ölçülü içki içmenin bile meme ve kolon kanseri görülme sıklığını artırabileceğini öne sürüyor. Günlük belirli bir doz alkolün faydalarının risklerinden ağır bastığına dair kanıtlar bulunana kadar, çoğu insan mahalledeki bara ya da içki dükkanına elinde doktor reçetesiyle gidemeyecek.

passages.passage_text:
Contrary to the impression that grandmothers are delighted to help their grown daughters and care for their grandchildren, a study of multi-generational families indicates that many older women resent the frequent impositions of the younger generations on their time and energy.

"Young women with children are under a lot of pressure these days, and they expect their mothers to help them pick up the pieces," noted Dr. Bertram J. Cohler, a behavioral scientist at the University of Chicago. "This is often the strongest source of resentment on the part of Grandmother, who has finished with child-caring and now has her own life to live. Grandmothers like to see their children and grandchildren, but in their own time."

Dr. Cohler is the director of a study, supported by the National Institute of Aging, of 150 working-class families that live in a Midwestern suburb. He and a collaborator, Dr. Henry U. Grunebaum of Harvard Medical School, have already completed an intensive investigation of four such families in New England, summarizing their findings in a book, Mothers, Grandmothers and Daughters, published recently by Wiley-Interscience for professional audiences.

Dr. Cohler tells of a middle-aged Boston woman who works as a seamstress all week and for her church on Sundays. Every Saturday (her only day off) her daughter and family visit, expecting Mother to make lunch, shop and visit. "That's not how she wants to grow old," said Dr. Cohler, who was told by the older woman: "My daughter would never speak to me if she knew how mad I get."

In all the four New England families studied, the older women resented the numerous phone calls and visits from their grown daughters, who often turned to their mothers for advice, physical resources, affection and companionship as well as baby-sitting services. "American society keeps piling on the burdens for older people, particularly those in their 50's and 60's," Dr. Cohler said in an interview here. "They are still working and taking care of their grown children and maybe also their aged parents. Sometimes life gets to be too much. That's one reason many of them move far away, to Florida or Sun City (Arizona). Older people need more space and time to attend to their own affairs and friends. Young people don't understand this, and that's part of what creates tension between generations."

He has found that, contrary to what the younger generations may think, older people have an enormous amount to do. "More than half of working-class grandmothers still work, and if they're retired they have activities in the community that keep them occupied," he said.

"Each generation has got to appreciate the unique needs of the other," Dr. Cohler went on. "The younger generation has to realize that grandparents have busy, active lives and that they need privacy and more space for themselves. Moreover, the older generation has to realize that continuing to be part of the family is important to the younger generation and that they need help and support."

task1.model_answer: Research led by Dr. Bertram J. Cohler challenges the common belief that grandmothers always welcome caring for their grandchildren. According to studies of working-class families, many older women feel burdened by frequent visits, phone calls, and childcare requests from their grown daughters. Because many people in their fifties and sixties are still employed, active in their communities, or even caring for elderly parents, constant family demands leave them little personal time. Consequently, some older adults relocate to retirement areas to regain independence. Dr. Cohler concludes that reducing generational tension requires mutual understanding: younger adults must respect grandparents' busy schedules and privacy, while older parents should recognize their children's need for family connection and support.
task1.prompt: Summarize Dr. Bertram J. Cohler's findings about the causes of tension between grandmothers and their grown daughters, and explain what he believes both generations need to understand.
task1.title: Summary: Understanding Generational Tension

task2.model_answer:
In many societies, grandparents are automatically expected to provide regular childcare and emotional support whenever their adult children face busy schedules. While family solidarity is valuable, assuming that older relatives are always available is neither fair nor realistic.

First, modern older adults often lead demanding lives of their own. Many people in their fifties and sixties are still working full-time, managing health concerns, or participating in community activities. After spending decades raising their own children, they deserve the freedom to pursue personal interests and rest. When adult children arrive unannounced or treat their parents' home as a free daycare center, resentment naturally builds.

On the other hand, young parents today face intense economic and professional pressures, often with both partners working. Having supportive grandparents nearby can make a tremendous difference for a young family's stability and give children meaningful bonds with older relatives.

Ultimately, the healthiest solution lies in open communication and clear boundaries. Adult children should ask rather than assume, and grandparents should feel comfortable expressing their limits honestly. Mutual respect allows both generations to enjoy each other's company without feeling exploited.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Kuşak Uçurumunun Diğer Tarafından.

Büyükannelerin yetişkin kızlarına yardım etmekten ve torunlarına bakmaktan büyük mutluluk duyduğu izleniminin aksine, çok kuşaklı aileler üzerine yapılan bir araştırma, birçok yaşlı kadının genç kuşakların zamanlarına ve enerjilerine sık sık el koymasından rahatsızlık duyduğunu gösteriyor.

Chicago Üniversitesi'nden davranış bilimci Dr. Bertram J. Cohler, "Çocuklu genç kadınlar bugünlerde büyük bir baskı altında ve annelerinin dağılan düzeni toplamalarına yardım etmesini bekliyorlar," diye belirtti. "Çocuk büyütme işini bitirmiş olan ve artık yaşayacak kendi hayatı bulunan büyükanne açısından bu durum genellikle en güçlü kırgınlık kaynağıdır. Büyükanneler çocuklarını ve torunlarını görmeyi severler, ancak bunu kendi belirledikleri zamanda yapmak isterler."

Dr. Cohler, Ulusal Yaşlanma Enstitüsü tarafından desteklenen ve Ortabatı'daki bir banliyöde yaşayan 150 işçi sınıfı ailesini kapsayan bir araştırmanın yöneticisidir. Kendisi ve Harvard Tıp Fakültesi'nden çalışma arkadaşı Dr. Henry U. Grunebaum, New England'daki bu tür dört aile üzerinde şimdiden kapsamlı bir inceleme tamamlamış ve bulgularını yakın zamanda Wiley-Interscience tarafından mesleki okurlar için yayımlanan Anneler, Büyükanneler ve Kızlar (Mothers, Grandmothers and Daughters) adlı kitapta özetlemişlerdir.

Dr. Cohler, hafta boyunca terzi olarak, pazar günleri ise kilisesi için çalışan orta yaşlı Bostonlu bir kadından söz ediyor. Tek boş günü olan her cumartesi günü, kızı ve ailesi ziyarete geliyor; annelerinden öğle yemeği yapmasını, alışverişe çıkmasını ve onlarla vakit geçirmesini bekliyorlar. Dr. Cohler, "Bu şekilde yaşlanmak istemiyor," dedi; yaşlı kadın da kendisine şunu söylemiş: "Ne kadar öfkelendiğimi bilseydi, kızım benimle bir daha asla konuşmazdı."

İncelenen dört New England ailesinin tamamında, yaşlı kadınlar; tavsiye, maddi kaynak, şefkat ve arkadaşlığın yanı sıra çocuk bakımı hizmetleri için de sık sık annelerine başvuran yetişkin kızlarının sayısız telefon aramalarından ve ziyaretlerinden içerliyordu. Dr. Cohler burada verdiği bir röportajda, "Amerikan toplumu yaşlıların, özellikle de ellili ve altmışlı yaşlarındakilerin üzerindeki yükleri artırmaya devam ediyor," dedi. "Hâlâ çalışıyorlar, yetişkin çocuklarıyla ve belki de yaşlı ebeveynleriyle ilgileniyorlar. Bazen hayat çekilmez bir hale geliyor. Birçoğunun çok uzaklara, Florida'ya ya da Arizona'daki Sun City'ye taşınmasının nedenlerinden biri de budur. Yaşlı insanların kendi işlerine ve arkadaşlarına vakit ayırmak için daha fazla alana ve zamana ihtiyacı var. Gençler bunu anlamıyor ve kuşaklar arasında gerilim yaratan şeyin bir kısmı da bu."

Cohler, genç kuşakların düşündüğünün aksine, yaşlı insanların yapacak çok fazla işi olduğunu tespit etti. "İşçi sınıfından büyükannelerin yarısından fazlası hâlâ çalışıyor; emekli olanların ise toplum içinde kendilerini meşgul eden faaliyetleri var," dedi.

Dr. Cohler sözlerini şöyle sürdürdü: "Her kuşağın diğerinin kendine özgü ihtiyaçlarını takdir etmesi gerekiyor. Genç kuşak, büyükanne ve büyükbabaların yoğun ve aktif bir hayatları olduğunu, mahremiyete ve kendileri için daha fazla alana ihtiyaç duyduklarını fark etmeli. Öte yandan yaşlı kuşak da ailenin bir parçası olmaya devam etmenin genç kuşak için önemli olduğunu ve onların yardıma ve desteğe ihtiyaç duyduğunu anlamalıdır."

passages.passage_text:
Learning a language at home via a home study course is often the most convenient, though not necessarily the most efficient. You can go at your own pace and needn't adjust your schedule to accommodate a regular class. Sets of recorded lessons are available at book and record stores or by mail order. They usually cover only the more common languages, and most do not go beyond the needs of the casual tourist. The tapes and records consist of groups of phrases and conversations you learn by repetition. A set of four to six tapes and accompanying workbook might cost about $125.

Taped lessons used by the Foreign Service Institute's School of Language Studies to train diplomats are more complete and cover a wider range of languages. The State Department does not market these tapes directly, but they are available by writing to Order Section, National Audio-Visual Center, General Services Administration, Washington, D.C. 20409. The price for a basic course of about 20 cassette tapes and a text is $100 or so; the more cassettes, the higher the price. Delivery generally takes four to six weeks after receipt of your order.

If you want to earn credits toward a degree or prepare yourself to read foreign literature, consider a university correspondence course. A one-semester course generally costs about $135 for beginners, postage not included. Any audio materials used may involve extra cost. Course quality is comparable to on-campus offerings. All assignments are reviewed by a professor or instructor and then returned, usually within a week.

Language courses are included among the 12,000 courses listed in The Guide to Independent Study Through Correspondence Instruction, prepared by the National University Continuing Education Association. It is available in libraries or from Peterson's Guides, P.O. Box 2123, Princeton, N.J. 08540, for $4.50 plus $1.25 for postage and handling.

One caveat about university correspondence courses: if your object is to achieve minimal conversational skills, either for business or pleasure, you may not be willing to expend the effort required for these courses, according to Dr. Robert Batchellor, associated with the NUCEA guide. Self-instruction requires a commitment of at least ten hours per week.

passages.title: Learning It at Home
passages.tts_script:
Learning It at Home.

Learning a language at home via a home study course is often the most convenient, though not necessarily the most efficient. You can go at your own pace and needn't adjust your schedule to accommodate a regular class. Sets of recorded lessons are available at book and record stores or by mail order. They usually cover only the more common languages, and most do not go beyond the needs of the casual tourist. The tapes and records consist of groups of phrases and conversations you learn by repetition. A set of four to six tapes and accompanying workbook might cost about $125.

Taped lessons used by the Foreign Service Institute's School of Language Studies to train diplomats are more complete and cover a wider range of languages. The State Department does not market these tapes directly, but they are available by writing to Order Section, National Audio-Visual Center, General Services Administration, Washington, D.C., 20409. The price for a basic course of about 20 cassette tapes and a text is $100 or so; the more cassettes, the higher the price. Delivery generally takes four to six weeks after receipt of your order.

If you want to earn credits toward a degree or prepare yourself to read foreign literature, consider a university correspondence course. A one-semester course generally costs about $135 for beginners, postage not included. Any audio materials used may involve extra cost. Course quality is comparable to on-campus offerings. All assignments are reviewed by a professor or instructor and then returned, usually within a week.

Language courses are included among the 12,000 courses listed in The Guide to Independent Study Through Correspondence Instruction, prepared by the National University Continuing Education Association. It is available in libraries or from Peterson's Guides, P.O. Box 2123, Princeton, New Jersey, 08540, for $4.50 plus $1.25 for postage and handling.

One caveat about university correspondence courses: if your object is to achieve minimal conversational skills, either for business or pleasure, you may not be willing to expend the effort required for these courses, according to Dr. Robert Batchellor, associated with the NUCEA guide. Self-instruction requires a commitment of at least ten hours per week.

The National Association of Self-Instructional Language Programs, or NASILP, assists schools in designing and operating self-instruction programs based on tape learning supplemented by text and tutorials and eligible for college credit. NASILP keeps up with all of the options, including commercial programs, and will help you find a course to fit your specifications, whether or not it is a NASILP product.

task1.model_answer: The passage outlines several options for learning a language at home, each suited to different goals. Commercial tape-and-workbook sets cost around $125, rely on repetition, and mainly serve casual tourists. By contrast, Foreign Service Institute courses cost roughly $100 for 20 tapes and cover more languages in greater depth, though delivery takes several weeks. Learners seeking academic credit or literature preparation can choose university correspondence courses for about $135 per semester, which match on-campus quality and provide weekly instructor feedback, yet demand at least ten hours of weekly commitment. Finally, NASILP helps schools run credit-bearing self-instruction programs and guides learners to courses matching their specific needs.

task2.model_answer:
Self-study language courses have become increasingly attractive for busy adults, yet they offer both clear advantages and notable limitations compared with traditional classrooms.

The greatest benefit of home study is flexibility. Learners can progress at their own speed without rearranging work or family schedules. For travelers who only need basic phrases, affordable audio sets provide a convenient way to practice through repetition. Furthermore, structured correspondence courses can deliver university-level quality and written feedback from instructors.

However, studying alone requires extraordinary self-discipline. Without regular classroom interaction, students miss spontaneous speaking practice and immediate correction from teachers and peers. As the passage warns, rigorous self-instruction programs often demand ten or more hours of weekly dedication, which many casual learners struggle to maintain once initial enthusiasm fades.

In conclusion, home-study courses work well for motivated, independent learners or travelers with modest goals, whereas students seeking rapid fluency and real-time conversation generally benefit more from guided classroom instruction.

Evde Öğrenmek.

Evde çalışma kursu aracılığıyla evde bir dil öğrenmek, mutlaka en verimli yol olmasa da genellikle en uygun yoldur. Kendi hızınızda ilerleyebilirsiniz ve programınızı düzenli bir derse uyacak şekilde ayarlamanız gerekmez. Kaydedilmiş ders setleri kitapçılarda ve plak dükkanlarında ya da posta siparişiyle temin edilebilir. Bunlar genellikle yalnızca daha yaygın dilleri kapsar ve çoğu, sıradan bir turistin ihtiyaçlarının ötesine geçmez. Kasetler ve plaklar, tekrar yoluyla öğrendiğiniz ifade gruplarından ve konuşmalardan oluşur. Dört ila altı kaset ve beraberindeki bir çalışma kitabından oluşan bir setin fiyatı yaklaşık 125 dolar olabilir.

Dışişleri Bakanlığı Hizmet Enstitüsü Dil Çalışmaları Okulu'nun diplomatları eğitmek için kullandığı kasetli dersler daha eksiksizdir ve daha geniş bir dil yelpazesini kapsar. Dışişleri Bakanlığı bu kasetleri doğrudan pazarlamaz, ancak Order Section, National Audio-Visual Center, General Services Administration, Washington, D.C., 20409 adresine yazılarak temin edilebilirler. Yaklaşık 20 kaset ve bir ders kitabından oluşan temel bir kursun fiyatı 100 dolar civarındadır; kaset sayısı arttıkça fiyat da yükselir. Teslimat genellikle siparişinizin alınmasından sonra dört ila altı hafta sürer.

Bir diploma için kredi kazanmak ya da yabancı edebiyat okumaya hazırlanmak istiyorsanız, mektupla öğretim veren bir üniversite kursunu düşünebilirsiniz. Bir dönemlik kurs, posta ücreti hariç yeni başlayanlar için genellikle yaklaşık 135 dolara mal olur. Kullanılan sesli materyaller ek ücrete tabi olabilir. Kurs kalitesi kampüsteki derslerle kıyaslanabilir düzeydedir. Tüm ödevler bir profesör veya eğitmen tarafından incelenir ve genellikle bir hafta içinde geri gönderilir.

Dil kursları, Ulusal Üniversite Sürekli Eğitim Derneği tarafından hazırlanan Mektupla Öğretim Yoluyla Bağımsız Çalışma Rehberi'nde (The Guide to Independent Study Through Correspondence Instruction) listelenen 12.000 kurs arasında yer almaktadır. Bu rehber kütüphanelerde mevcuttur veya 4,50 dolar artı 1,25 dolar posta ve işlem ücreti karşılığında Peterson's Guides, P.O. Box 2123, Princeton, New Jersey, 08540 adresinden temin edilebilir.

Üniversitelerin mektupla öğretim kursları hakkında bir uyarı: NUCEA rehberiyle bağlantılı Dr. Robert Batchellor'a göre, amacınız ister iş ister keyif için olsun asgari düzeyde konuşma becerisi kazanmaksa, bu kurslar için gereken çabayı harcamaya istekli olmayabilirsiniz. Kendi kendine eğitim, haftada en az on saatlik bir bağlılık gerektirir.

Ulusal Kendi Kendine Öğrenilen Dil Programları Derneği veya kısaca NASILP, okullara metin ve özel derslerle desteklenen, kasetle öğrenmeye dayalı ve üniversite kredisi almaya uygun kendi kendine öğrenme programları tasarlamada ve yürütmede yardımcı olur. NASILP, ticari programlar da dahil olmak üzere tüm seçenekleri yakından takip eder ve ister bir NASILP ürünü olsun ister olmasın, ihtiyaçlarınıza uygun bir kurs bulmanıza yardımcı olacaktır.

passages.passage_text:
No doubt the greatest single leap in human prehistory was the one we made from being helpless prey to becoming formidable predators (animals which hunt and eat others) of other living creatures, including, eventually, the ones with claws and fangs. This is the theme that is acted out over and over, obsessively, in the initiation rites of tribal cultures. In the drama of initiation, the young (usually men) are first humiliated and sometimes tortured, only to be 'reborn' as hunters and warriors. Very often the initial torment includes the threat of being eaten by costumed humans or actual beasts. Orokaiva children in Papua New Guinea are told they will be devoured like pigs; among Indians of the Pacific Northwest, the initiates were kidnapped or menaced by wolves; young Norwegian men, at least in the sagas, had to tackle bears single-handedly.

As a species, we've been fabulously successful at predation. We have enslaved the wild ungulates, turning them into our cattle and sheep, pushing them into ever narrower habitats. We have tamed some of the wolves and big cats, trivializing them as household pets. We can dine on shark or alligator fillets if we want, and the only bears we're likely to know are the ones whose name is teddy. In fact, horror movies wouldn't be much fun if real monsters lurked outside our cinemas. We can enjoy screaming at the alien or the monster or the blob because we know, historically speaking, it was our side that won.

But the defeat of the animal predators was not a clear-cut victory for us. With the big land carnivores out of the way, humans decided that the only worthwhile enemies were others like themselves - 'enemy' individuals or tribes or nations or ethnic groups. The criminal stalking his victim, the soldiers roaring into battle, are enacting an archaic drama in which the other player was originally non-human, something either to eat or be eaten by. For millenniums now, the earth's scariest predator has been ourselves.

In our arrogance, we have tended to forget that our own most formidable enemies may still be of the non-human kind. Instead of hungry tigers or fresh-cloned dinosaurs, we face equally deadly microscopic life forms. It will take a whole new set of skills and attitudes to defeat HIV or the TB bacterium - not the raging charge on the field of battle, but the cunning ambush of the lab.

passages.title: Animal Predators
passages.tts_script:
Animal Predators.

No doubt the greatest single leap in human prehistory was the one we made from being helpless prey to becoming formidable predators, animals which hunt and eat others, of other living creatures, including, eventually, the ones with claws and fangs. This is the theme that is acted out over and over, obsessively, in the initiation rites of tribal cultures. In the drama of initiation, the young, usually men, are first humiliated and sometimes tortured, only to be 'reborn' as hunters and warriors. Very often the initial torment includes the threat of being eaten by costumed humans or actual beasts. Orokaiva children in Papua New Guinea are told they will be devoured like pigs; among Indians of the Pacific Northwest, the initiates were kidnapped or menaced by wolves; young Norwegian men, at least in the sagas, had to tackle bears single-handedly.

As a species, we've been fabulously successful at predation. We have enslaved the wild ungulates, turning them into our cattle and sheep, pushing them into ever narrower habitats. We have tamed some of the wolves and big cats, trivializing them as household pets. We can dine on shark or alligator fillets if we want, and the only bears we're likely to know are the ones whose name is teddy. In fact, horror movies wouldn't be much fun if real monsters lurked outside our cinemas. We can enjoy screaming at the alien or the monster or the blob because we know, historically speaking, it was our side that won.

But the defeat of the animal predators was not a clear-cut victory for us. With the big land carnivores out of the way, humans decided that the only worthwhile enemies were others like themselves, 'enemy' individuals or tribes or nations or ethnic groups. The criminal stalking his victim, the soldiers roaring into battle, are enacting an archaic drama in which the other player was originally non-human, something either to eat or be eaten by. For millenniums now, the earth's scariest predator has been ourselves.

In our arrogance, we have tended to forget that our own most formidable enemies may still be of the non-human kind. Instead of hungry tigers or fresh-cloned dinosaurs, we face equally deadly microscopic life forms. It will take a whole new set of skills and attitudes to defeat HIV or the TB bacterium, not the raging charge on the field of battle, but the cunning ambush of the lab.

task1.model_answer: In "Animal Predators," the author traces humanity's transformation from vulnerable prey into Earth's dominant predator. Early tribal initiation rites symbolized this triumph by putting young people through beast-related trials before they became warriors. Over time, humans domesticated farm animals, turned fierce carnivores into pets, and eliminated wild predators as serious rivals. However, this victory proved bittersweet because humans soon redirected their predatory instincts toward other individuals, tribes, and nations. Ultimately, the author warns that humanity's arrogance overlooks a continuing non-human danger: microscopic pathogens like HIV and tuberculosis. Overcoming these invisible threats requires scientific skill and laboratory research rather than traditional warfare.

task2.model_answer:
Throughout history, humanity's greatest challenge was surviving physical threats from wild predators. Today, however, our survival depends far more on overcoming invisible biological dangers and human-made conflicts. While I partly agree that modern medicine has reduced the fear of many illnesses, infectious pathogens remain one of the gravest threats to global society.

First, microscopic organisms evolve rapidly and spread easily in an interconnected world. Unlike large predators, viruses and bacteria cannot be fenced out or defeated with physical weapons; as the passage notes, they demand sustained investment in laboratory research, vaccines, and public health systems. Second, modern technology has made human conflict equally dangerous. When nations treat one another as enemies, advanced weapons can cause devastation on a scale no wild animal could ever match.

In conclusion, humanity has conquered the wilderness only to confront more complex threats. Investing in scientific cooperation and peaceful diplomacy, rather than military aggression, is essential for our long-term survival.
