passages.title: Ghosts
passages.tts_script:
Ghosts.

Herr Adam is a lawyer working in Rosenheim, a small town in Bavaria, West Germany. In the summer of 1967, the telephones in his office seemed to go wrong. He called in Siemens, who had installed the phones, but they couldn't find a fault. He then called in the Post Office. They replaced the Siemens phones with official Post Office ones and put meters that showed calls being made in the office. On 10th October, for example, forty-six calls were made in fifteen minutes from 7:42 to 7:57 a.m.! The phones were replaced by ones which had locks. There was still no improvement: between five and six hundred calls were made in one week. When he saw the bills, Mr. Adam thought that someone at the Post Office was pocketing his money! A serious row developed between him and the Post Office Accounts Department.

Then, on 20th October 1967, all the office fluorescent lights came out of their sockets and fused. They were mended by a local electrician, but exactly the same thing happened again. The German Electricity Board took over the case. Paul Brunner, Auxiliary Works Manager, arrived on 15th November 1967. The next day, instruments were installed to measure the electricity coming into the office. At the same time as light bulbs exploded and the photocopier went wrong, abnormal amounts of electricity were recorded. These were so extreme that the instruments broke down. Readings from the central supply and then from the generator nearby were normal, however. The electricity was coming from somewhere else, but where? In the same month, a girl was cut by flying glass, lights began to swing and pictures on the walls changed places. Paul Brunner realised that this was beyond him and handed the matter over to two of Germany's leading physicists, Dr. Karga and Dr. Zicha. They were fascinated and did their own research. They could find no answer except that there was some external force that activated the electrics in the office and the telephones. They, in turn, handed the case over to parapsychologist Professor Bender and the police.

Professor Bender and the police centred their attention on the people working in the office and noticed that one office clerk in particular, Anne-Marie Schneider, showed signs of stress at the time of the happenings although she wasn't aware of it. Professor Bender noticed that the strange happenings began at 7:30 a.m., the time that this girl began work, and stopped completely when she took a week's holiday. On her return, things went from bad to worse. Desk drawers kept flying open and, on one occasion, a cash-box opened and the money inside fell onto the floor. The office was in chaos and everyone, including Anne-Marie, was terrified. Mr. Adam decided to ask her to leave.

From the day she left, the office returned to normal and there has been no other explanation other than ghosts for all these strange happenings.

task2.model_answer:
When unusual events occur without an immediate scientific explanation, people often turn to supernatural theories such as ghosts. However, jumping to paranormal conclusions too quickly can prevent us from discovering real, hidden causes.

First, human perception and stress can easily distort how we interpret strange coincidences. In high-pressure environments, people may overlook simple physical factors or unconscious human actions that trigger equipment problems. Even when instruments fail or behave unexpectedly, the limitation of current testing tools does not automatically prove a supernatural force is at work.

On the other hand, completely dismissing witness reports is also unhelpful. Scientists and investigators should carefully record all evidence, examine environmental factors, and even consider psychological stress before drawing conclusions.

In short, unexplained events deserve serious, open-minded investigation rather than instant belief in ghosts. Careful observation and patience are far more reliable than fear or superstition.

Telefonları kuran Siemens firmasını çağırdı ancak herhangi bir arıza bulamadılar. Bunun üzerine Posta İdaresi'ni çağırdı. Siemens telefonları resmî Posta İdaresi telefonlarıyla değiştirdiler ve ofisten yapılan aramaları gösteren sayaçlar taktılar. Örneğin 10 Ekim'de sabah 7:42 ile 7:57 arasındaki on beş dakika içinde kırk altı arama yapılmıştı! Telefonlar kilitli telefonlarla değiştirildi. Yine de hiçbir düzelme olmadı: bir haftada beş ila altı yüz arasında arama yapılıyordu. Faturaları gördüğünde Bay Adam, Posta İdaresi'nden birinin parasını cebine attığını düşündü! Kendisiyle Posta İdaresi Muhasebe Departmanı arasında ciddi bir tartışma çıktı.

Ardından, 20 Ekim 1967'de ofisteki tüm floresan lambalar yuvalarından çıkıp sigortaları attırdı. Yerel bir elektrikçi tarafından tamir edildiler ama tamamen aynı şey tekrar yaşandı. Olayı Alman Elektrik Kurumu devraldı. Yardımcı İşletme Müdürü Paul Brunner 15 Kasım 1967'de geldi. Ertesi gün ofise giren elektriği ölçmek için cihazlar kuruldu. Ampullerin patladığı ve fotokopi makinesinin bozulduğu sırada olağandışı miktarda elektrik kaydedildi. Bunlar o kadar aşırıydı ki cihazlar bozuldu. Ancak merkezî şebekeden ve ardından yakındaki jeneratörden alınan ölçümler normaldi. Elektrik başka bir yerden geliyordu ama nereden? Aynı ay içinde bir kız uçan cam parçasıyla yaralandı, lambalar sallanmaya başladı ve duvarlardaki tablolar yer değiştirdi. Paul Brunner bunun kendisini aştığını fark etti ve meseleyi Almanya'nın önde gelen iki fizikçisi Dr. Karga ve Dr. Zicha'ya devretti. Fizikçiler hayrete düştüler ve kendi araştırmalarını yaptılar. Ofisteki elektrik tesisatını ve telefonları harekete geçiren bir tür dış güç olduğu dışında bir yanıt bulamadılar. Onlar da vakayı parapsikolog Profesör Bender'e ve polise devrettiler.

Profesör Bender ve polis dikkatlerini ofiste çalışan kişiler üzerinde yoğunlaştırdı ve özellikle bir ofis memuru olan Anne-Marie Schneider'in, kendisi farkında olmasa da olayların yaşandığı sırada stres belirtileri gösterdiğini fark etti. Profesör Bender tuhaf olayların bu kızın işe başladığı saat olan sabah 7:30'da başladığını ve bir haftalık tatile çıktığında tamamen durduğunu fark etti. Dönüşünde işler daha da kötüye gitti. Masa çekmeceleri sürekli kendiliğinden açılıyor ve bir keresinde bir para kasası açılıp içindeki paralar yere saçılmıştı. Ofis tam bir kaos içindeydi ve Anne-Marie de dâhil olmak üzere herkes dehşete kapılmıştı. Bay Adam ondan işten ayrılmasını istemeye karar verdi.

İşten ayrıldığı günden itibaren ofis normale döndü ve tüm bu tuhaf olaylar için hayaletler dışında başka hiçbir açıklama bulunamadı.

passages.passage_text:
Every year, a magazine called Executive Travel organises a competition to find the Airline of the Year. Travellers from all over the world are invited to vote for the most efficient, the most punctual, the safest and the friendliest airline. The winner in 1985 was British Airways. The competition asked travellers what they expected most from an airline, and the results were as follows:

Punctual departures and arrivals 35%
Attentive cabin staff 35%
Comfort 18%
Safety 9%
Good food and wine 3%

The competition also invited travellers to tell their most horrific stories of international travel. Replies included six hijacks, fifty-three cases of engine failure or troubles with landing, eleven lightning strikes, twenty-three bomb scares, thirteen cases of food poisoning, eleven near misses and two accidents with airport trucks.

Bad flying experiences begin on the ground, naturally. One American airline managed to double-book an entire 747, but this is nothing compared to what happened on an internal flight on a certain African airline. The flight had been overbooked three times. The local military solved the problem by insisting that all passengers should run round the plane twice, the fastest getting the seats. An overbooked flight that was going from Heathrow to America gave one traveller a bit of a shock. Dressed only in trousers, shirt and socks, he had been allowed by the stewardess to leave the aircraft to speak to a friend. He returned a few minutes later to find the 747 closed up and about to start moving - with his shoes, wallet, passport and luggage inside. Banging frantically on the door got him back inside. A similar event was experienced by a businessman on a flight from Bangladesh. Passengers were waiting for take-off when there was a sudden hysterical banging on the door. At first, the cabin crew paid no attention. The banging continued. When the door was finally opened, the pilot got in.

One frequent flier lost a certain amount of confidence when the cabin staff asked him to sit in the lavatory during take-off so that they could occupy the seats nearest the emergency exit on a flight between London and Manchester. For nervous fliers, a shocking journey was one between Gatwick and Montpellier, during which they had to watch pieces of the engine falling off.

task2.model_answer:
Interestingly, the survey in the passage shows that airline passengers ranked punctuality and attentive staff far higher than safety. While good service and on-time arrivals make air travel convenient, I believe safety should always remain an airline's top priority.

One reason passengers take safety for granted is that modern aviation is generally very reliable. Because serious accidents are rare, travellers focus more on immediate frustrations such as delayed flights, uncomfortable seats, or unhelpful staff. When everything runs smoothly, passengers rarely think about aircraft maintenance or emergency procedures.

However, the terrifying stories shared by travellers prove that cutting corners on safety can quickly destroy passenger trust. Asking a customer to sit in a lavatory during take-off or flying a plane with loose engine parts puts lives at risk. No amount of free wine or punctual scheduling can compensate for unsafe conditions.

Therefore, while airlines should strive to be punctual and polite, strict safety standards must always come first.

Yolcuların Hikâyeleri.

Her yıl Executive Travel adlı bir dergi, Yılın Havayolu Şirketi'ni belirlemek için bir yarışma düzenler. Dünyanın dört bir yanından yolcular en verimli, en dakik, en güvenli ve en güler yüzlü havayolu şirketine oy vermeye davet edilir. 1985 yılının kazananı British Airways oldu. Yarışmada yolculara bir havayolundan en çok ne bekledikleri soruldu ve sonuçlar şöyle çıktı: dakik kalkış ve inişler, yüzde 35; ilgili kabin ekibi, yüzde 35; konfor, yüzde 18; güvenlik, yüzde 9; iyi yemek ve şarap, yüzde 3.

Yarışma ayrıca yolcuları uluslararası seyahatlerindeki en korkunç hikâyelerini anlatmaya da davet etti. Gelen yanıtlar arasında altı uçak kaçırma olayı, elli üç motor arızası veya iniş sorunu, on bir yıldırım çarpması, yirmi üç bomba ihbarı, on üç gıda zehirlenmesi vakası, on bir çarpışmadan kıl payı kurtulma ve havaalanı kamyonlarıyla yaşanan iki kaza yer aldı.

Kötü uçuş deneyimleri doğal olarak daha yerde başlar. Bir Amerikan havayolu şirketi koskoca bir 747'ye çift rezervasyon yapmayı başarmıştı, ancak bu belirli bir Afrika havayolunun iç hat uçuşunda yaşananların yanında hiçbir şey sayılır. Uçuşa kapasitenin üç katı bilet satılmıştı. Yerel ordu, tüm yolcuların uçağın etrafında iki kez koşmasında ısrar ederek sorunu çözdü; en hızlı koşanlar koltukları kaptı. Heathrow'dan Amerika'ya gidecek, kapasitesinin üzerinde bilet satılmış bir uçuş da bir yolcuya epey bir şok yaşattı. Üzerinde yalnızca pantolon, gömlek ve çoraplarla, bir arkadaşıyla konuşmak üzere hostesin izniyle uçaktan inmişti. Birkaç dakika sonra geri döndüğünde 747'nin kapılarının kapandığını ve hareket etmek üzere olduğunu gördü; ayakkabıları, cüzdanı, pasaportu ve bagajı ise içerideydi. Kapıya çılgınca vurması sayesinde tekrar içeri alınabildi. Benzer bir olay, Bangladeş'ten kalkan bir uçaktaki bir iş insanının da başına geldi. Yolcular kalkışı beklerken kapıya aniden histerik bir şekilde vurulmaya başlandı. Kabin ekibi ilk başta aldırmadı. Kapı vurulmaya devam etti. Sonunda kapı açıldığında içeri pilot girdi.

Sık uçan bir yolcu ise Londra ile Manchester arasındaki bir uçuşta, kabin ekibinin acil çıkışa en yakın koltuklara kendileri oturabilmek için kendisinden kalkış sırasında tuvalette oturmasını istemesi üzerine güvenini bir miktar kaybetti. Gergin yolcular için sarsıcı bir yolculuk da Gatwick ile Montpellier arasında gerçekleşen ve yolcuların uçuş boyunca motor parçalarının düşüşünü izlemek zorunda kaldıkları uçuştu.

passages.passage_text:
Thousands of jobs come into our Job Centres and Employment Offices every week, but they get snapped up quickly. So, although we shall do all we can to help you, it's important for you to do all you can to help yourself. This leaflet tells you how.

1 Registered for work

Once you have registered for work, we will consider you for the available jobs. You must also register for work at the Job Centre in order to claim unemployment pay. But you actually apply for pay at the local Unemployment Office.

2 Getting a job

Jobs that come in are noted on cards and displayed in the office window as soon as possible. You can call in at any time to look at the jobs displayed.

Half the people who find jobs through Job Centres or Employment Offices find them in this way.

The receptionist is here to help you, so if you see a job that looks right for you, tell the receptionist, giving the reference number on the card.

3 If you want further help with finding a job

If you want more help or advice, don't forget that's what we're here for. Our Employment Advisers can help you with things like:
- thinking about the different sorts of jobs you could do - and which are best for you
- jobs available locally or elsewhere
- training for a new job
- your suitability for a training course, during which you get an allowance
- loans to help you look for, and move to, work in other fields

Even though you have a clear idea of the sort of job and pay you want, you may find that something different will suit you quite well. Keep this in mind when you're talking with the Employment Adviser and don't stick to one job only.

4 If you don't find a job on your first visit

Come into our office as often as you can to look at the jobs on display here. Good vacancies are coming in all the time, but they do go quickly. Don't rely on being told about them just because you've been registered for employment.

If you can't get to the office every day easily, come in whenever you can - and enquire by telephone as often as you like.

It'll help you to find a job faster if you keep in touch.

Job Centre Leaflet.

Thousands of jobs come into our Job Centres and Employment Offices every week, but they get snapped up quickly. So, although we shall do all we can to help you, it's important for you to do all you can to help yourself. This leaflet tells you how.

1. Registered for work.

Once you have registered for work, we will consider you for the available jobs. You must also register for work at the Job Centre in order to claim unemployment pay. But you actually apply for pay at the local Unemployment Office.

2. Getting a job.

Jobs that come in are noted on cards and displayed in the office window as soon as possible. You can call in at any time to look at the jobs displayed.

Half the people who find jobs through Job Centres or Employment Offices find them in this way.

The receptionist is here to help you, so if you see a job that looks right for you, tell the receptionist, giving the reference number on the card.

3. If you want further help with finding a job.

If you want more help or advice, don't forget that's what we're here for. Our Employment Advisers can help you with things like: thinking about the different sorts of jobs you could do, and which are best for you; jobs available locally or elsewhere; training for a new job; your suitability for a training course, during which you get an allowance; and loans to help you look for, and move to, work in other fields.

Even though you have a clear idea of the sort of job and pay you want, you may find that something different will suit you quite well. Keep this in mind when you're talking with the Employment Adviser and don't stick to one job only.

4. If you don't find a job on your first visit.

Come into our office as often as you can to look at the jobs on display here. Good vacancies are coming in all the time, but they do go quickly. Don't rely on being told about them just because you've been registered for employment.

If you can't get to the office every day easily, come in whenever you can, and enquire by telephone as often as you like.

It'll help you to find a job faster if you keep in touch.

task2.model_answer:
When searching for a job, many people focus strictly on their preferred profession and salary expectations. However, being flexible and open to different opportunities can be much more beneficial, especially in a competitive job market.

One clear advantage of staying open-minded is that it increases your chances of finding work quickly. If someone refuses to consider any role outside a narrow field, they may remain unemployed for months while good vacancies pass by. Accepting a different position can provide immediate income, keep daily routines active, and prevent long gaps on a resume.

Furthermore, trying a new field or taking a training course often helps people discover hidden strengths. Many workers eventually build satisfying careers in areas they had never originally planned to enter.

Of course, having clear career goals is useful, as it gives direction to your search. Still, combining clear goals with flexibility allows job seekers to adapt to changing opportunities and succeed sooner.

task2.model_answer:
Living in harsh natural environments requires both ingenuity and determination. As the example of Lanzarote shows, people do not simply abandon difficult regions; instead, they study local resources and turn obstacles into advantages. Using volcanic cinder to trap scarce moisture is a smart, sustainable solution that allows agriculture to thrive in an arid climate.

In the modern world, climate change and water shortages are making farming harder in many regions. Traditional adaptation techniques, combined with modern science, can help communities survive without harming nature. For instance, drought-resistant crops and drip irrigation work on the same principle of conserving every drop of water. Ultimately, human adaptability remains our strongest tool when facing environmental challenges, provided we respect and work with the landscape rather than against it.

task2.model_answer:
Setting highway speed limits requires balancing economic efficiency with public safety. On one hand, commercial transport companies rightly note that faster deliveries can lower shipping costs and keep store prices affordable. Modern highways and advanced braking systems also allow vehicles to travel more safely than in past decades.

On the other hand, human life should never be compromised for minor time savings. Heavy trucks take much longer to stop and cause far more severe damage in collisions, which explains why fatal accidents remain a major concern. Raising speed limits for heavy vehicles increases both stopping distances and fuel consumption. Therefore, governments should prioritize safety by keeping stricter speed limits for commercial trucks while using dedicated lanes or smart traffic systems to maintain steady freight flow.

passages.title: The Tornado
passages.tts_script:
The Tornado.

One of the most feared occurrences in nature is the tornado. The area most frequently the target of this violent windstorm is the Great Plains, the region extending from the Rockies to the Mississippi, and from Canada down through Texas. When warm, moist air meets with cooler, drier air at low levels, a tornado often occurs. Prior to the formation of the familiar funnel-shaped cloud, the sky is very clear. Then, a black line suddenly appears. As this black area moves in, the fast wind becomes hot and moist and a deep stillness encircles the landscape. Because the air pressure drops steadily during a tornado, breathing becomes difficult. Insects fall to the ground, unable to balance themselves in flight. Suddenly, a black funnel resembling a giant whip dips down out of the sky, destroying whatever it touches, and then retreats. Although a tornado usually destroys property rather than lives, an average of 120 people die yearly as a result of these violent storms. It is obvious why the tornado is feared throughout the Great Plains.

task2.model_answer:
Because severe weather events like tornadoes can develop rapidly and cause massive destruction, communities in high-risk regions must prepare well in advance. First, local authorities should invest in reliable early-warning sirens and mobile alert systems so residents receive critical minutes to seek shelter before a funnel cloud touches down. Building codes should also require reinforced basements or community storm shelters in vulnerable towns.

In addition, public education plays an essential role in saving lives. Schools and workplaces ought to conduct regular emergency drills so people know immediately where to go and what supplies to keep ready. While humans cannot prevent violent storms from forming, thoughtful urban planning, clear communication, and consistent preparedness can significantly reduce both injuries and fatalities when disaster strikes.

passages.passage_text:
On their way to southern Spain last summer, George and Jean Glover stopped outside the city of Seville for a lunch-time picnic. They left their car by the road and walked down to the cool waters of a river for a very pleasant meal. When they returned to their car, they were horrified to discover that the back window had been forced and smashed. It took a while to sort out what had gone, mostly small things like their camera, tape player and tapes, a few clothes lying on the back seat - fortunately, they hadn't bothered with the suitcases.

It suddenly dawned on Jean that she had left her handbag in the car, containing their passports, travellers' cheques, cash, ferry tickets, car keys and front-door keys. "It was appalling. How could I have been so stupid? In London, I'd never have left my handbag in the car," recalls Jean.

Initially, they both felt like driving back to the ferry and going home. But they knew they had to report the theft to the police. And they had to call their motor insurance company to arrange for a new back window. The travel insurance company, which ran a 24-hour emergency assistance service, advised them to call a neighbour, who had a key for their house, to ask her to get the locks changed. They were also advised to speak to the local Consular Office to arrange emergency passports.

The travellers' cheque company arranged an immediate replacement of their holiday money.

Bit by bit, they realised that all was not lost, and they managed to continue with what turned out to be a very enjoyable holiday. "But if we hadn't had the help and advice available through our travel insurance company, we'd have been totally lost."

Incredibly, there are many people like the Glovers who run into trouble abroad, yet have no travel insurance. That's why these days people taking a package holiday are normally obliged by the tour operators to have travel insurance; if they don't take the policy offered in the brochure, then they have to show that they have made alternative arrangements. There is no such safety net for people travelling independently, but, thanks largely to newspaper horror stories of uninsured tourists having to sell their houses in order to meet £100,000 bills for medical treatment in the States, most travellers abroad appreciate the need to take out insurance.

Purchasing travel insurance before going abroad is not an unnecessary extra cost; rather, it is an essential safeguard against unexpected emergencies. Seyahat Sigortası.

Geçen yaz güney İspanya'ya giderken George ve Jean Glover, öğle yemeği pikniği için Sevilla şehrinin dışında durdular. Arabalarını yol kenarında bırakıp çok keyifli bir yemek için nehrin serin sularına doğru yürüdüler. Arabalarına döndüklerinde, arka camın zorlanarak kırıldığını görünce dehşete düştüler. Nelerin gittiğini anlamaları biraz zaman aldı; çoğunlukla fotoğraf makinesi, kasetçalar ve kasetler, arka koltukta duran birkaç giysi gibi küçük şeylerdi; neyse ki bavullarla uğraşmamışlardı.

Jean, içinde pasaportlarının, seyahat çeklerinin, nakit paranın, feribot biletlerinin, araba anahtarlarının ve evin ön kapı anahtarlarının bulunduğu el çantasını arabada bıraktığını birdenbire fark etti. "Korkunçtu. Nasıl bu kadar aptal olabildim? Londra'da olsam el çantamı asla arabada bırakmazdım," diye hatırlıyor Jean.

Başlangıçta ikisinin de içinden feribota geri dönüp eve gitmek geldi. Ama hırsızlığı polise bildirmeleri gerektiğini biliyorlardı. Ayrıca yeni bir arka cam ayarlamak için araç sigorta şirketlerini aramaları gerekiyordu. 24 saat acil yardım hizmeti sunan seyahat sigortası şirketi, evlerinin anahtarına sahip olan komşularını arayıp kilitleri değiştirtmesini istemelerini tavsiye etti. Ayrıca acil durum pasaportu düzenlemek için yerel Konsolosluk Ofisi ile görüşmeleri de tavsiye edildi.

Seyahat çeki şirketi, tatil paralarının derhal yenilenmesini sağladı.

Yavaş yavaş her şeyin kaybedilmediğini fark ettiler ve sonunda çok keyifli bir tatile dönüşen gezilerine devam etmeyi başardılar. "Ama seyahat sigortası şirketimizin sunduğu yardım ve tavsiyeler olmasaydı, tamamen çaresiz kalırdık."

İnanılmaz bir şekilde, Gloverlar gibi yurt dışında başı derde giren ancak seyahat sigortası olmayan pek çok insan var. Bu yüzden günümüzde paket tur tatiline çıkan kişiler genellikle tur operatörleri tarafından seyahat sigortası yaptırmakla yükümlü tutuluyor; eğer broşürde sunulan poliçeyi almazlarsa, alternatif düzenlemeler yaptıklarını göstermek zorundalar. Bağımsız seyahat edenler için böyle bir güvenlik ağı yoktur, ancak büyük ölçüde Amerika Birleşik Devletleri'ndeki tıbbi tedavi için 100.000 sterlinlik faturaları ödeyebilmek adına evlerini satmak zorunda kalan sigortasız turistlerle ilgili gazete korku hikayeleri sayesinde, yurt dışına çıkan yolcuların çoğu sigorta yaptırma gereğinin bilincindedir.

passages.passage_text:
(Adapted from "The Captain and the Enemy" by Graham Greene)

I am now in my twenty-second year and yet the only birthday which I can clearly distinguish among all the rest is my twelfth, for it was on that damp and misty day in September I met the Captain for the first time. I can still remember the wetness of the ground under my gym shoes and how the blown leaves made the courtyard slippery as I ran recklessly to escape from my enemies between one class and the next. I slithered and stopped abruptly while my pursuers went whistling away, because there, in the middle of the courtyard, stood our formidable headmaster talking to a tall man in a bowler hat, a rare sight already at that date, so that he looked a little like an actor in costume. He carried a walking-stick over his shoulder at the slope, like a soldier with a rifle. I had no idea who he might be, nor, of course, did I know that he had won me the previous night, in a backgammon game with my father.

I slid so far that I landed on my knees at the two men's feet, and when I picked myself up the headmaster was glaring at me from under his heavy eyebrows. I heard him say, "I think this is the one you want - Baxter Three. Are you Baxter Three?"

"Yes, sir," I said.

The man, whom I would never come to know by any more permanent name than the Captain, said, "What does Three indicate?"

"He is the youngest of three Baxters," the headmaster said, "but not one of them is related by blood."

"That puts me in a bit of a quandary," the Captain said. "For which of them is the Baxter I want? The first name, unlikely as it may sound, is Victor. Victor Baxter - the names don't pair very well."

"We have little occasion here for first names. Are you called Victor Baxter?" the headmaster inquired of me sharply.

"Yes, sir," I said after some hesitation, for I was unwilling to admit to a name which I had tried unsuccessfully to hide from my friends. I knew very well that Victor - for some obscure reason - was one of the unacceptable names, like Vincent or Marmaduke.

"Well then, I suppose that this is the Baxter you want, sir. Your face needs washing, boy."

The stern morality of the school prevented me from telling the headmaster that it had been quite clean until my enemies had splashed it with ink.

School culture often places immense pressure on students to fit in, and even seemingly minor details like a first name can become targets for ridicule. Şu anda yirmi ikinci yaşımdayım ve yine de tüm diğerleri arasından açıkça ayırt edebildiğim tek doğum günüm on ikinci yaş günümdür; çünkü Kaptanla ilk kez Eylül ayındaki o nemli ve sisli günde tanışmıştım. Bir dersten diğerine geçerken düşmanlarımdan kaçmak için çılgınca koştuğum sırada spor ayakkabılarımın altındaki zeminin ıslaklığını ve savrulan yaprakların avluyu nasıl kayganlaştırdığını hâlâ hatırlayabiliyorum. Kaydım ve aniden durdum, beni kovalayanlar ise ıslık çalarak uzaklaştılar; çünkü tam orada, avlunun ortasında, o tarihte bile artık nadir görülen bir manzara olan ve bu yüzden biraz kostümlü bir aktöre benzeyen melon şapkalı uzun boylu bir adamla konuşan heybetli okul müdürümüz duruyordu. Bastonunu, tüfek taşıyan bir asker gibi omzuna yatırmış taşıyordu. Onun kim olabileceği hakkında hiçbir fikrim yoktu ve elbette bir önceki gece babamla oynadığı bir tavla oyununda beni kazandığını da bilmiyordum.

O kadar çok kaydım ki iki adamın ayaklarının dibine dizlerimin üzerine düştüm ve ayağa kalktığımda müdür kalın kaşlarının altından bana öfkeyle bakıyordu. "Sanırım istediğiniz kişi bu - Baxter Üç. Sen Baxter Üç müsün?" dediğini duydum.

"Evet, efendim," dedim.

Kaptan dışında asla daha kalıcı bir adla tanımayacağım adam, "Üç neyi ifade ediyor?" dedi.

"Üç Baxter'ın en küçüğü," dedi müdür, "ama hiçbirinin birbiriyle kan bağı yok."

"Bu beni biraz ikilemde bırakıyor," dedi Kaptan. "Çünkü benim istediğim Baxter bunlardan hangisi? İlk adı, kulağa ne kadar ihtimal dışı gelse de, Victor. Victor Baxter - isimler pek iyi uyuşmuyor."

"Burada ilk adlara pek ihtiyacımız olmaz. Senin adın Victor Baxter mı?" diye sertçe sordu müdür bana.

"Evet, efendim," dedim biraz tereddüt ettikten sonra; çünkü arkadaşlarımdan saklamaya çalışıp da başaramadığım bir ismi itiraf etmek istemiyordum. Victor'un -belirsiz bir nedenden ötürü- tıpkı Vincent ya da Marmaduke gibi kabul edilemez isimlerden biri olduğunu çok iyi biliyordum.

"Pekala o halde, sanırım istediğiniz Baxter bu, efendim. Yüzünün yıkanmaya ihtiyacı var, evlat."

Okulun katı ahlak anlayışı, düşmanlarım mürekkep sıçratana kadar yüzümün gayet temiz olduğunu müdüre söylememe engel oldu.

passages.passage_text:
In the past, most shoplifters agreed that the January sales offered wonderful opportunities for the hard-working thief. With the shops so crowded and the staff so busy, it did not require any extraordinary talent to steal one or two little things and escape unnoticed. It was known, in the business, as 'hoisting'. But the hoisting game is not what it used to be. Even at the height of the sales, shoplifters today never know if they are being watched by one of those mechanical balls (with small cameras hidden inside) hanging from the ceilings of so many department stores, above the most desirable goods. As if that was not trouble enough for them, they can now be filmed at work and obliged to attend a showing of their performance in court.

Selfridges was the first big London store to install videotape equipment to watch its sales floors. In October last year, the store won its first court case for shoplifting using as evidence a videotape clearly showing a couple stealing dresses. It was an important test case which encouraged other stores to install similar equipment.

When the balls, called sputniks, first made an appearance in shops, it was widely believed that their only function was to frighten shoplifters. Their somewhat ridiculous appearance, the curious holes and red lights going on and off, certainly made the theory believable. It did not take long, however, for serious shoplifters to start showing suitable respect. Soon after the equipment was in operation at Selfridges, store detective Brian Chadwick was sitting in the control room, watching a woman secretly putting bottles of perfume into her bag.

"As she turned to go," Chadwick recalled, "she suddenly looked up at the sputnik and stopped. She could not possibly see that the camera was filming her because it is completely hidden, but she probably had a feeling that I was looking at her. For a moment she paused, then she returned to the counter and started putting everything back. When she had finished, she opened her bag towards the sputnik to show it was empty and hurried out of the store without a sign of regret on her face."

task1.model_answer: Shoplifting used to be relatively easy during busy January sales, when crowded aisles and preoccupied staff allowed thieves to escape unnoticed. However, department stores have made stealing much riskier by installing ceiling-mounted mechanical balls, known as sputniks, with hidden video cameras inside. Initially dismissed as mere deterrents to frighten thieves, these devices proved effective when Selfridges won a landmark court case using video footage of a couple stealing dresses. Even when thieves cannot see the cameras, the mere possibility of being watched can deter them, as shown by a woman who returned stolen perfume after looking up at a sputnik.

task2.model_answer:
Security cameras in stores and public areas have become an essential tool for preventing theft and maintaining safety. As demonstrated in the passage, visible surveillance devices not only provide solid evidence for legal action but also discourage criminal behavior before a crime is completed. For business owners, fewer thefts mean lower financial losses and safer working environments for employees.

However, the widespread use of hidden or constant surveillance raises legitimate concerns about personal privacy. Customers who have done nothing wrong may feel uncomfortable knowing that their every movement is recorded and monitored from a control room. To strike a fair balance, stores should clearly inform shoppers through visible signs that recording equipment is in use, limit cameras strictly to sales floors rather than private spaces like fitting rooms, and delete footage promptly unless an incident occurs. When regulated transparently, security cameras can protect businesses effectively without undermining public trust.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Mağaza Hırsızlığı.

Geçmişte, çoğu mağaza hırsızı ocak ayı indirimlerinin çalışkan bir hırsız için harika fırsatlar sunduğu konusunda hemfikirdi. Mağazalar bu kadar kalabalık ve çalışanlar bu kadar meşgulken, bir iki küçük şey çalıp fark edilmeden kaçmak olağanüstü bir yetenek gerektirmiyordu. Bu işin jargonunda buna 'aşırma' denirdi. Ama aşırma oyunu artık eskisi gibi değil. İndirimlerin en yoğun olduğu zamanlarda bile, günümüz mağaza hırsızları, pek çok büyük mağazanın tavanından en gözde ürünlerin üzerine sarkan ve içinde küçük kameralar gizli olan o mekanik toplardan biri tarafından izlenip izlenmediklerini asla bilemiyorlar. Bu onlar için yeterince büyük bir dert değilmiş gibi, artık iş başındayken filme alınabiliyor ve mahkemede kendi performanslarının gösterimine katılmak zorunda kalabiliyorlar.

Selfridges, satış katlarını izlemek için video kaset kayıt ekipmanı kuran ilk büyük Londra mağazasıydı. Geçen yılın ekim ayında mağaza, bir çiftin elbise çaldığını açıkça gösteren bir video kaseti delil olarak kullanarak mağaza hırsızlığıyla ilgili ilk mahkeme davasını kazandı. Bu, diğer mağazaları da benzer ekipmanlar kurmaya teşvik eden önemli bir emsal davaydı.

Sputnik adı verilen bu toplar mağazalarda ilk kez göründüğünde, tek işlevlerinin mağaza hırsızlarını korkutmak olduğuna yaygın olarak inanılıyordu. Biraz gülünç görünümleri, tuhaf delikleri ve yanıp sönen kırmızı ışıkları, bu teoriyi kesinlikle inandırıcı kılıyordu. Ancak, ciddi mağaza hırsızlarının gereken saygıyı göstermeye başlaması uzun sürmedi. Ekipmanın Selfridges'da faaliyete geçmesinden kısa bir süre sonra, mağaza dedektifi Brian Chadwick kontrol odasında oturmuş, gizlice çantasına parfüm şişeleri koyan bir kadını izliyordu.

"Gitmek için arkasını döndüğünde," diye hatırlıyor Chadwick, "aniden başını kaldırıp sputniğe baktı ve durdu. Kameranın kendisini çektiğini görmesi imkânsızdı çünkü tamamen gizlenmişti, ama muhtemelen ona baktığıma dair bir hisse kapılmıştı. Bir an duraksadı, sonra tezgâha geri dönüp her şeyi yerine koymaya başladı. İşini bitirdiğinde, boş olduğunu göstermek için çantasını sputniğe doğru açtı ve yüzünde hiçbir pişmanlık belirtisi olmadan aceleyle mağazadan çıktı."

passages.passage_text:
British pop stars Phil Collins and Duran Duran are to join an international campaign in London this week to stop the production of illegal tapes of the Live Aid concert for famine relief, held last July in London and Philadelphia. Members of Duran Duran told The Sunday Times, "Producing illegal tapes of something like Live Aid is criminal. These people are exploiting the means that should help feed starving Africans."

The illegal tapes, manufactured by several different companies in Indonesia, have become best-sellers in the Far and Middle East, making profits estimated at millions of dollars. Now IFPVP, the International Federation of Phonogram and Videogram Producers, which represents more than 600 record companies worldwide, is asking the British government to bring economic pressure on the Indonesian government to stop the illicit trade. The packaging of the unlawful tapes is produced to a high professional standard, bearing the Live Aid logo, a guitar in the shape of Africa, and the words "For Africa famine relief."

"Their packaging makes people believe that the money is going to Africa," says Dave Laing of IFPVP. The federation received reports of at least 30 illegal versions of the tapes sold in many countries such as Singapore, Malaysia and Portugal, where you can, in fact, easily get the real ones. Indonesia has not signed international copyright conventions, and the federation says no legal action can be taken against the people in that country. "It's big business," says Laing. "The people who manufacture these tapes have large factories and their own relationships with the authorities."

A spokesman for the Indonesian government in London last week denied any knowledge of the tapes' being manufactured or sold in his country although he acknowledged that production of illegal tapes in Southeast Asia in general was a major problem. "It is shameful that this is happening in our country," he said. "And our government will take action once the facts have been determined."

task2.model_answer:
Digital and physical piracy remains a widespread problem across music, film, and publishing, often defended by consumers as harmless. However, copying and selling creative work illegally causes severe damage, especially when profits are stolen from charitable initiatives like Live Aid. In such cases, piracy not only violates intellectual property laws but also deceives compassionate buyers and deprives vulnerable communities of vital aid.

Stopping international piracy requires more than moral appeals; it demands coordinated legal and economic measures. First, governments must join and strictly enforce international copyright treaties so that large-scale manufacturers cannot operate with impunity across borders. Second, authorities should apply trade or economic pressure on countries that fail to regulate illegal factories. Finally, public awareness campaigns and affordable, easily accessible official releases can encourage consumers to verify where their money goes. Only through global legal cooperation and consumer responsibility can creative work and charitable funds be properly protected.

Yasa Dışı Kasetler.

İngiliz pop yıldızları Phil Collins ve Duran Duran, geçen temmuz ayında Londra ve Philadelphia'da açlıkla mücadele amacıyla düzenlenen Live Aid konserinin yasa dışı kasetlerinin üretimini durdurmak için bu hafta Londra'da uluslararası bir kampanyaya katılacak. Duran Duran üyeleri The Sunday Times'a, "Live Aid gibi bir etkinliğin yasa dışı kasetlerini üretmek suçtur. Bu insanlar, açlıktan ölmek üzere olan Afrikalıları doyurmaya yardımcı olması gereken imkânları sömürüyorlar," dedi.

Endonezya'daki birkaç farklı şirket tarafından üretilen yasa dışı kasetler, Uzak ve Orta Doğu'da en çok satanlar arasına girerek milyonlarca dolar olduğu tahmin edilen kârlar sağladı. Şimdi, dünya çapında 600'den fazla plak şirketini temsil eden Uluslararası Fonogram ve Videogram Yapımcıları Federasyonu (IFPVP), İngiliz hükûmetinden bu yasa dışı ticareti durdurması için Endonezya hükûmetine ekonomik baskı uygulamasını istiyor. Bu yasa dışı kasetlerin ambalajları, üzerinde Live Aid logosu, Afrika kıtası şeklinde bir gitar ve "Afrika'daki açlıkla mücadele için" yazısı bulunacak şekilde yüksek bir profesyonel standartta üretiliyor.

IFPVP'den Dave Laing, "Ambalajları, insanları paranın Afrika'ya gittiğine inandırıyor," diyor. Federasyon, aslında orijinallerini kolayca bulabileceğiniz Singapur, Malezya ve Portekiz gibi birçok ülkede kasetlerin en az 30 yasa dışı versiyonunun satıldığına dair raporlar aldı. Endonezya uluslararası telif hakkı sözleşmelerini imzalamamış durumda ve federasyon, o ülkedeki kişilere karşı hiçbir yasal işlem başlatılamayacağını söylüyor. "Bu büyük bir iş," diyor Laing. "Bu kasetleri üreten kişilerin büyük fabrikaları ve yetkililerle kendi ilişkileri var."

Endonezya hükûmetinin Londra'daki bir sözcüsü geçen hafta, kasetlerin ülkesinde üretildiğinden veya satıldığından haberdar olduğu iddialarını reddetti; ancak genel olarak Güneydoğu Asya'da yasa dışı kaset üretiminin büyük bir sorun olduğunu kabul etti. passages.passage_text:
A thousand years ago, York was one of the largest, richest and most famous cities in the whole of Britain. In the 10th century, it was described as being packed with a huge population, and traders from all parts, especially Danes. People called it Jorvik, and knew it as the capital of the North of England, and one of Europe's greatest trading ports. It owed its prosperity to the hard work of Viking settlers from Scandinavia, who had captured it in 866.

Most of the city's buildings were made of wood, and have long since been demolished, or have burnt down or rotted away. In some parts of modern York, however, near the rivers of Ouse and Foss, which run through the centre of the city, archaeologists have found that remains of Jorvik do still survive. They are buried deep below the streets and buildings of the 20th century city. Here the damp soils have preserved the wooden buildings. Whole streets of houses, shops and workshops are found although not in very good condition. All the rubbish left by the people of Jorvik in and around their homes is still there as well.

Between 1976 and 1981, archaeologists from the York Archaeological Trust dug up a part of this lost and forgotten city and found four rows of buildings. Some of the remains were so well preserved - even down to boots and shoes, pins and needles, plants and insects - that every aspect of life at the time could be reconstructed.

The York Archaeological Trust decided to convert the place into a museum and try to tell the story of Jorvik as it was a thousand years ago. To do so, it built the Jorvik Viking Centre in the huge hole created by the archaeologists. Two of the rows of buildings were reconstructed as we think they were. A further two were preserved just as the archaeological team discovered them, the ancient beams set out as they were found in the late 1970's, deep below the new shopping centre, where they have lain for centuries.

In the Jorvik Viking Centre, people from the 20th century journey back in time to the 10th century in cars, which silently move through the place. Meanwhile, modern time travellers watch the townspeople buying and selling, working and playing, in an atmosphere full of the sights, sounds and smells of 10th century Jorvik.

task1.model_answer: In the 10th century, York, then known as Jorvik, thrived as a major Viking trading centre after Scandinavian settlers captured it in 866. Although most of its wooden structures eventually disappeared, damp soil near the Ouse and Foss rivers preserved buried remains beneath the modern city. Between 1976 and 1981, archaeologists uncovered four rows of buildings along with everyday objects and household waste, allowing experts to piece together daily Viking life. To share this discovery, the York Archaeological Trust opened the Jorvik Viking Centre directly inside the excavation site, combining reconstructed buildings with preserved beams and offering visitors a realistic sensory journey into the past.

task2.model_answer:
Preserving archaeological remains directly at their original excavation site offers unique educational value, even when it limits modern urban development. When visitors stand in the exact place where people lived centuries ago, history feels immediate and tangible rather than distant. In the case of Jorvik, keeping the ancient beams beneath a modern shopping centre connects everyday contemporary life with the Viking past.

Nevertheless, cities also need space for housing, businesses, and infrastructure. It is not practical to halt every construction project whenever old objects are found underground. The most balanced solution is to assess the historical significance of a site first. Ordinary fragments can be recorded and moved to traditional museums, whereas rare, well-preserved discoveries like Jorvik deserve on-site preservation. By integrating heritage centres into modern buildings, cities can honour their past while continuing to grow.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Jorvik - Kayıp Viking Başkenti.

Bin yıl önce York, tüm Britanya'daki en büyük, en zengin ve en ünlü şehirlerden biriydi. 10. yüzyılda, büyük bir nüfusla ve özellikle Danimarkalılar olmak üzere her yerden gelen tüccarlarla dolup taşan bir şehir olarak tanımlanıyordu. İnsanlar ona Jorvik adını vermişti; onu Kuzey İngiltere'nin başkenti ve Avrupa'nın en büyük ticaret limanlarından biri olarak biliyorlardı. Refahını, şehri 866 yılında ele geçiren İskandinavya'dan gelen Viking yerleşimcilerinin sıkı çalışmasına borçluydu.

Şehrin binalarının çoğu ahşaptan yapılmıştı ve çoktan yıkılmış, yanmış ya da çürüyüp yok olmuştur. Ancak modern York'un bazı bölgelerinde, şehrin merkezinden geçen Ouse ve Foss nehirlerinin yakınında, arkeologlar Jorvik kalıntılarının hâlâ ayakta kaldığını keşfettiler. Bu kalıntılar, 20. yüzyıl şehrinin sokaklarının ve binalarının derinliklerine gömülüdür. Buradaki nemli topraklar ahşap binaları korumuştur. Çok iyi durumda olmasalar da evler, dükkânlar ve atölyelerle dolu bütün sokaklar bulunmaktadır. Jorvik halkının evlerinin içinde ve çevresinde bıraktığı tüm çöpler de hâlâ oradadır.

1976 ile 1981 yılları arasında, York Arkeoloji Vakfı'ndan arkeologlar bu kayıp ve unutulmuş şehrin bir bölümünü kazıp çıkardılar ve dört sıra bina buldular. Kalıntıların bazıları çizmeler ve ayakkabılara, toplu iğneler ve dikiş iğnelerine, bitkilere ve böceklere kadar o kadar iyi korunmuştu ki, o dönemdeki yaşamın her yönü yeniden canlandırılabiliyordu.

York Arkeoloji Vakfı, burayı bir müzeye dönüştürmeye ve Jorvik'in bin yıl önceki hikâyesini anlatmaya karar verdi. Bunu yapmak için arkeologların açtığı devasa çukurun içine Jorvik Viking Merkezi'ni inşa etti. Bina sıralarından ikisi, olduklarını düşündüğümüz hâlleriyle yeniden inşa edildi. Diğer iki sıra ise tam olarak arkeoloji ekibinin keşfettiği şekilde korundu; eski kirişler, yüzyıllardır yattıkları yeni alışveriş merkezinin derinliklerinde, 1970'lerin sonlarında bulundukları hâlleriyle sergilendi.

Jorvik Viking Merkezi'nde, 20. yüzyıldan gelen insanlar, mekânın içinde sessizce hareket eden arabalarla zamanda geriye, 10. yüzyıla yolculuk ediyorlar. Bu sırada modern zaman yolcuları, 10. yüzyıl Jorvik'inin görüntüleri, sesleri ve kokularıyla dolu bir atmosferde kasaba halkının alışveriş yapışını, çalışmasını ve eğlenmesini izliyorlar.

passages.passage_text:
A child learning to talk notices a thousand times a day the difference between the language he uses and the language those around him use. Bit by bit, he makes the necessary changes to make his language like other people's. In the same way, children learn to do all the other things without being taught - to walk, run, climb, whistle, ride a bicycle - by comparing their own performances with those of more skilled people, and slowly making the needed changes. Yet, at school we never give a child a chance to find out his mistakes for himself, let alone correct them. We do it all for him. We act as if we think that he will never notice a mistake unless it is pointed out to him, or correct it unless he is made to. Soon, he becomes dependent on the teacher.

Let him work out, with other children if he wants, what this word means, whether this is a good way of saying or doing this or not. In mathematics or science, give him the answer book. Let him correct his own papers. Our job should be to show only the way to get the right answer when the child tells us he can't find a way himself. Let's end all this nonsense of grades, exams, marks. Let us throw them all out, and let the children learn what all educated persons must some day learn, how to measure their own understanding, how to know what they know or do not know. The idea that there is a body of knowledge to be learnt at school and used for the rest of one's life is nonsense in a world as complicated and rapidly changing as ours. Anxious parents and teachers say, "But suppose they fail to learn something essential, something they will need to get on in the world?" Don't worry! If it is essential, they will go out into the world and learn it.

task2.model_answer:
While the author raises valid concerns about over-reliance on teachers and rigid testing, completely removing grades and exams from schools could create serious practical problems. Without any formal assessment, students might struggle to identify subtle gaps in subjects like mathematics or science, especially if they lack the maturity to judge their own accuracy objectively. Furthermore, grades and exams help universities and employers evaluate applicants fairly.

However, the writer's core message about encouraging self-directed learning is extremely valuable. Teachers do not need to correct every single error immediately; allowing students to discuss answers with classmates and review their own work builds confidence and critical thinking. Rather than abolishing assessment altogether, schools should balance periodic, constructive exams with regular opportunities for self-evaluation and independent problem-solving. This balanced approach prepares students both for academic standards and for lifelong learning.

Çocuklar ve Öğrenme.

Konuşmayı öğrenen bir çocuk, günde binlerce kez kendi kullandığı dil ile çevresindekilerin kullandığı dil arasındaki farkı fark eder. Yavaş yavaş, kendi dilini diğer insanlarınkine benzetmek için gerekli değişiklikleri yapar. Aynı şekilde çocuklar; yürümek, koşmak, tırmanmak, ıslık çalmak veya bisiklete binmek gibi diğer her şeyi de kendilerine öğretilmeden, kendi performanslarını daha becerikli kişilerin performanslarıyla karşılaştırarak ve yavaş yavaş gereken değişiklikleri yaparak öğrenirler. Oysa okulda bir çocuğa bırakın hatalarını düzeltmeyi, onları kendi başına keşfetme şansını bile asla vermiyoruz. Onun yerine her şeyi biz yapıyoruz. Sanki kendisine gösterilmedikçe bir hatayı asla fark etmeyeceğini veya zorlanmadıkça düzeltmeyeceğini düşünüyormuşuz gibi davranıyoruz. Çok geçmeden çocuk öğretmene bağımlı hâle geliyor.

Bırakın isterse diğer çocuklarla birlikte bu kelimenin ne anlama geldiğini ya da bunu söylemenin veya yapmanın iyi bir yol olup olmadığını kendi bulsun. Matematik veya fen bilimlerinde ona cevap anahtarını verin. Kendi kâğıtlarını kendi düzeltsin. Bizim görevimiz, yalnızca çocuk kendi başına bir yol bulamadığını söylediğinde doğru cevaba ulaşmanın yolunu göstermek olmalıdır. Tüm bu not, sınav ve puan saçmalığına bir son verelim. Hepsini bir kenara atalım ve bırakalım çocuklar, her eğitimli insanın bir gün mutlaka öğrenmesi gereken şeyi; kendi anlayışlarını nasıl ölçeceklerini, neyi bilip neyi bilmediklerini nasıl anlayacaklarını öğrensinler. Okulda öğrenilip insanın hayatının geri kalanında kullanacağı sabit bir bilgi birikimi olduğu fikri, bizimki gibi karmaşık ve hızla değişen bir dünyada saçmalıktır. Endişeli ebeveynler ve öğretmenler, "Peki ya hayatta ilerlemek için ihtiyaç duyacakları çok temel bir şeyi öğrenemezlerse?" diyorlar. Merak etmeyin! Eğer temel bir şeyse, dünyaya açılacak ve onu öğreneceklerdir.

Preventing Accidents

Clearly a major way to prevent accidents before they occur is for the trade union safety representative to carry out regular and effective inspections of the workplace. Recognised safety representatives have the following legal rights:
- To carry out a formal inspection every three months.
- To carry out an immediate additional inspection:
  * when an accident has occurred,
  * when a disease has been contracted,
  * when there has been a change in working conditions,
  * when new information becomes available concerning hazards.
- To investigate members' complaints.

Near Misses

All union members should be encouraged to report 'near misses' that happen to themselves or others. Near misses are events such as slipping on wet floors, items falling off shelves and just missing people, loose guards on machinery, and fires that are quickly put out, that could have injured people but which, by luck, did not. Reporting such events to the safety representative may prevent a serious accident in the future.

When an Accident Happens

Union safety representatives should have an agreement with management on being informed as soon as possible of all accidents. Only under that condition will it be possible to reach the scene of the accident immediately to follow these procedures:
- Make sure it is safe to approach.
- Make sure anyone injured is receiving attention.
- Insist that nothing is removed or altered until inquiries are complete.
- Check the accident is recorded in the accident book and that the record is not concerned with blaming the victim, but is an accurate description.
- Take statements from the injured person(s), if possible, and other witnesses. Remind witnesses they do not have to give statements to the management by law.
- Check that the factory inspector has been informed, if required by law.
- Sketch accident area, take photographs, if possible, and samples of defective equipment or chemicals.

Only if these procedures are carried out properly will it be possible for safety representatives to find out the real cause of the accident.

task1.model_answer: To keep workplaces safe, trade union safety representatives rely on both preventive measures and strict post-accident procedures. Before any injury occurs, representatives have the legal right to inspect the workplace every three months, investigate complaints, and conduct immediate checks following hazards, illness, or changed working conditions. Workers should also report "near misses"—incidents that narrowly avoid causing harm—so future accidents can be prevented. If an accident happens, representatives must reach the scene quickly, ensure medical care, preserve evidence, verify accurate reporting without blaming victims, gather witness statements, notify inspectors when legally required, and document defective materials to identify the true cause.

task1.title: Summarizing Workplace Safety Procedures

task2.model_answer:
Reporting "near misses" is just as crucial as investigating actual accidents because both reveal hidden dangers in the workplace before severe harm occurs. When workers slip on a wet floor or notice a loose guard on a machine without getting hurt, luck is often the only thing preventing a major injury. If these warning signs are ignored, the same hazard will eventually cause a serious accident.

However, encouraging employees to report near misses requires the right workplace culture. Many workers hesitate to speak up if they fear being blamed, mocked, or punished for slowing down production. Management and safety representatives must therefore treat every report seriously and focus on fixing unsafe conditions rather than finding fault with individuals. By valuing near-miss reports and acting on them promptly, companies can eliminate risks early, build trust with staff, and create a genuinely safer environment for everyone.

İş Yerinizi Daha Güvenli Hâle Getirmek.

Kazaları Önleme.
Açıkçası, kazaları meydana gelmeden önce önlemenin başlıca yollarından biri, sendika güvenlik temsilcisinin iş yerinde düzenli ve etkili denetimler yapmasıdır. Tanınmış güvenlik temsilcileri şu yasal haklara sahiptir: üç ayda bir resmî denetim yapmak; bir kaza meydana geldiğinde, bir hastalığa yakalanıldığında, çalışma koşullarında değişiklik olduğunda veya tehlikelerle ilgili yeni bilgiler ortaya çıktığında derhâl ek bir denetim gerçekleştirmek ve üyelerin şikâyetlerini araştırmak.

Ramak Kala Olaylar.
Tüm sendika üyeleri, kendilerinin veya başkalarının başına gelen ramak kala olayları bildirmeye teşvik edilmelidir. Ramak kala olaylar; ıslak zeminde kaymak, raflardan düşüp insanları kıl payı sıyıran eşyalar, makinelerdeki gevşek koruyucular ve hızla söndürülen yangınlar gibi, insanları yaralayabilecekken şans eseri yaralamamış olaylardır. Bu tür olayları güvenlik temsilcisine bildirmek, gelecekte ciddi bir kazayı önleyebilir.

Bir Kaza Olduğunda.
Sendika güvenlik temsilcilerinin, tüm kazalardan mümkün olan en kısa sürede haberdar edilmek üzere yönetimle bir anlaşması olmalıdır. Ancak bu koşul altında kaza yerine derhâl ulaşarak şu prosedürleri uygulamak mümkün olacaktır:
İlk olarak, yaklaşmanın güvenli olduğundan emin olun.
İkinci olarak, yaralanan herkesle ilgilenildiğinden emin olun.
Üçüncü olarak, incelemeler tamamlanana kadar hiçbir şeyin kaldırılmaması veya değiştirilmemesi konusunda ısrarcı olun.
Dördüncü olarak, kazanın kaza defterine kaydedildiğini ve kaydın mağduru suçlamaya yönelik değil, doğru bir tanımlama olduğunu kontrol edin.
Beşinci olarak, mümkünse yaralanan kişi veya kişilerden ve diğer tanıklardan ifade alın ve tanıklara yasalar gereği yönetime ifade vermek zorunda olmadıklarını hatırlatın.
Altıncı olarak, yasalar gerektiriyorsa fabrika müfettişinin bilgilendirildiğini kontrol edin.
Son olarak, kaza alanının krokisini çizin, mümkünse fotoğraf çekin ve arızalı ekipman veya kimyasallardan numuneler toplayın.

Güvenlik temsilcilerinin kazanın gerçek nedenini ortaya çıkarması, yalnızca bu prosedürlerin düzgün bir şekilde uygulanması hâlinde mümkün olacaktır.

passages.passage_text:
Unfortunately, England's highest main-line railway station hangs on to life by a thread. Deserted and unmanned since it was officially closed in 1970, Dent, situated high in the hills of Yorkshire, wakes up on six summer weekends each year, when a special charter train unloads walkers, sightseers and people who simply want to catch a train from the highest station, onto its platforms. However, even this limited existence may soon be brought to an end. Dent station, situated on the Carlisle railway line, is said to be the most scenic in the country, but no amount of scenic beauty can save the line from British Rail's financial problems. This year, for the sake of economy, the express trains which used to pass through Dent station have been put onto another route. It is now an open secret that British Rail sees no future for this railway line. Most of its trains disappeared some time ago. The stations on it, besides its bridge, built on a grand scale a century ago, are falling down. It is not alone. Half a dozen railway routes in the north of England are facing a similar threat. The problem is a worn out system and an almost total lack of means to repair it. Bridges and tunnels are showing their age, the wooden supports for the tracks are rotting and engines and coaches are getting old.

On major lines between large cities, there is no problem. These lines still make a profit and money can be found to maintain them, but on the country branch line the story is rather sad. As a track wears out, it is not replaced. Instead, speed limits are introduced, making journeys longer than necessary and discouraging customers who live in the country and who travel only from time to time. If a bridge is dangerous, there is often only one thing for British Rail to do: go out and find money from another source. This is exactly what it did a few months ago, when a bridge at Bridlington station was threatening to fall down. Repairs were estimated at £200,000 and British Rail was delighted, and rather surprised, when the local authorities of two nearby towns offered half that amount between them. This was a good solution, which the British Rail can always make use of.

task1.model_answer: The passage highlights the severe financial difficulties threatening rural railway lines in northern England, focusing on Dent station on the Carlisle line. Although Dent still operates briefly on six summer weekends for charter trains, its future looks bleak after express trains were rerouted to cut costs. Aging bridges, tunnels, rotting track supports, and old trains remain unrepaired due to a lack of funds. In contrast to profitable intercity routes, rural branch lines suffer from neglect; instead of replacing worn tracks, British Rail imposes speed limits, lengthening journeys and driving passengers away. Consequently, when major repairs are needed—such as the bridge at Bridlington—British Rail must seek external funding from local authorities.
task1.prompt: Summarize the main challenges facing rural railway lines in England and how British Rail responds to them, based on the passage.
task1.title: Summarizing Rural Rail Decline

task2.model_answer:
Rural railway lines often struggle to remain profitable, yet closing them can isolate small communities and damage regional economies. Therefore, governments and local authorities should cooperate to keep these essential transport links running.

On the one hand, maintaining little-used country lines places a heavy financial burden on national rail operators. When ticket sales cannot cover expensive repairs to bridges and tracks, resources are naturally directed toward busy intercity routes that serve far more passengers.

On the other hand, public transport is a vital service rather than merely a profit-making business. Rural trains allow residents without cars to reach workplaces, schools, and hospitals, while also supporting local tourism, as seen with scenic routes in Yorkshire. Reducing journey speeds or closing stations simply pushes more people onto crowded roads, increasing carbon emissions.

In conclusion, rural railways should be preserved through shared public funding, combining central government subsidies with contributions from local councils to ensure fair mobility for everyone.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Demir Yolu Taşımacılığının Geleceği.

Ne yazık ki İngiltere'nin en yüksek rakımlı ana hat tren istasyonu hayata pamuk ipliğiyle tutunuyor. 1970 yılında resmen kapatıldığından beri ıssız ve görevlisiz olan, Yorkshire tepelerinin yükseklerinde kurulu Dent istasyonu, her yıl altı yaz hafta sonu boyunca özel bir tur treninin yürüyüşçüleri, gezginleri ve sırf en yüksek istasyondan trene binmek isteyenleri peronlarına indirmesiyle uyanıyor. Ancak bu sınırlı varoluş bile yakında sona erebilir. Carlisle demir yolu hattı üzerinde bulunan Dent istasyonunun ülkedeki en güzel manzaraya sahip olduğu söylenir; fakat hiçbir manzara güzelliği bu hattı British Rail'in mali sorunlarından kurtaramaz. Bu yıl, tasarruf amacıyla, eskiden Dent istasyonundan geçen ekspres trenler başka bir güzergâha alındı. British Rail'in bu demir yolu hattı için bir gelecek görmediği artık herkesin bildiği bir sır. Trenlerinin çoğu bir süre önce ortadan kayboldu. Hattın üzerindeki istasyonlar ve bir asır önce görkemli bir ölçekte inşa edilmiş köprüsü yıkılmaya yüz tutmuş durumda. Üstelik yalnız da değil. İngiltere'nin kuzeyindeki yarım düzine demir yolu güzergâhı benzer bir tehditle karşı karşıya. Sorun, yıpranmış bir sistem ve onu onaracak imkânların neredeyse tamamen yokluğu. Köprüler ve tüneller yaşını belli ediyor, rayların ahşap traversleri çürüyor, lokomotifler ve vagonlar ise eskiyor.

Büyük şehirler arasındaki ana hatlarda bir sorun yok. Bu hatlar hâlâ kâr getiriyor ve bakımları için para bulunabiliyor; ancak kırsaldaki tali hatlarda durum oldukça üzücü. Bir ray yıprandığında yenisiyle değiştirilmiyor. Bunun yerine hız sınırları getiriliyor; bu da yolculukları gereğinden uzun hâle getiriyor ve kırsalda yaşayıp yalnızca zaman zaman seyahat eden müşterilerin hevesini kırıyor. Bir köprü tehlike arz ediyorsa British Rail'in yapabileceği tek bir şey kalıyor: Dışarıdan, başka bir kaynaktan para bulmak. Birkaç ay önce Bridlington istasyonundaki bir köprü yıkılma tehlikesi gösterdiğinde de tam olarak bunu yaptı. Onarım maliyetinin 200.000 sterlin olduğu tahmin ediliyordu ve yakındaki iki kasabanın yerel yönetimleri bu tutarın yarısını aralarında karşılamayı teklif edince British Rail hem çok sevindi hem de bir hayli şaşırdı. Bu, British Rail'in her zaman yararlanabileceği iyi bir çözümdü.

passages.passage_text:
According to scientists at the Meteorological Office and the University of East Anglia, who have recently completed their analysis of global temperatures, the eighties were the earth's warmest decade since records began. Their findings show that six of the ten warmest years so far have occurred during the 1980's, with 1988 the hottest of all.

Since 1900, average temperatures have risen by about 0.5°C, which fits in well with predictions from climatologists about how human activities should have warmed the planet. The factors that contribute to the warming up of the atmosphere are mainly carbon dioxide gas, produced by the burning of fossil fuels and forests, pollutants, such as chlorofluorocarbons, used in refrigerators, and methane.

Climatologists predict that by midway through the next century, temperatures may have risen by as much as 4°C. Happening so quickly, that could catastrophically reduce mankind's ability to grow food, destroy or severely damage what wildlife and wildernesses remained and raise sea levels, flooding coastal cities and farmland. Phil Jones, senior researcher at the University of East Anglia, said: "If we are changing the climate, we should do something now rather than wait until the warming is more severe."

Dr. Paul Heaton and Dr. David Parker of the Meteorological Office gathered together temperature records from about 1000 different locations spread across every continent and compared them with the average for those places from 1951 to 1990. The research also included temperatures measured on ships. The scientists found 1989 was 0.23°C above the 1951-80 average, and 1988 was 0.31 above. They agree with American researchers that the warmest years during this century were the eighties, and the tendency may be for the nineties to be even hotter!

passages.title: Global Warming
passages.tts_script:
Global Warming.

According to scientists at the Meteorological Office and the University of East Anglia, who have recently completed their analysis of global temperatures, the eighties were the earth's warmest decade since records began. Their findings show that six of the ten warmest years so far have occurred during the 1980s, with 1988 the hottest of all.

Since 1900, average temperatures have risen by about 0.5 degrees Celsius, which fits in well with predictions from climatologists about how human activities should have warmed the planet. The factors that contribute to the warming up of the atmosphere are mainly carbon dioxide gas, produced by the burning of fossil fuels and forests, pollutants, such as chlorofluorocarbons, used in refrigerators, and methane.

Climatologists predict that by midway through the next century, temperatures may have risen by as much as 4 degrees Celsius. Happening so quickly, that could catastrophically reduce mankind's ability to grow food, destroy or severely damage what wildlife and wildernesses remained and raise sea levels, flooding coastal cities and farmland. Phil Jones, senior researcher at the University of East Anglia, said: "If we are changing the climate, we should do something now rather than wait until the warming is more severe."

Dr. Paul Heaton and Dr. David Parker of the Meteorological Office gathered together temperature records from about 1,000 different locations spread across every continent and compared them with the average for those places from 1951 to 1990. The research also included temperatures measured on ships. The scientists found 1989 was 0.23 degrees Celsius above the 1951 to 1980 average, and 1988 was 0.31 above. They agree with American researchers that the warmest years during this century were the eighties, and the tendency may be for the nineties to be even hotter!

passages.passage_text:
There can be few people who have not heard of comets, but there are still a great many non-scientists who have no real idea of what a comet is. The most popular mistake is to assume that a comet streaks across the sky and disappears in a few seconds. In fact, all comets are very distant - far beyond the top of the earth's atmosphere - and you cannot see them moving. If you see an object moving visibly, it certainly cannot be a comet. It will be either an artificial satellite, thousands of which have been launched since the Space Age opened with Russia's Sputnik I in October, 1957, or else a meteor. Of course, it can also be a weather balloon or a high-flying aircraft.

Comets belong to the Sun's family, or solar system, but they are quite unlike planets. They are not solid and rocky; a comet consists of an icy central part (or nucleus), a head (or coma) and a tail or tails made up of tiny particles of 'dust' together with extremely thin gas. Comets may be enormous (the head of the Great Comet of 1843 was larger than the Sun), but they are very light since the nucleus, the only relatively massive part of a comet, cannot be more than a few miles in diameter. If a comet fell to the earth, it would only cause local damage.

Comets move around the Sun. In almost all cases their paths (or orbits) are elliptical, and except for Halley's Comet, all the really bright comets take thousands or even millions of years to complete one circuit. This means that we cannot predict them. During the last century, several were seen but in our own time they have been extremely rare. The last really 'great' comet was that of 1910, though there have been others which have become bright enough to be seen with the naked eye. Halley's Comet is unique because it appears every 76 years, and it has been seen regularly since well before the time of Christ; there is even a Chinese record of it dating back to 1059 B.C. However, it was only recently that astronomers realised that there was something unusual about it.

Space exploration and astronomical research often require enormous public funding, leading some people to question their practical value when urgent issues exist on Earth. Nevertheless, investing in space science offers vital long-term benefits for humanity.

Critics argue that governments should prioritize healthcare, education, and poverty reduction over studying distant objects like comets. Since scientific missions rarely produce immediate financial returns, spending billions on telescopes and spacecraft can appear wasteful to taxpayers.

However, astronomical research deepens our understanding of the solar system and protects our planet. Tracking near-Earth objects, including asteroids and comets, allows scientists to identify potential collision threats early. Moreover, technologies originally developed for space exploration—such as satellite communications, weather forecasting, and advanced imaging—have transformed everyday life on Earth.

In conclusion, while domestic social needs must remain a priority, continued investment in astronomy is essential for technological innovation, planetary safety, and human knowledge.

Kuyruklu Yıldızlar.

Kuyruklu yıldızları duymamış çok az insan vardır; ancak bilim insanı olmayan pek çok kişinin hâlâ kuyruklu yıldızın gerçekte ne olduğuna dair pek bir fikri yoktur. En yaygın yanılgı, bir kuyruklu yıldızın gökyüzünü hızla geçip birkaç saniye içinde kaybolduğunu sanmaktır. Aslında bütün kuyruklu yıldızlar çok uzaktadır, Dünya atmosferinin en üst katmanının bile çok ötesindedir ve hareket ettiklerini göremezsiniz. Gözle görülür biçimde hareket eden bir cisim görürseniz, bu kesinlikle bir kuyruklu yıldız olamaz. Bu ya Ekim 1957'de Rusya'nın Sputnik 1 uydusuyla Uzay Çağı'nın başlamasından bu yana binlercesi fırlatılmış yapay bir uydu ya da bir meteordur. Elbette bir meteoroloji balonu ya da yüksekten uçan bir uçak da olabilir.

Kuyruklu yıldızlar Güneş'in ailesine, yani güneş sistemine aittir; fakat gezegenlerden oldukça farklıdırlar. Katı ve kayalık değillerdir; bir kuyruklu yıldız buzlu bir merkez kısımdan yani çekirdekten, bir baş kısımdan yani komadan ve son derece seyreltik gaz ile minik toz parçacıklarından oluşan bir ya da birden fazla kuyruktan meydana gelir. Kuyruklu yıldızlar devasa olabilir — nitekim 1843 Büyük Kuyruklu Yıldızı'nın başı Güneş'ten büyüktü — ancak çok hafiftirler; çünkü kuyruklu yıldızın görece kütleli tek parçası olan çekirdeğin çapı birkaç milden fazla olamaz. Bir kuyruklu yıldız Dünya'ya düşseydi yalnızca yerel düzeyde hasara yol açardı.

Kuyruklu yıldızlar Güneş'in etrafında döner. Hemen hemen her durumda izledikleri yollar, yani yörüngeleri eliptiktir ve Halley Kuyruklu Yıldızı dışında gerçekten parlak tüm kuyruklu yıldızların bir turu tamamlaması binlerce, hatta milyonlarca yıl sürer. Bu da onları önceden tahmin edemeyeceğimiz anlamına gelir. Geçen yüzyılda birkaç tanesi görülmüştü, ancak günümüzde son derece nadir hâle geldiler. Çıplak gözle görülebilecek kadar parlayan başka kuyruklu yıldızlar olmuşsa da gerçekten görkemli son kuyruklu yıldız 1910 yılındakiydi. Halley Kuyruklu Yıldızı benzersizdir çünkü her 76 yılda bir görünür ve İsa'dan çok önceki dönemlerden beri düzenli olarak gözlemlenmiştir; hatta MÖ 1059 yılına dayanan bir Çin kaydı bile vardır. passages.passage_text:
It is interesting to observe the effect that the arrival of snow has on people in different countries. There are those countries for whom the arrival of the first snow showers is an expected annual event. There are those countries for whom the arrival of snow at any time of the year would be almost unheard of, and would be regarded as a major climatic catastrophe, or even a miracle.

But there are countries between these two 'extremes' that normally expect snow some time over the winter months, but never receive it regularly or in the same quantities every year. For them (and Britain is a prime example of such a country), the arrival of snow quite simply creates havoc. Within hours of the first snowfalls, however light, roads (including motorways) are blocked, train services are disrupted and bus services to suburbs and country districts are withdrawn. Normal communications quickly begin to suffer as well; telephone calls become difficult and the post immediately takes twice as long as usual. And almost within hours there are also certain shortages - bread, vegetables and other essentials - not because all these things can no longer be produced or even delivered, although deliveries are disrupted, but mainly because people panic and go out and stock up with food and so on - 'just in case'.

But why does snow have this effect? After all, the Swiss, the Austrians and the Canadians don't have such problems. The answer is quite simply a lack of planning and preparation - and we can't blame the weather forecasters for that. We have to remember, however, that equipment needed for dealing with snow and ice costs money. To keep the roads clear, for example, requires snowploughs and vehicles to spread grit or salt. The argument against investing in snowploughs in a country like Britain is that they are only used for a few days in any one year, and that money could more usefully be put into other things such as the hospital system, social services, helping the elderly, and so on.

task1.model_answer: While some countries expect heavy snow every year and others rarely see it, nations with irregular winter snowfall like Britain face severe disruption whenever it snows. Even light snow quickly blocks roads, interrupts train and bus services, slows down postal and telephone communications, and leads to temporary food shortages driven by panic buying. Although better planning and equipment such as snowploughs and salt spreaders could prevent this chaos, governments are reluctant to spend limited public funds on machinery used only a few days annually instead of healthcare or social services.
task1.prompt: Summarize why irregular snowfall causes widespread disruption in countries like Britain and explain the main argument against investing heavily in snow-clearing equipment.
task1.title: Summary: Snow Disruption and Public Spending

task2.model_answer: Governments in countries with infrequent snowfall face a difficult choice when allocating public funds. On the one hand, investing in expensive snowploughs and gritting vehicles seems inefficient if they remain unused for most of the year, especially when hospitals, elder care, and social services require constant funding. On the other hand, even a few days of paralyzing snow can cost the economy millions in lost productivity, delayed deliveries, and stranded commuters. Furthermore, disruptions to transport and postal services can prevent vulnerable people from accessing essential supplies or medical appointments. A practical compromise would be maintaining a modest reserve of dual-purpose municipal vehicles and improving emergency coordination rather than purchasing large fleets of specialized equipment. By balancing cost-effective preparedness with core public services, governments can reduce winter chaos without neglecting vital social needs.
task2.prompt: Should countries that experience snow only a few days a year invest heavily in snow-clearing equipment, or should that money be spent on healthcare and social services? Discuss both sides and give your opinion.
task2.title: Opinion Essay: Budgeting for Rare Extreme Weather
