passages.tts_script_tr:
Karın Etkileri.

Karın gelişinin farklı ülkelerdeki insanlar üzerinde yarattığı etkiyi gözlemlemek ilginçtir. İlk kar yağışının gelişinin her yıl beklenen olağan bir olay olduğu ülkeler vardır. Yılın herhangi bir zamanında kar yağmasının neredeyse hiç duyulmadığı, büyük bir iklim felaketi ve hatta bir mucize olarak görüleceği ülkeler de vardır.

Fakat bu iki uç arasında, normalde kış ayları boyunca bir ara kar bekleyen ama hiçbir zaman düzenli olarak ya da her yıl aynı miktarda kar almayan ülkeler de bulunur. Onlar için — ve Britanya böyle bir ülkenin başlıca örneğidir — karın gelişi tam anlamıyla kargaşa yaratır. İlk kar yağışından sonraki birkaç saat içinde, ne kadar hafif olursa olsun, otoyollar dâhil yollar kapanır, tren seferleri aksar ve banliyölerle kırsal bölgelere giden otobüs seferleri iptal edilir. Normal iletişim de hızla sekteye uğramaya başlar; telefon görüşmeleri güçleşir ve posta hemen her zamankinin iki katı sürede ulaşır. Ve neredeyse birkaç saat içinde ekmek, sebze ve diğer temel ihtiyaç maddelerinde birtakım kıtlıklar da baş gösterir; bunun nedeni teslimatların aksamasına rağmen bu ürünlerin artık üretilememesi ya da ulaştırılamaması değil, esas olarak insanların paniğe kapılıp her ihtimale karşı dışarı çıkarak yiyecek ve benzeri şeyler stoklamasıdır.

Peki kar neden böyle bir etki yaratıyor? Sonuçta İsviçreliler, Avusturyalılar ve Kanadalılar böyle sorunlar yaşamıyor. Bunun cevabı basitçe planlama ve hazırlık eksikliğidir ve bundan meteoroloji uzmanlarını sorumlu tutamayız. Ancak kar ve buzla mücadele için gereken ekipmanın maliyetli olduğunu unutmamalıyız. Örneğin yolları açık tutmak için kar küreme araçlarına ve kum ya da tuz serpen araçlara ihtiyaç vardır. Britanya gibi bir ülkede kar küreme araçlarına yatırım yapılmasına karşı öne sürülen argüman, bu araçların bir yıl içinde yalnızca birkaç gün kullanıldığı ve bu paranın hastane sistemi, sosyal hizmetler, yaşlılara yardım ve benzeri başka alanlara daha faydalı biçimde aktarılabileceğidir.

passages.passage_text: Many of the scientific achievements that we take for granted today have reached far beyond the dreams of scientists and science fiction writers of just seventy-five years ago. One of the most spectacular of these scientific accomplishments was the splitting of the atom. Life has never been the same since that event. From microwave ovens to electrical power and nuclear medicine, to ships that can sail the seas for as long as twelve years without refueling, the atom provides a better life for many of the inhabitants of the earth. Yet, this same power that is used today to detect genetic disorders in unborn children or to destroy a malignant cancer cell was the destructive force that killed over one hundred thousand people in Hiroshima and Nagasaki at the end of World War II. The splitting of the atom, the unleashing of its terrific power, poses the greatest single threat known to humanity. We now have the power to destroy in a matter of minutes a civilisation that has taken centuries to develop. Never before has the power for such potential good or such total destruction existed.

passages.passage_text: Acid rain is rain, snow, or fog that contains high amounts of sulphuric or nitric acid. To some extent, acidic rain occurs naturally and can have a beneficial effect - for instance, serving as fertilizer. But, when the acidity of the precipitation is abnormally high over a prolonged period, it can overwhelm the ability of water and woods (and buildings, statues, car finishes, fish, game, and humans) to accommodate it. When this happens, lakes and trees may die, game species may weaken, and human health may be endangered. Those who have studied the current crisis believe it to be the result of high acid levels caused primarily by sulphur dioxide emissions from coal-fired utility plants and nitrogen oxide emissions from automobiles. These pollutants are either transformed to acid in the air or deposited on the ground in dry form, combining with ground water to form sulphuric or nitric acid.

task2.model_answer: Acid rain illustrates how everyday energy and transportation choices can quietly damage ecosystems, architecture, and human health. Because coal-fired power plants and private automobiles are the primary sources of acid-forming emissions, meaningful solutions must target both sectors simultaneously. Governments can begin by tightening emission standards on power stations and accelerating the transition toward renewable energy sources such as solar and wind. At the same time, cities should expand reliable electric public transport and offer incentives for low-emission vehicles so commuters rely less on conventional cars. Individual citizens also play a role by conserving electricity at home and choosing public transit, cycling, or carpooling whenever possible. Although shifting away from fossil fuels requires substantial investment, protecting forests, freshwater lakes, and public health makes these measures essential. Through coordinated policy changes and responsible daily habits, societies can significantly reduce acid rain and preserve the natural environment.

Asit Yağmuru.

Asit yağmuru, yüksek miktarda sülfürik veya nitrik asit içeren yağmur, kar ya da sistir. Asidik yağmur bir ölçüde doğal olarak da meydana gelir ve örneğin gübre görevi görerek yararlı bir etki yapabilir. Ancak yağışın asitlik düzeyi uzun bir süre boyunca anormal derecede yüksek olduğunda, suyun ve ormanların yanı sıra binaların, heykellerin, otomobil boyalarının, balıkların, av hayvanlarının ve insanların buna uyum sağlama kapasitesini aşabilir. Bu gerçekleştiğinde göller ve ağaçlar ölebilir, av hayvanı türleri zayıflayabilir ve insan sağlığı tehlikeye girebilir. Mevcut krizi inceleyenler, bunun başlıca kömürle çalışan elektrik santrallerinden kaynaklanan kükürt dioksit emisyonları ile otomobillerden kaynaklanan azot oksit emisyonlarının yol açtığı yüksek asit seviyelerinin sonucu olduğuna inanıyor. Bu kirleticiler ya havada aside dönüşüyor ya da kuru hâlde toprağa çöküp yer altı suyuyla birleşerek sülfürik veya nitrik asit oluşturuyor.

passages.passage_text:
A large-scale campaign to alert smokers to the dangers of filling the lungs with carcinogenic smoke has been undertaken in many countries. Cigarette promotions have been banned on television in several major areas, and there has been endless discussion of how to discourage children from taking up the habit. Gruesome films are shown of pathetic hospital patients in the advanced stages of lung cancer. A few smokers have responded intelligently and given up, but many others have become so alarmed that instead they have been forced to light up an extra cigarette to calm their shattered nerves. In other words, although the problem is at last being dealt with, it is by no means solved.

The great error of the anti-smoking campaigners is that they rarely stop and ask the basic question: why do people want to smoke in the first place? They seem to think it has something to do with drug addiction - with the habit-forming effects of nicotine. There is an element of this certainly, but it is by no means the most important factor operating. Many people do not even inhale their smoke and can be absorbing only minute amounts of the drug, so the causes of their addiction to cigarettes must be sought elsewhere. The answer clearly lies in the act of oral intimacy involved in holding the object between the lips and this answer almost certainly applies as the basic explanation for the full inhalers as well. Until this aspect of smoking is properly investigated, there will be little long-term hope of eliminating it from our stressed, comfort-seeking cultures.

extra_questions.explanation: The passage states that campaigners overlook the basic question of why people want to smoke, focusing too narrowly on nicotine addiction while ignoring the psychological comfort of holding the cigarette.
options: They failed to ban cigarette commercials on radio as well as television

passages.title: Nicotine Addiction
passages.tts_script:
Nicotine Addiction.

A large-scale campaign to alert smokers to the dangers of filling the lungs with carcinogenic smoke has been undertaken in many countries. Cigarette promotions have been banned on television in several major areas, and there has been endless discussion of how to discourage children from taking up the habit. Gruesome films are shown of pathetic hospital patients in the advanced stages of lung cancer. A few smokers have responded intelligently and given up, but many others have become so alarmed that instead they have been forced to light up an extra cigarette to calm their shattered nerves. In other words, although the problem is at last being dealt with, it is by no means solved.

The great error of the anti-smoking campaigners is that they rarely stop and ask the basic question: why do people want to smoke in the first place? They seem to think it has something to do with drug addiction, with the habit-forming effects of nicotine. There is an element of this certainly, but it is by no means the most important factor operating. Many people do not even inhale their smoke and can be absorbing only minute amounts of the drug, so the causes of their addiction to cigarettes must be sought elsewhere. The answer clearly lies in the act of oral intimacy involved in holding the object between the lips, and this answer almost certainly applies as the basic explanation for the full inhalers as well. Until this aspect of smoking is properly investigated, there will be little long-term hope of eliminating it from our stressed, comfort-seeking cultures.

As the passage points out, alarming messages can increase anxiety and drive stressed smokers right back to cigarettes for emotional relief. In my opinion, public health campaigns would be far more effective if they combined honest health information with practical support for stress management and psychological comfort. Birkaç sigara içicisi akıllıca bir tepki verip sigarayı bırakmıştır; ancak diğer birçoğu öylesine telaşlanmıştır ki, bunun yerine altüst olmuş sinirlerini yatıştırmak için fazladan bir sigara daha yakmak zorunda kalmıştır. passages.passage_text:
In India, parents have traditionally found husbands or wives for their sons and daughters. Today, the parents are using a new technique in their search: advertisements in the Sunday newspapers. Every Sunday morning millions of Indians settle down with a cup of tea and the special weekend issues of their newspapers, just as Americans do. But here, with the marriage season approaching, many of them turn quickly to a Sunday feature that is particularly Indian - the columns of marriage advertisements in which young people seek husbands and wives.

In addition to helping young people find suitable marriage partners, these advertisements reflect the changes that are occurring in Indian society. The thousands of advertisements published each week increasingly reflect social changes that are coming to this traditional society. For example, although women are still usually described in terms of appearance or skills in "the wifely arts", information about their earning power is entering more and more in the advertisements. This portrays the arrival of the working wife in India.

Divorce, which used to be almost unheard of in India, is sometimes now mentioned in the advertisements as in the case of a woman whose advertisement explained that she had been "the innocent party" when her marriage broke up.

As a sign of the slight loosening of the rigid caste (social class) system, a number of advertisements promise "caste not important", or "girl's abilities will be main consideration". The majority of them, however, still require not only caste but also a certain home region or ethnic origin.

Because of high unemployment and a generally poor standard of living here, one of the best attractions a marriage advertisement can offer is a permit to live abroad, especially in Canada or the United States. A person who has one can get what he wants.

One recent Sunday in Madras, for example, a Punjabi engineer living in San Francisco advertised for a "beautiful slim bride with lovely features knowing music and dance". And a man whose advertisement said that he had an American immigration permit was able to say, "Only girls from rich, well-connected families need apply".

Eş mi Arıyorsunuz?

Hindistan'da anne babalar geleneksel olarak oğulları ve kızları için eşleri kendileri bulurdu. Günümüzde anne babalar bu arayışlarında yeni bir yöntem kullanıyor: Pazar gazetelerindeki ilanlar. Her Pazar sabahı milyonlarca Hintli, tıpkı Amerikalıların yaptığı gibi bir fincan çay ve gazetelerinin özel hafta sonu ekleriyle köşesine çekilir. Ancak burada, evlilik mevsimi yaklaşırken, birçoğu hızla özellikle Hindistan'a özgü bir Pazar köşesine, yani gençlerin kendilerine eş aradığı evlilik ilanları sütunlarına yönelir.

Bu ilanlar gençlerin uygun evlilik eşleri bulmasına yardımcı olmanın yanı sıra, Hint toplumunda meydana gelen değişimleri de yansıtmaktadır. Her hafta yayımlanan binlerce ilan, bu geleneksel topluma girmekte olan toplumsal değişimleri giderek daha fazla gözler önüne sermektedir. Örneğin, kadınlar hâlâ genellikle dış görünüşleri veya "ev hanımlığı sanatlarındaki" becerileri üzerinden tanımlansa da, ilanlarda onların kazanç gücüne dair bilgiler giderek daha fazla yer almaya başlamıştır. Bu durum, Hindistan'da çalışan eş olgusunun ortaya çıkışını yansıtmaktadır.

Eskiden Hindistan'da neredeyse adı bile duyulmamış olan boşanma, evliliği sona erdiğinde "masum taraf" olduğunu açıklayan bir kadının ilanında olduğu gibi, artık zaman zaman ilanlarda anılmaktadır.

Katı kast ya da toplumsal sınıf sisteminin hafifçe gevşediğinin bir işareti olarak, bir dizi ilanda "kast önemli değil" ya da "kızın yetenekleri temel ölçüt olacaktır" ifadeleri yer almaktadır. Ancak ilanların çoğunluğu hâlâ yalnızca kastı değil, aynı zamanda belirli bir memleketi veya etnik kökeni de şart koşmaktadır.

Buradaki yüksek işsizlik ve genel olarak düşük yaşam standardı nedeniyle, bir evlilik ilanının sunabileceği en büyük cazibelerden biri, özellikle Kanada veya Amerika Birleşik Devletleri'nde olmak üzere yurt dışında yaşama iznidir. Böyle bir izne sahip olan bir kişi istediğini elde edebilmektedir.

Örneğin, yakın zamanda bir Pazar günü Madras'ta, San Francisco'da yaşayan Pencaplı bir mühendis "müzik ve dans bilen, hoş hatlara sahip güzel ve ince bir gelin" için ilan vermişti. İlanında Amerikan göçmenlik iznine sahip olduğunu belirten bir adam ise şunu söyleyebilmişti: "Yalnızca zengin ve çevresi güçlü ailelerin kızları başvursun".

passages.passage_text:
Feminist organizations showed people that discrimination existed everywhere. They showed that it was difficult for women to enter various professions. In 1972, for example, only 9.3% of doctors and dentists were women, only 4% of all lawyers and judges were female, and only a small percentage of all medical students were women. It was also shown that society preferred to promote men to the positions of highest responsibility - even in traditionally female professions. For example, although more than 90% of elementary school teachers in 1970 were women, more than 80% of the directors were men. In addition, in many areas of employment, women received lower wages than men for the same work.

According to feminists, this discrimination was made possible by the attitude of society to women. The U.S. society traditionally perceives women primarily as childraisers and homeworkers. Men have traditionally been the breadwinners, who support their families with their incomes. Therefore, when women began to work outside the home, their income did not seem to be as important as the income of their husbands. There was a belief that a man's wages needed to be enough to support his family. This idea was then used to justify higher wages for men than for women.

Feminists argued that these attitudes were based only on tradition and not on any law of nature. It is true, of course, that a woman's biological function requires her to remain at home for some time before and after a child is born. This is a fact of life. Only women can bear children. However, this does not necessarily mean that the woman has to raise the children and manage the house while the husband works outside the home. No law of nature forces people to accept these roles. A woman has the right to choose between a career as a full-time mother and housewife and a career outside the home. Or she can combine the two careers if her husband is prepared to assist her. Only tradition, not nature, prevents this.

Therefore, feminists argue, attitudes toward women and their roles in society must change. If society needs women workers, it must permit them to have the same opportunities as men. If men want the economic benefits of working wives, they will have to accept changes in the traditional system of male and female responsibilities. Since the early 1970's, feminist organizations have protested the lack of equality for women and have demanded an end to sex discrimination. They have tried to educate both men and women; they have attempted to show people that attitudes toward the roles of men and women can be more flexible. It is possible, they argue, for women and men to share the responsibilities of supporting and raising a family.

passages.title: Sex Discrimination in the Workplace
passages.tts_script:
Sex Discrimination in the Workplace.

Feminist organizations showed people that discrimination existed everywhere. They showed that it was difficult for women to enter various professions. In 1972, for example, only 9.3 percent of doctors and dentists were women, only 4 percent of all lawyers and judges were female, and only a small percentage of all medical students were women. It was also shown that society preferred to promote men to the positions of highest responsibility, even in traditionally female professions. For example, although more than 90 percent of elementary school teachers in 1970 were women, more than 80 percent of the directors were men. In addition, in many areas of employment, women received lower wages than men for the same work.

According to feminists, this discrimination was made possible by the attitude of society to women. The U.S. society traditionally perceives women primarily as childraisers and homeworkers. Men have traditionally been the breadwinners, who support their families with their incomes. Therefore, when women began to work outside the home, their income did not seem to be as important as the income of their husbands. There was a belief that a man's wages needed to be enough to support his family. This idea was then used to justify higher wages for men than for women.

Feminists argued that these attitudes were based only on tradition and not on any law of nature. It is true, of course, that a woman's biological function requires her to remain at home for some time before and after a child is born. This is a fact of life. Only women can bear children. However, this does not necessarily mean that the woman has to raise the children and manage the house while the husband works outside the home. No law of nature forces people to accept these roles. A woman has the right to choose between a career as a full-time mother and housewife and a career outside the home. Or she can combine the two careers if her husband is prepared to assist her. Only tradition, not nature, prevents this.

Therefore, feminists argue, attitudes toward women and their roles in society must change. If society needs women workers, it must permit them to have the same opportunities as men. If men want the economic benefits of working wives, they will have to accept changes in the traditional system of male and female responsibilities. Since the early 1970s, feminist organizations have protested the lack of equality for women and have demanded an end to sex discrimination. They have tried to educate both men and women; they have attempted to show people that attitudes toward the roles of men and women can be more flexible. It is possible, they argue, for women and men to share the responsibilities of supporting and raising a family.

They attributed these inequalities to traditional attitudes that viewed men as primary breadwinners and women mainly as homemakers, which led employers to undervalue women's earnings. task2.model_answer:
Sharing financial and childcare responsibilities equally between partners brings clear benefits to both families and society as a whole. In the past, rigid expectations forced men to focus exclusively on earning an income while women were expected to handle domestic work alone, even when they also held jobs. This imbalance often limited women's career advancement and left fathers less involved in their children's daily lives.

When couples divide both paid employment and caregiving tasks fairly, families become more resilient. A household with two supported earners enjoys greater financial security, while children benefit from stronger relationships with both parents. Furthermore, workplaces gain access to talented professionals who might otherwise leave the workforce due to unsupported family demands. Although balancing two careers requires communication and flexible workplace policies, equal partnership creates healthier families and a fairer, more productive economy.

passages.tts_script_tr:
İş Yerinde Cinsiyet Ayrımcılığı.

Feminist örgütler insanlara ayrımcılığın her yerde var olduğunu gösterdi. Kadınların çeşitli mesleklere girmesinin zor olduğunu ortaya koydular. Örneğin 1972'de doktor ve diş hekimlerinin yalnızca yüzde 9,3'ü kadındı; tüm avukat ve hâkimlerin sadece yüzde 4'ü kadındı ve tüm tıp öğrencilerinin yalnızca küçük bir yüzdesini kadınlar oluşturuyordu. Ayrıca toplumun, geleneksel olarak kadın mesleği sayılan alanlarda bile en yüksek sorumluluk gerektiren mevkilere erkekleri terfi ettirmeyi tercih ettiği de gösterildi. Örneğin 1970'te ilkokul öğretmenlerinin yüzde 90'ından fazlası kadın olmasına karşın, müdürlerin yüzde 80'inden fazlası erkekti. Buna ek olarak, pek çok istihdam alanında kadınlar aynı iş için erkeklerden daha düşük ücret alıyordu.

Feministlere göre bu ayrımcılık, toplumun kadınlara yönelik tutumu sayesinde mümkün oluyordu. ABD toplumu kadınları geleneksel olarak öncelikle çocuk yetiştirici ve ev işi yapan kişiler olarak görür. Erkekler ise geleneksel olarak kazançlarıyla ailelerini geçindiren, evin geçimini sağlayan kişiler olmuştur. Dolayısıyla kadınlar ev dışında çalışmaya başladığında, onların geliri kocalarının geliri kadar önemli görünmemiştir. Bir erkeğin ücretinin ailesini geçindirmeye yetecek kadar olması gerektiğine dair bir inanış vardı. Bu düşünce daha sonra erkeklere kadınlardan daha yüksek ücret ödenmesini haklı çıkarmak için kullanıldı.

Feministler bu tutumların herhangi bir doğa yasasına değil, yalnızca geleneğe dayandığını savundular. Elbette bir kadının biyolojik işlevinin, çocuk doğmadan önce ve doğduktan sonra bir süre evde kalmasını gerektirdiği doğrudur. Bu hayatın bir gerçeğidir. Yalnızca kadınlar çocuk doğurabilir. Ancak bu, kocası ev dışında çalışırken kadının çocukları yetiştirmek ve evi çekip çevirmek zorunda olduğu anlamına gelmez. Hiçbir doğa yasası insanları bu rolleri kabul etmeye zorlamaz. Bir kadının tam zamanlı bir anne ve ev hanımı olma kariyeri ile ev dışındaki bir kariyer arasında seçim yapma hakkı vardır. Ya da kocası kendisine yardım etmeye hazırsa, bu iki kariyeri birleştirebilir. Bunu engelleyen doğa değil, yalnızca gelenektir.

Bu nedenle feministler, kadınlara ve toplumdaki rollerine yönelik tutumların değişmesi gerektiğini savunmaktadır. Toplumun kadın çalışanlara ihtiyacı varsa, onlara da erkeklerle aynı fırsatları tanıması gerekir. Erkekler çalışan eşlerin getirdiği ekonomik faydalardan yararlanmak istiyorlarsa, kadın ve erkek sorumluluklarına dair geleneksel sistemdeki değişiklikleri kabul etmek zorunda kalacaklardır. 1970'lerin başından bu yana feminist örgütler kadınlara yönelik eşitlik eksikliğini protesto etmiş ve cinsiyet ayrımcılığına son verilmesini talep etmiştir. Hem erkekleri hem de kadınları eğitmeye çalışmışlar; insanlara kadın ve erkek rollerine yönelik tutumların daha esnek olabileceğini göstermeye gayret etmişlerdir. Onlara göre kadınların ve erkeklerin bir aileyi geçindirme ve yetiştirme sorumluluklarını paylaşmaları mümkündür.

passages.passage_text:
There is one part of women's magazines that every man reads. It is the section popularly known as the 'agony column', where women, and increasingly men, write for advice on what are sometimes referred to as 'affairs of the heart'. The person who answers these letters usually has a very reassuring sort of name, which suggests a gentle middle-aged lady of great wisdom and experience, but who at the same time is as homely and approachable as your favourite aunt. At one time, it used to be widely believed that the letters were, in fact, all made up by someone on the editorial staff, and that the 'Aunt Mary' who provided the answers was, in fact, a fat man with a beard, who drank like a fish, smoked like a chimney and was unfaithful to his wife. Although this may be true in some cases, the majority of advice columns today are completely genuine, and the advisory staff are highly-qualified people with a deep understanding of human problems. At one time the letters, which were published and answered in full, dealt with problems of a very general emotional nature. The recurrent themes were loneliness, unhappiness in marriages and problems of adolescence. Occasionally, only the answers were published, not the letters themselves. Much of the fun in reading them lay in trying to work out the problem that led to such peculiar answers.

Agony columns have undergone great change. Nowadays, everything is much more explicit, and questions of the most intimate kind are fully dealt with. As the agony columns have become more professional and more frank, a lot of the fun has gone out of them. This is undoubtedly a good thing because there is something sad about our tendency to laugh at the misfortunes of our fellow men. In addition, agony columns are no longer restricted to emotional problems. Problems of various natures are now dealt with. For example, the advice columns get a lot of letters from people who are distressed about what they believe to be terrible physical deformities. Others are terrified of meeting people because they suffer from shyness, or are convinced that they are unattractive. It is not really funny to be so self-conscious about your appearance, or so lacking in self-confidence, that you stay in your room instead of going out and meeting people. If they do nothing else, the agony columns let you know that you are not the only one who is suffering from that particular problem.

The advisers seem to be on much more dangerous ground when they start to give advice on the most delicate and intimate aspects of human relationships. We cannot doubt either their good intentions or their understanding of human nature. But it is risky business to advise a married couple on how to save their marriage when what you know about them is only what they reveal to you in a short letter. Not only that, but the chances are that you only get one side of the story because only one of the partners will write to tell you about the shortcomings of the other. It is difficult to know how you can usefully answer such letters.

To their credit, the best advisers always make the point that without knowing more, they must limit themselves to general advice, and in some cases will even offer to enter into private correspondence in order to get more information and consequently to give more useful advice. Without doubt, they are, in their way, performing a valuable social service. If they were not, the agony columns would soon dry up for lack of interest, and more importantly for lack of confidence.

task1.model_answer: Agony columns, which offer advice on personal problems, have changed considerably over time. In the past, people often suspected that the letters were invented and answered by unqualified staff, while readers enjoyed guessing the issues behind odd replies. Today, however, these columns are mostly genuine and run by trained professionals. They address not only romantic matters, but also anxiety about appearance and severe shyness, helping readers feel less isolated. Although advisers face risks when commenting on marriages with only one partner's brief account, the most responsible ones offer general guidance or private correspondence, providing a trusted social service.

task2.model_answer:
Today, people seeking help with relationships, anxiety, or personal insecurities frequently turn to online forums, podcasts, or social media advice pages rather than traditional magazine columns. While public advice platforms still offer clear benefits, they also carry notable limitations that users should keep in mind.

On the positive side, reading or listening to public advice can reduce feelings of isolation. When people see others describing similar fears about shyness, appearance, or family conflict, they realize they are not alone. Public advice can also provide helpful general perspectives and encourage people to reflect on their situations before acting.

However, such platforms are rarely sufficient for serious relationship or mental health problems. Just as a magazine adviser sees only one partner's short letter, online commentators rarely have complete, unbiased context. Moreover, advice from unverified sources may be harmful rather than helpful.

In conclusion, public advice columns and digital forums remain useful for general support and reassurance, yet complex personal issues are best addressed through private, qualified professional guidance.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Dert Köşesi.

Kadın dergilerinin her erkeğin okuduğu bir bölümü vardır. Bu bölüm, kadınların ve giderek artan sayıda erkeğin bazen "gönül işleri" olarak adlandırılan konularda tavsiye almak için yazdığı, halk arasında "dert köşesi" olarak bilinen kısımdır. Bu mektupları yanıtlayan kişi genellikle güven verici bir isme sahiptir; bu isim büyük bir bilgeliğe ve deneyime sahip, nazik, orta yaşlı, ama aynı zamanda en sevdiğiniz teyzeniz kadar samimi ve cana yakın bir hanımefendiyi çağrıştırır. Bir zamanlar, mektupların aslında tümüyle yazı işleri ekibinden biri tarafından uydurulduğuna ve yanıtları veren "Mary Teyze"nin gerçekte küp gibi içen, baca gibi sigara tüttüren ve karısını aldatan sakallı, şişman bir adam olduğuna yaygın biçimde inanılırdı. Bazı durumlarda bu doğru olabilse de, günümüzde tavsiye köşelerinin büyük çoğunluğu tamamen gerçektir ve danışman kadrosu insan sorunlarına dair derin bir anlayışa sahip son derece nitelikli kişilerden oluşmaktadır. Bir zamanlar tam metin olarak yayımlanıp yanıtlanan mektuplar çok genel duygusal nitelikteki sorunları ele alırdı. Tekrarlanan temalar yalnızlık, evliliklerdeki mutsuzluk ve ergenlik sorunlarıydı. Bazen mektupların kendisi değil, yalnızca yanıtlar yayımlanırdı. Bunları okumanın eğlencesinin büyük kısmı, böylesine tuhaf yanıtlara yol açan sorunun ne olduğunu çözmeye çalışmaktan gelirdi.

Dert köşeleri büyük bir değişim geçirmiştir. Günümüzde her şey çok daha açıktır ve en mahrem türden sorular bile tüm ayrıntılarıyla ele alınmaktadır. Dert köşeleri daha profesyonel ve daha açık sözlü hâle geldikçe, işin eğlencesinin büyük bir kısmı da kaybolmuştur. Bu hiç şüphesiz iyi bir şeydir, çünkü hemcinslerimizin talihsizliklerine gülme eğilimimizde hüzün verici bir yan vardır. Üstelik dert köşeleri artık yalnızca duygusal sorunlarla sınırlı değildir. Artık çok çeşitli nitelikteki sorunlar ele alınmaktadır. Örneğin, tavsiye köşelerine korkunç fiziksel kusurlara sahip olduğuna inandığı için büyük üzüntü duyan insanlardan çok sayıda mektup gelmektedir. Diğerleri ise utangaçlıktan muzdarip oldukları veya çekici olmadıklarına inandıkları için insanlarla tanışmaktan ödleri kopmaktadır. Dış görünüşünüz konusunda bu kadar kuruntulu ya da özgüveninizden bu kadar yoksun olup dışarı çıkıp insanlarla tanışmak yerine odanızda oturmanız gerçekten komik değildir. Başka hiçbir işe yaramasa bile, dert köşeleri o belirli sorundan muzdarip olan tek kişinin siz olmadığını size gösterir.

Danışmanlar, insan ilişkilerinin en hassas ve mahrem yönleri hakkında tavsiye vermeye başladıklarında çok daha tehlikeli bir zemine adım atıyor gibi görünmektedir. Ne iyi niyetlerinden ne de insan doğasını anlama becerilerinden şüphe edebiliriz. Ancak evli bir çifte, onlar hakkında bildiğiniz tek şey kısa bir mektupta size anlattıklarından ibaretken, evliliklerini nasıl kurtaracakları konusunda tavsiye vermek riskli bir iştir. One-fifth of the electricity used in the average U.S. home feeds the steel box that dominates the kitchen. America's 110 million refrigerators tax utilities and they also release pollutants. Power plants would produce 115 billion pounds of carbon dioxide a year running those appliances and they would eat 77 billion kilowatt-hours of electricity - if all were 1993 models. Many are older, so the true figures are higher. In addition, 275 million pounds of ozone-depleting chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) used as a refrigerant and in insulation are time bombs in current models.

However, much more efficient refrigerators will hit the market within the next year or two. To encourage improvements, 24 companies sponsored a contest to build the best new prototype. The two finalists are Frigidaire and Whirlpool, and the winner, soon to be announced, will collect 30 million dollars. If current models were that good, carbon dioxide emissions would drop by at least 28 billion pounds. Power consumption - and consumers' bills - would drop by 25 percent. And by 1998 all new models must be CFC free.

task2.model_answer:
Reducing household energy consumption is essential for protecting the environment, and both governments and private companies play vital roles in driving innovation. Financial incentives, such as industry-sponsored prizes, and strict environmental regulations often work best when used together.

Competition prizes like the 30-million-dollar refrigerator contest motivate manufacturers to invest in research before laws force them to change. When companies compete to win rewards or market leadership, they develop creative engineering solutions, such as advanced insulation and more efficient motors, faster than they might under normal market conditions.

Nevertheless, voluntary incentives alone are rarely enough. Some manufacturers may ignore energy efficiency if consumers only care about lower purchase prices. Therefore, clear government deadlines, such as banning ozone-depleting CFCs in new appliances, ensure that every company meets basic environmental standards.

In conclusion, while financial incentives successfully spark technological breakthroughs, strict regulations guarantee that cleaner, more efficient products become the standard across the entire industry.

passages.passage_text:
One of the unfortunate features of the human condition is that the natural exploratory behaviour of human infants has to be restricted, especially in conditions of civilization, where the hazards of traffic, electricity, gas, stairs and many other complex dangers have been added to those which are found in primitive, rural circumstances. We are forced to overprotect our children psychologically, because we live in an artificial environment. We also tend to guard them too carefully in situations where this is not necessary, because small children are ill-equipped to look after themselves when surrounded by the dangerous trappings of civilization.

In a recent experiment, Eleanor Gibson constructed a 'visual cliff'; that is, a floor which appears to end in a steep drop, but which is actually safe since the floor continues as a sheet of tough glass. Babies crawl to the apparent edge, but will not take the risk of crawling onto the glass even if encouraged to do so, since they are already aware of the danger of the drop. This is not to say that it is safe to leave a baby on the edge of a real cliff, since the child may turn round and fall off backwards.

The pioneer doctors who started the Peckham Health Centre discovered that quite tiny children could be safely left in the sloping shallow end of a swimming bath. Provided no adult interfered with them, they could teach themselves to swim, exploring the water gradually and never going beyond the point at which they began to feel unsafe. Similarly, children would teach themselves to ride bicycles and use gymnasium equipment, and did so more confidently and quickly than if adults tried either to urge them on or warn them to be careful.

task1.model_answer: Living in modern society introduces complex hazards such as traffic, gas, and electricity, forcing parents to restrict infants' natural curiosity. Unfortunately, adults often become overly protective even in safe situations. Research shows that young children possess a strong natural sense of risk. In Eleanor Gibson's visual cliff test, babies refused to crawl over a clear glass floor because they recognized the apparent drop. Likewise, doctors at the Peckham Health Centre observed that toddlers in a shallow pool taught themselves to swim safely at their own pace, gaining confidence faster when adults neither pushed nor warned them.

task1.title: Summary: Overprotection and Children's Natural Caution

task2.model_answer:
Raising children in modern cities requires a delicate balance between keeping them safe and allowing them to explore independently. While parental supervision is vital in genuinely dangerous environments, excessive protection can hinder a child's confidence and physical development.

On one hand, young children cannot understand artificial hazards like busy roads, electrical outlets, or deep stairwells. In such settings, clear rules and close adult attention prevent serious accidents. Without basic protection, children's natural curiosity could easily put them in danger.

On the other hand, guarding children too closely in safe spaces sends the message that the world is always frightening and that they are incapable of judging risks themselves. As the Peckham Health Centre findings suggest, children who explore playgrounds, bicycles, or shallow water at their own pace quickly learn their personal limits and develop genuine self-reliance.

In conclusion, parents should eliminate serious modern hazards rather than eliminate every small challenge. Giving children room to test their abilities safely helps them grow into confident, capable individuals.

Tel: 811966

A Unique Experience in Indian Cuisine

Opening night at the Gandhi Restaurant brought cries of praise and delight from customers when they tasted different samples of the unique cuisine on Monday night.

Officially opened by County Councillor, Mr. Tony Peaston, the Gandhi offers the discerning diner authentic Indian dishes, many available for the first time in Hampshire.

The secret lies in the preparation - only authentic Indian herbs and spices are used to individually prepare each special dish, following ancient recipes, many handed down through generations of Indian chefs.

High Standard

"I've travelled extensively and dined at many Indian restaurants throughout the country, but rarely have I tasted Indian food of such a high standard," extolled Councillor Peaston.

"Whilst Gandhi himself was a leader of men, the Gandhi Restaurant could be considered the leader of a new breed of Indian cuisine in Hampshire," he added.

"By far the best curry we have had in the Portsmouth area," was the comment of Havant diners, Mr. and Mrs. Jim Cairns of Denvilles.

"We enjoyed the different menu and found the advice of the staff, explaining how each dish was prepared, very helpful for deciding on our choice of menu," they said.

Such glowing comments reflect the exclusive nature of the dishes available at the Gandhi Restaurant.

Original Recipes

You can choose from a menu which offers curries and tandoories, knowing each one is specially cooked for you, with individual care and attention, according to strict original recipes, by a top London chef, formerly of Covent Garden.

And after you have sampled the spicy delights of your main course, you can select from a choice of original Indian sweets to temper your palate.

Relaxing in the comfortable surroundings of the restaurant, you can have a hot towel to freshen yourself or clean your fingers between courses - another touch of Indian living.

The Gandhi Restaurant, situated at 139 Kingston Road, Portsmouth, is fully licensed and open seven days a week.

You can pop in for a traditional Indian lunch between 12 and 2.30 pm or enjoy a languid evening meal, when the restaurant is open from 6 pm to midnight.

But take care to book in advance, as demand for this cuisine is expected to be high, so avoid disappointment by telephoning Portsmouth 811966.

As proof of confidence in your enjoyment, the Gandhi is offering a 10 per cent discount on the cost of your meal, when you produce this advertisement within three months of the opening.

The staff at the Gandhi look forward to serving you with your first taste of truly authentic Indian cuisine in this area - and they know you will come back again and again.

"Whilst Gandhi himself was a leader of men, the Gandhi Restaurant could be considered the leader of a new breed of Indian cuisine in Hampshire," he added.

And after you have sampled the spicy delights of your main course, you can select from a choice of original Indian sweets to temper your palate.

Relaxing in the comfortable surroundings of the restaurant, you can have a hot towel to freshen yourself or clean your fingers between courses, another touch of Indian living.

The Gandhi Restaurant, situated at 139 Kingston Road, Portsmouth, is fully licensed and open seven days a week.

You can pop in for a traditional Indian lunch between 12 and 2:30 p.m. or enjoy a languid evening meal, when the restaurant is open from 6 p.m. to midnight.

As proof of confidence in your enjoyment, the Gandhi is offering a 10 per cent discount on the cost of your meal, when you produce this advertisement within three months of the opening.

The staff at the Gandhi look forward to serving you with your first taste of truly authentic Indian cuisine in this area, and they know you will come back again and again.

passages.passage_text:
On a fine midsummer morning, dawn breaks slowly over Salisbury Plain. For a full hour before sunrise, Stonehenge, that prehistoric circle of standing stones, stands out in eerie silence against the first yellow-green light of day. In the shadow of the great stones, the modern-day 'druids', people clothed in the religious robes and hoods of the ancient Celtic priests, have begun their annual ceremony of fire and water, celebrating the dawning of the year's longest day. Only a few lucky people are allowed to watch the ritual inside the stone circle itself. These are people with official passes: journalists, photographers, television cameramen and the villagers of nearby Amesbury. Outside, a small crowd has gathered beyond the protective barbed-wire fence constructed to save the stones from the inquisitive touch of countless tourists whose busy fingers have gradually worn away the surface of many stones.

The sight they have all come to see begins a few seconds after 5 am, when the first rays of the sun appear over the edge of the horizon. It is the start of an event precisely planned by the people who built Stonehenge, a temple to the Sun, almost 4,000 years ago.

And yet no one knows for certain who erected the stone circles or why they did so. The reason for this is simple: the builders had no writing. The architects of Stonehenge could therefore not leave behind them any documents or inscriptions to explain why they chose to build this extraordinary construction on Salisbury Plain; why they mixed local stones with others cut more than 200 miles away; why they demolished and rebuilt it several times in the course of a thousand years; or why they balanced huge stones on top of each other in a style more suited to building in wood.

But Stonehenge is no isolated mystery, for it is just one of a thousand prehistoric stone circles scattered throughout the British Isles and northern France. They have survived because they were built in what are now remote and sparsely inhabited regions: perhaps thousands of others have not stood the test of time and have been deliberately destroyed or absorbed into the landscape.

task2.model_answer: Ancient monuments such as Stonehenge face a difficult balance between public access and physical preservation. On one hand, allowing visitors to experience historic sites directly fosters appreciation for human heritage and supports local education and tourism. Seeing a 4,000-year-old structure up close creates a powerful connection to the past that photographs or textbooks cannot match. On the other hand, unrestricted access can cause irreversible damage. As the passage illustrates, even something as harmless-seeming as tourists touching the stones has gradually worn away their surfaces, forcing authorities to install protective fencing. In my view, preservation must take priority over unrestricted access. Once prehistoric stonework or ancient inscriptions are eroded, they can never be replaced. A sensible compromise is to maintain physical barriers, limit entry into sensitive areas through regulated passes, and provide informative visitor centres nearby. In this way, the public can still learn from and admire these landmarks while ensuring they survive for future generations.

Dışarıda ise, meraklı dokunuşlarıyla pek çok taşın yüzeyini zamanla aşındıran sayısız turistin ellerinden taşları korumak için inşa edilen koruyucu dikenli tel çitin ötesinde küçük bir kalabalık toplanmıştır.

Yine de kimse bu taş çemberleri kimin diktiğini veya bunu neden yaptığını kesin olarak bilmiyor. Bunun nedeni basit: inşa edenlerin yazısı yoktu. Bu nedenle Stonehenge'in mimarları, bu olağanüstü yapıyı neden Salisbury Ovası'na kurmayı seçtiklerini; yerel taşları neden 200 milden daha uzaktan kesilen başka taşlarla karıştırdıklarını; bin yıl boyunca neden birkaç kez yıkıp yeniden inşa ettiklerini ya da devasa taşları neden ahşap yapı inşasına daha uygun bir tarzda birbirinin üzerine dengelediklerini açıklayacak hiçbir belge veya yazıt arkalarında bırakamadı.

Ancak Stonehenge tek başına kalmış bir gizem değildir; zira Britanya Adaları ve kuzey Fransa boyunca dağılmış bin tarih öncesi taş çemberden yalnızca biridir. passages.passage_text:
Knowledge of farming was brought into Central Europe by immigrants from the Middle East and appears to have spread widely and rapidly during 5000 B.C. This spread was encouraged by the presence of extensive areas of fertile soils which could be worked easily and successfully by the fairly simple techniques and equipment of the first farmers in Central Europe. Access to this desirable soil was made easy by the use of routes along natural waterways, such as the Danube and the Rhine. These factors helped the peasant farming economy to adjust to the environment successfully. Without this adjustment to the environment, there would have been little opportunity for further advance, either in technology or in social organisation.

The earliest farmers brought with them the knowledge of agriculture and of related crafts and skills which had been developed in the Middle East. These included such techniques as the making of pottery and stone tools, and the building of houses and farm buildings. The advance from a hunting to a farming economy was important not only in respect of food-winning, but also because the yearly farming cycle provided the farmers with a rest from the continual search for food. The hunting economy normally demanded full-time hard work to get food.

House construction, too, needed to adapt. Whereas, the flat-roofed, sun-dried mud-brick houses of the Middle East were ideally suited to its warm, dry climate, the moist European climate required something more suitable to withstand strong winds and keep off rain.

History of Farming.

Knowledge of farming was brought into Central Europe by immigrants from the Middle East and appears to have spread widely and rapidly during 5000 B.C. This spread was encouraged by the presence of extensive areas of fertile soils which could be worked easily and successfully by the fairly simple techniques and equipment of the first farmers in Central Europe. Access to this desirable soil was made easy by the use of routes along natural waterways, such as the Danube and the Rhine. These factors helped the peasant farming economy to adjust to the environment successfully. Without this adjustment to the environment, there would have been little opportunity for further advance, either in technology or in social organisation.

The earliest farmers brought with them the knowledge of agriculture and of related crafts and skills which had been developed in the Middle East. These included such techniques as the making of pottery and stone tools, and the building of houses and farm buildings. The advance from a hunting to a farming economy was important not only in respect of food-winning, but also because the yearly farming cycle provided the farmers with a rest from the continual search for food. The hunting economy normally demanded full-time hard work to get food.

House construction, too, needed to adapt. Whereas the flat-roofed, sun-dried mud-brick houses of the Middle East were ideally suited to its warm, dry climate, the moist European climate required something more suitable to withstand strong winds and keep off rain.

task1.model_answer: Around 5000 B.C., migrants from the Middle East introduced agriculture to Central Europe, where it spread rapidly thanks to large stretches of fertile soil accessible via major rivers like the Danube and the Rhine. Because early farming tools were simple, this favourable environment enabled successful adaptation, paving the way for technological and social progress. Alongside farming, settlers brought Middle Eastern skills such as pottery, stone toolmaking, and building. Crucially, the seasonal nature of farming freed communities from the constant labour required by hunting. However, immigrants still had to modify their architecture: flat-roofed mud-brick dwellings suited the dry Middle East, whereas Europe's damp weather demanded sturdier structures against wind and rain.

task2.model_answer: The transition from a hunting economy to a farming economy represents one of the most decisive turning points in human history because it fundamentally changed how societies used their time and resources. As the passage highlights, hunting demanded continuous, full-time effort simply to secure enough food. By contrast, agriculture operated on a seasonal cycle that offered farmers periods of rest and greater predictability. This shift was vital for human progress: once people were no longer occupied solely with daily survival, they could devote energy to improving tools, crafting pottery, constructing permanent buildings, and developing stronger forms of social organisation. Furthermore, settling near fertile river valleys encouraged stable communities rather than constant migration. Although early farmers still had to adapt to local challenges such as harsher weather, the security of a reliable food supply created the foundation for technological innovation and complex civilizations. In short, farming transformed survival into steady development.

passages.passage_text:
When you close your eyes and try to think of the shape of your own body, what you imagine (or, rather, what you feel) is quite different from what you see when you open your eyes and look in the mirror. The image you feel is much vaguer than the one you see. And if you lie still, it is impossible to imagine yourself as having any particular size or shape. When you move, when you feel the weight of your arms and legs and the natural resistance of the objects around you, the 'felt' image of yourself becomes clearer. It is almost as if it were created by your own actions and the sensations they cause.

The image you create for yourself has rather strange proportions: certain parts feel much larger than they look. If you poke your tongue into a hole in one of your teeth, it feels enormous; you are often surprised by how small it looks when you inspect it in the mirror.

But although the 'felt' image may not have the shape you see in the mirror, it is much more important. It is the image through which you recognise your physical existence in the world. In spite of its strange proportions, it is all one piece, and since it has a consistent right and left and top and bottom, it allows you to locate new sensations when they occur. It allows you to find your nose in the dark, scratch itches and point to a pain.

task2.model_answer:
Although modern culture places enormous emphasis on how we look in photographs and mirrors, internal physical awareness is far more fundamental to everyday life. Our visual reflection only tells us how we appear to others from the outside, whereas our felt body image guides almost every movement we make. For instance, we rely on this internal map to walk up stairs without watching our feet, reach for an object in the dark, or respond quickly when we feel pain. Without it, simple physical coordination would become nearly impossible.

Of course, visual appearance still serves important social and practical purposes, such as noticing an injury or grooming ourselves. Nevertheless, focusing too heavily on mirror image can distort self-confidence, while tuning into physical sensations encourages healthier habits and bodily awareness. In the end, feeling how our body moves and functions matters much more than merely observing how it looks.

Marine pollution is a shared problem that no single coastal country can solve alone. Because sea currents carry waste across national borders, cleaning up regions like the Mediterranean requires strict international cooperation alongside local enforcement. Governments must work together to ban untreated sewage and industrial dumping, upgrade wastewater treatment plants, and impose heavy fines on ships that release oil into coastal waters.

At the same time, public health authorities should strictly regulate seafood markets so that vendors use clean, safe water rather than contaminated coastal water. Public awareness campaigns can also encourage tourists and residents to reduce plastic waste and report illegal dumping. Only through coordinated regional laws, modern infrastructure, and everyday responsibility can endangered seas recover for future generations.

Project-based programs that connect school subjects to real-world problems are often far more effective than traditional memorization alone. passages.passage_text:
Deep in the far west of Cornwall, England, Minnie, a typical Himalayan bear, is sleeping peacefully through the winter, unaware that she may not survive to enjoy waking in the spring. Her owner, Mr. Ken Trengoved, has been told that unless he pays a £153.60 license fee, the bear he has owned since she was born may have to be destroyed. To Mr. Trengoved, however, the demand represents an impossible amount, for he has only an old-age pension on which to live.

The local authorities have only recently found out about Minnie and have to demand a fee according to the law: the Dangerous Wildlife Act, 1976.

Mr. Trengoved, who lives in a caravan in the mountains, said: "The last thing in the world I want to lose is Minnie, who has been my friend for 20 years. She is only halfway through her life." Minnie, who stands more than 2 metres tall and weighs 180 kg, is kept nearby the caravan, in a secure cage within a wired area which she shares with dogs, cats, horses and rabbits. Mr. Trengoved said: "I love animals but Minnie is special. Even if she was taken away to somewhere else, I don't think she would live long, for this is her home."

Mr. Bob Reason, the local health officer, said: "We have no option but to collect this license fee. If Mr. Trengoved cannot find the money, then perhaps a new home could be found for Minnie in a zoo or circus. The last thing we would like to do is to destroy her." He said the license fee was high because to comply with the law, the bear would have to be examined by a veterinarian specializing in wild animals.

Mr. Reason said that since Minnie's story had become known, some local people had contacted the authorities offering financial help to Mr. Trengoved, so it is possible that this story will have a happy outcome. Our hopes no doubt will be shared by Minnie, who, deep in hibernation, is probably dreaming of honey.

passages.passage_text:
For a long time, night dreaming was thought to interfere with the necessary rest that sleep provides. However, experiments have indicated that dreams are not only a normal part of the sleep process but also vital to psychological health. Dr. William Dement of the Sleep Center of Mount Sinai Hospital, who is conducting extensive experiments on the significance of dreaming, reports that subjects whose dreams were interrupted regularly exhibited emotional disturbances such as hypertension, anxiety, irritability, and concentration difficulties. "One of the subjects," Dement reported, "quit the study in panic and two insisted on stopping, because the stress was too great." It was also observed that in five subjects there was considerable increase in appetite, i.e. they ate a lot, during the period of dream deprivation. As soon as the subjects were allowed to dream again, all psychological disturbances vanished.

More drastic experiments in Edinburgh, Scotland, supported these findings. Volunteers who were kept awake for very long periods dreamed considerably more than usual when finally permitted to sleep. It is as though a pressure to dream builds up. That is, the more your dreaming is restricted, the more you are inclined to dream when allowed to sleep. If dream suppression is carried on long enough, the result is serious disorders in the personality and, therefore, experiments conducted in this area should be monitored by professionals only.

In Dr. William Dement's study, participants deprived of dreams suffered from anxiety, irritability, concentration problems, and increased appetite, with some even withdrawing due to severe stress. task2.model_answer:
Scientific research into sleep and dreaming offers valuable medical benefits, yet it must be governed by strict ethical standards. On one hand, understanding how dreaming supports emotional stability helps doctors diagnose and treat conditions such as insomnia, chronic stress, and mood disorders. Without controlled studies, researchers like Dr. Dement could never have proven how vital dreaming is to mental health.

On the other hand, as the Edinburgh and Mount Sinai experiments clearly demonstrate, depriving participants of dreams can trigger acute anxiety, panic, and potentially severe personality disorders. Therefore, researchers have a moral duty to minimize harm. Experiments involving sleep or dream deprivation should only proceed with informed consent, continuous professional monitoring, and clear stopping rules whenever stress levels rise. Ultimately, advancing scientific knowledge is important, but protecting the psychological safety of human volunteers must always come first.

Rüya Görmek Ne Kadar Hayati?

Uzun bir süre boyunca gece rüya görmenin, uykunun sağladığı gerekli dinlenmeyi engellediği düşünülüyordu. Ancak deneyler, rüyaların yalnızca uyku sürecinin normal bir parçası olmakla kalmayıp psikolojik sağlık için de hayati önem taşıdığını göstermiştir. Rüya görmenin önemi üzerine kapsamlı deneyler yürüten Mount Sinai Hastanesi Uyku Merkezi'nden Doktor William Dement, rüyaları düzenli olarak kesintiye uğratılan deneklerin yüksek tansiyon, kaygı, sinirlilik ve odaklanma güçlüğü gibi duygusal bozukluklar sergilediğini bildirmektedir. Deneklerin yeniden rüya görmesine izin verilir verilmez tüm psikolojik bozukluklar ortadan kalkmıştır.

Yani rüya görmeniz ne kadar kısıtlanırsa, uyumanıza izin verildiğinde rüya görmeye o kadar eğilimli olursunuz. passages.passage_text:
This is a British newspaper article which tries to explain why teenagers are attracted to certain teenage 'cults' - groups whose beliefs and behaviour are considered strange, unnatural, or harmful but which become very popular or fashionable for a short period of time.

Ever since the early 1950's, there have been attempts to explain why youth cults happen. None of them has been entirely convincing.

The Reaction Theory

Teenagers want to show how different they are from their parents and, perhaps more importantly, their older brothers and sisters. If the last fashion had long hair and wide trousers, then the next one will have short hair and narrow trousers. There seems to be a lot of truth in this.

The Global Village Theory

Because of films, records, television and radio, teenagers are aware of what their contemporaries are doing all around the English-speaking world. Almost as soon as there were hippies in San Francisco, we had them too. A problem with this theory is that the time has to be right for a style to be adopted. The main influence on teenagers remains their friends.

The Teenage Idol Theory

Teenagers imitate the people they look up to, chiefly film stars and pop performers. When David Bowie used eye shadow, so did many of his male fans. However, this only succeeds if the pop star is in tune with the way youth culture is already going.

The Technology Theory

Many developments in teenage culture were possible only because of new technology. Electric guitars plus amplification meant you could have pop groups and pop festivals. The transistor radio made pop music inevitable.

The Drug Culture Theory

This theory suggests that the nature of a youth cult is determined by the drugs that it takes. Speed (amphetamine) equals aggression and energy - think of punks and skinheads. Pot (cannabis) equals relaxation and mysticism - think of hippies. Even 'ordinary' society has its drugs, such as alcohol, nicotine, coffee, etc. But maybe the style came before the drug.

The Capitalist Domination Theory

Youth culture happened because commerce understood that teenagers had money to spend and worked out ways of making them buy more records, clothes and concert tickets. This does not account for cults that were anti-consumerist like the punks and hippies.

The Class Theory

This is a sophisticated left-wing theory. Youth cults assert the solidarity of young people who are victimized by society. Skinheads take aspects of working-class culture to an extreme. They almost enjoy people looking down on them.

There is no simple explanation. My own research points to these general observations. Firstly, cults don't arrive fully-formed, flourish and then die. They are constantly changing and their message evolving. Secondly, teenagers only join a cult if it feels right, but most kids want to be something and cults give them something to be.

task2.model_answer:
Today, youth subcultures continue to thrive, though they spread much faster through digital platforms than through the television and radio networks of the past. Just as the Global Village Theory suggested, young people still observe what their peers are doing worldwide and adopt new styles rapidly. However, social media algorithms have amplified the role of both technology and commerce, turning niche trends into global movements within days.

Despite these technological shifts, the fundamental psychological reasons behind youth subcultures remain unchanged. As the writer emphasizes, adolescents want to differentiate themselves from older generations and belong to a group that reflects their values. For example, modern online communities centered on gaming, sustainable fashion, or independent music offer teenagers a shared language and solidarity, much like punks or hippies did in earlier decades. While companies quickly try to monetize these trends, young people primarily join subcultures because they are searching for belonging and an authentic identity.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Gençlik Akımlarını Anlamak.

Bu, gençlerin neden belirli gençlik 'akımlarına' — yani inançları ve davranışları tuhaf, doğal olmayan ya da zararlı kabul edilen ancak kısa bir süreliğine çok popüler veya moda haline gelen gruplara — ilgi duyduğunu açıklamaya çalışan bir İngiliz gazete makalesidir.

1950'lerin başından bu yana gençlik akımlarının neden ortaya çıktığını açıklamaya yönelik girişimler olmuştur. Bunların hiçbiri tam olarak ikna edici olmamıştır.

Tepki Kuramı. Gençler anne babalarından ve belki daha da önemlisi ağabey ve ablalarından ne kadar farklı olduklarını göstermek isterler. Bir önceki modada uzun saç ve bol pantolon varsa, bir sonrakinde kısa saç ve dar pantolon olacaktır. Bunda büyük bir gerçeklik payı var gibi görünmektedir.

Küresel Köy Kuramı. Filmler, plaklar, televizyon ve radyo sayesinde gençler, İngilizce konuşulan dünyanın dört bir yanındaki yaşıtlarının neler yaptığından haberdardır. San Francisco'da hippiler ortaya çıkar çıkmaz neredeyse hemen bizde de oldular. Bu kuramla ilgili bir sorun, bir tarzın benimsenmesi için zamanın uygun olması gerektiğidir. Gençler üzerindeki başlıca etki hâlâ arkadaşlarıdır.

Gençlik İdolü Kuramı. Gençler, başta film yıldızları ve pop şarkıcıları olmak üzere örnek aldıkları kişileri taklit ederler. David Bowie göz farı sürdüğünde, pek çok erkek hayranı da aynısını yaptı. Ancak bu durum, yalnızca pop yıldızı gençlik kültürünün halihazırda gittiği yönle uyum içindeyse başarılı olur.

Teknoloji Kuramı. Gençlik kültüründeki pek çok gelişme yalnızca yeni teknoloji sayesinde mümkün olmuştur. Elektro gitarlar ve amfi kullanımı, pop gruplarının ve pop festivallerinin ortaya çıkabilmesi anlamına geliyordu. Transistörlü radyo ise pop müziği kaçınılmaz kıldı.

Uyuşturucu Kültürü Kuramı. Bu kuram, bir gençlik akımının doğasının kullandığı maddeler tarafından belirlendiğini öne sürer. Speed ya da amfetamin, saldırganlık ve enerji demektir — punkları ve dazlakları düşünün. Ot ya da kenevir ise gevşeme ve mistisizm demektir — hippileri düşünün. 'Sıradan' toplumun bile alkol, nikotin, kahve gibi kendi keyif verici maddeleri vardır. Ama belki de tarz, maddeden önce gelmiştir.

Kapitalist Egemenlik Kuramı. Gençlik kültürü, ticaret dünyasının gençlerin harcayacak parası olduğunu anlaması ve onlara daha fazla plak, kıyafet ve konser bileti sattırmanın yollarını bulması nedeniyle ortaya çıkmıştır. Bu durum, punklar ve hippiler gibi tüketim karşıtı olan akımları açıklamamaktadır.

Sınıf Kuramı. Bu, incelikli bir sol görüşlü kuramdır. Gençlik akımları, toplum tarafından mağdur edilen gençlerin dayanışmasını ortaya koyar. Dazlaklar, işçi sınıfı kültürünün belirli yönlerini uç noktalara taşır. İnsanların kendilerini küçümsemesinden neredeyse keyif alırlar.

Tek ve basit bir açıklaması yoktur. Kendi araştırmam şu genel gözlemlere işaret ediyor. İlk olarak, akımlar tamamen şekillenmiş olarak ortaya çıkıp serpilmez ve sonra yok olmaz. Sürekli değişir ve mesajları evrilir. İkinci olarak, gençler bir akıma yalnızca kendilerine doğru hissettirirse katılır, ancak çoğu genç bir şey olmak ister ve akımlar da onlara olabilecekleri bir kimlik sunar.

passages.passage_text:
The New Zealand weekend tells you a great deal about this country of three million people and ninety million sheep. The first carpenter to land in New Zealand went on strike the moment his feet touched the beach in the 1840's. "I'm on strike for a forty-hour week," he said, thinking of all those free weekends. Like so many of the settlers, he was determined not to bring the mistakes of the old world with him. A man called Charles Parnell then became the leader of a strong union movement and negotiated agreements with employers to carry out wishes like these. By 1900, workers had their free weekend, women had the right to vote and the foundations of a welfare state had been laid.

Many of the settlers were Anglo-Saxon Christians, mostly Protestants, and for them the weekend was equally important. They made sure that Sunday was a day of rest. The kiwi weekend (the kiwi bird is the national emblem of New Zealand) has not changed much since. The cities are silent, and everything is closed.

Christians influenced New Zealand life in other ways too. They felt strongly that drinking alcohol was sinful and, in the early days, the country was 'dry' (without alcohol). Until 1968, pubs closed at 6 pm and, even now, they close at 10 pm. What is more, hotels are still only allowed to sell alcohol with meals on Sundays. This is remarkable when you think how many hard-living gold-hunters came to New Zealand when gold was found in Otago and on the west coast of the South Island in the 1860's, and then stayed on. They brought a totally different set of values with them, but it was the original settlers, the Protestants and trade unionists, who laid the foundations of present-day New Zealand.

The paradoxes, or conflicting side of New Zealand life remain, however. The people are very conservative; and yet the socialist government in the early 1980's became famous for its efforts to create a nuclear-free zone. It has a reputation as a successful multi-racial society, where the island's original inhabitants, the Maoris, have always mixed peacefully with the white population. The number of Maoris has, however, gone down dramatically. When they started using European arms, tribal wars became a blood bath and, for them, European illnesses such as measles and the common cold were killers. As the Maoris slowly took to Christianity, their culture and community life suffered too, and they certainly had no say in the setting up of the state. Recently, though, things have improved.

task2.model_answer:
Many nations pride themselves on progressive reputations, yet their histories often reveal painful contradictions. New Zealand is a clear example: while early union activism produced progressive achievements such as women's voting rights and strong labor protections, the indigenous Maori population suffered devastating losses from introduced diseases, deadlier conflicts, and exclusion from forming the state.

Understanding this complex history is vital for modern society. When countries celebrate only their achievements, they risk ignoring ongoing inequalities experienced by minority or indigenous groups. Acknowledging past injustices does not erase positive reforms like the welfare state or environmental leadership; instead, it creates an honest foundation for genuine reconciliation and fairer policies. For example, recognizing how traditional Maori culture and community life were undermined helps explain why modern efforts to protect indigenous rights and languages are necessary. Ultimately, a society becomes truly strong not by pretending its past was conflict-free, but by learning from its paradoxes to build a more inclusive future.
task2.prompt: Why is it important for a country to acknowledge both its progressive achievements and the historical injustices experienced by its indigenous people? Write a short essay explaining your view.
task2.title: Reconciling Progress and Historical Injustice

Ancak Yeni Zelanda yaşamındaki paradokslar, yani çelişkili yönler varlığını sürdürmektedir. Maoriler yavaş yavaş Hristiyanlığı benimsedikçe kültürleri ve toplumsal yaşamları da zarar görmüş ve devletin kuruluşunda kesinlikle söz sahibi olmamışlardır. task2.model_answer:
Easy access to credit cards and online payment options has made impulsive spending far easier for young people today. Because digital transactions feel less real than handing over physical cash, many young consumers fail to notice how quickly small purchases accumulate into serious debt. Aggressive marketing and social media trends also encourage them to buy items they neither need nor can afford.

To prevent compulsive shopping among youth, strict regulations are essential. Banks and retail companies should not be allowed to offer credit cards or store cards to anyone under eighteen, and clear income checks should apply to young adults as well. In addition, schools and families should teach basic financial literacy early so young people learn how to budget and distinguish between genuine needs and temporary desires. Limiting easy credit alongside better financial education can protect many young people from long-term debt.

task2.model_answer:
Providing direct food supplies to developing regions can be essential immediately after disasters such as droughts or floods. However, continuing food aid once the emergency has passed often weakens local economies instead of strengthening them. When imported food is distributed cheaply or for free, local farmers cannot sell their own harvests at a fair price and eventually abandon agriculture.

A far better approach is to invest in long-term agricultural self-sufficiency. Aid organizations and governments should support local farmers with improved seeds, irrigation systems, storage facilities, and fair access to markets. When aid is needed, purchasing crops from nearby regions rather than importing them from abroad keeps money inside the local economy. In short, emergency food relief should only be a temporary bridge, while sustainable aid must empower communities to produce their own food reliably.

passages.title: Disasters in the Third World
passages.tts_script:
Disasters in the Third World.

In the Third World, droughts and floods are not the unexpected disasters we always imagine. In the Sahel region of Africa, drought is practically part of the environmental cycle, and in Asia everyone knows that floods will occur regularly. In Britain, we have a 'disaster' every year. It gets so cold that little grows for months; we call it winter. Throughout that time, supermarket shelves bulge with food and most of us manage to keep warm.

The difference is that in the Third World countries the poor just can't cope. For the pastoralist, drought kills his cattle and his future. For the poor in Calcutta, the recent floods meant total destruction of homes and livelihoods. Yet, the rich in those countries remain untouched. Their land is irrigated, their homes well built, their credit is good.

task1.title: Why Predictable Events Become Disasters

task2.model_answer:
Although droughts, floods, and storms are natural phenomena, the scale of destruction they cause is largely shaped by human preparedness and economic inequality. In regions with strong infrastructure, flood barriers, reliable insurance, and emergency reserves, extreme weather causes inconvenience rather than widespread devastation. By contrast, when people live in poorly constructed housing on vulnerable land without savings or credit, even predictable seasonal weather can destroy everything they own.

Therefore, governments and international organizations must treat disaster prevention as an issue of social justice and infrastructure investment. Building irrigation networks, strengthening housing standards, and providing affordable credit and crop insurance to low-income families can protect communities before disasters strike. While nature determines when rains fail or rivers rise, society decides whether its poorest citizens are left defenseless or given the means to survive safely.

passages.passage_text:
Although often misunderstood, the scientific rationale for rearing a chimpanzee in a human household is to find out just how far the ape can go in absorbing the civilizing influences of the environment. To what degree is it capable of responding like a child and to what degree will genetic factors limit its development? At least six comprehensive studies by qualified investigators have been directed wholly or partly to this problem. All of these studies employed young chimpanzees as subjects and some also had in-house child controls whose day-to-day development could be compared directly with that of the experimental animal. In general, the results of this sort of research show that the home-raised chimp adapts rapidly to the physical features of the household. It does many things as well as a human child and some of them better (for example, those involving strength and climbing).

By far the greatest deficiency shown by the ape in the human environment is its lack of language ability. This eliminates the verbal communication which humans enjoy, and with it the vast amount of social intercourse and learning which are dependent upon language. Even amid human surroundings, a chimp never prattles or babbles as a young child does when beginning to talk. Although it imitates the behavior of others readily, it seems to lack the ability for vocal imitation. The neural speech centers of the brain are no doubt deficient in this respect and it is possible also that the larynx and speech organs are incapable of producing the complex sound patterns of human language. One long-time attempt to teach a home-raised chimp to pronounce human words succeeded only in getting the animal to mouth unvoiced whispers of the words 'mama', 'papa', 'cup', and 'up'.

At the same time, a chimpanzee in the home, as in the wild state, uses gestures or movements as communicating signals. This suggests the possibility of training a home-raised ape to employ a standardized system of gestures as a means of two-way communication. Such an investigation is now under way, using a gesture language devised for the deaf. Considerable progress has already been made in both the receiving and sending of gesture signals by this method. The technique seems to offer a much greater likelihood of success than other methods of intercommunication between chimpanzees and humans.

task1.model_answer: Researchers raise chimpanzees in human households to investigate how strongly environment versus genetics shapes development. While home-raised chimps adapt quickly to physical routines and even surpass children in strength and climbing, they fail to acquire spoken language because their brains and vocal organs cannot handle complex speech. Consequently, scientists are finding far greater success using gesture languages created for the deaf, which build upon chimpanzees' natural use of physical signals for two-way communication.

task1.title: Summary of Chimpanzee Language Research

task2.model_answer:
Raising wild animals such as chimpanzees inside human households raises important scientific and ethical questions. Historically, such studies provided valuable insights into the boundary between nature and nurture, showing that environmental exposure cannot overcome biological limits on human speech. Discovering that chimpanzees can learn sign language rather than spoken words also deepened our understanding of animal intelligence and non-verbal cognition.

Nevertheless, keeping apes in human homes carries serious ethical drawbacks. Chimpanzees are wild animals with complex social and physical needs that a domestic setting cannot fully satisfy, especially as they grow older and stronger. Removing an infant ape from its mother and species can cause long-term psychological distress once an experiment concludes. Today, non-invasive observational research in natural habitats or well-designed sanctuaries offers a more humane alternative. Therefore, while past studies contributed meaningfully to science, future research should prioritize animal welfare over domestic rearing experiments.
