Evde Yetiştirilen Şempanzelerde İletişim ve Dil.

Çoğunlukla yanlış anlaşılsa da, bir şempanzeyi insan evinde yetiştirmenin bilimsel gerekçesi, bu maymunun çevrenin medenileştirici etkilerini özümsemede ne kadar ileri gidebileceğini ortaya çıkarmaktır. Ne ölçüde bir çocuk gibi tepki verebilir ve genetik faktörler gelişimini ne ölçüde sınırlar? Nitelikli araştırmacılar tarafından yürütülen en az altı kapsamlı çalışma, tamamen veya kısmen bu soruna odaklanmıştır. Bu çalışmaların tümünde denek olarak genç şempanzeler kullanılmış ve bazılarında, günlük gelişimleri deney hayvanınınkiyle doğrudan karşılaştırılabilsin diye ev içi çocuk kontrol gruplarına da yer verilmiştir. Genel olarak, bu tür araştırmaların sonuçları evde yetiştirilen şempanzenin evin fiziksel özelliklerine hızla uyum sağladığını göstermektedir. Birçok şeyi bir insan çocuğu kadar iyi, güç ve tırmanma gerektirenler gibi bazı şeyleri ise daha iyi yapar.

Maymunun insan ortamında gösterdiği açık ara en büyük eksiklik, dil becerisinden yoksun olmasıdır. Bu durum, insanların sahip olduğu sözlü iletişimi ve bununla birlikte dile bağlı olan muazzam miktardaki sosyal etkileşimi ve öğrenmeyi ortadan kaldırır. İnsan çevresinin ortasında bile bir şempanze, küçük bir çocuğun konuşmaya başlarken yaptığı gibi asla gevezelik etmez veya anlamsız sesler çıkarmaz. Başkalarının davranışlarını kolayca taklit etmesine rağmen, sesli taklit yeteneğinden yoksun görünmektedir. Beynin sinirsel konuşma merkezleri bu bakımdan şüphesiz yetersizdir ve gırtlak ile konuşma organlarının da insan dilinin karmaşık ses kalıplarını üretme kapasitesine sahip olmaması mümkündür. Evde yetiştirilen bir şempanzeye insan sözcüklerini telaffuz etmeyi öğretmeye yönelik uzun süreli bir girişim, hayvanın yalnızca 'mama', 'papa', 'cup' ve 'up' sözcüklerini sessiz fısıltılar halinde ağzıyla şekillendirmesini sağlamada başarılı olabilmiştir.

Aynı zamanda, vahşi doğada olduğu gibi evdeki bir şempanze de iletişim sinyalleri olarak el kol hareketlerini veya jestleri kullanır. Bu durum, evde yetiştirilen bir maymunun iki yönlü iletişim aracı olarak standartlaştırılmış bir işaret sistemi kullanmak üzere eğitilmesi olasılığını gündeme getirmektedir. İşitme engelliler için geliştirilmiş bir işaret dili kullanılarak böyle bir araştırma halihazırda sürdürülmektedir. Bu yöntemle işaret sinyallerinin hem alınması hem de gönderilmesi konusunda şimdiden kayda değer bir ilerleme kaydedilmiştir. Bu teknik, şempanzeler ve insanlar arasındaki diğer iletişim yöntemlerine kıyasla çok daha yüksek bir başarı olasılığı sunuyor gibi görünmektedir.

passages.passage_text:
The name Martha Graham is practically a synonym for the still young art form known as modern dance, which dates from her pioneering days in the late 1920's. Often seen as a rebellion against the 350-year-old tradition of classical ballet, modern dance is the world's first lasting alternative to that tradition. Graham has been rightly called a genius and one of the greatest artists the United States has ever produced. Yet, as she is now over 90 years old, many people have wondered whether her legend will survive.

This question is more to the point because change has certainly been a major factor in Graham's career. In the early 1920's, Graham came to feel that the radical changes brought by World War I required a new and different style of dancing. After attending a famous dance school in California called Denishawn, she and two other dancers made a dramatic breakaway from the Denishawn dance company. In 1927, a reporter for the New York Times coined the term 'modern dance' to describe their new and innovative style.

Graham's early dances of the 1930's were stark and simple; these contrast with the poetic theater pieces of the 1940's and even more sharply with the complex dance-dramas based on Greek mythology that characterized the 1950's and 1960's. In these, several performers would each portray different aspects of the same character's personality. Often, scenes from the past, present, and future would occur at the same time, making it impossible to distinguish clearly one period of time from another.

Even the dancers themselves don't look the same as they once did. The full-bodied dancers of the past, whose weight gave them a certain power, have been replaced by thinner dancers with a lighter style. In Graham's view, these younger dancers are the product of diets and vitamins, but by using them, she has kept pace with the changing times. "The absolute thing is now," she says, "change is the only constant."

Not surprisingly, Graham's changes of direction have caused controversy, and some of her most devoted admirers have been upset by her new work that does not fit their memories of her past. She protested strongly when, in 1984, an application for grant money was refused by a foundation that felt the artistic standards of her company were not what they used to be.

Yet, despite the changes and controversy, one of Graham's beliefs has remained fixed over the years: that dance expresses emotion we often try to hide and cannot express in words. "I don't want to be understandable," she declared. "I want to be felt."

Graham's dances are open to many interpretations, and like abstract painters, she invites the viewer to bring his or her emotions to the work, to complete the picture. She remembers being influenced by Wassily Kandinsky when, as a young woman, she happened to see a painting of his - a slash of red against a field of blue - and decided, "I will dance like that."

task1.model_answer: Martha Graham pioneered modern dance in the late 1920s as an alternative to classical ballet. Throughout her career, she embraced constant transformation, moving from stark, simple routines in the 1930s to poetic works in the 1940s and complex mythological dance-dramas in the mid-twentieth century. Even the physical appearance of her dancers shifted toward thinner performers with a lighter style. Although these changes sparked controversy and led to a rejected grant application in 1984, Graham never abandoned her core belief that dance must convey deep, unspoken emotion. Like an abstract painter, she encouraged audiences to interpret her performances through their own feelings.
task1.prompt: Summarize how Martha Graham's style evolved over the decades and what core artistic belief remained unchanged despite controversy.
task1.title: Summary: Evolution of Martha Graham's Modern Dance

task2.model_answer:
Change is often controversial in the arts, yet it is essential for keeping creative traditions alive and relevant. Martha Graham famously stated that change is the only constant, demonstrating how artists must respond to the world around them rather than merely repeating past successes.

When World War I transformed society, Graham realized that classical ballet could no longer capture modern human experiences. By adapting her choreography across decades and embracing new styles, she kept her art form vibrant. Critics and devoted fans sometimes resist unfamiliar directions because they feel attached to an artist's earlier achievements. However, rigid adherence to tradition can turn living art into a museum piece.

Ultimately, artists should value creative evolution over pleasing loyal audiences. While experimentation carries the risk of disapproval or lost support, true artistic progress depends on the courage to challenge established expectations and discover fresh ways of expressing human emotion.
task2.prompt: Some fans and critics prefer artists to stay faithful to their original style, while others believe artists must continually evolve. Write a mini-essay discussing whether artistic innovation is more important than preserving an established style.
task2.title: Essay: Artistic Evolution vs. Preserving Tradition

passages.tts_script_tr:
Modern Dansın Annesi: Martha Graham.

Martha Graham adı, 1920'lerin sonlarındaki öncü günlerine dayanan ve hâlâ genç bir sanat dalı olan modern dansla neredeyse eş anlamlıdır. Çoğunlukla 350 yıllık klasik bale geleneğine karşı bir başkaldırı olarak görülen modern dans, bu geleneğe karşı dünyanın ilk kalıcı alternatifidir. Graham, haklı olarak bir dahi ve Amerika Birleşik Devletleri'nin yetiştirdiği en büyük sanatçılardan biri olarak anılmıştır. Yine de artık 90 yaşını aşmış olduğundan, birçok kişi efsanesinin yaşayıp yaşamayacağını merak etmektedir.

Bu soru daha da yerindedir çünkü değişim, Graham'ın kariyerinde kesinlikle önemli bir etken olmuştur. 1920'lerin başlarında Graham, Birinci Dünya Savaşı'nın getirdiği köklü değişimlerin yeni ve farklı bir dans tarzı gerektirdiğini hissetmeye başladı. Kaliforniya'daki Denishawn adlı ünlü bir dans okuluna devam ettikten sonra, kendisi ve diğer iki dansçı Denishawn dans topluluğundan çarpıcı bir ayrılık gerçekleştirdi. 1927 yılında New York Times muhabirlerinden biri, onların bu yeni ve yenilikçi tarzını tanımlamak için "modern dans" terimini ortaya attı.

Graham'ın 1930'lardaki ilk dansları yalın ve sadeydi; bunlar 1940'ların şiirsel tiyatro eserleriyle ve 1950'ler ile 1960'lara damgasını vuran Yunan mitolojisine dayalı karmaşık dans dramalarıyla çok daha keskin bir tezat oluşturur. Bunlarda birkaç sanatçı, aynı karakterin kişiliğinin farklı yönlerini ayrı ayrı canlandırırdı. Çoğunlukla geçmişten, şimdiki zamandan ve gelecekten sahneler aynı anda gerçekleşir, bu da bir zaman dilimini diğerinden açıkça ayırt etmeyi imkânsız hale getirirdi.

Dansçıların kendileri bile eskiden oldukları gibi görünmüyor artık. Geçmişin, kilolarının kendilerine belirli bir güç kattığı dolgun vücutlu dansçılarının yerini, daha hafif bir tarza sahip daha ince dansçılar aldı. Graham'a göre bu genç dansçılar diyetlerin ve vitaminlerin ürünü, ancak onları kullanarak değişen zamanlara ayak uydurmayı başardı. "Mutlak olan şey şimdidir," diyor, "tek sabit şey değişimdir."

Bekleneceği üzere, Graham'ın yön değişiklikleri tartışmalara yol açtı ve en sadık hayranlarından bazıları, onun geçmişine dair anılarıyla örtüşmeyen yeni çalışmalarından rahatsız oldu. 1984 yılında, topluluğunun sanatsal standartlarının eskisi gibi olmadığını düşünen bir vakıf tarafından hibe başvurusu reddedildiğinde buna şiddetle karşı çıktı.

Yine de tüm değişimlere ve tartışmalara rağmen, Graham'ın inançlarından biri yıllar boyunca sabit kaldı: dansın, çoğu zaman gizlemeye çalıştığımız ve kelimelerle ifade edemediğimiz duyguları dışa vurduğu inancı. "Anlaşılır olmak istemiyorum," diye ilan etmişti. "Hissedilmek istiyorum."

Graham'ın dansları pek çok yoruma açıktır ve soyut ressamlar gibi o da izleyiciyi resmi tamamlamak üzere kendi duygularını esere katmaya davet eder. Genç bir kadınken Wassily Kandinsky'nin mavi bir zemin üzerindeki kırmızı bir darbeden oluşan bir tablosuna tesadüfen rastladığında ondan etkilendiğini ve "İşte böyle dans edeceğim," diye karar verdiğini hatırlar.

passages.passage_text:
The idea of working 'au pair', with full board and pocket money in return for help in the home, has been welcomed by thousands of girls coming from countries outside Britain. Many of them want to practise the English they have learned at school but cannot afford to live away from home without some kind of work to provide them with at least the necessities of life.

The aim of practising the language may be weaker in some girls than the desire to enjoy the freedom of being away from home and the excitement of living in a large city like London. The idea of working seriously for their living may be unattractive. It is experiences with the kind of girl who returns home at all hours of the night or not at all, is always complaining when asked to do anything, cannot be trusted to do the simplest thing properly, neglects her studies and gets into various kinds of trouble, that make many employers hesitate about taking a second 'au pair' into their home.

But the faults are not all on one side and many 'au pair' girls also have good cause for complaint, some of them becoming depressed and unhappy as a result. Unfortunately far too few girls who are attracted by the idea of earning their living in another land are prepared for the various difficulties that may await them.

It is essential that any girl who takes a post of this kind should be at least eighteen years old, and be sensible, practical and well able to look after herself. Wherever possible she should go to a family she knows something about possibly from a friend who has already worked with them. In any case she should make sure she has a letter from her employer stating clearly her terms of employment: exactly what she is expected to do (whether minding children or helping with light housework), how long she will be expected to work each week and her free days and half-days for attending language classes. She should be promised a single room of a satisfactory standard and she will want to eat with the family to have the opportunity of practising the language with them. Her earnings will not be high, but her employer will probably pay her return travel expenses, if the girl is prepared to stay with the same family all the time.

Two other pieces of advice are important. A girl should keep with her travellers' cheques of a sufficient value to pay for her journey home in case it becomes necessary to return urgently. In addition, she should know the addresses of one or two organisations which can give help and advice if there are problems. Several of these organisations exist in London and other large centres.

task1.model_answer: Working as an au pair in Britain allows young women from abroad to practise English while receiving accommodation, meals, and modest pocket money. However, problems can arise on both sides. Some au pairs prioritize freedom over serious work and study, making employers reluctant to hire again, while others feel unprepared and face unfair treatment. To ensure a positive experience, applicants should be at least eighteen, mature, and ideally placed with a known family. They must obtain a written agreement detailing duties, working hours, free time for classes, and a proper single room. task2.model_answer:
Working abroad as a young adult—whether as an au pair, intern, or seasonal worker—offers remarkable personal and linguistic growth, yet it also carries real challenges that require careful preparation.

On the positive side, living with local people provides daily immersion in a foreign language that classroom study cannot match. Beyond language skills, young people learn independence, cultural adaptability, and practical problem-solving when managing daily responsibilities away from home.

Nevertheless, inadequate preparation can quickly turn an exciting opportunity into a stressful experience. Without clear written terms regarding working hours, duties, and time off, young workers risk misunderstanding or exploitation. Similarly, moving to a foreign city without emergency money or local support contacts can leave someone vulnerable if conflicts arise.

Overall, working abroad is highly worthwhile for young people, provided they approach it responsibly. Combining curiosity with clear agreements, realistic expectations, and financial safeguards ensures the experience remains both safe and rewarding.

passages.tts_script_tr:
"Au Pair" Olmak: Bazı Gerçekler.

Ev işlerine yardım karşılığında tam pansiyon konaklama ve cep harçlığı alarak "au pair" olarak çalışma fikri, Britanya dışındaki ülkelerden gelen binlerce genç kız tarafından memnuniyetle karşılanmıştır. Birçoğu okulda öğrendikleri İngilizceyi pratik yapmak ister, ancak en azından temel yaşam ihtiyaçlarını karşılayacak bir işleri olmadan evden uzakta yaşamayı maddi olarak karşılayamazlar.

Dili pratik yapma amacı, bazı kızlarda evden uzakta olmanın özgürlüğünün ve Londra gibi büyük bir şehirde yaşamanın heyecanının tadını çıkarma arzusundan daha zayıf olabilir. Geçimlerini sağlamak için ciddi bir şekilde çalışma fikri onlara cazip gelmeyebilir. Birçok işverenin evine ikinci bir "au pair" alma konusunda tereddüt etmesine neden olan şey; gecenin her saatinde eve dönen ya da hiç dönmeyen, kendisinden bir şey yapması istendiğinde sürekli şikâyet eden, en basit işi bile düzgün yapacağına güvenilemeyen, derslerini ihmal eden ve türlü belalara bulaşan bu tür kızlarla yaşanan deneyimlerdir.

Ancak kusurlar tamamen tek taraflı değildir ve pek çok "au pair" kızın da şikâyet etmek için haklı nedenleri vardır; hatta bazıları bunun sonucunda bunalıma girip mutsuz olmaktadır. Ne yazık ki başka bir ülkede kendi geçimini sağlama fikrine kapılan kızların pek azı, kendilerini bekleyebilecek çeşitli zorluklara karşı hazırlıklıdır.

Bu tür bir görevi kabul eden her kızın en az on sekiz yaşında olması, sağduyulu, pratik ve kendi başının çaresine bakabilecek durumda olması şarttır. Mümkün olan her durumda, tercihen daha önce onlarla çalışmış bir arkadaşından hakkında bir şeyler bildiği bir ailenin yanına gitmelidir. Her halükârda, işvereninden çalışma şartlarını açıkça belirten bir mektup aldığından emin olmalıdır: kendisinden tam olarak ne beklendiği, çocuklara bakmak mı yoksa hafif ev işlerine yardım etmek mi olduğu, her hafta kaç saat çalışmasının beklendiği ve dil kurslarına katılmak için boş günleri ile yarım gün izinleri. Kendisine tatmin edici standartlarda tek kişilik bir oda sözü verilmelidir ve aileyle birlikte dili pratik etme fırsatı bulmak için yemeklerini onlarla yemek isteyecektir. Kazancı yüksek olmayacaktır, ancak kız tüm süre boyunca aynı aileyle kalmaya hazırsa işvereni muhtemelen dönüş seyahat masraflarını karşılayacaktır.

Diğer iki tavsiye de önemlidir. Bir kız, acilen dönmesi gerekmesi halinde eve dönüş yolculuğunu ödeyebilecek yeterli değerde seyahat çeklerini yanında bulundurmalıdır. Ayrıca, sorun çıkması durumunda yardım ve tavsiye verebilecek bir veya iki kuruluşun adresini bilmelidir. Londra'da ve diğer büyük merkezlerde bu kuruluşlardan birkaç tane bulunmaktadır.

passages.passage_text:
Hardly a week goes by without some advance in technology that would have seemed incredible 50 years ago. Over the past 20 years, computers have completely revolutionized our lives. Yet, we can expect the rate of change to accelerate rather than slow down within our lifetimes. The next 25 years will see as many changes as have been witnessed in the past 150.

These developments in technology are bound to have a dramatic effect on the future of work. By 2010, new technology will have revolutionized communications. People will be transmitting messages down telephone lines that previously would have been sent by post. A postal system which has essentially been the same since the Pharaohs will virtually disappear overnight. Once these changes are introduced, not only postmen but also clerks and secretaries will vanish in a paper-free society. All the routine tasks they perform will be carried on a tiny silicon chip. As soon as this technology is available, these people will be as obsolete as the horse and cart after the invention of the motor car. One change will make thousands, if not millions, redundant.

Even people in traditional professions, where expert knowledge has been the key, are unlikely to escape the effects of new technology. Instead of going to a solicitor, you might go to a computer which is programmed with all the most up-to-date legal information. Indeed, you might even come up before a computer judge who would, in all probability, judge your case more fairly than a human counterpart. Doctors, too, will find that an electronic competitor will be able to carry out a much quicker and more accurate diagnosis and recommend more efficient courses of treatment.

In education, teachers will be replaced by teaching machines far more knowledgeable than any human being. What's more, most learning will take place in the home via video conferencing. Children will still go to school though, until another place is created where they can make friends and develop social skills through play.

What, you may ask, can we do to avoid the threat of the dole queue? Is there any job that will be safe? First of all, we shouldn't hide our heads in the sand. Unions will try to stop change, but they will be fighting a losing battle. People should get computer literate as this just might save them from professional extinction. After all, there will be a few jobs left in law, education and medicine for those few individuals who are capable of writing and programming the software of the future. Strangely enough, there will still be jobs like rubbish collection and cleaning as it is tough to programme tasks which are largely unpredictable.

If we accept that people have the need to work, then an option might well be to introduce compulsory job sharing and to limit the length of the working week. Otherwise, we could find ourselves in an explosive situation where a technocratic elite is both supporting, and threatened by, vast numbers of unemployed. Whether the future is one of mass unemployment or greater freedom and leisure will depend on how change is managed over this difficult period and how the relationship between work and reward is viewed.

The Menace of the Micro.

Hardly a week goes by without some advance in technology that would have seemed incredible 50 years ago. Over the past 20 years, computers have completely revolutionized our lives. Yet, we can expect the rate of change to accelerate rather than slow down within our lifetimes. The next 25 years will see as many changes as have been witnessed in the past 150.

These developments in technology are bound to have a dramatic effect on the future of work. By 2010, new technology will have revolutionized communications. People will be transmitting messages down telephone lines that previously would have been sent by post. A postal system which has essentially been the same since the Pharaohs will virtually disappear overnight. Once these changes are introduced, not only postmen but also clerks and secretaries will vanish in a paper-free society. All the routine tasks they perform will be carried on a tiny silicon chip. As soon as this technology is available, these people will be as obsolete as the horse and cart after the invention of the motor car. One change will make thousands, if not millions, redundant.

Even people in traditional professions, where expert knowledge has been the key, are unlikely to escape the effects of new technology. Instead of going to a solicitor, you might go to a computer which is programmed with all the most up-to-date legal information. Indeed, you might even come up before a computer judge who would, in all probability, judge your case more fairly than a human counterpart. Doctors, too, will find that an electronic competitor will be able to carry out a much quicker and more accurate diagnosis and recommend more efficient courses of treatment.

In education, teachers will be replaced by teaching machines far more knowledgeable than any human being. What's more, most learning will take place in the home via video conferencing. Children will still go to school though, until another place is created where they can make friends and develop social skills through play.

What, you may ask, can we do to avoid the threat of the dole queue, meaning money given to the unemployed by the government? Is there any job that will be safe? First of all, we shouldn't hide our heads in the sand. Unions will try to stop change, but they will be fighting a losing battle. People should get computer literate as this just might save them from professional extinction. After all, there will be a few jobs left in law, education and medicine for those few individuals who are capable of writing and programming the software of the future. Strangely enough, there will still be jobs like rubbish collection and cleaning as it is tough to programme tasks which are largely unpredictable.

If we accept that people have the need to work, then an option might well be to introduce compulsory job sharing and to limit the length of the working week. Otherwise, we could find ourselves in an explosive situation where a technocratic elite is both supporting, and threatened by, vast numbers of unemployed. Whether the future is one of mass unemployment or greater freedom and leisure will depend on how change is managed over this difficult period and how the relationship between work and reward is viewed.

Routine office and postal roles will soon become obsolete as electronic communication and silicon chips replace paper-based tasks. Even traditional experts such as lawyers, doctors, and teachers face competition from intelligent software, computer judges, and teaching machines, although schools may remain important for children's social development. task2.model_answer:
Automation and artificial intelligence are transforming modern workplaces faster than ever before. While many people fear that machines will cause widespread unemployment, I believe technology will create greater freedom if societies adapt their education systems and labor policies responsibly.

First, governments and schools should prioritize digital skills and lifelong learning. Just as the author notes that computer literacy protects workers from redundancy, today's workforce needs continuous training in data analysis, software design, and complex problem-solving. When routine tasks are handled by computers, people can focus on creative, empathetic, and strategic roles that machines cannot easily replicate.

Second, economic policies must evolve alongside productivity gains. If automation allows companies to produce more in less time, reducing the standard working week or encouraging job sharing can distribute both work and wealth more fairly. Without such reforms, inequality between a small technical elite and displaced workers could grow dangerously wide.

In conclusion, technological progress does not automatically lead to mass unemployment. With proactive education and fairer labor policies, automation can reduce tedious labor and give people more leisure time.

Mikroçipin Tehdidi.

50 yıl önce inanılmaz görünecek bir teknolojik gelişme olmadan neredeyse tek bir hafta bile geçmiyor. Son 20 yılda bilgisayarlar hayatlarımızda tamamen devrim yarattı. Yine de yaşam sürelerimiz içinde değişim hızının yavaşlamak yerine daha da artmasını bekleyebiliriz. Önümüzdeki 25 yıl, son 150 yılda tanık olunanlar kadar çok değişime sahne olacak.

Teknolojideki bu gelişmelerin iş hayatının geleceği üzerinde çarpıcı bir etkisi olması kaçınılmazdır. 2010 yılına gelindiğinde, yeni teknoloji iletişimde devrim yaratmış olacak. İnsanlar, daha önce postayla gönderilecek olan mesajları telefon hatları üzerinden iletiyor olacaklar. Firavunlar döneminden beri özünde aynı kalan posta sistemi neredeyse bir gecede ortadan kalkacak. Bu değişiklikler uygulamaya konulduğunda, kâğıtsız bir toplumda yalnızca postacılar değil, memurlar ve sekreterler de ortadan kaybolacak. Onların yaptığı tüm rutin işler küçücük bir silikon çip üzerinde yürütülecek. Bu teknoloji kullanıma sunulur sunulmaz, bu insanlar da motorlu taşıtın icadından sonraki at arabası kadar modası geçmiş hâle gelecek. Tek bir değişiklik, milyonlarca olmasa bile binlerce kişiyi işsiz bırakacak.

Uzmanlık bilgisinin temel belirleyici olduğu geleneksel mesleklerdeki insanların bile yeni teknolojinin etkilerinden kaçabilmesi pek olası değildir. Bir avukata gitmek yerine, en güncel hukuk bilgilerinin tümüyle programlanmış bir bilgisayara gidebilirsiniz. Hatta büyük olasılıkla davanızı insan bir meslektaşından daha adil bir şekilde yargılayacak bir bilgisayar yargıcın karşısına bile çıkabilirsiniz. Doktorlar da elektronik bir rakibin çok daha hızlı ve daha doğru bir teşhis koyabildiğini ve daha etkili tedavi yöntemleri önerebildiğini göreceklerdir.

Eğitimde, öğretmenlerin yerini herhangi bir insandan çok daha bilgili olan öğretim makineleri alacak. Dahası, öğrenmenin büyük kısmı video konferans yoluyla evde gerçekleşecek. Yine de çocuklar, oyun yoluyla arkadaş edinebilecekleri ve sosyal beceriler geliştirebilecekleri başka bir yer oluşturulana kadar okula gitmeye devam edecekler.

Devlet tarafından işsizlere verilen para anlamına gelen işsizlik maaşı kuyruğu tehdidinden kaçınmak için ne yapabiliriz diye sorabilirsiniz. Güvende olacak herhangi bir iş var mı? Her şeyden önce, başımızı kuma gömmemeliyiz. Sendikalar değişimi durdurmaya çalışacak, ancak kaybedecekleri bir savaş veriyor olacaklar. İnsanlar bilgisayar okuryazarı olmalı, çünkü bu onları mesleki olarak yok olmaktan kurtarabilir. Ne de olsa hukuk, eğitim ve tıp alanlarında, geleceğin yazılımını yazabilen ve programlayabilen o az sayıdaki kişi için birkaç iş kalacaktır. Tuhaf bir şekilde, büyük ölçüde öngörülemez olan görevleri programlamak zor olduğundan çöp toplama ve temizlik gibi işler hâlâ var olmaya devam edecektir.

İnsanların çalışma ihtiyacı olduğunu kabul edersek, o hâlde zorunlu iş paylaşımını getirmek ve çalışma haftasının süresini sınırlamak pekâlâ bir seçenek olabilir. Aksi takdirde, kendimizi teknokratik bir seçkin sınıfın çok sayıdaki işsizi hem geçindirdiği hem de onlar tarafından tehdit edildiği, patlamaya hazır bir durumun içinde bulabiliriz. Geleceğin kitlesel bir işsizlik mi yoksa daha fazla özgürlük ve boş zaman dönemi mi olacağı, bu zorlu süreçte değişimin nasıl yönetildiğine ve iş ile ödül arasındaki ilişkinin nasıl görüldüğüne bağlı olacaktır.

passages.passage_text:
In recent years, computer programmers have tried to make it easy for people to use computer systems. Unfortunately, in some situations the systems are too easy to use; they don't have enough restrictions to safeguard secret information or to prevent an unauthorized person from using that information. Therefore, several methods have been devised to prevent computer crime. One of them is data encryption.

When secret personal and financial data is transmitted to and from remote terminals, it must be encrypted (translated into a secret code) at one end and decrypted (translated back into plain text) at the other. Since it is impractical to keep secret the algorithms that are used to encrypt and decrypt data, these algorithms are designed so that their operation depends on a certain data item called the key. It is the key that is kept secret. Even if you know all the details of the encrypting and decrypting algorithms, you cannot decrypt any messages unless you know the key that was used when they were encrypted. For instance, the National Bureau of Standards has adopted an algorithm for encrypting and decrypting the data processed by federal agencies. The details of the algorithm have been published in the Federal Register. Plans are under way to incorporate the algorithm in special purpose microprocessors, which anyone can purchase and install in his computer. So the algorithm is available to anyone who bothers to buy one of the special purpose microprocessors. But the operation of the algorithm is governed by a sixty-four-bit key. Since there are a vast number of possible sixty-four-bit keys, no one is likely to discover the correct one by chance. And, without the correct key, knowing the algorithm is useless.

task1.model_answer: The passage explains why data encryption is essential for preventing computer crime when systems lack strict access controls. Because sensitive personal and financial information travels between remote terminals, it must be converted into secret code before transmission and restored to plain text upon arrival. Rather than hiding the mathematical algorithms—which is impractical—modern encryption relies on a secret item called a key. Even when an algorithm is publicly available, such as the federal standard published by the National Bureau of Standards and built into commercial microprocessors, unauthorized users cannot read the data without the specific key. With a vast number of possible sixty-four-bit keys, guessing the right one by chance is virtually impossible.

task2.model_answer:
In today's digital world, software designers face a constant challenge: systems must be simple enough for everyday users yet secure enough to protect private information. In my view, strong security should always come before convenience, especially when personal and financial data are involved.

Making systems effortless to access can create dangerous weaknesses. As the passage points out, when restrictions are too weak, unauthorized individuals can easily exploit sensitive information. For example, banking apps or hospital databases that skip multi-step verification may save users a few seconds, but a single breach can cause severe financial loss or identity theft.

At the same time, good design can keep security manageable. Automated encryption, biometric locks, and password managers allow people to stay safe without needing deep technical knowledge. Users may accept slightly longer sign-in steps once they understand the risks of weak protection.

In short, convenience should never excuse poor security. Protecting sensitive data must remain the top priority in computer system design.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Veri Şifreleme.

Son yıllarda bilgisayar programcıları, insanların bilgisayar sistemlerini kullanmasını kolaylaştırmaya çalıştı. Ne yazık ki bazı durumlarda sistemlerin kullanımı fazlasıyla kolay; gizli bilgileri korumak veya yetkisiz bir kişinin bu bilgileri kullanmasını önlemek için yeterli kısıtlamalara sahip değiller. Bu nedenle, bilgisayar suçlarını önlemek için çeşitli yöntemler geliştirilmiştir. Bunlardan biri de veri şifrelemedir.

Gizli kişisel ve finansal veriler uzak terminallere gönderilirken veya oralardan alınırken, bir uçta şifrelenmeli, yani gizli bir koda çevrilmeli, diğer uçta ise şifresi çözülmeli, yani tekrar düz metne dönüştürülmelidir. Verileri şifrelemek ve şifresini çözmek için kullanılan algoritmaları gizli tutmak pratik olmadığından, bu algoritmalar çalışmaları anahtar adı verilen belirli bir veri öğesine bağlı olacak şekilde tasarlanır. Gizli tutulan şey anahtardır. Şifreleme ve şifre çözme algoritmalarının tüm ayrıntılarını bilseniz bile, mesajlar şifrelenirken kullanılan anahtarı bilmediğiniz sürece hiçbir mesajın şifresini çözemezsiniz. Örneğin, Ulusal Standartlar Bürosu, federal kurumlar tarafından işlenen verileri şifrelemek ve şifresini çözmek için bir algoritma benimsemiştir. Algoritmanın ayrıntıları Federal Sicil'de yayımlanmıştır. Algoritmayı herkesin satın alıp bilgisayarına takabileceği özel amaçlı mikroişlemcilere yerleştirme planları sürmektedir. Dolayısıyla algoritma, bu özel amaçlı mikroişlemcilerden birini satın alma zahmetine giren herkesin erişimine açıktır. Ancak algoritmanın çalışması altmış dört bitlik bir anahtar tarafından yönetilir. Olası altmış dört bitlik anahtarların sayısı çok fazla olduğundan, hiç kimsenin doğru anahtarı tesadüfen bulması olası değildir. Ve doğru anahtar olmadan, algoritmayı bilmek hiçbir işe yaramaz.

passages.passage_text:
"Mr. Watson, come here, please; I want you."

With these commonplace words a new era was ushered in. That sentence marked the achievement of a man who changed the face of the world in his lifetime. For the speaker was Alexander Graham Bell, and the sentence was the first to be spoken and received over the telephone.

Although telegrams had been in use for some time and the equipment was in some ways similar, the Morse code being tapped out on the same telegraph wires, it was not sophisticated enough to pick up speech. No other invention has surpassed the usefulness of the telephone.

Alexander Bell was born on March 3, 1847 in Edinburgh. His genius was inherited from his father, who was a famous teacher of elocution, and an expert on phonetics. Even as a boy his mind was inventive, but in 1870 Bell's health began to fail and there were fears of tuberculosis. So, he left his native country with his father and went to Canada. Two years later he was in Boston, where he set up a school for training teachers of the deaf and he also gave instruction in the mechanics of speech. Here he started experimenting on a machine which he believed would make the deaf 'hear'. While he was doing this, he accidentally came across the clue for the correct principles of telephony. "If," he said, "a current of electricity could be made to vary in intensity precisely as the air varies in density during the production of sound, I should be able to transmit speech telegraphically." So, he turned to studying the workings of a deaf man's ear, and the movement of air while a sound is produced.

By February 15, 1876, Bell had filed an application for a patent for his 'improvement in telegraphy' at the United States Patent Office. Only two hours later, Elisha Gray of Chicago filed an application for almost the same invention! The great Edison, A.E. Dolbear and Daniel Drawbraugh were all working in the same field: all claimed the invention or part of the invention of the telephone. The great telephone war was on! There was hardly any time to spare.

Bell and his assistant, Watson, hid themselves in two rooms of a cheap Boston boarding house, rigged up apparatus and worked day and night trying to transmit and receive sentences spoken by the human voice over the telephone. On the afternoon of March 10, 1876, Watson was in the basement with the receiver to his ear. Suddenly he started. Words - real distinguishable words - had come through at last. Sharply and clearly the sentence came through, "Mr. Watson, come here, please; I want you." Watson flung down the receiver, rushed up the stairs like a schoolboy, clearing them two at a time, and burst into Bell's room.

task1.model_answer: Alexander Graham Bell, born in Edinburgh in 1847, inherited a strong interest in speech and phonetics from his father. After moving to Canada for his health and later opening a school for teachers of the deaf in Boston, Bell experimented with devices to help deaf people hear. This work led him to discover how electrical currents could vary like sound waves to transmit speech. Facing fierce competition from rival inventors such as Elisha Gray, who filed a nearly identical patent application just two hours after Bell in February 1876, Bell and his assistant Watson worked tirelessly in a Boston boarding house. task2.model_answer:
Major technological breakthroughs rarely appear in isolation; instead, they often emerge from intense competition among ambitious minds. As the story of the telephone illustrates, several inventors were racing toward the same goal in the 1870s, and that rivalry pushed Alexander Graham Bell and his assistant to work relentlessly.

Competition in science and technology brings clear benefits. First, rivalry creates urgency, encouraging researchers to test ideas quickly and turn theory into working devices. Without the pressure of competing patent claims, Bell might have taken far longer to achieve his breakthrough. Second, multiple inventors approaching a problem from different angles increase the chances of solving technical obstacles.

At the same time, fierce competition can have drawbacks. Secretiveness and patent battles may delay collaboration or lead to costly legal disputes rather than open knowledge sharing. Nevertheless, when balanced with fair patent laws, healthy rivalry remains a powerful driver of progress, continuously delivering tools that transform everyday communication.

Alexander Bell, 3 Mart 1847'de Edinburgh'da doğdu. Dehası, ünlü bir güzel konuşma öğretmeni ve ses bilgisi uzmanı olan babasından miras kalmıştı. Burada, işitme engellilerin duymasını sağlayacağına inandığı bir makine üzerinde deneyler yapmaya başladı. Bunu yaparken, tesadüfen telefon teknolojisinin doğru ilkelerine giden ipucuna rastladı. Böylece işitme engelli bir insanın kulağının işleyişini ve bir ses üretilirken havanın hareketini incelemeye yöneldi.

Kaybedecek neredeyse hiç zaman yoktu.

Bell ve asistanı Watson, Boston'daki ucuz bir pansiyonun iki odasına kapandılar, düzenekleri kurdular ve insan sesiyle söylenen cümleleri telefon üzerinden iletip almaya çalışarak gece gündüz çalıştılar. 10 Mart 1876 öğleden sonra Watson, alıcı kulağında olacak şekilde bodrumdaydı. passages.title: Teenage Vandalism
passages.passage_text:
The image of the teenage vandal as an isolated, lonely, anti-social figure has been shattered by a school survey which shows that most hooligans are regular attenders at youth clubs and enjoy going to an organised disco. The profile of a typical vandal built up by teachers and police in Blyth, Northumberland, paints a picture of a sociable youth who is likely to be an enthusiastic cyclist and a football fan.

Nearly two-thirds of 2,500 children who answered a questionnaire in Northumberland secondary schools admitted acts of vandalism. Most blamed unemployment and also their parents for not being strict enough. Many said they would commit vandalism again.

In a preliminary analysis of 1,600 anonymous replies, Northumbria police and the Keep Britain Tidy Group — who commissioned the survey — found that 84 per cent of the teenagers thought there was little or nothing wrong with dropping litter. Almost two-thirds felt the same about damaging garden plants, 40 per cent saw "little or nothing wrong" with torturing a pet and 6 per cent felt that there was little or nothing wrong with setting fire to a building.

Most children said the answer to vandalism was to give children more to do, while some thought inflicting punishments of all kinds and having more police on the streets could be the answer. About half said they were most likely to listen to their parents, but only eight per cent said they would listen to a youth club leader.

task1.title: Survey Summary
task1.prompt: Summarize the main misconceptions about teenage vandals and the key findings of the Northumberland survey in your own words.
task1.model_answer: Contrary to the common stereotype that teenage vandals are lonely, anti-social misfits, a survey in Northumberland revealed that typical offenders are sociable youths who regularly attend youth clubs, go to discos, and enjoy sports. Among 2,500 secondary school students surveyed, nearly two-thirds admitted to vandalism, blaming unemployment and lenient parenting. An analysis of 1,600 responses showed that while 84% saw little harm in littering, tolerance dropped sharply to 40% for harming pets and just 6% for arson. Rather than stricter policing alone, most students felt providing more activities for young people and stronger parental guidance—since half would listen to parents versus only 8% to youth leaders—would best curb vandalism.

task2.title: Preventing Youth Vandalism
task2.prompt: In your opinion, is providing more recreational activities or enforcing stricter punishments more effective in reducing teenage vandalism? Support your view with reasons.
task2.model_answer:
Reducing teenage vandalism requires addressing its root causes rather than relying solely on punitive measures. While stricter policing and legal penalties may deter occasional offenders in the short term, the Northumberland survey highlights that even socially active teenagers engage in destructive behaviour when they lack constructive outlets or clear boundaries at home.

Providing accessible recreational activities, such as sports leagues, creative workshops, and community projects, offers young people meaningful ways to channel their energy and build a sense of pride in their neighbourhood. When teenagers feel invested in local spaces, they are far less likely to damage them. At the same time, activities alone are insufficient without consistent parental involvement. Because roughly half of the students surveyed stated they listen to their parents, families must play an active role in teaching responsibility and setting firm expectations.

In conclusion, combining constructive youth programmes with supportive yet consistent parental guidance is far more effective than punishment alone.

passages.passage_text:
Once you realise that no method of language teaching is going to give you the ability to speak a foreign tongue to business standards in a few weeks, the selection of a system of teaching becomes a simple calculation of time, money and need.

There are three levels of language ability - tourist, social and fluent - and the gaps between them are huge. Most of us are aware that the schoolboy German that gets us into hotels and through supermarkets is not sufficient to keep up a pleasant dinner party conversation. Similarly, the ability to join in such a conversation, which is about as much as most of us could hope to achieve, is a long way from a full intelligent grasp of the language and its culture.

For a quick introduction to the basics, I prefer the cassette/book system. Language books alone cannot offer the necessary pronunciation skills, skills which you are going to need in order to understand, for example, the train announcements on the Moscow underground. Cassettes, however, have proved a great aid for the language student.

The essential requirement when learning a language, even at that level, remains effort. The more willingness the student brings to the task, the easier the course will be. For European languages that effort comes a little easier. The Londoner learning French or the Parisian learning English can readily find newspapers, radio stations and restaurants where the language is used and can thus become familiar with that culture before his visit. If the tongue is to be Tamil or Serbo-Croat, the task is a little more difficult. With languages such as French and German, it is also possible to listen to, or record, the BBC Schools programmes, which are always helpful.

There is no question, however, that the best teaching, and obviously the most expensive, is in the classroom, the very best being a one-to-one teaching basis, that is, private tutoring. For this, you will be paying a few hundred pounds per week and it is important to check carefully on the chosen place of learning. Language teaching attracts some dishonest establishments. Watch out for the school that promises an ability to 'reach the moon' after a couple of hours in the language lab!

task2.model_answer:
Choosing between self-study tools and private tutoring depends largely on a learner's budget, goals, and self-discipline. Both approaches offer clear advantages, yet neither guarantees success without consistent personal effort.

Self-study materials, such as audio courses, books, and online media, are affordable and flexible. They allow learners to practice pronunciation, listen to native speakers, and study at their own pace. For someone aiming for basic tourist communication, self-study is often practical and sufficient. However, learners who lack motivation may struggle without regular guidance or feedback on their mistakes.

By contrast, private tutoring provides personalized instruction tailored to an individual's weaknesses and goals. Direct interaction with a skilled teacher accelerates speaking confidence and helps students reach social or fluent standards more reliably, even though it is costly. Ultimately, the most effective strategy combines the structure of professional instruction with daily independent practice and genuine willingness to learn.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Dil Öğrenimi.

Hiçbir dil öğretim yönteminin size birkaç hafta içinde iş dünyası standartlarında yabancı bir dil konuşma becerisi kazandırmayacağını fark ettiğinizde, bir öğretim sistemi seçimi zaman, para ve ihtiyaçla ilgili basit bir hesaba dönüşür.

Dil becerisinin üç düzeyi vardır: turist düzeyi, sosyal düzey ve akıcı düzey; ve bunlar arasındaki uçurumlar çok büyüktür. Çoğumuz otellere girmemizi ve süpermarketlerde işimizi halletmemizi sağlayan okul düzeyindeki Almancanın keyifli bir akşam yemeği sohbetini sürdürmek için yeterli olmadığının farkındayız. Benzer şekilde, çoğumuzun ulaşmayı umabileceği en iyi düzey olan böyle bir sohbete katılabilme becerisi de dili ve kültürünü tam ve derinlemesine kavramaktan çok uzaktır.

Temellere hızlı bir giriş yapmak için ben kaset ve kitap sistemini tercih ederim. Dil kitapları tek başına gerekli telaffuz becerilerini kazandıramaz; oysa bu becerilere, örneğin Moskova metrosundaki tren anonslarını anlamak için ihtiyacınız olacaktır. Ancak kasetlerin dil öğrencileri için harika bir yardımcı olduğu kanıtlanmıştır.

Bir dil öğrenirken, o düzeyde bile, temel gereksinim çaba olmaya devam eder. Öğrenci bu işe ne kadar istekli yaklaşırsa, kurs da o kadar kolay geçecektir. Avrupa dilleri için bu çaba biraz daha kolay gelir. Fransızca öğrenen bir Londralı ya da İngilizce öğrenen bir Parisli, o dilin kullanıldığı gazeteleri, radyo istasyonlarını ve restoranları kolayca bulabilir ve böylece ziyaretinden önce o kültüre aşina olabilir. Öğrenilecek dil Tamilce veya Sırp-Hırvatça olacaksa, iş biraz daha zordur. Fransızca ve Almanca gibi dillerde her zaman faydalı olan BBC Okul programlarını dinlemek veya kaydetmek de mümkündür.

Ancak en iyi ve doğal olarak en pahalı eğitimin sınıfta verildiği tartışmasızdır; en iyisi ise bire bir öğretim, yani özel derstir. Bunun için haftada birkaç yüz sterlin ödersiniz ve seçilen eğitim kurumunu dikkatlice araştırmanız önemlidir. Dil öğretimi alanı bazı dürüst olmayan kurumları kendine çeker. Dil laboratuvarında birkaç saat geçirdikten sonra size "aya ulaşma" becerisi vaat eden okullara karşı dikkatli olun!

passages.passage_text:
These two letters appeared in a radio and TV magazine.

Sir,
Last Saturday I watched the TV programme on the latest Grand Prix motor race and noticed how much advertising there was. In particular, the leading car (and the one that eventually won) was almost constantly on the screen: it was painted to look like a packet of well-known cigarettes. Not only that, but the car was, on more than one occasion, referred to by the reporter not by the name of the driver or the motor company, but by the name of the product.

Since the football team that I support is not allowed to wear shirts advertising anything when their matches are being televised, isn't this a case of 'double standards'? The rule preventing sportsmen and sportswomen from carrying advertisements on television is a good one. Keep it and enforce it. To take one example, what is the effect, I wonder, on the young and old, of the apparent connection between cigarette smoking and an exciting sport like motor-racing?

L. H. Gray

Sir,
What a ridiculous situation our television companies find themselves in with regard to sports and advertising! I watched a televised football match in which the players did not carry any advertisements on their shirts, and yet there was advertising all around. (Do the TV producers think we viewers are blind or something?) And when a well-known international player was interviewed after the match, both he and the interviewer referred by name to the cosmetics firm that finances the team! And as if that were not enough, the sports item that followed was the National Bank Golf Tournament.

Advertising is all around us every day. Long live advertising, I say, and let the television companies recognise it and allow football players, athletes, racing drivers and others to wear sponsors' advertisements. At least we would all know where we were!

(Mrs.) R. P. Laing, Bristol

task2.model_answer:
Whether commercial advertising should be allowed in televised sports is a complex issue with valid arguments on both sides. On the one hand, major sporting events and local clubs rely heavily on corporate sponsorship to cover high operating costs, maintain stadiums, and develop young talent. As Mrs. Laing points out, advertising is already visible on pitch-side boards and in tournament names, so banning logos on players' shirts can seem artificial and inconsistent.

On the other hand, unrestricted sponsorship can harm public health and sports integrity. Allowing tobacco, alcohol, or gambling brands to link themselves with healthy, exciting activities like football or motor racing sends a misleading message, particularly to young viewers. Therefore, the most sensible solution is not a total ban on all advertising, nor complete deregulation, but clear, consistent guidelines. Broadcasters and sports authorities should permit transparent sponsorship from responsible businesses while strictly prohibiting harmful products such as cigarettes across every televised sport equally.

passages.passage_text:
In its search for alternatives to fossil-fuel energy sources, science is looking back in history at the windmill. Small windmills once were seen everywhere in rural America, but most were abandoned with the emergence of rural electrification programs in the 1930's. Now energy shortages and rising petroleum prices have brought renewed interest in putting the wind to work. Some scientists estimate that with enough investment in research and development, windmills could supply 20 per cent of U.S. electrical needs by the year 2000.

The Sandia Laboratories in New Mexico are testing an altogether different device that looks more like a giant eggbeater than a conventional windmill. Its principal advantage is that its symmetrical shape catches wind from any direction.

All designers of new windmills face one very old problem, however: what to do when the wind dies. One solution would be to use windmills to pump water uphill into storage reservoirs. When the wind stops, the water would be released to drive hydraulic turbines.

Meanwhile, U.S. ranchers and farmers in the southwest are so eager to utilize wind power that New Mexico State University is offering a special course in the operation and maintenance of windmills built a generation ago.

Investing in renewable energy sources such as wind power is one of the smartest decisions a country can make today. In addition to the established energy sources such as gas, coal, oil and nuclear, there are a number of other sources that we ought to consider. Two of these are hydro-electric and tidal power.

These two sources are similar in that they are both renewable. However, hydro-electric power is more widely used than tidal. In fact, a substantial amount of electricity is already produced in HEP stations world-wide, whereas tidal stations are still in the very early stages of development.

As far as geographical location is concerned, HEP schemes are to be found on lakes and rivers, while tidal schemes are constructed only in estuaries where tidal variation is great. Unfortunately, these are few in number. At present HEP stations are found mainly in Norway, Canada, Sweden and Brazil, whereas tidal plants are in operation in France, the CIS and China.

As regards capital outlay, both require very high investment. On the other hand, generating costs are quite low in both cases. In fact, a large-scale HEP plant is capable of producing power more cheaply than conventional sources, such as coal, oil and nuclear plants. Tidal power also compares favourably with nuclear and oil generated electricity, in terms of production costs. Like HEP stations, tidal barrages have a long life-expectancy. It is estimated that they can operate for over 100 years.

With respect to continuity of supply, tidal stations differ from HEP schemes in that they often can only supply power intermittently. HEP stations, however, provide a constant supply of electricity.

Turning now to environmental impact, tidal plants do not seem to create too many problems. In contrast, HEP stations often involve the flooding of large amounts of agricultural land, the destruction of ecological habitats, and may even cause a change in the climate of the area.

Both tidal power and HEP have one big disadvantage in that if the demand for power exists at any distance from the generating plant, transmitting the electricity is expensive.

task2.model_answer:
Choosing between hydro-electric and tidal power requires balancing energy reliability against environmental protection. Hydro-electric power has clear practical advantages because rivers and lakes are widely available and dams can supply steady, continuous electricity to cities and industries. Moreover, large-scale hydro-electric plants produce electricity cheaply once built. However, their environmental cost can be severe: flooding large valleys displaces communities, destroys agricultural land, and harms natural ecosystems.

Tidal power, by contrast, leaves farmland untouched and avoids major ecological damage while offering low operating costs and a lifespan of over a century. Yet its dependence on rare estuaries and its intermittent output make it unsuitable as a country's primary energy source. In my view, nations should prioritize tidal power wherever geographical conditions permit, while developing hydro-electric power only with strict environmental safeguards and pairing both with modern grid storage to reduce transmission and supply limitations.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Hidroelektrik ve Gelgit Enerjisi.

Gaz, kömür, petrol ve nükleer gibi yerleşik enerji kaynaklarına ek olarak, göz önünde bulundurmamız gereken başka kaynaklar da vardır. Bunlardan ikisi hidroelektrik ve gelgit enerjisidir.

Bu iki kaynak, her ikisinin de yenilenebilir olması bakımından benzerdir. Ancak hidroelektrik enerjisi gelgit enerjisinden daha yaygın olarak kullanılmaktadır. Nitekim dünya genelinde hidroelektrik santrallerinde hâlihazırda önemli miktarda elektrik üretilirken, gelgit santralleri hâlâ gelişiminin çok erken aşamalarındadır.

Coğrafi konum söz konusu olduğunda, hidroelektrik tesisleri göl ve nehirlerde bulunurken, gelgit tesisleri yalnızca gelgit farkının büyük olduğu haliçlerde inşa edilir. Ne yazık ki bunların sayısı azdır. Günümüzde hidroelektrik santralleri ağırlıklı olarak Norveç, Kanada, İsveç ve Brezilya'da bulunurken, gelgit santralleri Fransa, BDT ve Çin'de faaliyet göstermektedir.

Sermaye harcaması açısından her ikisi de çok yüksek yatırım gerektirir. Öte yandan, üretim maliyetleri her iki durumda da oldukça düşüktür. Hatta büyük ölçekli bir hidroelektrik santrali; kömür, petrol ve nükleer santraller gibi geleneksel kaynaklardan daha ucuza enerji üretebilmektedir. Gelgit enerjisi de üretim maliyetleri bakımından nükleer ve petrolden üretilen elektrikle kıyaslandığında avantajlı bir konumdadır. task2.model_answer:
Understanding genetics has become one of the most influential achievements in modern science, with major impacts on medicine, agriculture, and daily life. In healthcare, genetic knowledge allows doctors to identify inherited risks early and develop targeted treatments for diseases that were once impossible to explain. In agriculture, scientists can cultivate crops that resist pests or survive harsh weather, helping secure food supplies for growing populations.

However, genetic research also brings important ethical responsibilities. Issues such as genetic privacy, unequal access to expensive therapies, and the modification of human traits require careful public debate and strict regulation. Even so, if used wisely, the principles that began with Mendel's simple pea plant experiments will continue to improve human health and well-being around the world.

passages.passage_text:
Stopping cigarette smoking has become a big problem for all governments. In democratic countries, the economic strength of the tobacco industry is so great that measures taken by governments to protect the rights of nonsmokers cannot be applied effectively. In some undemocratic countries, on the other hand, governments cannot be trusted and they lack the motivation to deal with the problem. And under any political system, social conditioning and chemical habituation make banning tobacco a formidable task and one that would take a long time. Yet, current information campaigns are failing as worldwide use increases faster than the population.

Totally banning cigarette smoking so far has been unsuccessful in all countries. An alternative approach includes either the prohibition of smoking in the workplace and public buildings or the strict limitation of smoking to specified areas. This movement may be the greatest success of the information campaign against tobacco. Its leaders insist that despite the continued sale, advertising, and use of tobacco, nonsmokers have every right not to be exposed to the carcinogens, carbon monoxide, and irritants in tobacco smoke. Such a campaign can have three important effects.

First, by banning the use of tobacco from places where nonsmokers would be exposed, thousands of lives may be saved. Second, forcing smokers to give up their habit while in the presence of nonsmokers will provide them with an added force to quit. If smokers must get through working days without smoking, then they are more likely to be able to quit completely. And third, by stigmatizing tobacco use as dangerous and antisocial, the campaign for nonsmokers' rights can accomplish a goal of all anti-smoking information campaigns: to make smoking socially unattractive.

Interestingly, nonsmokers have important supporters in the workplace: their employers. Companies, at least in the United States, are rapidly realizing that most of their employees do not smoke and do not like to breathe the smoke of others, and that smokers cost employers money. Surveys indicate that inefficiency and ill-health attributable to smoking waste about 7% of a smoker's working time. Smokers also add to insurance and cleanup costs, and lower the morale of nonsmoking employees.

task2.model_answer:
Banning smoking in all enclosed public spaces and workplaces is a justified policy that balances public health with individual freedom. While smokers may argue that restricting where they smoke limits their personal choice, one person's habit should not endanger the health of others. Secondhand smoke contains toxic chemicals and carcinogens that directly harm bystanders who have no choice but to share the same air.

In addition, smoke-free policies create practical benefits for society as a whole. Hospitals face lower rates of smoking-related illnesses, and businesses avoid unnecessary losses in productivity and maintenance costs. Most importantly, when smoking is no longer permitted in restaurants, offices, or public buildings, young people are less likely to view it as normal behavior, and current smokers receive strong encouragement to cut down or quit. Allowing smoking in designated outdoor areas respects personal choice without forcing nonsmokers to sacrifice their health. Therefore, strict smoke-free rules in public places remain an essential public health measure.

Sigara Karşıtı Kampanyalar.

Sigara içmeyi durdurmak tüm hükümetler için büyük bir sorun hâline gelmiştir. Demokratik ülkelerde tütün endüstrisinin ekonomik gücü o kadar büyüktür ki hükümetlerin sigara içmeyenlerin haklarını korumak için aldığı önlemler etkili bir şekilde uygulanamaz. Demokratik olmayan bazı ülkelerde ise hükümetlere güvenilememekte ve bu sorunla başa çıkmak için gerekli motivasyondan yoksun kalmaktadırlar. Üstelik hangi siyasi sistem altında olursa olsun, toplumsal koşullanma ve kimyasal bağımlılık, tütünü yasaklamayı çok zorlu ve uzun zaman alacak bir görev hâline getirmektedir. Yine de dünya genelindeki kullanım nüfustan daha hızlı arttığı için mevcut bilgilendirme kampanyaları başarısız olmaktadır.

Sigara içmeyi tamamen yasaklamak şimdiye kadar tüm ülkelerde başarısız olmuştur. Alternatif bir yaklaşım ise iş yerlerinde ve kamu binalarında sigara içilmesinin yasaklanmasını ya da sigara içmenin yalnızca belirlenmiş alanlarla sıkı bir şekilde sınırlandırılmasını içerir. Bu hareket, tütüne karşı yürütülen bilgilendirme kampanyasının en büyük başarısı olabilir. Hareketin öncüleri; tütün satışının, reklamının ve kullanımının sürmesine rağmen sigara içmeyenlerin tütün dumanındaki kanserojen maddelere, karbonmonoksite ve tahriş edici maddelere maruz kalmama hakkına sonuna kadar sahip olduklarında ısrar etmektedir. Böyle bir kampanyanın üç önemli etkisi olabilir.

İlk olarak, sigara içmeyenlerin dumana maruz kalabileceği yerlerde tütün kullanımını yasaklayarak binlerce hayat kurtarılabilir. İkinci olarak, sigara içenleri sigara içmeyenlerin bulunduğu ortamlarda bu alışkanlıklarından vazgeçmeye zorlamak, onlara sigarayı bırakmaları için ek bir itici güç sağlayacaktır. Sigara içenler iş günlerini sigara içmeden geçirmek zorunda kalırlarsa, tamamen bırakma olasılıkları daha yüksek olur. Üçüncü olarak ise tütün kullanımını tehlikeli ve toplum dışı bir davranış olarak damgalayarak sigara içmeyenlerin hakları için yürütülen kampanya, tüm sigara karşıtı bilgilendirme kampanyalarının ortak hedefini gerçekleştirebilir: sigara içmeyi toplumsal açıdan cazibesiz hâle getirmek.

İlginç bir şekilde, sigara içmeyenlerin iş yerinde önemli destekçileri vardır: işverenleri. En azından Amerika Birleşik Devletleri'ndeki şirketler, çalışanlarının çoğunun sigara içmediğini ve başkalarının dumanını solumaktan hoşlanmadığını, ayrıca sigara içenlerin işverenlere maddi yük getirdiğini hızla fark etmektedir. Araştırmalar, sigara kullanımından kaynaklanan verimsizliğin ve sağlık sorunlarının sigara içen bir çalışanın çalışma süresinin yaklaşık yüzde 7'sini boşa harcadığını göstermektedir. Sigara içenler ayrıca sigorta ve temizlik maliyetlerini artırmakta ve sigara içmeyen çalışanların moralini düşürmektedir.

task2.model_answer:
People frequently assume that newer technology is automatically better than older tools, yet practical experience often proves otherwise. Modern devices tend to prioritize speed and extra features, whereas earlier inventions were frequently built for durability, simplicity, and easy repair. When we mistake novelty for quality, we risk overlooking solutions that are more reliable and sustainable in everyday life.

A clear example can be seen in home appliances and everyday tools. Older mechanical washing machines or manual kitchen gadgets often last for decades and can be fixed with simple replacement parts. By contrast, many modern smart appliances rely on delicate touchscreens and software updates; when a single sensor malfunctions, repairing the device can cost nearly as much as buying a new one. Similarly, paper books require no battery or charger and remain readable for centuries, even though e-readers offer convenience while traveling. Therefore, evaluating technology by its real reliability and usefulness—rather than its release date—helps us make wiser, less wasteful choices.

passages.passage_text:
Cardiologists divide us into two types according to how our personality affects our heart. Type A individuals are highly competitive, fast acting, rapid talking, and thus more exposed to stress whilst B types drown in the milk of human kindness and are indifferent to the passage of time. It is an uncomfortable fact that A types die twice as frequently from heart disease as B types, even when the risks of cigarettes, alcohol and cream cakes are taken into account.

Personality is genetically determined; that is, A-type parents usually get A-type children. But the environment has a more important effect. One place where children soak up A-type behaviour is school, which is, by its very nature, a highly competitive institution. Too many schools adopt the 'Win at all costs' principle and measure their success by sporting achievements. What I can't forgive actually is not the current emphasis on making children compete against their friends or against the clock, but the system in which competitive A types are provided with more opportunity to succeed than their B-type fellows.

By far, the worst form of competition in schools is the disproportionate emphasis on examination. Rather than concentrating on those things they do well, pupils are forced to compete by exams. For those who will inevitably fail, however, this kind of competition is definitely harmful.

Obviously, it is neither practical nor desirable that all A youngsters change into B's. The world needs both types, and schools have an important duty to try to fit a child's personality to his possible future employment. If the preoccupation of schools with academic work was lessened, more time might be spent teaching children better values. Perhaps selection for the caring professions, such as medicine, should be made not only by good grades but also by such considerations as sensitivity, kindness and honesty.

task2.model_answer:
Competition through exams is a central feature of modern education, yet educators continue to debate whether it helps or harms students. Supporters argue that standardized testing sets clear benchmarks, motivates hard work, and prepares young people for competitive universities and workplaces. Without objective exams, evaluating large numbers of applicants fairly would be much harder.

However, excessive exam pressure carries serious drawbacks. As the passage points out, constant comparison rewards fast, competitive learners while demoralizing students whose talents lie outside test-taking. Over time, an obsession with grades can increase chronic stress and crowd out essential qualities like creativity, collaboration, and empathy.

In my view, schools should reduce their reliance on high-stakes examinations rather than abandon assessment altogether. Combining project work, practical skills, and character evaluation with traditional tests would give every student a fair chance to thrive. Education should prepare young people not only to pass exams, but also to lead healthy, meaningful lives.

Kardiyologlar, kişiliğimizin kalbimizi nasıl etkilediğine göre bizi iki tipe ayırır. Kişilik genetik olarak belirlenir; yani A tipi ebeveynlerin genellikle A tipi çocukları olur. Ancak çevrenin daha önemli bir etkisi vardır. Okullardaki açık ara en kötü rekabet biçimi, sınavlara verilen orantısız önemdir. Öğrenciler iyi yaptıkları şeylere odaklanmak yerine sınavlarla yarışmaya zorlanmaktadır. Ancak kaçınılmaz olarak başarısız olacaklar için bu tür bir rekabet kesinlikle zararlıdır.

Dünyanın her iki tipe de ihtiyacı vardır ve okulların, bir çocuğun kişiliğini gelecekteki olası mesleğine uydurmaya çalışmak gibi önemli bir görevi bulunmaktadır. passages.passage_text:
On any weekend at sunrise, while most of the country still sleeps, vans, pickup trucks, campers, and cars crammed with every conceivable item gather in empty parking lots and fairgrounds across the U.S. By noon, the scene overflows with thousands of people who have come to bargain and look around this mad carnival called the flea market.

People have traded and bartered for centuries. Whatever else the flea market may appear to be, its purpose is the sale and exchange of goods. Whether they are knowledgeable collectors or just plain bargain hunters, people are drawn to the flea market by the enormous amount and variety of merchandise offered. The possibility of finding something truly valuable before anybody else does makes shopping at a flea market a treasure hunt.

For many buyers, the ritual of bargaining at a flea market is more fun than the bargain itself. It's not the money they save that gives them a feeling of accomplishment; it's the satisfaction of playing an ancient game.

Satisfaction also comes from the nature of a flea-market exchange. After you negotiate your price, taking your time, it is 'cash and carry' - the dealer pockets your money, you go home with your purchase, and that's that. You got what you wanted, and the dealer got what he or she wanted. In today's world of credit cards, the flea market takes you back to a time when life was simpler and money had more meaning.

The people who set up stalls at the flea market, vendors, may have nothing in common during their weekday lives, but over the weekend their diversity becomes community. A Chinese couple sells embroidered slippers next to a punk teenager displaying cat's-eye sunglasses across from another dealer's plastic potted plants. On the street, they would probably never talk to each other. Here they do.

What do these 'fleas' have in common here? Perhaps it is a belief in getting ahead, in becoming economically self-sufficient, and in taking control of their own lives. Vendors willingly give up the security of a nine-to-five job in exchange for freedom: freedom from rigid working hours; freedom from the world of inflation and taxation; freedom to choose when, where, and what they will sell; freedom to be what they want to be.

task2.model_answer:
Choosing between a conventional nine-to-five job and self-employment often comes down to whether a person values security or autonomy more. Traditional employment offers a predictable salary, paid leave, and clear working hours, which makes financial planning far less stressful. For people supporting families or paying off loans, that stability is a major advantage.

On the other hand, working independently, whether running a flea-market stall or launching a small business, provides unmatched control over one's schedule and goals. Self-employed individuals decide how hard to work, what to sell, and how to adapt to customers, and they gain direct pride from every success. Even though their income may fluctuate, the sense of ownership can make daily work far more rewarding.

Personally, I believe a balanced approach works best: starting in a stable job to build skills and savings, and then moving toward self-employment once one has a safety net. That way, a person can enjoy greater freedom without facing unnecessary financial risk.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Bitpazarı.

Herhangi bir hafta sonu gün doğumunda, ülkenin büyük bölümü hâlâ uyurken, akla gelebilecek her türlü eşyayla tıka basa dolu minibüsler, kamyonetler, karavanlar ve otomobiller Amerika Birleşik Devletleri genelindeki boş otoparklarda ve panayır alanlarında toplanır. Öğlene doğru ortalık, bitpazarı adı verilen bu çılgın karnavalda pazarlık yapmaya ve etrafa bakınmaya gelen binlerce insanla dolup taşar.

İnsanlar yüzyıllardır ticaret ve takas yapmaktadır. Bitpazarı başka ne gibi görünürse görünsün, amacı malların satışı ve değiş tokuşudur. İster bilgili koleksiyoncular ister sıradan kelepir avcıları olsunlar, insanlar sunulan ürünlerin muazzam miktarı ve çeşitliliği nedeniyle bitpazarına çekilirler. Herkesten önce gerçekten değerli bir şey bulma ihtimali, bitpazarında alışveriş yapmayı bir hazine avına dönüştürür.

Birçok alıcı için bitpazarındaki pazarlık ritüeli, kelepirin kendisinden daha eğlencelidir. Onlara başarı duygusu veren şey tasarruf ettikleri para değil; kadim bir oyunu oynamanın verdiği tatmindir.

Tatmin duygusu, bitpazarındaki alışverişin doğasından da kaynaklanır. Zaman ayırıp fiyat üzerinde pazarlık yaptıktan sonra işlem 'peşin öde ve götür' şeklindedir; satıcı paranızı cebine koyar, siz satın aldığınız eşyayla eve dönersiniz ve hepsi bu kadardır. Siz istediğinizi almışsınızdır, satıcı da istediğini almıştır. Günümüzün kredi kartları dünyasında bitpazarı, sizi hayatın daha sade olduğu ve paranın daha fazla anlam taşıdığı bir zamana geri götürür.

Bitpazarında tezgâh kuran kişilerin, yani satıcıların, hafta içi hayatlarında hiçbir ortak noktası olmayabilir; ancak hafta sonu boyunca bu çeşitlilik bir topluluğa dönüşür. Çinli bir çift, başka bir satıcının plastik saksı bitkilerinin karşısında kedi gözü güneş gözlüğü sergileyen punk bir gencin yanında işlemeli terlikler satar. Sokakta muhtemelen birbirleriyle hiç konuşmazlardı. Burada ise konuşurlar.

Bu 'bitlerin' buradaki ortak noktası nedir? Belki de bu, hayatta ilerlemeye, ekonomik olarak kendi kendine yetmeye ve kendi hayatlarının kontrolünü eline almaya duyulan bir inançtır. Satıcılar, özgürlük karşılığında dokuz-beş bir işin güvencesinden gönüllü olarak vazgeçerler: katı çalışma saatlerinden özgürlük; enflasyon ve vergilendirme dünyasından özgürlük; ne zaman, nerede ve ne satacaklarını seçme özgürlüğü; olmak istedikleri kişi olma özgürlüğü.

passages.passage_text:
It was civilization that created the dilemma of sleep loss. The sun presumably dictated the habits of ancient people: when it was up they were awake, and when it went down they slept. The discovery of fire probably allowed the first change in that pattern. As flames lit the dark, surely some adventurous souls delayed bedtime. But sweeping change came only a century ago with the introduction of the light bulb. U.S. inventor Thomas Edison's glowing device permitted cheap, safe and efficient illumination throughout the darkest nights. By the end of World War II, Americans were sleeping about eight hours a night.

Today new cultural and economic forces are combining to turn the U.S. into a 24-hour society. Many TV stations, restaurants and supermarkets operate through the day and night. Business is increasingly plugged into international markets that require round-the-clock monitoring and frequent travel across time zones.

But not all sleeplessness is caused by hectic schedules. Clinical sleep disorders are a major contributor to the national drowsiness. Many Americans suffer from nocturnal myoclonus, a condition in which their legs twitch throughout the night and break up their sleep. About 3 million adults, mostly overweight men, are afflicted with sleep apnea. In this disorder, muscles in the upper airway regularly sag and fail to keep the passage open. The struggle to take in air can result in snoring that rivals a jackhammer, though sufferers are often oblivious. "A person with apnea might not even be aware that he woke up 500 to 1,000 times last night because the arousals are so brief," says psychologist Thomas Roth, Chief of Henry Ford Hospital's Sleep-Disorder Center in Detroit. Both apnea and myoclonus can be treated, once diagnosed.

By far the most common complaint resulting in lack of sleep is insomnia. About a third of all Americans have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep - problems that result in listlessness and loss of alertness during the day. Most of the time the distress is temporary, brought on by anxiety about a problem at work or a sudden family crisis. But sometimes sleep difficulties can extend for months and years. Faced with a chronic situation, insomniacs frequently medicate themselves with alcohol or drugs. Doctors warn that in most cases sleeping pills should not be taken for longer than two or three weeks. Such drugs can lose their effectiveness in time, and it takes larger and larger doses to work. People run the risk of becoming dependent on the pills.

Because so few studies have been done, scientists cannot make definitive comparisons between American sleep patterns and those of other countries.

task1.model_answer: Human sleep patterns have changed dramatically since ancient times, shifting from sun-regulated rest to a modern 24-hour society driven by artificial lighting, round-the-clock services, and global business demands. Beyond busy lifestyles, clinical disorders also cause widespread sleep loss. Conditions such as nocturnal myoclonus and sleep apnea repeatedly interrupt rest, though both are treatable once diagnosed. The most frequent problem, however, is insomnia, which affects roughly a third of Americans and reduces daytime alertness.
