task2.model_answer:
Modern technology has undeniably transformed daily life, offering constant access to entertainment, shopping, and international communication. However, this 24-hour culture also encourages people to sacrifice essential rest, which harms both physical and mental health. Because work emails, streaming platforms, and late-night services remain available around the clock, many individuals delay bedtime even when they are exhausted.

In my view, society must set clearer boundaries between work and rest. Employers can discourage after-hours messaging and limit expectations for constant availability across time zones, while individuals should establish regular sleep routines and keep electronic devices out of the bedroom. Moreover, raising awareness about treatable conditions such as sleep apnea and insomnia can help people seek medical advice instead of relying on sleeping pills. Ultimately, technological convenience should support human well-being rather than undermine a basic biological need.

task2.title: Sleep in a 24-Hour Society

Günümüzde yeni kültürel ve ekonomik güçler birleşerek ABD'yi 24 saat yaşayan bir topluma dönüştürüyor. Birçok televizyon kanalı, restoran ve süpermarket gece gündüz faaliyet gösteriyor. İş dünyası, günün her saati takip ve saat dilimleri arasında sık sık seyahat gerektiren uluslararası piyasalara giderek daha fazla entegre oluyor.

Ancak tüm uykusuzluklar yoğun programlardan kaynaklanmaz. Klinik uyku bozuklukları, ülke genelindeki uyuşukluk ve uyku hâlinin başlıca nedenlerinden biridir. Pek çok Amerikalı, gece boyunca bacakların seğirmesine ve uykunun bölünmesine yol açan bir durum olan nokturnal miyoklonustan muzdariptir. Çoğunluğu fazla kilolu erkeklerden oluşan yaklaşık 3 milyon yetişkin uyku apnesinden etkilenmektedir. Bu rahatsızlıkta, üst solunum yolundaki kaslar düzenli olarak gevşeyip sarkar ve hava geçidini açık tutamaz. Hava alma mücadelesi, bir asfalt kırıcıyla yarışacak şiddette horlamalara yol açabilir; ancak bu rahatsızlığı yaşayanlar genellikle bunun farkında değildir. Detroit'teki Henry Ford Hastanesi Uyku Bozuklukları Merkezi Başkanı psikolog Thomas Roth, "Apnesi olan bir kişi, uyanmalar çok kısa sürdüğü için dün gece 500 ila 1.000 kez uyandığının farkında bile olmayabilir," diyor. Hem apne hem de miyoklonus, teşhis edildikten sonra tedavi edilebilir.

Uyku eksikliğine yol açan açık ara en yaygın şikâyet insomniadır. Tüm Amerikalıların yaklaşık üçte biri uykuya dalmakta veya uykuda kalmakta güçlük çekmektedir; bu sorunlar gün içinde hâlsizliğe ve dikkat kaybına neden olur. Çoğu zaman bu sıkıntı geçicidir ve iş yerindeki bir soruna dair kaygı ya da ani bir aile krizi tarafından tetiklenir. Ancak bazen uyku sorunları aylarca, hatta yıllarca sürebilir. Kronik bir durumla karşı karşıya kalan insomnia hastaları sık sık kendi kendilerini alkol veya ilaçlarla tedavi etmeye çalışırlar. Doktorlar, çoğu durumda uyku haplarının iki veya üç haftadan daha uzun süre kullanılmaması gerektiği konusunda uyarmaktadır. Bu tür ilaçlar zamanla etkilerini yitirebilir ve işe yaramaları için giderek daha yüksek dozlara ihtiyaç duyulur. İnsanlar haplara bağımlı hâle gelme riskiyle karşı karşıya kalır.

Çok az çalışma yapıldığı için bilim insanları, Amerikalıların uyku düzenleri ile diğer ülkelerdeki uyku düzenleri arasında kesin karşılaştırmalar yapamamaktadır.

passages.passage_text:
Most industries produce waste products which can be difficult or dangerous to dispose of. Coal and oil fired power stations produce enormous amounts of waste. A large coal power station will send 17 million tons of flue gas out of its chimney each year. It will also make around 2 million tons of ash, a fine white powder which is difficult to dispose of. Nuclear power stations also produce waste. The problem is that this waste is radioactive, and is dangerous unless kept safely away from living creatures.

High-level waste is the radioactive 'ash' from used nuclear fuel. This waste must be prevented from mixing with the environment until the radioactivity has decayed to safe levels. Radioactivity, unlike other poisons which are with us forever, disappears with time. So the highly radioactive 'ash' begins to lose its activity as soon as it is taken out of the reactor. It is normally kept at the bottom of a deep tank of water at the power station for several months. At the end of a year 90 per cent of the radioactivity is gone. At the end of 10 years 99 per cent would have ceased to exist. But what's left of this high-level waste is still very dangerous and will go on being so for thousands of years. However, the volume is not great, which makes storage comparatively simple. The total amount produced for the entire nuclear programme since 1956 would take up about the space of a pair of semi-detached houses - less than 1,500 cubic metres.

Intermediate-level wastes are far less radioactive. Currently, they are contained in solid concrete stores. The quantities involved are larger - about 2,500 cubic metres each year. There are no technical or safety-related advantages in storing these wastes for long periods. Plans are being developed to dispose of these wastes either deep underground or deep under the seabed. In the meantime, they will be specially encapsulated in cement to make them easier to store and handle.

Low-level wastes consist of gases and liquids as well as solid laboratory refuse - protective clothing, gloves, used syringes and tissues. Much of the radioactive waste from hospitals and industry is low-level. The gases and liquids can, with government authorisation, be released directly into the environment, where they quickly become diluted to a level that presents no appreciable risk. At present, the low-level solid wastes are disposed of in a shallow disposal site at Drigg, Cumbria. In the longer term they can be put in the same repository as the intermediate-level wastes either deep underground or under the seabed. Our only 'vested interest' in nuclear waste is to dispose of it without harm to the public. Surely the most balanced approach you could wish for.

task1.model_answer: Industrial power stations generate vast quantities of waste, with nuclear facilities producing radioactive materials divided into three categories. High-level waste, though small in volume at under 1,500 cubic metres since 1956, remains hazardous for thousands of years despite losing 99 per cent of its radioactivity within a decade; it is initially cooled in deep water tanks. Intermediate-level waste, generated in larger amounts of around 2,500 cubic metres annually, is currently kept in concrete stores before future deep underground or seabed disposal. Finally, low-level waste from hospitals and industry includes gases and liquids safely diluted in the environment, alongside solids buried in shallow sites.
task1.prompt: Summarize how the three categories of nuclear waste differ in radioactivity, volume, and disposal methods.
task1.title: Comparing Categories of Nuclear Waste

task2.model_answer:
Energy production always involves environmental trade-offs, and managing industrial waste safely is one of the greatest challenges modern societies face. While fossil fuel power stations release millions of tons of flue gas and ash each year, nuclear power generates far smaller volumes of radioactive waste that can be carefully isolated from living creatures.

In my opinion, nuclear waste can be managed responsibly if strict scientific oversight and transparent public policies are maintained. As the passage explains, high-level waste occupies relatively little space and loses most of its radioactivity within ten years, while intermediate and low-level wastes can be encapsulated in cement or placed in deep geological repositories. Nevertheless, because remaining high-level materials stay dangerous for millennia, governments must invest continuously in secure long-term storage and independent monitoring rather than relying on temporary solutions. Only through rigorous regulation can public safety be guaranteed.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Tehlikeli Atık.

Çoğu endüstri, bertaraf edilmesi zor veya tehlikeli olabilen atık ürünler üretir. Kömür ve petrol yakıtlı elektrik santralleri muazzam miktarlarda atık üretir. Büyük bir kömür santrali her yıl bacasından 17 milyon ton baca gazı salar. Ayrıca bertaraf edilmesi zor, ince beyaz bir toz olan yaklaşık 2 milyon ton kül de üretir. Nükleer santraller de atık üretir. Sorun şu ki bu atık radyoaktiftir ve canlı varlıklardan güvenli bir şekilde uzak tutulmadıkça tehlikelidir.

Yüksek düzeyli atık, kullanılmış nükleer yakıttan çıkan radyoaktif 'küldür'. Radyoaktivite güvenli seviyelere düşene kadar bu atığın çevreye karışması önlenmelidir. Sonsuza dek bizimle kalan diğer zehirlerin aksine radyoaktivite zamanla yok olur. Dolayısıyla yüksek düzeyde radyoaktif olan bu 'kül', reaktörden çıkarılır çıkarılmaz aktivitesini kaybetmeye başlar. Normalde birkaç ay boyunca santraldeki derin bir su tankının dibinde tutulur. Bir yılın sonunda radyoaktivitenin yüzde 90'ı gitmiş olur. 10 yılın sonunda ise yüzde 99'u ortadan kalkmış olacaktır. Ancak bu yüksek düzeyli atıktan geriye kalan kısım hâlâ çok tehlikelidir ve binlerce yıl boyunca da öyle olmaya devam edecektir. Bununla birlikte hacmi büyük değildir, bu da depolanmasını nispeten basit hale getirir. 1956'dan bu yana tüm nükleer program boyunca üretilen toplam miktar, bir çift bitişik nizam ev kadar, yani 1.500 metreküpten daha az bir yer kaplar.

Orta düzeyli atıklar çok daha az radyoaktiftir. Şu anda sağlam beton depolarda muhafaza edilmektedirler. Söz konusu miktarlar daha büyüktür; her yıl yaklaşık 2.500 metreküp kadardır. Bu atıkları uzun süre depolamanın teknik veya güvenlikle ilgili bir avantajı yoktur. Bu atıkları yerin derinliklerinde ya da deniz tabanının çok altında bertaraf etmek için planlar geliştirilmektedir. Bu arada, depolanmalarını ve taşınmalarını kolaylaştırmak amacıyla özel olarak çimento içine hapsedileceklerdir.

Düşük düzeyli atıklar gazlar ve sıvıların yanı sıra katı laboratuvar çöplerinden oluşur: koruyucu giysiler, eldivenler, kullanılmış şırıngalar ve kâğıt mendiller. Hastanelerden ve endüstriden kaynaklanan radyoaktif atıkların çoğu düşük düzeylidir. Gazlar ve sıvılar, hükümet izniyle doğrudan çevreye salınabilir ve burada hızla kayda değer bir risk oluşturmayan bir seviyeye kadar seyrelirler. Şu anda düşük düzeyli katı atıklar Cumbria'daki Drigg'de bulunan sığ bir bertaraf sahasında imha edilmektedir. Uzun vadede ise orta düzeyli atıklarla aynı depoya, yani yerin derinliklerine veya deniz tabanının altına konulabilirler. Nükleer atık konusundaki tek 'çıkarımız', onu halka zarar vermeden bertaraf etmektir. Elbette isteyebileceğiniz en dengeli yaklaşım budur.

passages.passage_text:
Until recently daydreaming was generally considered either a waste of time or a symptom of neurotic tendencies, and many psychiatrists claimed that habitual daydreaming was evidence of maladjustment or an escape from life's realities and responsibilities. As with anything carried to excess, daydreaming can be harmful when 'fantasy addicts' withdraw from people and can no longer cope with reality. Then their mental health is impaired. But such extremes are relatively rare, and there is a growing body of evidence to support the fact that most people suffer from a lack of daydreaming rather than an excess of it. We are now beginning to learn how valuable it really is and that when individuals are completely prevented from daydreaming, not only are they less able to deal with the pressures of day-to-day existence, but also their self-control and self-direction become endangered.

Daydreaming, science has discovered, is an effective relaxation technique. Results of experiments conducted by psychotherapists indicate that daydreaming significantly contributes to intellectual growth, powers of concentration, attention span, and the ability to interact and communicate with others.

Contrary to popular belief, incessant and conscious effort at solving a problem is, in reality, one of the most inefficient ways of treating it. Effective solutions to severe problems frequently occur when conscious attempts to solve them have been suspended. Inability to relax, to let go of a problem, often prevents its solution.

A life lived without fantasy and daydreaming is a seriously impoverished one. Each of us should put aside a few minutes daily, taking short 10-15 minute vacations. Daydreaming is highly beneficial to your psychological and mental well-being and you'll find that this modest, inexpensive investment in time will add up to a more creative, more imaginative, more satisfied, and more self-fulfilled you. It offers us a fuller sense of being intensely alive from moment to moment, and this, of course, contributes greatly to the excitement of life.

task2.model_answer:
In today's fast-paced world, productivity is often measured by continuous, visible effort, leading many people to view daydreaming as laziness. However, constant mental exertion without rest frequently reduces creativity and leads to burnout rather than better results.

I strongly agree that taking short daily breaks to let the mind wander makes both students and workers more effective. As scientific experiments indicate, suspending conscious focus on a difficult task allows the brain to relax and form fresh connections, often producing solutions that forced concentration cannot achieve. Of course, daydreaming should remain a balanced habit rather than an escape from responsibilities. Yakın zamana kadar hayal kurmak genellikle ya zaman kaybı ya da nevrotik eğilimlerin bir belirtisi olarak görülürdü ve birçok psikiyatrist, alışkanlık haline gelmiş hayal kurmanın uyumsuzluğun bir kanıtı ya da hayatın gerçeklerinden ve sorumluluklarından bir kaçış olduğunu öne sürerdi. Aşırıya kaçılan her şeyde olduğu gibi, 'hayal bağımlıları' insanlardan uzaklaşıp artık gerçeklikle başa çıkamadıklarında hayal kurmak zararlı olabilir. O zaman ruh sağlıkları bozulur. Ancak bu tür aşırı durumlar nispeten nadirdir ve çoğu insanın hayal kurmanın fazlalığından ziyade eksikliğinden muzdarip olduğu gerçeğini destekleyen giderek artan kanıtlar vardır. Artık bunun gerçekte ne kadar değerli olduğunu ve bireylerin hayal kurması tamamen engellendiğinde, yalnızca günlük yaşamın baskılarıyla başa çıkmakta daha az başarılı olmakla kalmayıp aynı zamanda öz denetimlerinin ve kendi kendilerini yönlendirme becerilerinin de tehlikeye girdiğini öğrenmeye başlıyoruz.

Bilimin keşfettiğine göre hayal kurmak etkili bir rahatlama tekniğidir. Psikoterapistler tarafından yürütülen deneylerin sonuçları, hayal kurmanın zihinsel gelişime, odaklanma gücüne, dikkat süresine ve başkalarıyla etkileşim kurup iletişim kurma becerisine önemli ölçüde katkıda bulunduğunu göstermektedir.

Yaygın inanışın aksine, bir sorunu çözmek için durmaksızın ve bilinçli bir çaba harcamak, gerçekte onu ele almanın en verimsiz yollarından biridir. Ciddi sorunlara yönelik etkili çözümler, sıklıkla onları çözmeye yönelik bilinçli girişimler askıya alındığında ortaya çıkar. Rahatlayamamak, bir sorunu akışına bırakamamak çoğu zaman onun çözümünü engeller.

Düşler ve hayal kurma olmadan yaşanan bir hayat ciddi anlamda yoksul bir hayattır. Her birimiz her gün birkaç dakika ayırmalı, 10 ila 15 dakikalık kısa tatillere çıkmalıyız. Hayal kurmak psikolojik ve zihinsel sağlığınız için son derece faydalıdır ve zamana yapılan bu mütevazı, masrafsız yatırımın sizi daha yaratıcı, daha geniş hayal gücüne sahip, daha tatmin olmuş ve kendini daha fazla gerçekleştirmiş biri haline getireceğini göreceksiniz. Bize andan ana yoğun bir şekilde yaşadığımızı daha derinden hissettirir ve bu da elbette hayatın heyecanına büyük ölçüde katkıda bulunur.

passages.passage_text:
The beauty of numbers is in their precision. They express exactly how much, neither more nor less. Numbers reveal relationships more clearly and more accurately than any other language. Once numbers are correctly established, they eliminate all differences of opinion. Eight fingers are more than seven fingers.

Suppose that we are interested in contrasting employment practices in economically developed countries with those in underdeveloped countries. The United States of America and the People's Republic of China are good examples. A study of these two countries reveals a startling set of numbers.

Distribution of farm employment is by far the most surprising. Seventy-five per cent of all the people gainfully employed in China work on farms; only 4 per cent work on farms in the United States. This is a fundamental distinction, for it tells us something of the effort necessary to stay alive in these two countries.

Farm employment in China is so high that only 15 per cent of the workers are available to carry on trade, commerce, manufacturing, and other special services. The same group of occupations in the United States is carried on by 85 per cent of the work force.

These figures indicate that a well-developed economy places great emphasis on manufacturing, trade, commerce, and services. The raw materials on which these functions are based are obtained efficiently with a small manpower commitment. Underdeveloped countries exhaust their manpower resources in the effort to obtain enough food.

The people who make life comfortable for the rest of us are the doctors, lawyers, preachers, teachers, artists, hairdressers, repairmen, cobblers, entertainers, civil servants, and military personnel. Imagine the price paid by the Chinese with only 4 per cent of their gainfully employed population working in service jobs! The same category makes up 24 per cent of the gainfully employed population of the United States.

That is quite a difference. Without manufacturing, trade, and commerce there can be little in the way of consumer goods available to the people. The United States was in this position in the eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries. At that time, the population was centered on the farms and forced to make many things for themselves. This is exactly what we saw in China as the 1970s came to a close. Science, aided by a new technology, especially the availability of abundant farm machinery, will put an end to the China we once knew.

The lesson here is not really one in economics. It rests with an understanding of numbers. Counting things gives reliable information and permits us to draw reliable conclusions. There is a formal beauty and uncompromising power in measurement.

task1.model_answer: In the passage, the author argues that numbers reveal relationships more accurately than any other form of expression. To illustrate this point, the text compares employment figures in the United States and China during the late 1970s. Whereas 75 per cent of China's workforce was employed in farming and only 4 per cent worked in service jobs, merely 4 per cent of Americans worked on farms while 85 per cent worked in manufacturing, trade, commerce, and services. These figures demonstrate that developed economies obtain raw materials efficiently and produce abundant consumer goods, while underdeveloped economies spend most of their labor securing food. Ultimately, the author concludes that careful measurement leads to reliable conclusions.

task1.title: Summarizing Employment Statistics and Economic Development

task2.model_answer:
Numbers undoubtedly play a crucial role in helping us understand social and economic realities. As the passage demonstrates, comparing employment percentages across countries immediately clarifies how different societies allocate their labor and resources. Without accurate data on agriculture, manufacturing, and services, discussions about economic development would rely on vague impressions rather than concrete evidence.

However, it is an exaggeration to say that numbers eliminate all differences of opinion. First, statistics require careful interpretation; the same figure can be used to support opposing policies depending on which factors are emphasized. For instance, a low percentage of farm workers may reflect technological efficiency, yet it does not by itself explain income inequality or working conditions. Second, human well-being involves qualities—such as cultural vitality, freedom, and job satisfaction—that cannot always be captured through counting alone.

In conclusion, while numerical measurement provides an essential and objective foundation for analysis, sound judgment also depends on context and thoughtful interpretation.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Sayıların Güzelliği.

Sayıların güzelliği kesinliklerindedir. Tam olarak ne kadar olduğunu ifade ederler; ne daha fazla ne daha az. Sayılar, ilişkileri başka herhangi bir dilden daha net ve daha doğru bir şekilde ortaya koyar. Sayılar doğru bir şekilde belirlendiğinde tüm görüş ayrılıklarını ortadan kaldırırlar. Sekiz parmak, yedi parmaktan fazladır.

Ekonomik olarak gelişmiş ülkelerdeki istihdam uygulamalarını az gelişmiş ülkelerdekilerle karşılaştırmakla ilgilendiğimizi varsayalım. Amerika Birleşik Devletleri ve Çin Halk Cumhuriyeti iyi örneklerdir. Bu iki ülke üzerine yapılan bir inceleme şaşırtıcı bir dizi sayıyı ortaya koymaktadır.

Tarım istihdamının dağılımı açık ara en şaşırtıcı olanıdır. Çin'de gelir getirici bir işte çalışan tüm insanların yüzde 75'i çiftliklerde çalışmaktadır; Amerika Birleşik Devletleri'nde ise yalnızca yüzde 4'ü çiftliklerde çalışmaktadır. Bu temel bir ayrımdır; çünkü bize bu iki ülkede hayatta kalmak için gereken çaba hakkında bir şeyler söyler.

Çin'de tarım istihdamı o kadar yüksektir ki işçilerin yalnızca yüzde 15'i ticaret, alım satım, imalat ve diğer özel hizmetleri yürütmek için uygundur. Amerika Birleşik Devletleri'nde ise aynı meslek grubu iş gücünün yüzde 85'i tarafından yürütülmektedir.

Bu rakamlar, iyi gelişmiş bir ekonominin imalat, ticaret, alım satım ve hizmetlere büyük önem verdiğini göstermektedir. Bu işlevlerin dayandığı ham maddeler, küçük bir iş gücü kullanımıyla verimli bir şekilde elde edilir. Az gelişmiş ülkeler ise yeterli gıda elde etme çabası içinde iş gücü kaynaklarını tüketirler.

Geri kalanımız için hayatı konforlu hale getiren insanlar doktorlar, avukatlar, vaizler, öğretmenler, sanatçılar, kuaförler, tamirciler, ayakkabı tamircileri, eğlence sektörü çalışanları, devlet memurları ve askeri personeldir. Gelir getirici işlerde çalışan nüfusunun yalnızca yüzde 4'ü hizmet işlerinde çalışan Çinlilerin ödediği bedeli hayal edin! Aynı kategori, Amerika Birleşik Devletleri'nde gelir getirici işlerde çalışan nüfusun yüzde 24'ünü oluşturmaktadır.

Bu oldukça büyük bir farktır. İmalat, ticaret ve alım satım olmadan halka sunulabilecek tüketim malları son derece kısıtlı olur. Amerika Birleşik Devletleri on sekizinci yüzyılda ve on dokuzuncu yüzyılın başlarında bu durumdaydı. O dönemde nüfus çiftliklerde yoğunlaşmıştı ve birçok şeyi kendi başına yapmak zorundaydı. 1970'ler sona ererken Çin'de gördüğümüz şey de tam olarak buydu. Yeni bir teknolojinin, özellikle de bol miktarda tarım makinesinin mevcudiyetinin desteklediği bilim, bir zamanlar bildiğimiz Çin'e son verecektir.

Buradaki ders aslında ekonomiyle ilgili değildir. Sayıları anlamaya dayanır. Bir şeyleri saymak güvenilir bilgi verir ve güvenilir sonuçlar çıkarmamızı sağlar. Ölçümde biçimsel bir güzellik ve tavizsiz bir güç vardır.

passages.passage_text:
An increasing number of teachers, from kindergarten through college, have altered lesson plans to include the art of thinking. Many others are being trained so that they can shift the classroom emphasis away from just giving pupils information and move toward making them think about the issues raised by that information. Educators say that students have become obsessed with getting the right answers on tests and so they are weak at analyzing what they are learning and at grasping implications. These weaknesses, the educators say, will affect the students' ability to make future decisions about career and marriage, what candidates to vote for and what products to buy. "It's not just the ability to remember things and feed them back on tests that determines how well you're going to do in life," said Dr. Heidi Jacobs, a professor at Teachers College at Columbia University. "It's the ability to solve problems and reflect and to, in fact, think critically."

Unfortunately, about 80 per cent of class questions, according to Dr. Jacobs, are designed simply to have students recall information. Moreover, the pressure to raise student performance on standardized tests created an exaggerated stress on memorized information. In reaction to this, more teachers have begun to support the movement to teach critical thinking in schools. While schools and teachers have always assumed that thinking was part of their mission, educators are now making the teaching of thinking skills a more formal part of their programs. For example, there has been a dramatic push in the last few years by at least 28 states and hundreds of schools to re-train teachers and revise curriculums.

In the early 1980's, reports by several influential commissions claimed that it was vital to improve reasoning abilities for a population that would have to adjust to sweeping changes in technology in a more competitive world. Since 1985, the California State University system has required its one million students to take a course in critical thinking before they can graduate. New York City's Board of Education created a Reasoning Skills Unit to prepare analytical questions to be used by the teachers of various subjects. Such questions will encourage students to think about what they have been taught and use the information in a more practical way. Students are now being taught analytical skills such as inferring explanations, supporting an argument, judging the credibility of a source, verifying an observation, identifying underlying assumptions, and designing experiments so that a particular variable can be controlled.

Articles on teaching the concept of 'critical thinking' have been published in educational journals since the late 1970's. Starting in the 1980's, supporters have set up three professional associations and currently publish six journals. In fact, the critical-thinking movement has become so strong that it now has three factions: teachers who say thinking should be taught separately, those who argue that it should be only integrated into the normal curriculum, and those who believe that both these approaches are equally applicable.

Even in teaching mathematics, some supporters suggest that instructors move away from the assumption that there is always one correct answer. Instead, they say, students should be encouraged to explain how they arrived at a different answer. Mr. Ewen, a math teacher, said he could accept 6 as a plausible answer to "What is 29 divided by 5?" if the student provided a reasonable explanation. A student, he said, might calculate that 29 chips divided into piles of 5 each will yield 6 piles, even though one of the piles is shorter than the others. "The greatest discoveries," he added, "have come from people who have looked at a standard situation and seen it differently."

Mister Ewen, a math teacher, said he could accept 6 as a plausible answer to "What is 29 divided by 5?" if the student provided a reasonable explanation. A student, he said, might calculate that 29 chips divided into piles of 5 each will yield 6 piles, even though one of the piles is shorter than the others. "The greatest discoveries," he added, "have come from people who have looked at a standard situation and seen it differently."

task1.model_answer: The passage explains that many educators are shifting away from rote memorization toward formally teaching critical thinking from kindergarten through college. Previously, standardized testing pushed schools to focus heavily on recalling facts, leaving students poorly prepared for real-world decisions. In response, numerous states, universities, and school boards have revised curriculums and trained teachers to cultivate analytical skills such as evaluating sources and identifying assumptions. Although educators debate whether critical thinking should be taught separately or integrated into existing subjects, supporters even apply this flexible approach to mathematics by encouraging students to justify unconventional solutions.
task1.prompt: Summarize the shift toward teaching critical thinking in schools and explain the different ways educators are implementing it, using your own words.

task2.model_answer:
Although standardized tests remain a common way to measure academic progress, schools should place greater emphasis on critical thinking than on memorizing facts. In today's rapidly changing world, memorized information quickly becomes outdated, whereas analytical skills remain valuable throughout life.

When students focus only on recalling facts for exams, they often struggle to apply knowledge to unfamiliar situations. For example, evaluating news sources, comparing financial options, or solving workplace problems all require reasoning rather than simple recall. Teaching students to question assumptions and justify their conclusions prepares them to make informed personal and civic decisions.

Critics argue that standardized exams require students to master core facts first. However, facts are learned more deeply when students actively analyze and use them in meaningful contexts rather than repeating them mechanically.

In conclusion, while foundational knowledge is necessary, prioritizing critical thinking equips learners with adaptable problem-solving skills that serve them far beyond the classroom.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Eleştirel Düşünme Memnuniyetle Karşılanıyor.

Anaokulundan üniversiteye kadar giderek daha fazla sayıda öğretmen, düşünme sanatını içerecek şekilde ders planlarını değiştirdi. Birçok öğretmen de sınıftaki ağırlığı öğrencilere yalnızca bilgi vermekten uzaklaştırıp onları bu bilginin ortaya çıkardığı meseleler üzerine düşündürmeye yöneltebilmek için eğitim alıyor. Eğitimciler, öğrencilerin sınavlarda doğru yanıtları vermeyi saplantı haline getirdiğini ve bu nedenle öğrendiklerini analiz etmekte ve çıkarımları kavramakta zayıf kaldıklarını söylüyor. Eğitimcilere göre bu zayıflıklar, öğrencilerin gelecekte kariyer ve evlilik, hangi adaylara oy verecekleri ve hangi ürünleri satın alacakları konusunda karar verme becerilerini etkileyecek. Columbia Üniversitesi Eğitim Fakültesi profesörlerinden Doktor Heidi Jacobs, "Hayatta ne kadar başarılı olacağınızı belirleyen şey yalnızca bir şeyleri hatırlayıp sınavlarda geri sunma becerisi değildir," dedi. "Bu, sorun çözme, derinlemesine düşünme ve aslında eleştirel düşünme becerisidir."

Doktor Jacobs'a göre ne yazık ki sınıf içi soruların yaklaşık yüzde 80'i yalnızca öğrencilerin bilgiyi hatırlamasını sağlamak üzere tasarlanmaktadır. Dahası, standart testlerdeki öğrenci performansını artırma baskısı, ezberlenen bilgiye abartılı bir vurgu yapılmasına yol açtı. Buna tepki olarak, daha fazla öğretmen okullarda eleştirel düşünme öğretme hareketini desteklemeye başladı. Okullar ve öğretmenler düşünmenin her zaman kendi görevlerinin bir parçası olduğunu varsaymış olsalar da eğitimciler artık düşünme becerilerinin öğretimini programlarının daha resmi bir parçası haline getiriyor. Örneğin, son birkaç yılda en az 28 eyalet ve yüzlerce okul tarafından öğretmenleri yeniden eğitmek ve müfredatları gözden geçirmek için çarpıcı bir atılım yapıldı.

1980'lerin başında, birkaç etkili komisyon tarafından hazırlanan raporlarda, daha rekabetçi bir dünyada teknolojideki köklü değişimlere uyum sağlamak zorunda kalacak bir nüfus için muhakeme becerilerini geliştirmenin hayati önem taşıdığı ileri sürüldü. 1985'ten bu yana Kaliforniya Eyalet Üniversitesi sistemi, bir milyon öğrencisinin mezun olabilmesi için eleştirel düşünme dersi almasını zorunlu kılmaktadır. New York Şehri Eğitim Kurulu, çeşitli derslerin öğretmenleri tarafından kullanılacak analitik sorular hazırlamak üzere bir Muhakeme Becerileri Birimi kurdu. Bu tür sorular öğrencileri kendilerine öğretilenler üzerinde düşünmeye ve bilgiyi daha pratik bir şekilde kullanmaya teşvik edecektir. Öğrencilere artık açıklamalar çıkarma, bir savı destekleme, bir kaynağın güvenilirliğini değerlendirme, bir gözlemi doğrulama, altta yatan varsayımları belirleme ve belirli bir değişkenin kontrol edilebilmesi için deneyler tasarlama gibi analitik beceriler öğretilmektedir.

'Eleştirel düşünme' kavramının öğretilmesi üzerine makaleler 1970'lerin sonlarından beri eğitim dergilerinde yayımlanmaktadır. 1980'lerden başlayarak destekçiler üç mesleki dernek kurmuşlardır ve şu anda altı dergi yayımlamaktadırlar. Aslında eleştirel düşünme hareketi o kadar güçlenmiştir ki artık üç gruba ayrılmaktadır: düşünmenin ayrı olarak öğretilmesi gerektiğini söyleyen öğretmenler, yalnızca normal müfredata entegre edilmesi gerektiğini savunanlar ve bu iki yaklaşımın da eşit derecede uygulanabilir olduğuna inananlar.

Matematik öğretiminde bile bazı destekçiler, eğitmenlerin her zaman tek bir doğru yanıt olduğu varsayımından uzaklaşmasını önermektedir. Bunun yerine öğrencilerin farklı bir yanıta nasıl ulaştıklarını açıklamaya teşvik edilmesi gerektiğini söylemektedirler. Bir matematik öğretmeni olan Bay Ewen, öğrencinin makul bir açıklama sunması halinde "29 bölü 5 kaçtır?" sorusuna makul bir yanıt olarak 6'yı kabul edebileceğini söyledi. Bir öğrencinin, yığınlardan biri diğerlerinden daha kısa olsa bile, her biri 5'li yığınlara bölünen 29 pulun 6 yığın oluşturacağını hesaplayabileceğini belirtti. "En büyük keşifler," diye ekledi, "standart bir duruma bakıp onu farklı gören insanlardan çıkmıştır."

task1.model_answer: The writer argues that although children initially enjoy recognizing words, this enthusiasm disappears if early reading materials rely on repetitive drills instead of meaningful texts. While mastering basic reading skills such as decoding is necessary, treating these skills as an isolated objective turns reading into dull rote learning. Consequently, teachers, schools, and textbooks must immediately show young learners that foundational skills are merely a tool for a larger purpose: becoming truly literate so they can understand, enjoy, and benefit from literature.

task2.model_answer:
Early reading textbooks should prioritize engaging stories alongside basic phonics instruction rather than relying solely on repetitive word drills. While recognizing letters and sounds is essential for beginners, motivation plays an equally vital role in building lifelong reading habits.

If young learners spend months reading artificial sentences that repeat the same three or four words, they quickly associate books with boredom rather than curiosity. Children naturally want to discover ideas, follow characters, and make sense of the world around them. When teachers introduce short, meaningful stories early on, students immediately see why sounding out words is worthwhile.

Of course, basic decoding practice cannot be skipped altogether, because children need reliable strategies for unfamiliar words. However, these exercises work best when paired with interesting content that rewards their effort.

In short, effective early reading instruction balances technical skills with genuine storytelling so children learn both how to read and why reading is enjoyable.

Bir çocuk, bazı kelimeleri okuyabilmeye başladığında bundan büyük bir keyif alır. Ancak okuması gereken metinler onu aynı kelimeyi durmadan yeniden okumaya zorladığında bu heyecan söner. Eğitim kuramcılarının kullandığı terimle 'çözümleme' yani kelime tanıma, doğrudan anlamlı içerikler okumaya yönelmediğinde boş bir ezberciliğe dönüşür. Çocuğun çözümlemeden anlamlı okumaya geçmesi ne kadar uzun sürerse, kitaplardan aldığı zevkin buharlaşıp uçması da o kadar olası hale gelir. Bir çocuğun okuma becerisi hiç kuşkusuz gerekli becerileri öğrenmesine bağlıdır; fakat çocuk, temel okuma becerilerini yalnızca kendi başlarına öğrenmesi beklendiğini düşünürse bunları öğrenmeye ilgi duymayacaktır. Bu nedenle öğretmenin, okulun ve ders kitaplarının neyi vurguladığı çok büyük önem taşır. task1.model_answer: The passage defines a rumour as a widely shared report without factual proof that can trigger or intensify antisocial group actions. Rather than reflecting poor communication, rumours often spread rapidly through effective communication channels because the term describes unverified content rather than transmission methods. In large crowds, individuals struggle to verify the origin and reliability of what they hear, causing them to treat rumours as facts. Ultimately, rumours emerge either to fill an information gap when people want answers or to justify intense emotions and collective behaviour.
task1.prompt: Summarize how the passage defines rumour and explains the reasons why rumours develop and spread.

task2.model_answer:
Rumours often cause serious harm in society because they spread rapidly during moments of uncertainty when people are eager for answers. To minimize their damage, both institutions and individuals must take active steps to verify information.

First, authorities and organizations should share accurate updates promptly during crises or unexpected events. As the passage notes, rumours thrive when there is a lack of reliable information. Transparent communication removes the vacuum that false reports usually fill. Second, individuals need to pause and check the source and accuracy of striking claims before passing them on, especially in emotional or crowded situations.

Some may argue that rumours are harmless everyday gossip, yet unverified claims can easily provoke panic, unfair blame, or antisocial group actions.

Therefore, combining timely official communication with critical evaluation by listeners is the most effective way to prevent rumours from turning into harmful collective behaviour.

Söylenti terimi, iletişim kurma yöntemine değil, içeriğine atıfta bulunur. passages.passage_text:
Within a few days of starting work, I had grasped the main principles on which the hotel was run. The thing that would astonish anyone coming for the first time into the service quarters of a hotel would be the fearful noise and disorder during the rush hours. It is something so different from the steady work in a shop or a factory that it looks at first sight like mere mad management. But it is really quite unavoidable and part of the whole. Hotel work is not particularly hard, but by its nature it comes in rushes and cannot be economised. You cannot, for instance, grill a steak two hours before it is wanted; you have to wait till the last moment, by which time a mass of other work has accumulated, and then do it all together in frantic haste. It was for this reason that during the rush hours the whole staff raged and cursed like demons. A girl in the bakery, aged sixteen, used swear words that would have defeated a taxi driver. But we were not losing our heads and wasting time; we were just stimulating one another for the effort of packing four hours' work into two hours.

What keeps a hotel going is the fact that the employees take a genuine pride in their work, beastly and silly though it is.

passages.passage_text:
By Bertrand Russell.

Is it possible to persuade mankind to live without war? War is an ancient institution which has existed for at least six thousand years. It has always been cruel and usually foolish, but in the past the human race managed to live with it. Modern ingenuity has changed this. Either Man will abolish war, or war will abolish Man. For the present, it is nuclear weapons which may, before long, offer an even greater threat. If we succeed in abolishing nuclear weapons, our work will not be done. It will never be done until we have succeeded in abolishing war. To do this, we need to persuade mankind to look upon international questions in a new way, not as contests of force, in which the victory goes to the side which is most skillful in massacre, but by arbitration in accordance with agreed principles of law. It is not easy to change age-old mental habits, but this is what must be attempted.

There are those who say that the adoption of this or that ideology would prevent war. I believe this to be a profound error. All ideologies are based upon dogmatic assertions which are, at best, doubtful, and at worst, totally false. Their adherents believe in them so fanatically that they are willing to go to war in support of them.

The movement of world opinion during the past two years has been very largely such as we can welcome. It has become a commonplace that nuclear war must be avoided. Of course, very difficult problems remain in the international sphere, but the spirit in which they are being approached is a better one than it was some years ago. It has begun to be thought, even by the powerful men who decide whether we shall live or die, that negotiations should reach agreements even if both sides do not find these agreements wholly satisfactory. It has begun to be understood that the important conflict nowadays is not between East and West, but between Man and the H-bomb.

task1.model_answer: In this excerpt, Bertrand Russell argues that modern nuclear technology makes the complete abolition of war essential for human survival. Although humanity endured warfare for millennia, modern weapons present an existential threat. Eliminating nuclear arms alone is insufficient; nations must abandon force and resolve disputes through legal arbitration. Russell also rejects the belief that any ideology can guarantee peace, noting that dogmatic beliefs often inspire fanatical violence. Nevertheless, he finds hope in shifting global attitudes: leaders increasingly recognize that nuclear conflict must be prevented through compromise, realizing that the true struggle is not between rival political blocs, but between humanity and nuclear annihilation.

task2.model_answer:
Whether international law and diplomacy can permanently eliminate war remains one of the most pressing questions in global politics. While human history suggests that conflict is deeply rooted, strong legal institutions and diplomacy offer the most realistic path toward lasting peace.

Skeptics argue that nations act primarily out of self-interest and will always resort to force when vital security or economic interests are threatened. Indeed, even well-designed international treaties can fail if powerful states refuse to enforce or obey them.

However, Bertrand Russell rightly points out that modern weapons have raised the stakes to total destruction, making compromise a necessity rather than a choice. When countries settle disputes through arbitration, trade agreements, and international courts, they build trust and reduce the temptation to use violence. Furthermore, mutual economic interdependence raises the cost of conflict significantly.

In conclusion, although legal frameworks cannot transform human nature overnight, consistent diplomacy and enforceable international law remain humanity's strongest safeguard against catastrophic war.

passages.passage_text:
One of the most disturbing predictions following the near meltdown of the Chernobyl nuclear power plant on April 26, 1986, was that cancer cases would eventually begin to rise in areas where fallout from the accident landed. What no one suspected was that it would happen so soon, or that many of the first victims would be children. Two reports in Nature, one by the World Health Organisation and one by health officials in Belarus, the ex-Soviet Republic immediately downwind from Chernobyl, indicate that childhood thyroid cancer has jumped from an average of four cases a year to about 50. In the Gomel region, hit first by the radiation, the thyroid cancer rate is now about 80 times the world average. "The only reasonable explanation," write the Belarus officials, "is that it is a direct consequence of the accident at Chernobyl."

In retrospect, the phenomenon makes sense: the thyroid gland tends to concentrate iodine ingested by the body, and radioactive iodine was released in bulk during the accident. Moreover, radiation is known to cause thyroid cancer, and children are especially susceptible. But previous studies of nuclear accidents in Britain and the U.S. and studies of nuclear-weapons testing in Japan and the South Pacific failed to prove a conclusive fallout-cancer correlation. The probable difference this time: the radiation was more highly concentrated and hit a heavily populated area.

passages.title: Chernobyl
passages.tts_script:
Chernobyl.

One of the most disturbing predictions following the near meltdown of the Chernobyl nuclear power plant on April 26, 1986, was that cancer cases would eventually begin to rise in areas where fallout from the accident landed. What no one suspected was that it would happen so soon, or that many of the first victims would be children. Two reports in Nature, one by the World Health Organisation and one by health officials in Belarus, the ex-Soviet Republic immediately downwind from Chernobyl, indicate that childhood thyroid cancer has jumped from an average of four cases a year to about 50. In the Gomel region, hit first by the radiation, the thyroid cancer rate is now about 80 times the world average. "The only reasonable explanation," write the Belarus officials, "is that it is a direct consequence of the accident at Chernobyl."

In retrospect, the phenomenon makes sense: the thyroid gland tends to concentrate iodine ingested by the body, and radioactive iodine was released in bulk during the accident. Moreover, radiation is known to cause thyroid cancer, and children are especially susceptible. But previous studies of nuclear accidents in Britain and the U.S. and studies of nuclear-weapons testing in Japan and the South Pacific failed to prove a conclusive fallout-cancer correlation. The probable difference this time: the radiation was more highly concentrated and hit a heavily populated area.

Because the thyroid gland absorbs iodine and the accident released vast quantities of radioactive iodine, children were particularly vulnerable. Unlike earlier nuclear incidents and weapons tests that showed inconclusive results, Chernobyl delivered highly concentrated radiation over a densely populated area.

task2.model_answer:
Nuclear power remains one of the most fiercely debated energy sources in the modern world. While it offers a reliable, low-carbon alternative to fossil fuels, disasters like Chernobyl remind societies of its severe long-term risks.

Supporters of nuclear energy point out that modern reactors produce large amounts of electricity without emitting greenhouse gases, helping countries combat climate change. With strict safety standards and improved engineering, catastrophic accidents are rare compared to the ongoing air pollution caused by coal and oil.

Nevertheless, opponents argue that even a low probability of failure carries unacceptable consequences. Radioactive fallout can contaminate land for generations, harm vulnerable populations such as children, and generate toxic waste that remains difficult to store safely.

In my view, countries should invest primarily in safer renewable sources like solar and wind power, while keeping existing nuclear plants operational only under rigorous international safety oversight until clean alternatives can fully meet energy demand.

passages.passage_text:
The nineteenth century brought about the greatest expansion of wealth the world had ever known. Its sources lay in the industrialisation of Europe and the techniques for assuring the continuance of this growth were by no means exhausted or compromised in 1900. There had not only been a vast and accelerating flow of commodities available only in (relatively) tiny quantities a century before, but whole new ranges of goods had come into existence. Oil and electricity had joined coal, wood, wind and water as sources of energy. A chemical industry existed which could not have been envisaged in 1800. Growing power and wealth had been used to tap seemingly inexhaustible natural resources, both agricultural and mineral. Railways, electric trams, steamships, motor cars and bicycles gave millions of men a new control over their environment; they accelerated travel from place to place and eased transport for the first time since animals had been harnessed to carts thousands of years before. In terms of consumption, or of the services to which they had access, or in the enjoyment of better health, even the mass of the population in developed countries were much better off in 1900 than their predecessors a hundred years before.

In spite of this cheerful picture, doubts could break in. Even if what might happen in the future were ignored, contemplation of the cost of the new wealth and doubts about the social justice of its distribution were troubling. Most people were still terribly poor, whether or not they lived in rich countries, where the illogicality of this was particularly more striking than in earlier times. Another change in the way men thought about their condition arose over their power to get a livelihood at all. It was not new that men should be without work. What was new was that situations could suddenly arise in which the operation of blind forces of boom and slump produced millions of men without work concentrated in great towns. This was 'unemployment', the new phenomenon for which a new word had been needed. Nor were the cities themselves yet rid of all the evils which had so struck the first observers of industrial society. By 1900 the majority of western Europeans were town-dwellers and they lived in more than 140 cities of over 100,000 inhabitants in 1914. In some of them, millions of people were living in cramped, badly-maintained housing, under-provided with schools and fresh air, let alone amusement other than that of the street, and this often in sight of the wealth their society helped to produce. 'Slums' was another word invented by the nineteenth century.

task1.model_answer: During the nineteenth century, European industrialisation generated unprecedented wealth, new energy sources such as oil and electricity, and revolutionary transport systems that markedly improved consumption and public health. Nevertheless, this material triumph was shadowed by stark social inequalities. Even within prosperous nations, widespread poverty endured, while unpredictable boom-and-slump cycles created mass urban joblessness, giving rise to the term 'unemployment'. Furthermore, rapid urbanisation concentrated millions of people into overcrowded, poorly maintained districts lacking basic education and clean air, leading to the invention of another nineteenth-century term: 'slums'. Together, these contrasts reveal an era of remarkable technological progress paired with deep social hardship.

task2.model_answer:
Rapid economic and technological growth has historically raised average living standards, yet it does not automatically produce fair outcomes for everyone. As the nineteenth-century experience demonstrates, expanding industries and new transport networks can generate enormous wealth while leaving large segments of the working population in insecure, overcrowded conditions. Without deliberate social policies, market cycles of boom and slump expose workers to sudden unemployment, widening the gap between those who own capital and those who supply labour.

Admittedly, free enterprise encourages innovation and productivity, which provide the resources needed for better healthcare, education, and infrastructure. However, the benefits of growth reach all citizens only when institutions actively regulate working conditions, invest in public housing and schools, and protect workers during economic downturns. Therefore, economic expansion should be viewed as a necessary foundation rather than a guarantee of social justice; lasting prosperity depends equally on equitable distribution and civic responsibility.

passages.tts_script_tr:
On Dokuzuncu Yüzyıla Genel Bir Bakış.

On dokuzuncu yüzyıl, dünyanın o zamana dek gördüğü en büyük refah artışını beraberinde getirdi. Bunun kaynakları Avrupa'nın sanayileşmesinde yatıyordu ve bu büyümenin devamını güvence altına alan teknikler 1900 yılında hiçbir şekilde tükenmiş ya da zayıflamış değildi. Yalnızca bir yüzyıl önce nispeten çok küçük miktarlarda bulunabilen ticari malların devasa ve hızlanan bir akışı yaşanmakla kalmamış, aynı zamanda tamamen yeni ürün yelpazeleri de ortaya çıkmıştı. Petrol ve elektrik, enerji kaynakları olarak kömür, odun, rüzgar ve suyun yanına katılmıştı. 1800 yılında hayal bile edilemeyecek bir kimya sanayisi artık mevcuttu. Artan güç ve zenginlik, hem tarımsal hem de madensel açıdan tükenmez gibi görünen doğal kaynaklardan yararlanmak için kullanılmıştı. Demiryolları, elektrikli tramvaylar, buharlı gemiler, motorlu arabalar ve bisikletler milyonlarca insana çevreleri üzerinde yeni bir kontrol sağladı; binlerce yıl önce hayvanların arabalara koşulmasından bu yana ilk kez bir yerden bir yere seyahati hızlandırdı ve ulaşımı kolaylaştırdı. Tüketim, erişebildikleri hizmetler ya da daha iyi sağlık koşullarına sahip olma açısından, gelişmiş ülkelerdeki nüfusun büyük çoğunluğu bile 1900 yılında yüz yıl önceki atalarından çok daha iyi durumdaydı.

Bu neşeli tabloya rağmen şüpheler baş gösterebiliyordu. Gelecekte neler olabileceği göz ardı edilse bile, yeni refahın bedeli üzerine düşünmek ve dağılımındaki toplumsal adalete dair kuşkular kaygı vericiydi. Çoğu insan, zengin ülkelerde yaşasın ya da yaşamasın, hala korkunç derecede yoksuldu; üstelik zengin ülkelerde bu durumun mantıksızlığı önceki dönemlere kıyasla özellikle daha çarpıcıydı. İnsanların kendi durumları hakkındaki düşünce biçiminde meydana gelen bir başka değişiklik ise geçimlerini sağlama güçleriyle ilgiliydi. İnsanların işsiz kalması yeni bir şey değildi. Yeni olan şey, ekonomik yükseliş ve çöküşün kör güçlerinin işleyişinin büyük kentlerde toplanmış milyonlarca işsiz insan yarattığı durumların aniden ortaya çıkabilmesiydi. Bu, kendisi için yeni bir kelimeye ihtiyaç duyulan o yeni olguydu: 'işsizlik'. Şehirlerin kendileri de sanayi toplumunun ilk gözlemcilerini bu denli sarsan tüm kötülüklerden henüz arınmış değildi. 1900 yılına gelindiğinde Batı Avrupalıların çoğunluğu kent sakiniydi ve 1914'te nüfusu 100.000'in üzerinde olan 140'tan fazla şehirde yaşıyorlardı. Bunların bazılarında milyonlarca insan, sokak eğlencesi dışında hiçbir eğlencenin bulunmadığı, okul ve temiz havadan yoksun, sıkışık ve bakımsız konutlarda, üstelik çoğu zaman kendi toplumlarının üretilmesine yardımcı olduğu zenginliğin gözü önünde yaşıyordu. 'Sefalet mahalleleri' de on dokuzuncu yüzyılın icat ettiği bir başka kelimeydi.

passages.passage_text:
Marianne Hardwick was timid and unadventurous, her vitality consumed by physical activity and longing, her intelligence by indecisiveness, but this had less to do with the innate characteristics of the weaker sex (as her father, Creighton Montgomery, called it) than with the enfeebling circumstances of her upbringing. Creighton Montgomery had enough money to mould his daughters according to his misconceptions: girls were not meant to fend for themselves, so he protected them from life. This meant that Marianne Montgomery grew up without making any vital choices for herself. Prevented from acquiring the habits of freedom and strength of character which grow from decision-making, very rich girls whose parents protect them in such a crippling fashion are the last representatives of Victorian womanhood. Though they may have the boldest manners and most up-to-date ideas, they share their great-grandmothers' humble dependence.

Most parents these days have to rely on their force of personality and whatever love and respect they can inspire to exert any influence over their children at all, but there is still an awful lot of parental authority that big money can buy. Multi-millionaires have more of everything than ordinary mortals, including more parent power, and their sons and daughters have about as much opportunity to develop according to their own inclinations as they would have had in the age of absolute monarchy.

The great divide between the generations (so much taken for granted that no one remarks on it any longer) is the plight of the lower and middle classes, whose children begin to drift away as soon as they are old enough to go to school. The parents cannot control the school, and have even less say as to what company and ideas the child will be exposed to; nor can they isolate him from the public mood, the spirit of the age. It is an often-heard complaint of the middle-class mother, for instance, that she must let her children watch television for hours on end every day if she is to steal any time for herself. The rich have no such problems; they can keep their offspring busy from morning to night without being near them for a minute more than they choose to be, and can exercise almost total control over their environment. As for schooling, they can hand-pick tutors with sound views to come to the children, who may never leave the grounds their parents own, in town, in the country, by the sea, unless for an exceptionally secure boarding school or a well-chaperoned trip abroad. It would have been easier for little Marianne Montgomery to go to Cairo than to the nearest newsstand.

passages.title: Child-Raising
passages.tts_script:
Child-Raising.

Marianne Hardwick was timid and unadventurous, her vitality consumed by physical activity and longing, her intelligence by indecisiveness, but this had less to do with the innate characteristics of the weaker sex, as her father, Creighton Montgomery, called it, than with the enfeebling circumstances of her upbringing. Creighton Montgomery had enough money to mould his daughters according to his misconceptions: girls were not meant to fend for themselves, so he protected them from life. This meant that Marianne Montgomery grew up without making any vital choices for herself. Prevented from acquiring the habits of freedom and strength of character which grow from decision-making, very rich girls whose parents protect them in such a crippling fashion are the last representatives of Victorian womanhood. Though they may have the boldest manners and most up-to-date ideas, they share their great-grandmothers' humble dependence.

Most parents these days have to rely on their force of personality and whatever love and respect they can inspire to exert any influence over their children at all, but there is still an awful lot of parental authority that big money can buy. Multi-millionaires have more of everything than ordinary mortals, including more parent power, and their sons and daughters have about as much opportunity to develop according to their own inclinations as they would have had in the age of absolute monarchy.

The great divide between the generations, so much taken for granted that no one remarks on it any longer, is the plight of the lower and middle classes, whose children begin to drift away as soon as they are old enough to go to school. The parents cannot control the school, and have even less say as to what company and ideas the child will be exposed to; nor can they isolate him from the public mood, the spirit of the age. It is an often-heard complaint of the middle-class mother, for instance, that she must let her children watch television for hours on end every day if she is to steal any time for herself. The rich have no such problems; they can keep their offspring busy from morning to night without being near them for a minute more than they choose to be, and can exercise almost total control over their environment. As for schooling, they can hand-pick tutors with sound views to come to the children, who may never leave the grounds their parents own, in town, in the country, by the sea, unless for an exceptionally secure boarding school or a well-chaperoned trip abroad. It would have been easier for little Marianne Montgomery to go to Cairo than to the nearest newsstand.

task1.model_answer: The passage contrasts how wealth shapes parental control over child-raising. Using Marianne Hardwick as an example, the author shows how a multi-millionaire father can shield his daughters from everyday decisions, leaving them dependent despite modern manners and ideas. Whereas ordinary lower- and middle-class parents lose influence once their children enter school and encounter outside peers, television, and wider cultural currents, the super-rich can purchase almost absolute authority. By hiring approved private tutors, arranging constant activities, and restricting travel to secure boarding schools or supervised trips abroad, wealthy parents regulate every aspect of their children's environment without even needing to be physically present.

task2.model_answer:
When parents shield their children from every challenge or independent decision, they often achieve the opposite of what they intend. Instead of creating confident adults, excessive protection deprives young people of the chance to make mistakes, weigh consequences, and build resilience. As the example of Marianne Hardwick illustrates, someone who is never permitted to fend for herself may grow up indecisive and timid, unable to exercise genuine freedom even when surrounded by material comfort.

At the same time, children who receive little guidance at all can struggle just as much, as they are left entirely to the influence of peers and commercial media. Healthy upbringing therefore lies in guided autonomy: parents should set clear ethical boundaries and provide emotional support while gradually handing over real choices. By allowing children to navigate ordinary daily responsibilities, parents foster both character and lasting self-reliance.

Marianne Hardwick ürkek ve maceradan uzak biriydi; canlılığı fiziksel aktiviteler ve özlemlerle, zekâsı ise kararsızlıkla tükenmişti; ancak bunun, babası Creighton Montgomery'nin deyimiyle zayıf cinsin doğuştan gelen özelliklerinden ziyade, yetiştirilme koşullarının güçsüzleştirici etkisiyle ilgisi vardı. Creighton Montgomery kızlarını kendi yanlış kanaatlerine göre şekillendirecek kadar paraya sahipti: kızlar kendi başlarının çaresine bakmak üzere yaratılmamıştı, bu yüzden onları hayattan korudu. Bu durum, Marianne Montgomery'nin kendi adına hiçbir hayati seçim yapmadan büyümesi anlamına geliyordu. Karar verme sürecinden beslenen özgürlük alışkanlıklarını ve karakter gücünü edinmeleri engellenen, anne babaları tarafından böylesine kısıtlayıcı bir biçimde korunan çok zengin kızlar, Viktorya dönemi kadınlığının son temsilcileridir. En cesur tavırlara ve en güncel fikirlere sahip olsalar bile, büyük ninelerinin mütevazı bağımlılığını paylaşırlar.

Günümüzde çoğu anne baba, çocukları üzerinde herhangi bir etki kurabilmek için kişilik güçlerine ve uyandırabildikleri sevgi ile saygıya güvenmek zorundadır; ancak büyük paranın satın alabildiği hâlâ çok fazla ebeveyn otoritesi vardır. Multimilyonerler, daha fazla ebeveyn gücü de dâhil olmak üzere sıradan ölümlülerden her şeye daha fazla sahiptir ve oğullarıyla kızlarının kendi eğilimlerine göre gelişme fırsatı, mutlak monarşi çağında sahip olacaklarından pek de fazla değildir.

Artık o kadar kanıksandığı için kimsenin üzerinde durmadığı kuşaklar arasındaki büyük uçurum, çocukları okula gidecek yaşa gelir gelmez kendilerinden uzaklaşmaya başlayan alt ve orta sınıfların çaresiz durumudur. Anne babalar okulu kontrol edemez, çocuğun hangi arkadaş çevresine ve fikirlere maruz kalacağı konusunda ise daha da az söz sahibidir; ayrıca onu toplumun ruh halinden, çağın ruhundan da yalıtamazlar. Örneğin orta sınıf bir annenin, kendine biraz olsun zaman ayırabilmek için her gün çocuklarının saatlerce aralıksız televizyon izlemesine izin vermek zorunda kalması sıkça duyulan bir şikâyettir. Zenginlerin böyle sorunları yoktur; çocuklarını sabahtan akşama kadar meşgul tutabilir, kendi istediklerinden bir dakika bile fazla yanlarında olmadan çevreleri üzerinde neredeyse tam bir kontrol kurabilirler. Eğitime gelince; son derece güvenli bir yatılı okul ya da sıkı gözetim altında yapılan bir yurt dışı gezisi dışında, anne babalarının şehirde, kırsalda ya da deniz kıyısında sahip olduğu arazilerden hiç ayrılmayabilen çocukların ayağına sağlam görüşlere sahip özel öğretmenleri özenle seçip getirebilirler. Küçük Marianne Montgomery için Kahire'ye gitmek, en yakın gazete bayisine gitmekten daha kolay olurdu.

task1.model_answer: According to the passage, heroism has existed in every historical era. True heroes stand out in their communities through remarkable accomplishments that reflect an exceptional personal virtue, such as courage, wisdom, or faith. Because their achievements demonstrate these qualities clearly, public admiration of heroes inspires others to imitate their conduct. task2.model_answer:
In an age dominated by social media and constant publicity, the idea of a quiet, selfless hero can seem increasingly rare, yet genuine heroism has not disappeared. While online platforms often reward people who actively chase recognition, everyday acts of courage and integrity continue to take place far from the spotlight. Doctors serving in crisis zones, firefighters risking their lives, and ordinary citizens helping neighbours during disasters rarely act for applause.

Of course, public visibility can sometimes help good causes by inspiring others to follow a positive example, as the passage notes. Even so, recognition must remain a by-product rather than the goal. When individuals perform noble deeds purely to gain followers or praise, their motivation becomes egotistical. Ultimately, true heroism is still defined not by how loudly someone is celebrated, but by selfless action rooted in lasting human virtues.

passages.passage_text:
It is interesting to compare the brain of a very large dinosaur with the brain of an equally large modern mammal like the whale. The largest dinosaurs weighed as much as 100 tons. Whales also weigh as much as 100 tons and are, as the dinosaurs were in their time, the largest animals alive today. The brain of a large whale is a huge mass of gray matter, nearly a foot and a half across, that weighs about 20 pounds. The possessor of this mammoth brain is an intelligent animal. Some whales have a remarkable memory capacity; they can memorize a complex whale song that goes on for hours, and repeat it note for note a year later. The brains of the largest dinosaurs, on the other hand, such as Supersaurus, were only the size of an orange, and weighed about half a pound. Yet, that small amount of gray matter had to exercise control over the same 100-ton bulk that is commanded by the 20-pound brain of the largest whales.

Scientists who specialize in the study of brains and intelligence have plotted charts of brain weight against body weight for many kinds of animals. They find that when the ratio of brain weight to body weight is as small as it was in the Supersaurus, the behavior of the animal is stereotyped, automatic, and unintelligent. The reason is clear: a large body has many large muscles and needs many nerve fibers for its coordination. When that large body is controlled by a small brain, every neuron in this brain must be used to move the body through its basic survival routines: find food, flee from the predator, and so on.

The Supersaurus was not an unusually stupid dinosaur, and dinosaurs were not unusually stupid reptiles. In fact, dinosaurs had normal intelligence for reptiles. Of course, there was a spread in braininess among the dinosaurs. But the same is true among modern mammals; plant-eaters like the cow are among the least intelligent mammals, while alert carnivores like the wolf are among the most intelligent. However, the dinosaurs as a group were generally less intelligent than the early mammals as a group. This held then, and still holds today, all the way up and down the scale of sizes. A little lizard, for example, has a considerably smaller brain than a chipmunk of the same size and displays a far less flexible repertoire.

task1.model_answer: Although both the largest dinosaurs, like the Supersaurus, and modern whales reach about 100 tons, their brain sizes differ dramatically. A whale has a 20-pound brain capable of impressive feats such as memorizing hours-long songs for a year, whereas the Supersaurus relied on a half-pound, orange-sized brain. Because coordinating huge muscles consumes nearly every neuron in such a small brain, the dinosaur's behavior was limited to automatic survival routines. While dinosaurs had typical intelligence for reptiles, reptiles as a group consistently have smaller brains and less flexible behavior than mammals of comparable size, just as a lizard is far less adaptable than a chipmunk.
task1.prompt: Summarize how brain-to-body weight ratios explain differences in intelligence between giant dinosaurs, whales, and modern reptiles versus mammals.
task1.title: Summary: Brain Size and Animal Intelligence

task2.model_answer: Evaluating animal intelligence through a single standard, such as brain-to-body weight ratio, reveals useful patterns but fails to capture the full picture. As the passage shows, comparing brain weight with body weight explains why massive reptiles like the Supersaurus relied on fixed survival routines while whales display remarkable memory. Larger relative brain size generally allows neurons to handle learning and flexible problem-solving rather than just muscle coordination. However, measuring physical proportions alone overlooks how differently brains are organized across species. For example, birds have relatively small brains in absolute terms, yet crows and parrots can use tools and solve multi-step puzzles. Similarly, social cooperation, sensory perception, and environmental adaptation vary widely among species and cannot be predicted solely by weight charts. Therefore, while brain-to-body ratios provide a helpful starting point for biologists, assessing animal intelligence accurately requires observing actual behavior, memory, and adaptability in each species' natural habitat.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Beyinler.

Çok büyük bir dinozorun beynini, balina gibi aynı büyüklükteki modern bir memelinin beyniyle karşılaştırmak ilginçtir. En büyük dinozorlar 100 tona kadar çıkıyordu. Balinalar da 100 tona kadar çıkar ve tıpkı dinozorların kendi dönemlerinde olduğu gibi, bugün yaşayan en büyük hayvanlardır. Büyük bir balinanın beyni, çapı neredeyse bir buçuk fit olan ve yaklaşık 20 pound ağırlığında devasa bir gri madde kütlesidir. Bu devasa beynin sahibi zeki bir hayvandır. Bazı balinaların olağanüstü bir hafıza kapasitesi vardır; saatlerce süren karmaşık bir balina şarkısını ezberleyebilir ve bir yıl sonra notasını şaşmadan tekrarlayabilirler. Öte yandan, Supersaurus gibi en büyük dinozorların beyinleri yalnızca bir portakal büyüklüğündeydi ve yaklaşık yarım pound ağırlığındaydı. Yine de bu küçücük gri madde miktarı, en büyük balinaların 20 pound'luk beyni tarafından yönetilen aynı 100 tonluk kütleyi kontrol etmek zorundaydı.

Beyin ve zekâ araştırmalarında uzmanlaşmış bilim insanları, birçok hayvan türü için vücut ağırlığına karşılık beyin ağırlığı grafikleri çizmişlerdir. Beyin ağırlığının vücut ağırlığına oranı Supersaurus'taki kadar küçük olduğunda, hayvanın davranışlarının basmakalıp, otomatik ve zekâdan yoksun olduğunu görmüşlerdir. Bunun nedeni açıktır: büyük bir vücudun çok sayıda büyük kası vardır ve koordinasyonu için pek çok sinir lifine ihtiyaç duyar. Bu büyük vücut küçük bir beyin tarafından kontrol edildiğinde, beyindeki her nöron vücudu temel hayatta kalma rutinlerinde — yiyecek bulmak, yırtıcıdan kaçmak vb. — hareket ettirmek için kullanılmak zorundadır.

Supersaurus olağanüstü aptal bir dinozor değildi ve dinozorlar da olağanüstü aptal sürüngenler değildi. Aslında dinozorlar, sürüngenler için normal bir zekâya sahipti. Elbette dinozorlar arasında da zekâ düzeyi bakımından bir çeşitlilik vardı. Ancak aynı durum modern memeliler için de geçerlidir; inek gibi otçullar en az zeki memeliler arasında yer alırken, kurt gibi tetikte etçiller en zekiler arasındadır. Bununla birlikte, bir grup olarak dinozorlar genel olarak ilk memeliler grubundan daha az zekiydi. Bu durum o zaman geçerliydi ve bugün de en küçüğünden en büyüğüne tüm boyut ölçeği boyunca hâlâ geçerlidir. Örneğin küçük bir kertenkele, kendisiyle aynı boyuttaki bir çizgili sincaptan çok daha küçük bir beyne sahiptir ve çok daha az esnek bir davranış repertuvarı sergiler.

passages.passage_text:
For adults who remain physically childlike in old age, there has to be a sustained enthusiasm for some aspect of life. People who want a long life with an alert old age should never retire. If they are forcibly retired, they should immerse themselves in some new, absorbing activity.

Some people are naturally more physically active than others, and are at a considerable advantage, providing their activities are not the result of stress. Such activities as walking and gardening prolong life spectacularly because they are 'non-intensive' forms of all-over bodily movement. The more earnest ageing exercisers display a conscious or unconscious anxiety about their health. If they take exercise too seriously, it will work against them. Older individuals who take up intensive athletic activity are usually people who fear declining health. Yet, it is crucial that physical exercise - as we grow past the young sportsman stage - should be extensive rather than intensive and, above all, fun.

A calm temperament favours longevity. Those who are sharply aggressive, emotionally explosive or naggingly anxious are at a grave disadvantage. But it is important to make a distinction between calmly relaxed and passively lazy. Relaxation does not contradict the idea of passionate interest. Indeed, zest for living, eagerness to pursue chosen subjects are vital in long life.

Thinking about 'the good old days', complaining about how the world is deteriorating, criticising the younger generations are sure signs of an early funeral.

Being successful is a great life-stretcher, and can even override such life-shorteners as obesity and fondness for drink. But, in gaining success, individuals should not overstress themselves. And success must always be measured in personal terms. A hill-shepherd may feel just as successful in his own way as a Nobel Laureate.

Long-lived individuals seem to be more concerned with what they do than who they are. They live outside themselves rather than dwelling on their own personalities.

In personal habits, the long-lived are generally moderate. Extremes of diet are not common. A mixed diet seems to favour longevity. Puritanical arguments about smoking and drinking have little to support them. Many long-lived individuals enjoy nicotine and alcohol - in moderation.

Most long-lived people have a sense of self-discipline. That does not imply a harsh military-style masochism, but the ordering of life and the imposition of a pattern on the events of the day. The man who lives long because he walks a mile a day does so because he does it every day, as part of an organised existence.

Over and over, during my researches, it emerged that long life goes with a 'twinkle in the eye'. A sense of humour, impishness, a feeling that life is fun, are strong weapons against ageing. The sour-faced puritan and the solemn bore soon begin to lose ground, leaving their more amused contemporaries to enjoy the last laugh.

Most important of all, we should always keep in mind that nothing is to be gained by a head-in-the-sand avoidance of the facts of life and death. The healthiest solution is to accept that one's span on Earth is limited and then to live every day, in the present, and to the full.

passages.tts_script_tr:
Yüz Yaşına Kadar Nasıl Yaşanır.

Yaşlılıkta fiziksel olarak çocuksu kalabilen yetişkinlerde, hayatın bir yönüne karşı sürekli bir coşku bulunması gerekir. Zinde bir yaşlılıkla birlikte uzun bir ömür isteyen insanlar asla emekli olmamalıdır. Eğer zorunlu olarak emekli edilirlerse, kendilerini yeni ve sürükleyici bir uğraşa kaptırmalıdırlar.

Bazı insanlar doğaları gereği diğerlerinden fiziksel olarak daha aktiftir ve aktiviteleri stresten kaynaklanmadığı sürece önemli bir avantaja sahiptirler. Yürüyüş ve bahçe işleri gibi aktiviteler, tüm vücudu çalıştıran ama aşırı yoğun olmayan hareket biçimleri oldukları için ömrü olağanüstü ölçüde uzatır. Egzersizi gereğinden fazla ciddiye alan yaşlanan kişiler ise sağlıkları hakkında bilinçli ya da bilinçsiz bir kaygı sergilerler. Egzersizi fazla ciddiye alırlarsa, bu durum aleyhlerine işleyecektir. Yoğun atletik aktivitelere başlayan yaşlı bireyler genellikle sağlığının bozulmasından korkan insanlardır. Oysa genç sporcu evresini geride bıraktıkça, fiziksel egzersizin yoğun değil yaygın olması ve her şeyden önce eğlenceli olması çok önemlidir.

Sakin bir mizaç uzun ömrü destekler. Sert biçimde saldırgan, duygusal olarak patlamaya hazır ya da sürekli endişeli olanlar ciddi bir dezavantaj içindedir. Ancak sakin bir rahatlık ile pasif bir tembellik arasında ayrım yapmak önemlidir. Rahatlama, tutkulu ilgi fikriyle çelişmez. Gerçekten de yaşama sevinci ve seçilen konuların peşinden gitme hevesi uzun bir yaşamda hayati önem taşır.

Eski güzel günleri düşünüp durmak, dünyanın nasıl kötüye gittiğinden yakınmak ve genç kuşakları eleştirmek erken bir cenazenin kesin işaretleridir.

Başarılı olmak büyük bir ömür uzatıcıdır ve obezite ya da içkiye düşkünlük gibi ömür kısaltıcı etkenlerin bile üstesinden gelebilir. Ancak başarıya ulaşırken bireyler kendilerini aşırı strese sokmamalıdır. Ve başarı her zaman kişisel ölçütlerle değerlendirilmelidir. Bir dağ çobanı da kendi çapında bir Nobel Ödülü sahibi kadar başarılı hissedebilir.

Uzun ömürlü bireyler, kim olduklarından ziyade ne yaptıklarıyla daha fazla ilgileniyor görünmektedir. Kendi kişiliklerine takılıp kalmak yerine, kendilerinin dışındaki dünyaya dönük yaşarlar.

Kişisel alışkanlıklarda uzun ömürlü insanlar genellikle ölçülüdür. Beslenmede aşırılıklar yaygın değildir. Karma bir beslenme biçimi uzun ömrü destekliyor görünmektedir. Sigara ve içki konusundaki katı ahlakçı savların pek dayanağı yoktur. Uzun ömürlü birçok birey ölçülü biçimde nikotin ve alkolden keyif alır.

Uzun ömürlü insanların çoğunda bir öz disiplin duygusu vardır. Bu, sert ve askeri tarzda bir eziyet değil, yaşamı düzene sokmak ve günün olaylarına belli bir düzen getirmek anlamına gelir. Günde bir mil yürüdüğü için uzun yaşayan adam, bunu düzenli bir yaşamın parçası olarak her gün yaptığı için uzun yaşar.

Araştırmalarım sırasında tekrar tekrar, uzun ömrün gözlerdeki bir ışıltıyla birlikte geldiği ortaya çıktı. Mizah anlayışı, muziplik ve hayatın eğlenceli olduğu hissi, yaşlanmaya karşı güçlü silahlardır. Asık suratlı katı ahlakçılar ve sıkıcı ağırbaşlı tipler kısa sürede güç kaybeder, son gülüşün tadını çıkarma şansını ise hayattan daha çok keyif alan yaşıtlarına bırakırlar.

Hepsinden önemlisi, yaşam ve ölüm gerçeklerinden başını kuma gömerek kaçınmakla hiçbir şey kazanılamayacağını her zaman aklımızda tutmalıyız. En sağlıklı çözüm, insanın yeryüzündeki ömrünün sınırlı olduğunu kabul etmek ve ardından her günü, şimdiki zamanda ve dolu dolu yaşamaktır.
